title: Fanatics Sportsbook agrees to pay fine for contacting self-excluded gambler
summary: As the sports betting industry continues to grow, regulation of it becomes critical.
full_text: ' As the sports betting industry continues to grow, regulation of it becomes critical. Enforcing those regulations is part of that effort. In Colorado, Fanatics Sportsbook has agreed to pay a $20,000 fine for contacting a gambler who self-excluded from further promotions. Via Noelle Phillips of the Denver Post , the fine was levied on Thursday following an agreement between the company and the Colorado Limited Gaming Control Commission. The self-exclusion list, a tool for addressing gambling addiction, prohibits sportsbooks from sending promotional information to those on it. A Fanatics VIP host contacted the gambler in question twice. Fanatics Sportsbook, one of three NFL sportsbook partners for 2026, also agreed to audit its self-exclusion list, in order to determine whether others from a group of roughly 1,200 Coloradans were sent marketing promotions via text message between January 1, 2024, and March 1, 2026. It also will train staff members on the self-exclusion rules. Much more regulation of the industry is needed. And all regulations need to be properly applied. Many gamblers have become addicted, thanks to the ease of placing bets by phone. They win some, then they lose. Then they chase their losses. And then they fall into a hole that only gets deeper. It's a basic reality that anyone working in sports media needs to recognize, and to repeat. The house wins. That's why it's a good business model. Which means the gamblers lose. That fact must be accepted by anyone who tiptoes down the primrose path of easy money before learning a very hard, and perhaps irreversible, lesson.
author: Mike Florio

title: SEC will defend its effort to ban former NFL players in court on Thursday
summary: The legal imbroglio over former NFL players returning to play college football is far from over.
full_text: ' The legal imbroglio over former NFL players returning to play college football is far from over. Last week, a temporary restraining order prevented the SEC from enforcing its prohibition on its member schools using players who have spent time with NFL teams. This week, the SEC will try again. Via Mark Schlabach of ESPN, the SEC intends to contest the TRO during a hearing set for Thursday. "The order entered against the SEC and commissioner Sankey is a temporary restraining order, not a final ruling on the merits ," the SEC said in a statement Sunday, via Schlabach. "The SEC and commissioner Sankey are prepared to contest the allegations in the plaintiffs' petition at Thursday morning's hearing and defend the SEC's rights as a voluntary association to fulfill its mission to its member institutions. "In the meantime, the SEC and commissioner Sankey will continue to comply with the court's order. Following the hearing, the SEC will carefully review the court's decision and determine the appropriate next steps." The uncertainty lingers as college football season commences. No one knows what the rule will be. And it serves only to highlight the sense of chaos that the college football fat cats surely hope to parlay into the passage of the Protect College Sports Act, under the idea that it's the lone antidote to restoring sanity to an insane situation spawned by decades of blatant antitrust violations that robbed players of the ability to get fair compensation for their abilities, efforts, and sacrifices in the name of "amateur athletics."
author: Mike Florio

title: Joe Burrow on Super Bowl goals: "If you don’t talk about it, I don’t know how you can do it.”
summary: Not many teams that have missed the playoffs for three straight seasons are viewed as a team of destiny.
full_text: '' Not many teams that have missed the playoffs for three straight seasons are viewed as a team of destiny. That isn't stopping Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow from attempting to speak a Super Bowl win into existence. “ I’ve never understood why people are scared to say it ,” Burrow told Albert Breer of SI.com. “I guess people get scared of how the media will portray them or their team in a certain way. But you have to set expectations with yourself, your teammates, your organization. Everybody says they want to win the Super Bowl, you talk about it every day, you set that expectation every day, you go and work for it every single day. I mean, I don’t know the answer to that for everybody, but that’s what I want to do, that’s what I’m trying to do, that’s what I do this for. “I won the championship in college, and there’s no freaking better feeling than that. And if you don’t talk about it, I don’t know how you can do it.” He's right about that. He's also right about the other 31 teams having the same goal. Whether they talk about it or not, they enter each season at 0-0 and with high hopes. For Burrow, he's basing his belief on something tangible. He's comparing the vibe at the 2026 Bengals to the sense he had at LSU, seven years ago. “I don’t know, it just felt inevitable,” Burrow told Breer. “We finished stronger the year before. I knew how good Justin [Jefferson] was. I didn’t quite know how good Ja’Marr [Chase] was going to be yet because his superpower is after the catch, and in practice you can’t really see that. He was getting open and making plays. Obviously, that’s what he does, but what makes him one of one is after the catch. I realized that somewhere in the early 2019 season. “But, yeah, I just knew how things felt around the building. I knew how practices were going. I knew that offense fit my skill set more so than any one I had been in. It just made sense to me. As I said, there was just a feeling around the building that it was inevitable.” Burrow's confidence in the Bengals is bolstered by the other side of the ball. “The vibe of the defense is really good right now,” Burrow said. “Our defensive line is so deep this year. The depth of that unit was a weak point last year, [but] now we have nine or 10 guys that we feel good about putting out there in five-down sets. Obviously, Dexter [Lawrence II] plays a big role in that. Jonathan Allen plays a big role in that. And those guys have been vocal leaders for us to start this out, which is something that we needed." Whatever happens, the stakes are high. A fourth straight year with no postseason appearance will likely spark a coaching change. And it could make Burrow, after seven years in Cincinnati, look for a place where it will seem even more inevitable that he'll be smoking a locker-room cigar in one or more of the remaining Februarys of his career.
author: Mike Florio

title: Sean McVay still isn't talking about travel plans for Australia
summary: Earlier this month, Rams coach Sean McVay turned uncharacteristically truculent when asked about reports that his team would arrive late and leave early from Australia.
full_text: ' Earlier this month, Rams coach Sean McVay turned uncharacteristically truculent when asked about reports that his team would arrive late and leave early from Australia. It was clear McVay didn't want to talk about the topic publicly until he talked to his team, which meant there was no reason to talk to a 90-man team about something that would ultimately impact only 53 of them (plus the practice squad). On Sunday, he was asked whether he has spoken to the team about the itinerary. “I haven't done that yet," McVay said, "so that means I'm not talking to you about it either." The next question was whether he has a timeline for doing so. “I'll probably do it the week of the game so don’t ask me until then," McVay said. "Here’s what I would tell you though. I know we've laughed and had some good fun interactions about it, but I do want to be able — I think they have a loose idea of what we're doing but I do still think it is appropriate in terms of the trajectory. I want to be able to talk to them about it, but we're leaving later than most people would probably expect." In other words, yep, they're going late. And they're leaving early. With the apparent goal of minimizing the impact of the stay in Melbourne on their body clocks. The question is whether they'll be appropriately acclimated to perform in Australia, given the long flight and the short lag time. Especially since the 49ers apparently plan to get there several days before the Rams. Either way, the game is only 10 days away. And the travel discrepancy could be an issue during the game. After the game, the question will be whether the Rams recover more quickly than the 49ers from the ordeal, given the decision not to stick around long enough to adjust to being in the land down under.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jadarian Price set for heavy workload with Zach Charbonnet out to start the season
summary: The Seahawks made it official that running back Zach Charbonnet will start the season on the physically unable to perform list, and that makes it clear how big a role rookie running back Jadarian Price is going to have in the defending champions' offense.
full_text: The Seahawks made it official that running back Zach Charbonnet will start the season on the physically unable to perform list , and that makes it clear how big a role rookie running back Jadarian Price is going to have in the defending champions' offense. Last year the Seahawks used a two-back system with Charbonnet and Kenneth Walker sharing carries. Walker left in free agency and Charbonnet has still not fully recovered from the knee injury he suffered in last season's playoffs, and the Seahawks did not add any notable running backs other than Price. Price is the clear-cut No. 1 running back in Seattle, and backing him up will be George Holani, who gained just 73 yards on 22 carries last season, and Emanuel Wilson, a career backup in Green Bay who signed with the Seahawks this offseason. The good news for the Seahawks is that Price got rave reviews in the offseason, with head coach Mike Macdonald saying he was ready for a big workload and quarterback Sam Darnold calling Price a special player . The Seahawks may need Price to be special if they're going to repeat as champions.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Dolphins' initial 53-man roster is youngest in the league
summary: Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley said last week that the team's success for the 2026 season won't be measured by their place in the standings because "this year’s so much about developing who we are as a football team" as they move into the future.
full_text: Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley said last week that the team's success for the 2026 season won't be measured by their place in the standings because "this year’s so much about developing who we are as a football team " as they move into the future. The team's initial 53-man roster reflects that focus. As Joe Schad of the Palm Beach Post points out, the Dolphins have the youngest roster in the NFL after cutdown day on Sunday. Miami's average player is 25.3 years old and the Browns are the only other team in the league with an average age of under 26. Schad also notes that 47 percent of the players on the initial roster are between 22 and 24. All of that youth could make for some tough sledding for Hafley in his first season on the job, but the hope in Miami is that short-term pain results in a long-term foundation for success that can be measured more tangibly than what they're pitching this season.
author: Josh Alper

title: Dolphins will waive Mark Gronowski, add Kyle McCord
summary: As of Saturday, Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said he thinks it's likely the team will keep two quarterbacks on the 53-man roster.
full_text: As of Saturday, Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said he thinks it's likely the team will keep two quarterbacks on the 53-man roster. But it will be only one of the four quarterbacks who were on the roster 24 hours ago. With Quinn Ewers traded to the Jaguars and Cam Miller waived, the Dolphins reportedly will also waive Mark Gronowski . And they'll replace him with Kyle McCord. The Dolphins have agreed to send a 2028 sixth-round pick to the Packers for McCord, who was signed to a futures contract by the Packers on January 20. For Miami, which is now led by former Packers executive Jon-Eric Sullivan and former Packers defensive coordinator Hafley, the move taps into the Green Bay pipeline. And it gives the Dolphins their apparent backup to Malik Willis — even though McCord is arriving with no practice or preseason reps in Miami. (However, as Mike Garafolo of NFL Network notes, the move reunites McCord with former Eagles offensive coordinator Kevin Patullo, who is now the passing game coordinator in Miami.) As to Gronowski, he'll reportedly be added to the Miami practice squad, if/when he clears waivers.
author: Mike Florio

title: Can the Rams get Aaron Donald ready for Week 1?
summary: Rams defensive tackle Aaron Donald returned to the team on August 30.
full_text: Rams defensive tackle Aaron Donald returned to the team on August 30. They play the 49ers in Australia on September 10. The most immediate question is whether he'll play and, if so, the number of snaps he'll take. Several weeks ago, it was believed that the target for Donald would be 30 to 40 snaps. That was based on Donald returning in time to have a sufficient ramp-up process for the first game. While it took a little longer than originally expected, there's an apples-to-apples comparison. In 2018, Donald held out until August 31. And the Rams played their first game on Monday, September 10, against the Raiders. In that game, the Rams had 70 defensive snaps. Donald participated in 62 of them. Although Donald is eight years older ago than he was in 2018 (as we all are), 30-40 doesn't seem ridiculous. Regardless, the clock is ticking. And Donald is practicing. He'll eventually be playing. Whether that's Week 1 against the 49ers or Week 2 against the Giants remains to be seen.
author: Mike Florio

title: John Schneider on Terrion Arnold: "The character didn't really fit with the allegations"
summary: The Seahawks finally signed cornerback Terrion Arnold, more than two weeks after agreeing to a deal with him.
full_text: The Seahawks finally signed cornerback Terrion Arnold, more than two weeks after agreeing to a deal with him. The league, as expected, promptly placed Arnold on paid leave. The administrative move flows from eight felony charges against Arnold, arising from an alleged kidnapping and armed robbery that happened earlier this year in Florida. On Sunday, Seahawks G.M. John Schneider was asked about the factors the team considered in signing the 2024 first-round pick. “There is a ton of different factors that went into it," Schneider told reporters. "Obviously, the legal stuff has to take care of itself, and we totally respect that. There are tons of different buckets to this situation. Just the advocates that we had, you know. We traded for Leon Washington the first year that we were here, and he’s basically like his father. Leon [Washington] will always be a legend here, and he has a great relationship with the organization. "The character just didn’t really fit with the allegations and everybody we’ve talked to. But yes, there’s a long-term play. This isn’t a, 'Let’s see how quickly we can get this done.' Let’s get him in the building and see how it goes.” Still, the allegations aren't pretty. Schneider himself has called them " shocking ." He also has admitted that, if Arnold had been on the Seahawks roster when the allegations came to light, they "probably" would have had to release him. With the allegations still unresolved, it's hard to understand why, if the allegations would have compelled the Seahawks to cut Arnold, they were comfortable signing him. This isn't a second chance. The aftermath of first chance still lingers; Arnold hasn't had his day in court. If Arnold is convicted, he'll likely never play for the Seahawks. If he agrees to a plea deal and satisfies its terms, then it will be time for a second chance. Frankly, this seems to be a wager by the Seahawks. They're willing to pay him not to play so that they'll have a relationship in place with him if/when the case is resolved and he's able to play. For now, Arnold remains entitled to all constitutional protections. He gets his day in court. Still, until the allegations are resolved, they are (as Schneider said) "shocking." It's hard to imagine the league letting Arnold play until the criminal case is completely wrapped up with something other than a guilty verdict and a lengthy prison sentence.
author: Mike Florio

title: Titans waive Hendon Hooker and Will Levis as they drop to 53 players
summary: The Titans confirmed that they waived quarterback Will Levis on Sunday afternoon and they also announced the departure of Hendon Hooker.
full_text: The Titans confirmed that they waived quarterback Will Levis on Sunday afternoon and they also announced the departure of Hendon Hooker. With both quarterbacks on the list of cuts, the Titans have Cam Ward and Mitchell Trubisky on the depth chart. Teams can begin filling out their practice squads and the Titans seem likely to have a third quarterback on that roster. The Titans also waived or released wide receivers Courtney Jackson, Lance McCutcheon, Bryce Oliver, Mason Kinsey, Hank Beatty, KJ Osborn, and Tyren Montgomery; tight end Joel Wilson; offensive linemen Rasheed Miller, Drew Moss, Zachary Thomas, Cordell Volson, and Aamil Wagner; running backs Michael Carter, D'Ernest Johnson, and Kalel Mullings; defensive linemen Earnest Brown, Malik Herring, Jalyn Holmes, Khalen Saunders, and Laki Tasi; linebackers Derrick Canteen, Reid Carrico, Dyontae Johnson, and Mani Powell; and defensive backs Kendell Brooks, Keydrain Calligan, Bishop Fitzgerald, Mario Goodrich, Corey Mayfield and Jalen McMurray. Linebacker Dorian Mausi and cornerback Joshua Williams were placed on injured reserve with designations to return. Center Andre James and defensive end Tanoh Kpassagnon are also on injured reserve, but do not have that designation.
author: Josh Alper

title: USC issues statement regarding poor attendance at home opener
summary: College football season began this weekend.
full_text: ' College football season began this weekend. Thousands of USC fans apparently didn't get the memo. Images from the Trojans' home opener showed barely enough people in the stands to fit inside a wooden horse. It was bad enough to prompt USC to issue a statement regarding the substandard showing. "We understand the factors that impacted Saturday’s attendance," USC said, via Jordan Mendoza of USA Today . "We have high expectations and a premier home schedule this season, and we know the competitive advantage an electric Coliseum atmosphere can provide our program. We thank our fans who showed up Saturday and look forward to seeing increased attendance the rest of the season." The announced attendance was 51,144, the lowest of coach Lincoln Riley's time with the team. And it looked like a lot fewer fans than that. In the defense of those who opted to stay home, it was hot. Very hot. The temperature was 94 degrees, with a "real feel" temperature of 104. The Coliseum has little or no shade. It likely was an aberration. But it was still a tough look, especially in such an iconic venue. The Coliseum has hosted multiple Super Bowls. It's been the home stadium of the Raiders, the Rams, and (in 1960) the Chargers. On Saturday, it looked like the crowd for a spring game. Or for a sport other than football. The first opportunity for redemption comes on Friday night, when Fresno State comes to town.
author: Mike Florio

title: NFL places Josh Jacobs on paid leave
summary: Jacobs was charged this week with two misdemeanors, including battery.
full_text: As various teams and players brace for the possibility of paid leave , one key player for the Packers has gotten clarity. The NFL has announced that it has placed running back Josh Jacobs on the Commissioner Exempt list. Jacobs was arrested in May on five different counts arising from a domestic incident. He was formally charged this week with a pair of misdemeanors , including battery. The NFL has the ability to use paid leave in certain circumstances. The league regards the move as not punishment (even though it absolutely is). In theory, the paid leave lasts until the criminal case is resolved. That puts extra pressure on the player to accept a plea deal, when he otherwise could be inclined to fight the case through its normal conclusion. It's also possible that he will be reinstated from paid leave before the prosecution ends. That happened two years ago with Patriots safety Jabrill Peppers, who missed seven games on paid leave. After the 2024 season, he was acquitted. “Josh Jacobs has been placed on the Commissioner’s Exempt List, which is an administrative procedure used by the NFL while a matter is being reviewed," Jacobs's lawyers said in a statement. "It is not a final determination. Josh respects the NFL process , the Packers, and his Coaches and Teammates. He looks forward to his return to the team and the NFL." A first-round pick in 2019, Jacobs spent five years with the Raiders before signing with the Packers in 2024. He rushed for 1,329 yards during his first year in Green Bay and 929 in 2025. He scored 16 total touchdowns in 2024 and 14 last year. Jacobs has a base salary of $10.2 million. He'll receive that money while on paid leave. Whether Jacobs will receive $41,176 in per-game roster bonuses likely depends on the specific language of his contract. Either way, the Packers won't have Jacobs until further notice. His absence will create opportunities for other tailbacks on the team, including Chris Brooks and MarShawn Lloyd. There's apparently video of the incident that led to Jacobs's charges. If/when it's released, public opinion could turn sharply enough to make it hard for him to get back on the field. On Friday, coach Matt LaFleur said he expects Jacobs to be a member of the team .
author: Mike Florio

title: Packers move Micah Parsons to reserve/PUP to open season
summary: We've known for some time that Packers defensive end Micah Parsons would not be ready to play at the start of the regular season and the team made it official on Sunday.
full_text: We've known for some time that Packers defensive end Micah Parsons would not be ready to play at the start of the regular season and the team made it official on Sunday. Adam Schefter of ESPN reports that they have moved Parsons to the regular season version of the physically unable to perform list. The move means Parsons will not be eligible to play until the team's fifth game of the season. Parsons's return could take even longer than that, however. He said earlier this month that the team's Week 6 game against the Cowboys would be the " most optimistic " date for him to return from last season's torn ACL. Whether that's a realistic return date for Parsons or not will become clearer over the coming weeks and the Packers will have to count on others to pick up the defensive slack until he's back in the lineup.
author: Josh Alper

title: Steelers keep four quarterbacks on 53-man roster, for now
summary: Mike McCarthy's first official roster in Pittsburgh will have four quarterbacks.
full_text: Mike McCarthy's first official roster in Pittsburgh will have four quarterbacks. For now. Via Adam Schefter of ESPN, the Steelers will have Aaron Rodgers, Mason Rudolph, Will Howard, and Drew Allar on the 53-man roster. That doesn't mean it'll stay that way. One of them could be put on short-term IR. Or traded or cut in the coming days. Releasing Howard (a sixth-round pick in 2025) or Allar (a third-round pick in 2026) would have exposed the player to waivers. Which could have prevented signing one of them to the practice squad. For now, however, the Steelers are moving forward with four quarterbacks — which means only 49 players at all of the other positions.
author: Mike Florio

title: Vikings keep four quarterbacks on 53-man roster
summary: The Vikings have trimmed their roster to 53.
full_text: The Vikings have trimmed their roster to 53. The names of players terminated or waived do not include any of their four quarterbacks. For now, they'll proceed with Kyler Murray, Carson Wentz, J.J. McCarthy, and Max Brosmer. The following players were waived: CB Da'Veawn Armstead; WR Michael Briscoe; G Henry Byrd; WR Terrill Davis; C Gavin Gerhardt; G Joshua Gray; S Kahlef Hailassie; CB Tre Hawkins;LB Bangally Kamara; TE Marshall Lang; TE Matt Lauter; G Vershon Lee; OL Tristan Leigh;OL Delby Lemieux; CB Bryce Phillips; OL Tomas Rimac; DL Jahvaree Ritzie; LB Josh Ross; WR Trayvon Rudolph; WR Marcus Sanders, Jr.; RB Zavier Scott; OLB Cam'Ron Stewart; DL Smith Vilbert; and CB Jarod Washington. author: Mike Florio

title: Packers cut roster to 53, confirm placement of Micah Parsons on reserve/PUP
summary: To get to 53 players on the roster, the Packers continue to keep linebacker Micah Parsons off the roster.
full_text: To get to 53 players on the roster, the Packers continue to keep linebacker Micah Parsons off the roster. As expected, he has been moved from active/physically unable to perform to reserve/PUP. Elsewhere, the Packers have released the following players: LS Cal Adomitis; T Brant Banks; G Dylan Barrett; CB Shemar Bartholomew; T Dalton Cooper; DT Jaden Crumedy; TE Drake Dabney; CB MJ Devonshire Jr.; G Josh Gesky; WR Chris Hilton Jr.; CB Domani Jackson; WR Kisean Johnson (KEY-shawn); EDGE Nyjalik Kelly; S Murvin Kenion III; T/G Darian Kinnard; RB Damien Martinez; EDGE Arron Mosby; WR Isaiah Neyor; RB Jaden Nixon; S Mark Perry; WR Kaden Prather; LB TJ Quinn; WR Will Sheppard; CB Jaylin Simpson; DT Nazir Stackhouse; RB Pierre Strong Jr.; TE Messiah Swinson; G Dillon Wade; EDGE Arden Walker; and LB Kristian Welch. The Packers also waived/injured TE McCallan Castle, S Trey Dean III, and TE Thomas Yassmin, placed EDGE Collin Oliver and WR Savion Williams on injured reserve/designated for return, and placed TE Luke Musgrave, Parsons, and DT Jordon Riley on reserve/physically unable to perform. The Packers have two quarterbacks on the roster — Jordan Love and Tyrod Taylor. Also, pending the physical that will finalize the trade with the Steelers for running back Kaleb Johnson, the Packers will have three tailbacks: Chris Brooks, MarShawn Lloyd, and Johnson.
author: Mike Florio

title: Odell Beckham Jr. makes the Giants' initial 53-man roster
summary: Odell Beckham Jr.'
full_text: Odell Beckham Jr.'s second tour of duty with the Giants isn't ending on Sunday. Jordan Raanan of ESPN.com reports that Beckham has made the team's initial 53-man roster. Head coach John Harbaugh suggested Beckham would survive cutdown day when he said the wideout has done enough to make an NFL roster after the team's final preseason game, but hedged a bit the next day when asked if he had made the Giants' 53-man roster. Beckham was a Giants first-round pick in 2014 and remained with the club until he was traded to the Browns in 2018. He went on to play for the Rams, Ravens and Dolphins, but missed the 2022 season after tearing his ACL and was out of the league last year. Calvin Austin's torn ACL likely helped solidify Beckham's hold on a roster spot and there's been speculation about Darius Slayton's possible departure ahead of the 6 p.m. ET deadline to set the initial roster.
author: Josh Alper

title: Puka Nacua, Alaric Jackson won't be placed on paid leave today
summary: On Sunday, the league has placed two players on paid leave: Packers running back Josh Jacobs and Broncos linebacker Jonathon Cooper.
full_text: On Sunday, the league has placed two players on paid leave: Packers running back Josh Jacobs and Broncos linebacker Jonathon Cooper. Seahawks cornerback Terrion Arnold will join them soon. We're told there will be no further players placed on the Commissioner Exempt list today. This means that neither Rams receiver Puka Nacua nor Rams tackle Alaric Jackson will be placed on paid leave, at least for now. Nacua has been sued for biting a woman on New Year's Eve. Reporting on the matter has included reference to a potential diversion program . That would trigger automatic review under the Personal Conduct Policy — and likely discipline. Ditto for Jackson , who has previously served a two-game suspension under the Personal Conduct Policy. He was arrested for domestic battery, but he won't face felony charges. A diversion program is on the table in lieu of misdemeanor charges.
author: Mike Florio

title: Puka Nacua returns to practice, Myles Garrett working on the side
summary: Aaron Donald isn't the only Rams player making a return to practice on Sunday.
full_text: Aaron Donald isn't the only Rams player making a return to practice on Sunday. Via multiple reporters on the scene, receiver Puka Nacua is back on the field participating in the day's session. Nacua had been sidelined by a groin issue. But while Nacua is on the field, edge rusher Myles Garrett is still out of practice. While he's on the field, he's not in uniform and is working with trainers off to the side as he deals with swelling in his knee. With their 53-man roster set, the Rams are now ready to prepare to play the 49ers in Australia to open the season on Sept. 10.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Aaron Donald takes part in Rams practice Sunday
summary: Defensive tackle Aaron Donald returned to the Rams' roster on Sunday and he returned to the field with the team later in the day.
full_text: Defensive tackle Aaron Donald returned to the Rams' roster on Sunday and he returned to the field with the team later in the day. Video from Rams practice shows Donald going through drills with his teammates for the first time since he retired after the 2023 season. Donald worked out at the team's facility on his own multiple times while making up his mind about ending that retirement to suit up alongside Myles Garrett on the team's defensive line. That became reality on Sunday and Donald's presence on the practice field shows that he'll be pushing to get on the field when the Rams face the 49ers in Australia to open the season. That game is on September 10, so there's a little more than a week of time for Donald to work with the team before they are on the field in Melbourne.
author: Josh Alper

title: Rams, already Super Bowl favorites, boost their odds to +500 after adding Aaron Donald
summary: The Rams were the clear Super Bowl favorites even before Aaron Donald came out of retirement. Now it's not even close.
full_text: The Rams were the clear Super Bowl favorites even before Aaron Donald came out of retirement. Now it's not even close. The current Super Bowl odds have the Rams as +500 favorites to win it all. At the start of this month, when it was unclear whether Donald would return, the Rams were at +550. After trading for Myles Garrett, the Rams were at +600. Before adding Garrett, the Rams were +850. Betting on the Super Bowl favorites is usually a way to lose money, because most years, the preseason Super Bowl favorite doesn't end up winning it all. Last year, the Eagles, Bills and Ravens were co-favorites heading into the season at +700. The eventual Super Bowl winners, the Seahawks, were tied for the 15th longest odds at +6000. This year's odds now have the Bills and Ravens tied for second at +1000 to win the Super Bowl, followed by the Seahawks at +1200 and Chiefs at +1600. Super Bowl LXI will be played on February 14, 2027, at the Rams’ home field, SoFi Stadium. The last time the Super Bowl was there, the Rams won it all. They're the favorites, but by no means a sure thing, to win on their home field again at the end of this season.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Sean McVay on Aaron Donald: We'll see if we think it’s best to play him in Australia
summary: Now that Aaron Donald is officially back with the Rams, when will he play?
full_text: Now that Aaron Donald is officially back with the Rams, when will he play? Could it be as soon as Week 1? Head coach Sean McVay didn't rule out Donald potentially playing in Australia when the Rams open the season against the 49ers. But he also didn't want to put a timetable on anything for the three-time AP defensive player of the year. "I’m not going to talk about any sort of plans, it’s going to be a day at a time for us ," McVay said in his Sunday press conference. "What does that mean for Australia? The first step was, alright, if you’re coming back, let’s do that, let’s get you back on the practice field, let’s get you acclimated to your teammates, to your coaches. And then we’ll see what that ramp-up period looks like, whether or not he’s available or whether or not we think it’s best to play him in Australia. I think the best way to do it is take it one day at a time. "But, we’re obviously excited to be able to have him back." As he has throughout the summer, McVay noted how much Donald means to him personally when discussing his enthusiasm for the defensive tackle's return. "It’s way bigger than football," McVay said. "There’s a lot of history. There’s a lot of experiences that we’ve shared. A lot of love for each other’s families. So, I know for him to want to be able to explore this and come back into the mix is a real credit to the special people that he’s got a chance to be around, and that’s his teammates, and that’s obviously his coaches. And excited to start this journey. "He's one of one." So how did it get to this point? "I think he wanted to get to a point where he knows just from his previous experiences, alright, I want to be able to be there, be a part of the football team, and I think there were some things that he wanted to be able to work through — just in terms of his workouts and where he felt his body was before he could comfortably get to this spot," McVay said. "And so, that was really what went into it. "He and I both kind of had an unspoken understanding like, once we get the roster down, where are you at with it? You don’t owe us anything. And no matter what, there’s a lot of love. We wanted to make sure that he felt good about doing that. He obviously is incredibly — his priority is with his family. And so when he does something, he does it all in. That’s what led to being able to get it done today."
author: Myles Simmons

title: Aaron Donald: "Do I feel like I can still be myself? 100 percent"
summary: Donald told reporters after his first practice back with the Rams that he's known for about two weeks that he would be returning to the field in 2026.
full_text: ' Aaron Donald officially ended his two-season retirement on Sunday, returning to the Rams on a one-year deal for 2026. He even participated in practice on his first day, going through individual drills with his fellow D-linemen before heading to the locker room. While the world found out Donald’s plans on Sunday, he told reporters after practice that he’d known he was coming back for some time. “I know the world was saying all types of different things and nobody knew what was going on. But I kind of knew for two weeks ,” Donald said in his press conference. “And then I talked to Sean [McVay] every single week. Damn near every day. So, we stayed in contact, I’d give him all my updates, how I was feeling, how things were going. So, I know he got annoyed with asking all the questions in camp every damn day, so I felt bad for him at that point. But I was doing everything I needed to do to give myself the peace of mind to see if I could do it. So there wasn’t any rushing. “Just wanted to take my time to make the right decision, because once you choose to come back, you’re all the way back in. Can’t be halfway in, you’ve got to be all the way in it. So, had to get to that point where I felt like I would feel like I’m 100 percent committed to playing football again — because the last two years have been amazing. Building things I’ve been building, working on what I’ve been working on. Kind of working from home and jumping back in the fire playing football again. So, really had to sit back, think about it — not just from a physical aspect, but from a mental aspect as well. Everything just played out how it played out and we’re back here now.” Donald said he felt like the Rams were already a complete team without him. But based on some of the team made throughout the offseason, Donald started to get that itch to play again. He seemed particularly intrigued by the thought of playing with reigning defensive player of the year Myles Garrett. “[Y]ou bring a guy in like Myles Garrett, a generational talent, and it’s like,” Donald paused and smiled before continuing, “that can be fun, right? And, obviously, what they did on the backend with bringing certain pieces they needed in the secondary, man. And I think this is a complete team with me here or without me here. So, for me to even have the opportunity to be a part of this, be with this team, I take nothing for granted. “It’s a blessing to be retired from the game for two years and have the opportunity to come back and be a part of something special. Nothing’s promised, nothing’s guaranteed. But I’m willing to try to get to that ultimate goal, what it is, day by day, week by week, and just stack those days.” Donald’s work ethic and his workouts are famous for being strenuous. He said he’s been seriously training to get back into football shape for about 13 to 14 weeks and now feels like he can be himself on the field. “To be honest with you, I’ve kind of been in the football mindset the last 14 weeks, grinding,” Donald said. "If anything, it’s getting back on the grass and knocking the rust off as far as playing football again — 11-on-11, working my eyes, getting a feel for the game, certain reaction things that made me who I am. So, I put myself in the best position the best way I can by training to get to where I’m at now. And the only thing I can do now is play 11-on-11 and knock the rust off, get going, get caught up with the speed of the game, and the rest is the rest. “But do I feel like I can play at a high level? Yes. Do I feel like I can still be myself? 100 percent. If I didn’t feel like that, I wouldn’t be here. So, from everything I did, from training with just conditioning to the football transition and doing football drills and things of that nature — I recorded everything, I studied myself to a T, watched every movement, every cut, every hip flip. In my opinion, I don’t see a difference. If not, it looks a little cleaner to me. Two years, your body feels a little different. But still got to go out there, play 11-on-11, get myself going, and get myself where I need to be as far as playing football again.” So will Donald be on the field in Australia when the Rams play the 49ers in Week 1? That’s still — at least publicly — to be determined. But at this point, it would almost seem like an upset if Donald weren’t available to play to start the season. “I’m here to just go day by day, work,” Donald said. “I’m not here to be given nothing. I earn any position that I’m in. Whatever that is, whatever my role is, I’m going to earn it. “So, day by day, just work, grind, get myself to where I need to be, at the level that I want to play at. And that’s all I can do.”
author: Myles Simmons

title: Mike Vrabel on Christian Gonzalez: I expect every healthy player to play and practice
summary: Christian Gonzalez returned to Patriots practice last week, but the cornerback's lack of a contract extension has led some to wonder if he might be off the field again as the team heads into their Week 1 game against the Seahawks.
full_text: '' Christian Gonzalez returned to Patriots practice last week, but the cornerback's lack of a contract extension has led some to wonder if he might be off the field again as the team heads into their Week 1 game against the Seahawks. Head coach Mike Vrabel fielded a question about that possibility during an appearance on WEEI on Monday morning. "I expect him to be there today and I’m gonna focus on today," Vrabel said. "I expect every healthy player to play and practice for our football team. That’s my expectation as a head coach." PFT reported on Sunday that Gonzalez and the Patriots are still engaged in contract talks despite what's believed to be a significant gap between what the two sides are proposing. Vrabel was also asked about where things stand on that front. "I don’t have anything new to add with Christian," Vrabel said. "Whatever the events over the weekend or whatever happened over the weekend or didn’t happen over the weekend or what’s gonna happen today moving forward, I don’t think I have anything new to update you on." Gonzalez's status on and off the field will continue to be of interest until a deal comes together that secures his long-term future in New England.
author: Josh Alper

title: Aaron Donald: My longtime speed trainer told me I haven't lost a step
summary: Donald says he has stayed in good shape during his two-year retirement and resumed football-specific conditioning this summer.
full_text: Aaron Donald is returning to the Rams at the age of 35 after two years of retirement, and he says he hasn't lost a step. More importantly, the trainer who has been timing Donald in speed workouts throughout his football career says he has the data to show that Donald hasn't lost a step. "Everybody knows I kept myself in shape, lifting weights," Donald said. "Conditioning, I did condition myself. I did run full-speed on the treadmill. It was a little different transition to the grass again, running, cutting. The first day I got to train with my speed trainer since high school, he looked and me and said, 'You ain't missed a step.' That's why it was important for me to work with a guy that's known me been around me since Day One, since high school, just to get his advice of how I'm looking, what he's thinking." Donald's trainer, Dewayne Brown, posted video a week ago showing Donald doing the footwork drills he has done throughout his NFL career. Donald said the three months of workouts he's been doing while considering a comeback made him confident that he's ready to go. "A long process, but it was my process that I needed to do, to make myself feel like I could do it," Donald said. We'll see whether Donald can do it soon, as Rams coach Sean McVay says Donald could be on the field when the Rams open the season against the 49ers in Australia on September 10.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Falcons 2024 third-round pick Bralen Trice cut without ever playing in a game
summary: When the Falcons drafted defensive end Bralen Trice in the third round in 2024, they thought he had a bright future.
full_text: ' When the Falcons drafted defensive end Bralen Trice in the third round in 2024, they thought he had a bright future. Instead, he never played in a regular-season game for them. Trice was among the Falcons' roster cuts on Sunday, the end of a highly disappointing two years in Atlanta. The 25-year-old Trice tore his ACL in his first preseason game, missed his entire rookie year, and then aggravated the same knee in 2025 and never played that year either. Trice was a two-time first-team All-Pac-12 selection at Washington, and a two-time bowl game MVP. He wasn't necessarily a bad pick at the time the Falcons chose him, but he turned into a rare third-round pick who never got on the field for the team that drafted him.

title: What we learned from NFL roster cuts: Struggling QBs J.J. McCarthy and Anthony Richardson stay put
summary: Initial 53-man rosters revealed five unusually crowded quarterback rooms, uncertain futures for former first-round picks and a frightening new pass-rush pairing in Los Angeles.
full_text:
NFL franchises tell us a lot when they cut their roster down to 53 . Where do they feel like they have good depth, where do they feel like they're thin, which players surprisingly made an impact in camp, which players missed out on opportunities they could have been granted and more.
With that in mind, these are the top takeaways from this series of preseason roster cuts.
Anthony Richardson requested a trade out of Indianapolis earlier this offseason, but none ever came to fruition. The Colts granted permission for Richardson to seek said trade, but general manager Chris Ballard said they wouldn't deal him without a significant return on investment. That compensation apparently never materialized, and Indy held onto Richardson.
Richardson completed 21 of his 33 pass attempts for 249 yards, no touchdowns and an interception during his preseason appearances, while also rushing 10 times for 68 yards and a score. He looked more comfortable in the pocket than he had during his time as the starter, but it still looks like he's going to be the team's third quarterback behind Daniel Jones and Riley Leonard for now. Perhaps if some other team loses a quarterback in the final days before the start of the season, then he gets his trade, but otherwise, he'll be sticking it out for the final year of his rookie contract.
J.J. McCarthy , meanwhile, was in a quarterback "competition" with Kyler Murray at the start of training camp, but that was put to bed fairly quickly as the Vikes named Murray the starter early on. McCarthy reportedly struggled throughout camp, and he wasn't much better during the preseason games, completing just 9 of 17 passes for 115 scoreless yards. He also notably missed a wide-open receiver in the end zone.
The Vikings reportedly looked into trades for McCarthy in the final days leading into cutdown weekend, but couldn't find one that was agreeable. Given how poorly he played during his lone season as the starter and apparently during camp, that's probably not surprising. What is more surprising is that Minnesota kept him around rather than merely cutting its losses, but it would have incurred a $9.7 million dead cap charge to cut ties ($3.8 million more than if they kept him), which is probably why he stuck on the roster.
Typically, NFL teams keep two or maybe three quarterbacks on their 53-man roster. You can only use so many roster spots at the position before you star having to go thin elsewhere, and since only one quarterback can be on the field at a time, most teams choose to go thin there rather than elsewhere.
Five teams this year swung WAY in the opposite direction. Each of the Falcons , Browns , Vikings, Eagles and Steelers chose to keep four quarterbacks on cutdown day.
Atlanta has injury issues as Penix only recently returned to practice. Tagovailoa played so poorly in the preseason that he couldn't win a quarterback competition where there was no actual competition. Rush is a replacement-level backup. Strand flashed in preseason but isn't ready to be a starter yet.
The Browns engaged in some shenanigans with their QB room, sliding Gabriel onto injured reserve with a back issue after he played -- and fared far better than either Watson or Sanders did at any point during their own QB competition -- in their preseason finale just days ago, so he'll miss at least the first four games of the season.
Given how poorly McCarthy played last year, perhaps it's not surprising that the Vikings elected to go long at the position with several options behind their starter.
Philly keeping four quarterbacks is surprising, given how good the team feels about McKee as the backup. But Dalton is a solid veteran option and Payton was a mid-Day 3 draft pick this year, and we know Howie Roseman likes to keep the assembly line moving in the quarterback factory.
Pittsburgh is probably the least surprising team on this list. We knew Rodgers would be here, obviously, and Rudolph is more suited to being the primary backup than either Howard or Allar, whom the team drafted on Day 3 in each of the last two years.
One of the best defensive players in football history is returning to the field . Donald signed a one-year, $20 million contract to return to the Rams and play on the same defensive line as Myles Garrett . If Donald can recapture anything close to the form he showed the last time we saw him on the field (8 sacks, 16 tackles for loss, 23 quarterback hits, First Team All-Pro berth), this will be one of the most unblockable duos in recent memory. Quarterbacks everywhere should be very afraid.
The Rams were already the Super Bowl favorites after making big moves for Garrett, Trent McDuffie , Jaylen Watson and more this offseason to revamp their defense, and that status has only been solidified with the addition of Donald.
Madubuike suffered a serious neck injury last season, knocking him out for the final 15 games of the Ravens ' season. There was a time when we didn't know if Madubuike would ever play again, but he returned to the fold for Baltimore's offseason program.
Madubuike has been taking things slowly in his recovery and only recently started hitting the sled in practice, for example, but Baltimore not putting him on either the Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) list or injured reserve is a good sign that he could potentially be available to the team sometime in the first few weeks of the season. For a team that desperately needs help up front to improve under first-year head coach Jesse Minter, Madubuike's return to the field would be a very welcome one.
John Harbaugh played coy when asked if Beckham had made the 53-man roster after the Giants ' final preseason game , but the suspense didn't last long . OBJ caught seven passes during the preseason and was open several times for deep balls where the Giants either didn't see him or else overthrew the pass, or he could have had an even bigger stat line during the exhibition season.
It remains to be seen how much Beckham actually has left in the tank. He didn't play at all in 2025, and caught just nine passes for 55 scoreless yards across nine games with the Dolphins in 2024. He hasn't caught more than 44 pases or gained more than 537 yards in a season since 2019. That was seven years ago.
It's a feel-good story to see him back in New York, but expecting him to make much of an impact might be expecting too much.
This one was not unexpected. Parsons tore his ACL last December and has been talking throughout the offseason about how he would likely miss the start of the year. Now, it's confirmed that he'll be out for at least the first four games. You can bet your bottom dollar that he'd like to be back for the Packers ' Week 6 game against his former team, the Dallas Cowboys , and if he does, that would immediately become one of the most anticipated games of the season. The Packers have a new defensive coordinator in Jonathan Gannon, but they will need Parsons to return at full strength to be the best version of themselves.
The Cowboys came into camp expecting one of Jaydon Blue or Phil Mafah to take the No. 2 running back job behind starter Javonte Williams , whom they signed to a three-year, $24 million contract this offseason. Blue had the lead early in camp and had head coach Brian Schottenheimer talking up his maturity and his potential to make plays in space, but as things progressed, it was 27-year-old former undrafted free-agent Malik Davis , who has mostly been a special teams player throughout his career, who looked like the most reliable option.
So Dallas not only handed the backup job to Davis, but cut both Blue and Mafah, electing to carry only two running backs in addition to fullback Hunter Luepke on the initial 53-man roster. Perhaps the Boys will bring back one of the young guys on the practice squad or else claim or trade for someone from another team's roster, but for now, they're very thin at running back.
Notable cuts: Jaydon Blue and Phil Mafah.

title: NFL winners and losers from preseason: Fernando Mendoza falls behind as Rams strengthen Super Bowl candidacy
summary: The Rams and Ravens strengthened their Super Bowl cases, but injuries, uneven quarterback play and roster concerns created trouble elsewhere
full_text:
NFL teams finalized their initial 53-man rosters Sunday, but the word "initial" is important. Between now and Week 1, teams will be making tweaks to their teams via waiver claims, free agent adds, injury designations and maybe even a trade or two more. After all, we saw 15(!) trades on Sunday alone.
With teams finally, fully turning their attention to Week 1, we can do the same -- but not before we name the biggest winners and losers from the past month of training camp and preseason action.
What more is there to say? After the Rams added one of the best defensive players of all time ( Myles Garrett ) and two cornerbacks ( Trent McDuffie , Jaylen Watson ) to address their biggest need, Aaron Donald officially un-retired on a one-year deal. Donald is now 35, but if he is even 70% of his peak self, he's still a star. Los Angeles can work him in slowly if they need to. A pass rush with Garrett, Donald, Kobie Turner , Byron Young , Braden Fiske and others is nightmare fuel for opponents.
Furthermore, unlike last year, Matthew Stafford has seemingly no back concerns entering the year. And if he should miss time, both Ty Simpson and Stetson Bennett flashed in preseason action.
The Ravens are another Super Bowl contender feeling good. There were positive developments on both sides of the ball, with Ja'Kobi Lane emerging as a training camp star and impressing in the preseason as well. On defense, the best news is Nnamdi Madubuike , who has worked his way back from a career-threatening neck injury to be in line to play early this season. He hasn't practiced fully yet, but Baltimore not placing him on IR shows he's trending in the right direction. Players have lauded new coach Jesse Minter, Trey Hendrickson has impressed, and even undrafted quarterback Joe Fagnano made the 53-man roster. If he can be an eventual QB2, Baltimore has unearthed another gem.
Who says you can't go home? After not playing last year, Odell Beckham Jr . made the Giants ' roster. Forget the name recognition and the nice storyline; he had to earn his way, playing alongside and against backups.
shifty as ever 🔥 @obj pic.twitter.com/i1Vftm8UFn
Beckham's role is TBD. It might be pretty small. But good on him for sticking with it, through injuries, aging and many team changes.
The Broncos won 14 games last year, were the AFC's No. 1 seed, and were likely a Bo Nix broken ankle away from going to the Super Bowl. And yet it seems like they've flown under the radar . The same goes for Nix, who is bunched in with Patrick Mahomes , Daniel Jones , Kyler Murray and Jayden Daniels among quarterbacks returning from injury.
Nix played two series this preseason. He went 6-for-9 for 76 yards and a beautiful touchdown to RJ Harvey . He also connected with his new top weapon, Jaylen Waddle , on a 35-yarder.
Jaylen Waddle' FIRST big catch as a Bronco 🐎 GBvsDEN on @nflnetwork Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/u7UD9EloUb
Waddle adds the explosiveness to take this passing game to another level. Courtland Sutton looked awesome in the preseason, and Pat Bryant made waves as well. Same for rookie running back Jonah Coleman . The Broncos also return one of the NFL's best offensive lines. It's all adding up for a big year for Nix.
In just 34 snaps across two preseason games, De'Zhaun Stribling caught 11 passes for 109 yards. He was a surprise and much-criticized pick at No. 33 overall, but all he has done since then is impress pretty much everyone. He has impressive size (6-foot-2, 207 pounds) and YAC ability, and with Ricky Pearsall out for the season, he is likely to step in as a starter right away. He earned rave reviews from Brock Purdy .
It's easy to look past it now, but many contract situations leaked into training camp. Many -- but not all -- got resolved.
Running backs were big winners. Bijan Robinson signed a record-setting three-year, $66.75 million deal in early August. Jonathan Taylor got a two-year, $44 million extension a few days later. Then Jahmyr Gibbs signed a three-year, $67.5 million extension to top Robinson's contract.
There were other winners, too. The reigning-champion Seahawks made Devon Witherspoon the highest-paid cornerback in the NFL and, more recently, extended Leonard Williams . Elsewhere, Peter Skoronski , Darnell Wright and Jalen Carter all became the highest-paid players at their respective positions.
Sorry for the spoiler, "Hard Knocks" fans: Montorie Foster Jr . made the Seahawks' initial 53-man roster. As the show details, Foster was a substitute teacher and realtor last year after failing to make Seattle's team. Now, he's back.
On a Sunday when hundreds of players' dreams of making an NFL roster went up in smoke, there were plenty of good stories like Foster's. Here are two:
"Infectious" became the word of Giants camp after this John Harbaugh quote :
"Skatt's great. He does bring a lot of energy. But he did get a 15-yard penalty at the end of practice. Did you notice that? That's not infectious. Well, it is infectious, actually. Infectious in a bad way. Like an infectious disease type of thing. You don't want that. You want it to be directed in a positive way."
The quote came after a testy practice in which Cam Skattebo rankled some defensive players with his play in non-tackling drills. It also isn't the first time Harbaugh hasn't exactly been pleased with Skattebo. Remember the failed backflip ? (Skattebo is coming off a major leg fracture, by the way.)
Perhaps none of that impacts the on-field product, but the Giants' signing of Najee Harris might.
Another telling quote , this time from Raiders coach Klint Kubiak about No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza :
"He needs another three preseason games, all those rookies do. Now that the season's starting the practice reps get smaller and that's just life."
We won't go as far as to say Mendoza was a preseason loser, but that quote shows there's a ways to go. After a strong preseason Week 1 , Mendoza threw an interception in both Week 2 and Week 3, threw no touchdowns, completed roughly half of his passes and took a beating behind an offensive line that did him few favors.
OPEN UP A CAN OF WOODAZZZZZZ 🤯 📺: @nflonespn pic.twitter.com/Ke0lrYupPs
Kubiak is right. Mendoza needs time. Kirk Cousins looked solid in the preseason, which should give Mendoza even more time. But those "he should start immediately" thoughts? Let's reassess in six weeks.
I'll keep this quick, because I've written extensively about it : Shedeur Sanders will get his shot this year, whether it's due to Deshaun Watson's performance or a potential injury. After all, Watson has played 19 of a possible 68 games since joining Cleveland and is coming off two Achilles tears.
Still, it's surely a disappointment for Sanders that he didn't get the starting job and a chance to run with it. Perhaps he was never going to win the job. Perhaps interceptions in both preseason games were the deciding factor. Regardless, Sanders missed on what could be the best shot he'll ever have to be a Week 1 starter.
J.J. McCarthy went from battling for the starting job to battling for a roster spot . Though he ultimately made the Vikings ' initial 53, his future is uncertain , given that he was splitting QB2 reps with Carson Wentz . Maybe a fresh start would have been better.
In preseason action, McCarthy showed all-too-familiar, frustrating inconsistencies. He is woefully inaccurate. Against the Ravens in Week 2, McCarthy missed an open Tai Felton and then missed a wide, wide, wide open Myles Price in the end zone two plays later. Both have to be touchdowns. McCarthy's processing speed still isn't up to par, either, and he got beat up behind a leaky offensive line. In fact, he emerged from the Ravens game with a slight injury.
The Commanders were having a strong training camp by all accounts before star left tackle Laremy Tunsil tore his triceps. He'll miss much, if not all, of the season. The hits kept coming, revealing a roster that lacks both top-end talent and depth. In a joint…

title: One bold prediction for every NFL team in 2026: Giants make stunning run while Dolphins face 0-17
summary: The Ravens win the Super Bowl, the Chiefs miss the playoffs again and the Dolphins go 0-17 in one daring prediction for every NFL team
full_text:
Last NFL football season presented some insane moments that would have even seemed outlandish before Week 1. Sam Darnold won a Super Bowl . The Patriots made the Super Bowl a year after a 4-13 season. Philip Rivers returned to the NFL after four years in retirement.
The list goes on and on. And it will happen again this season. Clearly, nothing is out of bounds. Ben Johnson proved that recently. He wants the Bears to break the NFL record for points per game in a season while winning the Super Bowl. With that in mind, here's a bold prediction for every team from record-breaking years to worst-to-firsts, coach firings, shocking benchings, 0-17 seasons and more.
Prediction: Rashid Shaheed will have 1,000 receiving yards
The Seahawks are going to work Rashid Shaheed into the offense to the tune of a 1,000-yard receiving season. The gamebreaker became the fifth player in NFL history with 800+ scrimmage yards and at least three return touchdowns in a season last year (including playoffs), along with Gale Sayers, Troy Brown , Reggie Bush and Tyreek Hill. Now he's going to break out after an entire offseason to get acclimated to the Seahawks playbook.
Prediction: No. 1 scoring offense and No. 1 scoring defense
The Rams will become the third team since 1970 to have the NFL's No. 1 scoring offense and defense (the 1972 Dolphins and 1996 Packers ). The Rams defense was terrible down the stretch last year (25th in defensive EPA in their last nine games) so they added Myles Garrett , Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson . They will be the top unit in the NFL this year, thanks to those additions and now Aaron Donald's comeback.
Prediction: Healthy core after substation theory debunked
The viral substation conspiracy theory has been debunked, but the 49ers have still had a lot of banged-up players in training camp. Still, they will do a 180 and their entire star core will finish the season healthy. Brock Purdy , Christian McCaffrey , Mike Evans , Trent Williams , George Kittle , Nick Bosa and Fred Warner will defy logic and all be a force heading into the postseason. That would be pretty crazy considering the 49ers six highest-paid players combined to miss more games (64) than they played (50) last season. They missed 25 more games than any other playoff team's six highest-paid players.
Prediction: Trey McBride will lead the NFL in catches
Trey McBride set the single-season TE record with 126 catches last season as the Cardinals led the NFL in pass attempts and had ample garbage time to pad stats. He finished second in the NFL in receptions behind Puka Nacua (129). So what will he do for an encore? He will be the first TE to lead the NFL in receptions since Tony Gonzalez in 2004.
Prediction: Bryce Young gets benched
Bryce Young has slowly taken steps forward in the Panthers offense, capped by going worst to first in the abysmal NFC South last season. Perhaps the improvements have been exaggerated, though. He was 28th in the NFL in EPA per dropback last season and he will be benched in 2026 when he is unable to take Carolina to the next level. Patience will run thin, especially after the team made two big signings on defense in free agency ( Devin Lloyd and Jaelan Phillips ). The team picked up his fifth-year option this offseason, but the Panthers' brash owner David Tepper won't put up with a step backward from Young.
Prediction: Rueben Bain Jr . will break rookie sacks record
Short arms (and AC sprain) be damned. First-round pick Rueben Bain Jr. will break Jevon Kearse's rookie record (14.5 sacks in 1999) with 15.0 sacks in 2026. Production over projection will win the day this year as the Miami Hurricanes standout will spit in the face of the detractors who would point to how he had the second-shortest arm length among edge rushers drafted in the first round since 2003.
Prediction: Bijan Robinson will have 1,000 rush yards and 1,000 receiving yards
Kevin Stefanski will lean heavily on Bijan Robinson, especially with Tyler Allgeier out of the picture and uncertainty at the quarterback position. Robinson will become the fourth player all-time with 1,000+ rush yards and 1,000+ rec yards in a season (Roger Craig, Marshall Faulk, Christian McCaffrey). He already had 820 receiving yards a year ago, so getting to 1,000 would not be a stretch.
Prediction: Tyler Shough will make the year two leap
Sure, not all year-two leaps are created equal; after all, Tyler Shough is older (age 26) than Trevor Lawrence . However, he will build on an excellent rookie season (he was top 10 in most passing stats since becoming the starter in Week 9 last year) by taking a Drake Maye-esque year two leap. The addition of first-round pick WR Jordyn Tyson and free agent RB Travis Etienne Jr. will only speed up Shough's development. The competition in his division will help the cause, too.
Prediction: First team in NFL history with a 4K passer, 1K rusher and trio of 3K receivers
Ben Johnson already said he wants to break the 2013 Broncos NFL record for points per game in a season (37.9). The top 14 scoring teams in the Super Bowl era did not win a Super Bowl, though, so I'll do Johnson one better. The Bears will be the first team in NFL history with a 4,000-yard passer (they've never had one!), a 1,000-yard rusher ( D'Andre Swift ) and a trio of 1,000-yard receivers ( Rome Odunze , Luther Burden III and Colston Loveland )
Prediction: Tucker Kraft will lead all TE in receiving yards
The Packers gave extensions to WRs Christian Watson and Jayden Reed and would love to see a breakout from 2025 first-round WR Matthew Golden , but it'll be TE Tucker Kraft emerging in the Packers offense in 2026. Kraft was one of the league's most productive tight ends last year before tearing his ACL around the midway point of the year. He's been the best tight end in terms of YAC on record (9.1 YAC per reception in his career), so he will explode this season and lead all tight ends in receiving yards. One thing that could hold him back is a limited workload at the start of the season.
Prediction: Kyler Murray will win NFL MVP
Kyler Murray will win NFL MVP. Sam Darnold took the success of reboot quarterbacks to a new level by winning the Super Bowl last season after the Vikings let him walk. Minnesota will make up for that by rebooting Murray, who will have a chip on his shoulder after his tenure ended with the Cardinals. We have seen him play like an MVP for parts of a season before, when he had DeAndre Hopkins , and now the pieces are in place for a historic rebound with Justin Jefferson , Jordan Addison and Jauan Jennings in his WR room.
Prediction: Jahmyr Gibbs will break Chris Johnson's scrimmage yards record
Jahmyr Gibbs will break Chris Johnson's NFL record for most scrimmage yards in a season (2,509 in 2009). Dan Campbell said Gibbs will be the "bell cow" in 2026 after Detroit traded David Montgomery (182 touches last year) to the Texans .
Gibbs is already on a historic two-year run as the only RB all-time with 100+ scrimmage yards per game, 1+ scrimmage TD per game on fewer than 20 touches per game in back-to-back years. Imagine what he can do with say 400 touches, instead of the 320 he logged in 2025? He doesn't even have a 30-touch game in the last two years. Add in an improved Detroit offensive line that added C Cade Mays (even though he's out 8-10 weeks) and first-round pick RT Blake Miller and you have a recipe for a record-breaking season from perhaps the game's most electric RB.
Prediction: Nick Sirianni will be the first coach fired
Nick Sirianni will be the first coach fired this year. The Eagles have either gone one-and-done in the playoffs or made the Super Bowl in five seasons with Philadelphia. That trend will end, and the Eagles will quickly grow impatient after another slow start on offense, leading to Sirianni's quick hook. It wouldn't be that different from the Phillies firing manager Rob Thomson this past April or the Eagles canning Doug Pederson three years after winning a…

This is an article version of the CBS Sports HQ AM Newsletter, the ultimate guide to every day in sports. You can sign up to get it in your inbox every weekday morning here .
By the time Week 3 of the NFL preseason rolls around, coaches and front offices know just about everything they need to know about their teams. The moral of the story is to only put so much stock into what you saw in these last few games. Some performances absolutely mattered, but others should be taken with a boulder of salt . Some Tigers fans booed Tarik Skubal in his return to Comerica Park . title: Aaron Donald back: Three-time Defensive Player of the Year returning to Rams for 2026 season
summary: Donald will join forces this season with fellow former DPOY Myles Garrett
full_text:
After over a month of speculation, Aaron Donald , a three-time former Defensive Player of the Year who last played in the NFL in 2023, is indeed unretiring and will return to the Los Angeles Rams , the team announced, on a one-year, $20 million deal with incentives that could be worth up to $30M, per an ESPN report,
Donald, 35, alluded to a possible comeback shortly after the Rams traded for Myles Garrett , the reigning Defensive Player of the Year. He said in June that the trade "for sure got me thinking" and that he wanted to see if "that fire can light back up." He took a key step in that process on Aug. 5 when he worked out with the Rams , and he tried out again for the team 11 days later. He said he knew he was coming back two weeks ago.
"If the wife wasn't happy it wasn't gonna get done,'' Donald said after signing. "My wife was on board and she was with me 100%."
The comeback is now firmly in motion with Donald set to join forces with Garrett in a defensive front that, on paper, is as formidable as any in recent years. Sean McVay wouldn't commit to Donald playing in Week 1.
"Good to be able to get Aaron back into the mix," McVay said. "You guys know how close we are and there's been a lot of dialogue that we've had and excited to be able to just take it a day at a time. I'm not going to talk about any sort of plans. It's going to be a day at a time for us. What does that mean for Australia? The first step was, all right, if you're coming back, let's do that, let's get you on the practice field, let's get you acclimated to your teammates, to your coaches, and then we'll see what that ramp-up period looks like, whether or not he's available or whether or not we think it's best to be able to play him in Australia. I think the best way to do it is to take it one day at a time, but we're obviously excited to be able to have him back."
pic.twitter.com/fIAFPIm61f
Between the star linemen, Garrett and Donald have won five Defensive Player of the Year awards and have recorded a combined 236.5 sacks during their Hall of Fame careers. Their partnership evokes memories of the Rams' famous "Fearsome Foursome" defensive line of the 1960s that featured future Hall of Famers Deacon Jones and Merlin Olsen.
The 13th overall pick in the 2014 NFL Draft , Donald enjoyed a dominant 10-year run with the Rams that saw him record a franchise-record 111 sacks. His first decade with the Rams also included 10 consecutive Pro Bowl nods (he and Hall of Fame running back Barry Sanders are the only players to start their careers with 10 straight Pro Bowl selections), nine All-Pro selections and being the league's Defensive Player of the Year recipient in 2017, 2018 and in 2020. Donald, former Texans pass rusher J.J. Watt and former Giants Hall of Fame linebacker Lawrence Taylor are the only players to win Defensive Player of the Year three times.
Donald is Pro Football Reference's highest-rated defensive tackle of all-time, ahead of Hall of Famers Bob Lilly, Randy White, Alan Page, and Joe Greene, among others.
Donald's success during his first decade in Los Angeles coincided with the Rams' resurgence. In 2017 (after winning just 17 games during his first three seasons with the Rams), Donald helped the Rams win their first division title since 2003. The following season, Donald led the NFL with 20.5 sacks (a career-high) while leading the Rams to their first Super Bowl appearance since the 2001 season. The Rams gave up only 13 points but still came up short against the Patriots in Super Bowl LIII.
Donald and the Rams had a far different experience three years later in Super Bowl LVI. After allowing 17 unanswered points, Donald and the Rams' defense shut out the Bengals ' offense for the game's final 25 minutes. Donald led the charge with two sacks and a pivotal hurry of Joe Burrow on the Bengals' final offensive play that sealed the Rams' 23-20 victory.
After contemplating retirement following the Rams' Super Bowl win, Donald ultimately returned for the 2022 season, which was cut short by injury. Donald returned to his usual All-Pro form in 2023, recording eight sacks while helping the Rams clinch a playoff berth. He retired two months following the Rams' season-ending loss to the Lions in the NFC wild card round.
"For 10 years, I have been fortunate to play the game of football at the highest level," Donald wrote in his retirement post. "I'm thankful for the people I've met along the way, the friendships I've built, and the things I've accomplished with my teammates and individually."
After two years away, Donald is rejoining a Rams team that has legitimate Super Bowl expectations. The Rams, who reached the NFC title game last season, have a star-studded roster that includes Donald, Garrett, former Chiefs All-Pro cornerback Trent McDuffie , former All-Pro receiver Davante Adams , fellow wideout Puka Nacua , and quarterback Matthew Stafford , the reigning league MVP.
Donald also joins the list of notable NFL players to return after a brief retirement, which includes Tom Brady , Rob Gronkowski , Philip Rivers , Marshawn Lynch , Deion Sanders, and Reggie White.
author: Bryan DeArdo
