title: Snap reactions to Buffalo Bills initial 53-man roster
summary: The Buffalo Bills roster cuts are complete, and the team has has set its initial 53-man roster for the 2026 NFL season, therefore it’s time to react to everything that transpired over the weekend. Here were my initial thoughts once I saw the Bills 53-man roster on cutdown day (although don’t forget, this roster can […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - AUGUST 22: Tight end Keleki Latu #83 of the Buffalo Bills waits for a play during the third quarter of a preseason game against the Cleveland Browns at Huntington Bank Field on August 22, 2026, in Cleveland, Ohio. The Bills defeated the Browns 31-7. (Photo by Jason Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buffalo Bills roster cuts are complete, and the team has has set its initial 53-man roster for the 2026 NFL season, therefore it’s time to react to everything that transpired over the weekend. Here were my initial thoughts once I saw the Bills 53-man roster on cutdown day (although don’t forget, this roster can very easily morph slightly before Week 1’s kickoff on September 13). Hats off to Keleki Latu and Ar’Maj Reed-Adams… The 2025 undrafted free-agent tight end from Washington (and previously of Nevada and Cal) earned a spot on Buffalo’s 53-man roster in his second season. The nearly 6’7”, 250-ish pounder made six snags for 53 yards in the preseason but I have a hunch it was his blocking improvement — willingness, technique, and power — that were the key factors in Latu making the team. And how about Reed-Adams, a seventh-round pick from Texas A&M who was a workhorse blocker in the preseason and did not allow a pressure on 103 pass-blocking snaps. I adore ARA’s upside at over 6’5” and 315 pounds (right now) with an outrageous 85” wingspan (long for an offensive tackle). …and to Mike Danna I singled out Danna after the final preseason game for his tireless work… in the final preseason game, as he logged over 40 snaps and was as energetic and annoying to block as ever. Now he’s in the rotation. And because of his vast experience — and Buffalo’s experience dealing with him as an opponent in the past — I could see him on the field sooner than later this season as the fourth or fifth rush linebacker in Jim Leonhard’s scheme. No Kani Walker?! Walker’s exclusion from the 53-man roster should serve as a reminder of the frequency of use in the practice squad in today’s NFL. Sure, he’s vulnerable to get poached now. But those type of transactions aren’t super common during the season. With his size, length, quality summer, and connection to cornerbacks coach Jay Valai, Walker is about as ready and likely to play as an undrafted free agent rookie can be. This is very unlikely to be the end of Walker’s story in Buffalo. The ripple effect of Zane Durant’s injury Late in the second half against the Steelers, I noticed Durant hobbling off the field under his own power, but clearly in pain. Now he’s on IR (designed to return) for the first four games of the season, and that fluky injury in the final preseason game almost assuredly allowed DeWayne Carter to make the initial 53-man roster. Only five receivers? This perplexed me slightly, although it’s not as if the Bills were operating with a surplus of ridiculous talent at that position this summer. Mecole Hardman’s drop issues certainly didn’t help, and I was even more surprised Trent Sherfield wasn’t kept on the original 53, especially considering Keon Coleman and Khalil Shakir are technically still nursing injuries. Maybe the Bills don’t deem them to be that serious? That must be the case. That or Joe Brady plans to trot out plenty of 12, 13, and 22 personnel early in the season. Or, the Bills has their eyes on a recently cut receiver (or Brandin Cooks?!). Good development for Ty Johnson Johnson got injured in early August during the Blue and Red Scrimmage and hasn’t been on the field since. He felt destined for IR-designated to return. Not the case, which indicates the do-everything veteran speedster should be ready for Week 1. No fullback after all Ben VanSumeren got plenty of run in the final two preseason games after he won the fullback job out of camp, which led to a sudden surge in interest in that position again in the post Reggie Gilliam era. But he doesn’t make the team — although he feels like a practice-squad candidate — and now it’s unlikely that position is heavily utilized in Joe Brady’s offense… at least to begin the season.

Given the harsh nature of NFL employment, there’s also a chance anyone who made the initial roster could also find themselves released the next day if the Bills claim someone else. However, many of those players released now or later on could find their way back to the team through the practice squad, which for Buffalo can contain as many as 17 players. Among the other moves that the Bills will have to address in the coming weeks are roster moves for three players. Wide receiver Tyrell Shavers has been moved to Reserve/PUP; defensive lineman Zane Durant was placed on Injured Reserve (designated to return, per Sal Capaccio ); and defensive lineman Phidarian Mathis will begin the season on the NFL’s Reserve/Suspended list for a violation per the league’s banned substances list. There are of course several notable moves related to the Bills’ first active roster of this season, but what stands out is their decision to keep four tight ends, while also retaining zero fullbacks. title: Buffalo Bills 2026 practice squad tracker
summary: The Buffalo Bills are still in the midst of reducing their roster from a summer high of 91 players down to the league-mandated 53-man active roster for Week 1, where all that’s likely left at this point is the official reporting process. The regular season is just around the corner, which means new head coach […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - AUGUST 27: Buffalo Bills general manager Brandon Beane on the field before a pre-season game against the Pittsburgh Steelers at Highmark Stadium on August 27, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Timothy T Ludwig/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buffalo Bills are still in the midst of reducing their roster from a summer high of 91 players down to the league-mandated 53-man active roster for Week 1, where all that’s likely left at this point is the official reporting process. The regular season is just around the corner, which means new head coach Joe Brady must have assembled the best active roster he can in hopes of Buffalo claiming a road win opening weekend against the Houston Texans. It’s a huge first task for Brady and company, given the franchise’s historical struggles in NRG Stadium — the Bills have never won in the Texans’ cozy house. But for a team that has Super Bowl aspirations with quarterback Josh Allen at the helm, there’s no time like the present. The oddsmakers at FanDuel Sportsbook believe that’s true , currently listing the Bills with the best odds of making the playoffs in the AFC (-330), and the second-best odds (+1000) of winning Super Bowl LXI. The bulk of roster cuts are in the rearview mirror and the waiver-wire process is actively playing out still with a deadline of 1 p.m. EDT on Monday, August 31. Buffalo is 26 in the waiver-wire claim process (based of 2025 NFL standings). But the waiver wire is only part of the equation. It’s important to remember that veteran players who are not subject to waivers can immediately negotiate with teams or sign with a practice squad. The Bills undoubtedly hope to bring back as many of their own released players as possible. But they may also have their radar attuned to other team’s cuts for a player they coveted in the draft, as an undrafted rookie free agent, or even a vested veteran. As such, this tracker seeks to keep Bills Mafia up to date with any practice squad news, which will include rumors about potential signings. Let’s get to it, shall we? NFL Practice Squad FAQ Sara Larson has put together a great article with some of finer detailed rules for the practice squad as it pertains to the Bills. That, in addition to the notes below should keep you up to date with how the process works. Teams can begin forming their practice squads after the waiver period expires at 1 p.m. EDT on Monday, August 31. The NFL will send a subsequent Personnel Notice confirming the results of the waiver process, and teams can begin signing practice squad players after receiving that notice. A player claimed off waivers cannot go directly to a practice squad. A successful waiver claim means that player goes onto the claiming team’s 53-man roster. The player must first clear waivers before becoming eligible to sign with a practice squad. A standard practice squad consists of 16 players. Teams can have a 17th player if that player qualifies for and is designated under the NFL’s International Player Pathway Program. The Bills have reportedly released offensive-lineman-turned-defensive-lineman Travis Clayton (IPP player). Players who are not subject to waivers can immediately sign with another team or join a practice squad. Players with four or more accrued seasons are unrestricted free agents when released and are not subject to waivers. Players with three or fewer accrued seasons are subject to the waiver process. the NFL’s standard elevation mechanism allows practice squad players to be moved to the active roster for a game and subsequently return to the practice squad without immediately being subjected to waivers, subject to the league’s elevation limits. For purposes of an accrued season, a player generally needs to be on full pay status for at least six regular-season games. That includes time on a club’s active/inactive list or certain reserve lists like IR and PUP. Players may routinely find themselves signed, released, or elevated to the active roster depending on team needs week to week. That means this list should be view only as an initial group rather than a list of practice squad players set in stone. Think you’ve got what it takes to make a play with the Buffalo Bills in 2026? title: Buffalo Bills now have Aaron Donald on their 2026 schedule
summary: Make that two future first-ballot Hall of Famers on the Los Angeles Rams defensive line, and this one is quite familiar with the organization, unlike Myles Garrett who was acquired via trade on June 1. Jordan Schultz reported the return of Aaron Donald to the Rams roster after he retired following the 2023 season: With […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - JANUARY 14: Aaron Donald #99 of the Los Angeles Rams looks on during pregame warmups prior to an NFC Wild Card Playoff football game against the Detroit Lions at Ford Field on January 14, 2024 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Ryan Kang/Getty Images) | Getty Images Make that two future first-ballot Hall of Famers on the Los Angeles Rams defensive line, and this one is quite familiar with the organization, unlike Myles Garrett who was acquired via trade on June 1. Jordan Schultz reported the return of Aaron Donald to the Rams roster after he retired following the 2023 season: BREAKING: Aaron Donald tells me he’s coming out of retirement and returning to play for the #Rams . Donald, in part, tells me: “I’ve been working the last 12-13 weeks to train my body and get it to a point where I felt like I could still play the game at a high level and be… pic.twitter.com/eJu19Bbvv6 — Jordan Schultz (@Schultz_Report) August 30, 2026 With this late-August add, the Rams now have five of the last nine Defensive Players of the Year on their defensive front. Donald, now 35, last played in the wild-card round on January 14, 2024, a narrow defeat at the hands of the Detroit Lions. Of course this now means the Bills are set to see Donald — along with Garrett, who otherwise would never get second billing in a sentence like this — when Buffalo travels to Los Angeles to face the Rams in Week 5, on Monday Night Football October 12. I’m already giddy about that game. In the 2023-2024 season with the Rams, Donald amassed a whopping 87 pressures on 596 pass-rush snaps — including playoff games — which amounted to a massive 14.5% pressure rate. Anything above 10% for a defensive tackle is outstanding. As far as classic stats go, Donald had 53 tackles, eight sacks, and 16 tackles for loss during that regular season. While he is distinctly in his mid-30s now, Donald regularly reminds everyone of his 1.4 million Instagram followers that he’s stayed in fantastic shape. However, being even as outrageously in shape as Donald is and being in ready-to-play NFL football shape are often very different. But now, after a third massive acquisition of the offseason for the Rams, the Bills offensive front will be tasked with facing Donald in what will be a Week 5 primetime matchup that features a constellation of stars on both sides of the ball.

title: Best cut players from other teams Buffalo Bills should consider signing
summary: As you likely have heard, the NFL roster cuts deadline is today at 6 p.m. EST. And for as much as this day does feature over 1,000 players losing their jobs, I like to spin it into a positive and focus on new opportunities for released players to land gigs on different teams, including, of […]
full_text: LONDON, ENGLAND - OCTOBER 09: Dean Lowry of Green Bay Packers looks on prior to the NFL match between New York Giants and Green Bay Packers at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on October 9, 2022 in London, England. (Photo by Vincent Mignott/DeFodi Images via Getty Images) | DeFodi Images via Getty Images As you likely have heard, the NFL roster cuts deadline is today at 6 p.m. EST. And for as much as this day does feature over 1,000 players losing their jobs, I like to spin it into a positive and focus on new opportunities for released players to land gigs on different teams, including, of course, the Buffalo Bills. Let’s track the recently cut players who I believe the Bills should consider signing before their regular season begins. And, yes, the second and third chance opportunities ahead for many of my former draft crushes makes today obscurely fun for the NFL Draft nerd in me. If the Bills sign any of these players on waivers, they’ll have to be added directly to the team’s 53-man roster, which is a relatively big — but hardly unprecedented — ask. After they clear waivers, they can be added to Buffalo’s practice squad. Released players I still believe in who could help Bills WR Greg Dortch The rest of this list isn’t necessarily in order of priority, but I’d be lying to you if I wrote I didn’t place Dortch atop the list on purpose. Clearly, the Bills don’t want to use a roster spot on player who only returns kicks and punts (and I agree with that philosophy), but Dortch is also a wily veteran who’s averaged 40 catches for 361 yards over the past four seasons. He’s returned 99 punts and 75 kicks in his NFL career and was with Bills currently special teams coordinator Jeff Rodgers with the Cardinals for five seasons. CB Fabian Moreau Now 32, Moreau has logged more than 4,500 snaps in his NFL career. Last season in Minnesota indicated he’s not washed, either. On just under 200 snaps for the Vikings, the 6’0”, 200-pound outside corner made 17 tackles with two pass breakups and and was only charged for eight grabs for 53 yards in his coverage area. He could provide ideal, veteran depth on the boundary and has ties to secondary coach Joe Danna (together in Houston in 2022) and Leonhard (in Denver in 2023). DL Dean Lowry The 32-year-old Lowry was the consummate dirty-work defensive lineman for seven years in Green Bay and actually amassed a low-key 42 pressures during the 2021 season. He spent 2023 in Minnesota and 2024 with the Steelers but tore his ACL last year in training camp. He’s a thick 6’6” and 296 pounds and understands how to eat blockers to free teammates along the defensive line and linebacker group. DL Jared Harrison-Hunte The former UDFA from SMU built on a reasonable rookie-year preseason with seven pressures on 55 pass-rush snaps in his second August with the Panthers. At 6’4” and 294 pounds with 33” arms, he has quality size to play inside or as a heavy end in a base look in Leonhard’s defense. He is a 26 year old second-year player but I still think there’s room for growth, and he’d presumably work best in an odd-man front. His collegiate film was a blast, and he’s parlayed it to quality reps the past two preseasons in Carolina. EDGE Andre Carter The former Army superstar has bounced around the league in his first now four seasons in the NFL and only has 84 total regular-season snaps on his resume to date. As more of a project than a ready-to-go contributor right now, I’m more interested in what he’s done in the preseason in those four years — Carter has accumulated a pressure rate of 15.6% and has freaky traits at 6’5” and 256 pounds with and 81” wingspan. QB Will Levis I know Levis has not worked out, which is why he was released in Tennessee. He is 27 now. But the talent is undeniable. While reckless, he has higher-end running abilities and a hose. He’s attempted slightly less than 600 passes in his NFL career. He’d be an intriguing as a practice-squad addition behind Josh Allen and Kyle Allen. EDGE Bradyn Swinson A 2025 fifth-round pick of the Patriots out of LSU, Swinson registered four pressures in each of the past two preseasons in New England. While his pressure rate didn’t even eight 8.0% — anything below 10% is low for an edge rusher — at 6’3” and 255 pounds with a 81 1/4” wingspan, I love him as a developmental rusher. RB Jarquez Hunter I have no idea if there’s like an unwritten gentlemen’s agreement between teams when this type of rare occurrence takes place. But the Dolphins traded for Hunter just a few days ago, and now released him in hopes of just stashing him on the practice squad (and riding themselves of the guaranteed portion of Tutu Atwell’s contract in the process). I compared Hunter to Kyren Williams as a prospect, and in the second preseason game just a few weeks ago, he looked ready to go, toting the rock 12 times for 57 yards and a score. The Bills do have two capable running backs presumably on their practice squad in Frank Gore Jr. and Ian Wheeler. But Hunter is a four-year high-caliber starter at Auburn. Would the Bills claiming him on waivers set a bad precedent for Beane and Co? I’m not sure. But strictly from a team-building perspective, I’d consider signing him. Cut players with past connections to Bills LB Tyrel Dodson, CB Alex Austin, CB Kaiir Elam, CB/returner Brandon Codrington, WR Isaiah Hodgins, DL Carlos Basham

title: Carolina Panthers waiver wire order and NFL rules
summary: The end of the offseason is here. All NFL teams were required to cut their 90-man preseason rosters down to 53 players by Sunday evening. Carolina Panthers gneral manager Dan Morgan and head coach Dave Canales (+3300 to win AP NFL Coach of the Year per FanDuel) had their work cut out for them. The […]
full_text: CANTON, OHIO - AUGUST 06: Akayleb Evans #29 of the Carolina Panthers looks on during the first quarter of the 2026 Pro Football Hall of Fame Game against the Arizona Cardinals at Tom Benson Hall Of Fame Stadium on August 06, 2026 in Canton, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images The end of the offseason is here. All NFL teams were required to cut their 90-man preseason rosters down to 53 players by Sunday evening. Carolina Panthers gneral manager Dan Morgan and head coach Dave Canales (+3300 to win AP NFL Coach of the Year per FanDuel ) had their work cut out for them. The roster announcement coming an hour late not withstanding, there is plenty of suspense left for the Panthers roster. Look no further than fan favorite wide receiver Ja’seem Reed, who is currently subject to waivers. The Panthers have a surprising amount of talent they may want to bring back into their fold. Doing so to either their 53-man roster or practice squad requires following the rules of the NFL waiver wire. How does the waiver wire work? Teams have until 1 PM ET the day after roster cuts—that’s Monday, August 31st for those following along at home—to file a waiver claim. That’s just 19 hours after cuts are finalized. The NFL will then review claims and assign players to teams in order of their waiver wire priority. What is waimver wire priority? Waiver wire priority follows, for the first three weeks of the NFL season, the pre-trade NFL draft order. That order then adjusts to a record-based order, essentially the next year’s projected draft order. The Carolina Panthers are currently 19th in the waiver wire priority order. The full list is as follows: Las Vegas Raiders New York Jets Arizona Cardinals Tennessee Titans New York Giants Cleveland Browns Washington Commanders New Orleans Saints Kansas City Chiefs Cincinnati Bengals Miami Dolphins Dallas Cowboys Atlanta Falcons Baltimore Ravens Tampa Bay Buccaneers Indianapolis Colts Detroit Lions Minnesota Vikings Carolina Panthers Green Bay Packers Pittsburgh Steelers Los Angeles Chargers Philadelphia Eagles Jacksonville Jaguars Chicago Bears Buffalo Bills San Francisco 49ers Houston Texans Los Angeles Rams Denver Broncos New England Patriots Seattle Seahawks

title: The Panthers initial 53 man roster is set
summary: Sunday was the deadline for NFL teams to cut their rosters down from the preseason 90 to the regular season 53. Reports on the Carolina Panthers’ cuts were kind of hard to come by at times, but we eventually got a full 53 man roster, and there were a handful of surprises. On Saturday, we […]
full_text: JACKSONVILLE, FL - AUGUST 21: A Carolina Panthers helmet rests on the sidelines during the NFL preseason game between the Carolina Panthers and the Jacksonville Jaguars on Friday, August 21, 2206 at EverBank Stadium in JAcksonville, FL (Photo by Peter Joneleit/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Sunday was the deadline for NFL teams to cut their rosters down from the preseason 90 to the regular season 53. Reports on the Carolina Panthers’ cuts were kind of hard to come by at times, but we eventually got a full 53 man roster, and there were a handful of surprises. On Saturday, we predicted what the final 53 would look like. Let’s see how it stacks up. Offense Quarterback Projected (3): Bryce Young. Kenny Pickett, Haynes King Actual (3): Bryce Young, Kenny Pickett, Haynes King No surprises here. The only question was whether or not the Panthers were going to use King’s hamstring injury as a way to sneak him onto the roster via injured reserve, but they opted not to do that. He’ll be on the active roster come week one, and I wouldn’t be surprised to see him check in for some short yardage situations at some point. Running back Projected: Chuba Hubbard, Jonathon Brooks, Trevor Etienne/AJ Dillon Actual: Chuba Hubbard, Jonathon Brooks, AJ Dillon The slash between Etienne and Dillon was dependent upon the severity of the ankle injury Etienne suffered in the preseason finale. It turns out he’ll be heading to IR with a return designation. In the meantime, Dillon will handle third running back and special teams duties. Again, no surprises here. Wide receiver Projected (7): Tetairoa McMillan, Jalen Coker, Xavier Legette, Brycen Tremayne, Jimmy Horn Jr., John Metchie III, Ja’seem Reed Actual (6): Tetairoa McMillan, Jalen Coker, Xavier Legette, Brycen Tremayne, Jimmy Horn Jr., John Metchie III Again, not many surprises here. Veteran David Moore ends up not making the cut after a couple seasons doing a little bit of everything, but he could be a practice squad candidate. Training camp favorite Ja’Seem Reed apparently didn’t do quite enough to make the final roster, but I imagine he’s going straight to the practice squad if he clears waivers (he probably will). Tight end Projected (3): Tommy Tremble, Mitchell Evans, Ja’Tavion Sanders Actual (5): Tommy Tremble, Mitchell Evans, Ja’Tavion Sanders, Feleipe Franks, Darren Waller Five tight ends is a lot of tight ends. I don’t think this group is going to look like this by the time the regular season starts. The Panthers have reportedly been shopping Ja’Tavion Sanders, and I kind of expect them to take the best offer available sometime this week. He and Waller are redundant, and the Panthers clearly have plans for Waller at some point given that he made the roster. Since he’s a veteran, he wouldn’t have to go through waivers before signing to the practice squad. Also Feleipe Franks gets on for his special teams proficiency. Also, Darren Waller is number 35. That’s weird. Offensive line Projected (9): Rasheed Walker, Damien Lewis, Luke Fortner, Robert Hunt, Monroe Freeling, Brady Christensen, Sam Hecht, Chandler Zavala, Stone Forsythe Actual (10): Rasheed Walker, Damien Lewis, Luke Fortner, Robert Hunt, Monroe Freeling, Stone Forsythe, Chandler Zavala, Sam Hecht, Brady Christensen, Albert Reese IV All nine of the offensive linemen we expected to make the roster did in fact make the roster. The only change was an additional lineman, Albert Reese IV, made the squad as well. The undrafted rookie out of Mississippi State will backup at tackle but also has experience on the interior. Defense Defensive line Projected (5): Derrick Brown, Bobby Brown III, Cam Jackson, Lee Hunter, Jared Harrison-Hunte Actual (6): Derrick Brown, Bobby Brown III, Cam Jackson, Lee Hunter, Aaron Hall, TeRah Edwards The last defensive line spot seemed to come down to a battle between Harrison-Hunte and Hall, and Hall ended up claiming the spot. The Panthers also traded a 2028 sixth round pick for TeRah Edwards. Edwards was an undrafted free agent last year and has never appeared in a regular season game. Clearly someone really likes what they’ve seen on tape from him in the preseason. We’ll see what he brings to the table once the season starts. Edge Projected (5): Jaelan Phillips, Patrick Jones II, Princely Umanmielen, Trevis Gipson, Thomas Incoom Actual (5): Jaelan Phillips, Patrick Jones II, Princely Umanmielen, Thomas Incoom, Trevis Gipson It’s the five we expected, though the team swapped Incoom and Gipson in the pseudo-depth chart order they posted. This group looks like it should have more juice than it has in recent years. Still a shame to not see what it would look like with Nic Scourton. Linebacker Projected (5): Devin Lloyd, Trevin Wallace, Claudin Cherelus, Bam Martin-Scott, Jackson Kuwatch Actual (3): Devin Lloyd, Claudin Cherelus, Jackson Kuwatch Here’s a surprising one. Trevin Wallace not only loses his starting spot, he gets released from the roster entirely. The Panthers are reportedly signing Bobby Okereke, though the move isn’t official yet. If I had to guess, the Panthers are going to trade Ja’Tavion Sanders or release one of the linemen and then use the opening to sign Okereke to start alongside Devin Lloyd. Bam Martin-Scott lands on IR with a return designation, so he’s still in the picture as well. Cornerback Projected (5): Jaycee Horn, Mike Jackson, Chau Smith-Wade, Will Lee III, Akayleb Evans Actual (5): Jaycee Horn, Mike Jackson, Chau Smith-Wade, Will Lee III, Akayleb Evans The five expected corners are the five actual corners. The top three are a formidable group, Lee is a promising rookie behind them, and Evans is a very good gunner that can fill in at corner in a pinch. Safety Projected (5): Tre’von Moehrig, Nick Scott, Lathan Ransom, Zakee Wheatley, Isaiah Simmons Actual (4): Tre’von Moehrig, Nick Scott, Lathan Ransom, Zakee Wheatley I thought Simmons would make the team since the decision makers have spoken so highly of his special teams ability, but he’s not on the final 53. I wouldn’t be surprised to see him land on the practice squad for his versatility. Otherwise, we see the expected veterans getting the start with some interesting rookies filling in behind them. Specialists Kicker: Ryan Fitzgerald Punter: Sam Martin Long snapper: JJ Jansen These three were the only players on the roster at their positions so of course they’re on the 53 man roster.

title: 2026 Season Opener Countdown: 13 Days Remaining
summary: Here at Cat Scratch Reader we have counted down the final 100 days leading up to the Carolina Panthers season opener for at least the past ten years. We’ve always done this by highlighting the current player on the roster whose jersey number matches the day on the countdown. This year, we decided to change […]
full_text: 18 October 2015: Carolina Panthers center Ryan Kalil (67) as the Carolina Panthers defeat the Seattle Seahawks 27-23 in NFL action at CenturyLink Field in Seattle, WA. (Photo by Joshua Weisberg/Icon Sportswire) (Photo by Joshua Weisberg/Icon Sportswire/Corbis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) Here at Cat Scratch Reader we have counted down the final 100 days leading up to the Carolina Panthers season opener for at least the past ten years. We’ve always done this by highlighting the current player on the roster whose jersey number matches the day on the countdown. This year, we decided to change that up a bit by counting down our own list of the Top 100 Panthers of all time. This does not correspond to jersey number, does not need to be somebody who wore a jersey, and will in no way be controversial. #13. Ryan Kalil Panthers stats: 148 games, 145 starts; 5X Pro Bowl, 2X All-Pro Career stats: 155 games, 152 starts; 5X Pro Bowl, 2X All-Pro Offensive linemen often toil in relative obscurity, but that isn’t the case with center Ryan Kalil and the Carolina Panthers. Over his 12 years with the Panthers from 2007 through 2018 he made five Pro Bowls, was All-Pro First team twice and All-Pro Second Team once. But his impact transcended what he did on the field. Kalil was a vocal, influential presence in the Panthers locker room and helped shape the team’s culture. He endeared himself to teammates and fans with his humor. In 2014 ESPN’s David Newton named him the “ Funniest Panther ” and shared some humorous anecdotes like Kalil appearing on NFL Network dressed in a bear costume as he was right in the middle of playing Lions, Tigers, and Bears with his daughters when his live segment began. He also inspired his teammates and Panthers fans with his confidence and dedication. In 2012 he took out a full-page ad in the Charlotte Observer (remember when people did that?) thanking Carolina’s fans and predicting a Super Bowl victory. Per ESPN , Kalil said it was a “war cry to fans” and then dropped this absolute gem: “We’ve said it in the past in meeting rooms and behind closed doors. This year’s different. There’s a sense of urgency, a winning attitude that I haven’t seen before. And it’s in the way we prepare. It’s in the way we approach each workday, and I think fans will see it in the way that we play.” Now, the Panthers only went 7-9 in 2012, but the bold gesture is still remembered by old-school fans 14 years later. Kalil was an integral part of four Panthers teams that won at least 11 games during his tenure, including the team’s historic 15-1 season in which they won the NFC and reached the Super Bowl. Between 2011 and 2015 he was arguably the best center in the NFL. In the four healthy seasons he had during that timeframe (his 2012 campaign was limited to five games), he was All-Pro First Team twice and All-Pro Second Team once. The only slight stain on his otherwise pristine reputation was publicly declaring that he would retire after the 2018 season, doing so, only to later sign with the New York Jets for the 2019 season. Panthers fans have long since forgiven him for this, knowing he had 8.4 million reasons to ultimately play just seven games for the Jets. Ryan Kalil is a legend, and arguably the best offensive lineman in franchise history. If anything, No. 13 might be a little low on the list of the Top 100 Panthers of all time.

title: Carolina Panthers practice squad roster tracker
summary: With the this afternoon’s looming cut deadline, the 2026 NFL season is starting to take shape. The final piece of that puzzle, from a personnel side, will be each team’s practice squad. This is a good list to watch to see who the team really valued coming out of the preseason. Ja’Seem Reed landed here […]
full_text: CANTON, OHIO - AUGUST 06: Haynes King #16 of the Carolina Panthers throws a pass during the third quarter of the 2026 Pro Football Hall of Fame Game against the Arizona Cardinals at Tom Benson Hall Of Fame Stadium on August 06, 2026 in Canton, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images With the this afternoon’s looming cut deadline, the 2026 NFL season is starting to take shape. The final piece of that puzzle, from a personnel side, will be each team’s practice squad. This is a good list to watch to see who the team really valued coming out of the preseason. Ja’Seem Reed landed here last season before making the 53-man roster this season. Quarterback Hendon Hooker, another fan favorite from last season, also landed on the practice squad. He ended the year on his third NFL team and is hoping to start the 2026 season on his fourth. Every guy who makes the step from here speaks to highly motivated player, excellent scouting, and long odds. Practice Squad Eligibility The current rules for NFL practice squad allow for the following mix of players: Up to ten players per team with two or fewer accrued seasons Up to six players per team with no limitations on accrued seasons (veterans) Up to 17 total players so long as at least one of those 17 is an International Player Pathway participant A minimum of six (or seven if IPP) players with zero accrued seasons Rumored candidates There is a lot of smoke right now after the Panthers finally dropped their final cuts. title: Bears betting big on Jordan van den Berg
summary: There had been rumors for months, largely fanned by Fox’s Jordan Schultz, that the Chicago Bears were looking to move Gervon Dexter. Over the weekend, those rumors materialized as there were reports that Dexter was on the move and headed to the Atlanta Falcons. The trade makes some sense. Dexter’s in the last year of […]
full_text: Aug 22, 2026; Cincinnati, Ohio, USA; Chicago Bears defensive tackle Jordan van den Berg (96) makes a tackle against Cincinnati Bengals running back Kentrel Bullock (31) during the second quarter at Paycor Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Joseph Maiorana-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect There had been rumors for months, largely fanned by Fox’s Jordan Schultz, that the Chicago Bears were looking to move Gervon Dexter. Over the weekend, those rumors materialized as there were reports that Dexter was on the move and headed to the Atlanta Falcons. The trade makes some sense. Dexter’s in the last year of his deal and the Bears have never really made any indication that they were planning on giving him a second contract. Ian Cunningham is now the GM in Atlanta, and he was a big part of the Dexter draft selection a few years ago. And the Bears receive CB Clark Phillips (and a 5th round pick) in return, and the Bears secondary is certainly a mess right now. But for all the reasons that it makes sense, there’s one reason it makes no sense: the Bears need all the talent they can get on the defensive line. It’s no secret that their defensive line is the weakest position group on the team. After Montez Sweat, there are some has-beens, some never-wases, and some hopeful prospects, but there certainly isn’t much in terms of established help for Sweat. Dexter was that guy. He certainly had weaknesses in his game, largely against the run, but he was able to get some interior pressure, and his play was consistently better than many others in that room. So why make a weak position group even weaker? Enter Jordan van den Berg. Van den Berg has had an excellent training camp and has turned heads with some of his preseason highlights. His play has certainly been inconsistent, but that should be expected for a rookie 6th-round pick. The fact that the Bears traded two sevenths to move up to get him shows that they spent almost zero draft capital on this player, and he could be a contributor in year one. But that’s a key word there. He could be a contributor in year one; we don’t necessarily know if he will be. But the Bears think they do know, and they think he will be. . @ChicagoBears @Titans @JordanvandenB12 @StaceyDales Some guys just know how to play the game….And with a maniac's intensity. He was born to be a Bear. #dabears #BaldysBreakdowns pic.twitter.com/ELi5BzKOvm — Brian Baldinger (@BaldyNFL) August 30, 2026 When Brian Baldinger starts highlighting a player like this, people should listen. But are the Bears betting too much on a 6th-round rookie? You can certainly make that case. The Bears have opened up a Super Bowl window, many of us think if the Bears aren’t a true Super Bowl contending team this year, the defensive line is going to be the reason why they are not. The Bears just took their most consistent defensive tackle and traded him away because they are betting on a 6th-round rookie being just as reliable, if not more so than what Dexter has been. Now, from a roster building exercise, if you can get draft capital for a player you don’t see fitting into your longterm plans, it certainly makes sense to get something for them. But when you are as thin at a position as the Chicago Bears are, trading away a player is certainly risky business. But Dexter is gone, and it’s van den Berg time. I think there’s no question that van den Berg is going to be a fan favorite. We will see van den Berg jerseys at Soldier Field sooner rather than later. We are going to see the rookie make some splash plays from time to time. But will the rookie have the learning curve and ability to be consistent and not either be wildly successful or wildly dominated during a series (something we saw in preseason). The Bears believe they have found a diamond in the rough and that made Dexter expendable. Time will tell if the Bears scored something special with this year’s sixth round pick. They are betting on it. As Bears fans, we are certainly hoping they are correct.

title: Three things the Gervon Dexter trade tells you about Ryan Poles and the Bears
summary: You know what they say: turn your weaknesses into bigger weaknesses. Well, I’ve never heard that, but that’s what the Chicago Bears are ostensibly doing after trading starting defensive tackle Gervon Dexter Sr. to the Atlanta Falcons for Clark Phillips and a fifth-round pick. The former Bears second-round pick from the 2023 NFL Draft has […]
full_text: You know what they say: turn your weaknesses into bigger weaknesses . Well, I’ve never heard that, but that’s what the Chicago Bears are ostensibly doing after trading starting defensive tackle Gervon Dexter Sr. to the Atlanta Falcons for Clark Phillips and a fifth-round pick. The former Bears second-round pick from the 2023 NFL Draft has been rumored to be on the trading block for much of the offseason and goes to reunite with Ian Cunningham, the assistant general manager who was part of bringing him to Chicago. While the move isn’t a total surprise, nor is it crazy in a vacuum, the concept of making the league’s worst run defense and pass rush demonstrably worse on paper is…a choice, to be sure, especially given how relatively little Chicago did in the offseason to address their defensive front. But if there are three things you can take away from this move, here’s what I’d say they are. 1. Keeping Dexter simply wasn’t worth it The NFL can be an unsentimental business. And the cold reality for Dexter was this: the Bears had no reason to keep him long-term based on what he’s done on the field. While posting a solid showing in 2024 under the previous regime, he simply didn’t seem to fit Dennis Allen’s vision for a quick, explosive 3-technique (55.6 overall grade). Retaining him beyond this year would’ve necessitated extending him to the tune of something like $15-20 million a season. The Bears are in no financial state to do this. So Poles and the Bears weighed the value of him being on the field providing mediocre play on a potentially expensive contract versus recouping what value they could for him in a swap and leaning on what they already have. Which leads us to… 2. The Bears think Jordan van den Berg is ready for a bigger role We were all thinking it, right? The sixth-round pick out of Georgia Tech has arguably been the biggest winner of the Bears’ preseason slate, popping repeatedly on film with a combination of top-flight athletic traits and an always-hot motor that makes him hard to miss. Now, doing this against another team’s starting offensive line versus feasting on backups will be something to watch. But one doesn’t need to be a first-round pick to be effective in the NFL, and van den Berg clearly fits the archetype of what Allen wants—an aggressive, athletic gap-shooter who beats offensive linemen to the spot and doesn’t allow them to block linebackers. It’s a risky move given that veteran Grady Jarrett is the only player in that position group with a track record of success, and Neville Gallimore and Kentavius Street are little more than depth pieces. That means the rookie will have to learn on the job fast, especially on early downs. But if the kid is as relentless against the starters as he looks against backups, one can understand making room for him rather than parking him behind a veteran in Dexter that you know isn’t part of the future. 3. This is the offense’s team now To be clear, the Bears don’t want to give up 30 points a game. One imagines the expectation for this year is no different than any other: get stops, keep teams out of the end zone. But in practical terms, this defense is leaving a lot to good execution and takeaway luck, which they benefited a ton from last season. The reality: they’re probably going to give up some points this season. It’s going to be the offense’s job to pick up the slack. They have the horses to do it. That much is for sure. Caleb Williams will continue his ascension into being one of the NFL’s best quarterbacks this season. The likes of Colston Loveland and Luther Burden III are primed to become stars. And Ben Johnson’s balance of creative passing concepts and dedication to pounding opposing defenses into the ground with his run game has proven for several years in a row now to be successful. (The latter, in particular, will be important to saving the defense’s stamina.) Poles, Johnson, and Allen have no doubt discussed the full-team implications of sending Dexter out of town and how they’re going to work around it. If the Bears are able to control the football effectively on offense, opposing offenses will have fewer chances to expose the defense. Plus, adding cornerback depth for a team with several injury question marks at the position, as well as future draft ammo, is useful. Hopefully, they’re right and that this skeleton crew is enough to get them to more home playoff games.

That means by this time tomorrow we’ll know who the initial 53-man roster for the Chicago Bears’ 2026 season will be, and the quest for Super Bowl LXI is on! Our partners at FanDuel Sportsbook have the Bears odds to win it all at +2700, the 16th-best. Here are a few things to keep in mind as the Bears get down to 53. Players with fewer than four credited seasons will go through waivers, and once players clear waivers — this year’s waiver deadline is Monday, August 31 at Noon (CT) — they are eligible to be signed to a team’s 16-man practice squad. A 17th practice squad spot is available if the player qualifies and is designated as an International Player. We have all the specifics on the waiver wire process here . We’ll launch our practice squad tracker on Sunday. If a club has a player on the Active/Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) list — the Bears have three such players — or the Active/Non-Football Injury or Illness (NFI) list, then they must select one of the following options: Move the player to the Reserve/PUP or Reserve/NFI, whichever is applicable, and any player on the Reserve PUP or NFI list will need to remain there for at least 4 games Terminate or request waivers with the designation of a failed physical or NFI, whichever is applicable Request waivers Terminate the contract Trade the player Take him off the list and add him to the active 53-man roster Teams are also permitted to place up to two players on injured reserve at the 5:00 pm deadline. Those players will be sidelined for at least 4 games, with up to eight players eligible to be designated to return (10 if the team makes the playoffs). Any player put on IR before the cut-down deadline will be ineligible to play the entire season. The Bears currently have 4 such players. title: 2026 Chicago Bears Practice Squad Rules and Rumor Tracker
summary: The NFL’s cut-down deadline is later today at 5:00 pm (CT), but several teams have already gotten an early start in whittling their offseason roster down to 53 players. Clubs can’t establish their 16-man practice squads until the claiming period for players placed on waivers expires at Noon (CT) tomorrow (8/31), but plenty of rumors […]
full_text: CHICAGO, IL - AUGUST 17: Detailed view of a Chicago Bears helmet during an NFL football game against the Cincinnati Bengals at Solider Field on August 17, 2024 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NFL’s cut-down deadline is later today at 5:00 pm (CT), but several teams have already gotten an early start in whittling their offseason roster down to 53 players. Clubs can’t establish their 16-man practice squads until the claiming period for players placed on waivers expires at Noon (CT) tomorrow (8/31), but plenty of rumors about players teams want back will be floating around before then. If you want to catch up on any Chicago Bears news, you can check out our 53-Man Roster Transaction Tracker . Here are the qualifications for practice squad eligibility. A 17th player is permitted as long as he qualifies for the NFL’s International Pathway Program. Players with no accrued seasons (rookies) and those with fewer than nine regular-season games in their lone accrued season. A maximum of ten players are allowed who have earned no more than two accrued seasons. Up to six players with unlimited accrued seasons are permitted on the practice squad. However, the number of players in the last two categories cannot exceed 10 total players. Teams can elevate up to two practice squad players for each game, but they can still only have 48 players active on game day. After each game, the elevated player(s) will revert to the practice squad without having to pass through waivers. A player can be elevated up to three times a season, but a fourth would require him to be signed to the 53-man active roster. If they want to place him back on the practice squad, they’d need to release him and have him clear waivers. If that happens, the club could elevate him three more times. Another point to keep in mind about the practice squad is that all these players are free agents. They can negotiate and sign to another team’s active roster without being blocked by their current employer. The current club can make a counteroffer, but if the practice squadder wants to leave, he’s gone. If a player is signed away, his new team must keep him on its 53-man roster for at least three weeks; if he’s released before then, he reverts to his previous team. Players signed to another active roster are also guaranteed three weeks’ salary. Also, a practice squad player can’t sign with his team’s upcoming opponent unless it’s done six days before the upcoming game or ten days prior if his team is on its bye week. Bears Practice Squad Tracker Brad Biggs believes that the Bears could bring veteran DE Marcus Davenport back to the practice squad. You can find the list of the players the Bears have waived and released on Sunday right here . The Bears have waived running back Salvon Ahmed, and he’s a likely candidate to be back on the practice squad. ( link ) Per Brad Biggs , the Bears could bring wideout JP Richardson and safety Marlen Sewell back to the practice squad. The Bears are waiving UDFA OL Cade “Vanilla Gorilla” Barnett, and if he clears waivers, he’s expected back on the practice squad. ( link ) With left tackle Jedrick Wills Jr. waived by Chicago, it’s believed they want him back for the practice squad. ( link ) Much like the UDFA frenzy that occurs after the NFL Draft, a team’s practice squad isn’t official until it is announced. And once the Bears announce theirs, we’ll share it here at Windy City Gridiron. The Bears are set to play the Carolina Panthers in Week 1, and our partners at FanDuel Sportsbook have the visiting Bears as a 2.5-point favorite. The point total over/under is 47.5, with the moneyline for the Bears at -154. They also have a 2-leg Same Game Parlay of the Over at 47.5 and the Bears -2.5 at +230.

title: Bears vs Titans: Inside the snap counts, stats, and an injury update
summary: The Chicago Bears’ backups beat the Tennessee Titans’ backups last night, 24 to 15, and the NFL is done with the preseason games, so bring on Week 1 and the Carolina Panthers! The Bears had more yards (398 to 259), more first downs (19 to 13), and led in time of possession (35:44 to 24:16). […]
full_text: Aug 29, 2026; Nashville, Tennessee, USA; Chicago Bears running back Roschon Johnson (23) celebrates with wide receiver Zavion Thomas (81) after scoring a touchdown against the Tennessee Titans during the third quarter at Nissan Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Chicago Bears’ backups beat the Tennessee Titans’ backups last night, 24 to 15, and the NFL is done with the preseason games, so bring on Week 1 and the Carolina Panthers! The Bears had more yards (398 to 259), more first downs (19 to 13), and led in time of possession (35:44 to 24:16). The Bears also converted 4 of 5 fourth-down attempts, while the Titans converted their only 4th-down try. Chicago was also better on third downs: 6-15 (40.0%) to 3-11 (27.3%). The Bears were flagged 10 times for 71 yards to Tennessee’s 7 for 46 yards. In his postgame press conference, head coach Ben Johnson said that running back Brittain Brown left the game with a concussion, and that cornerback Jaylon Jones and wideout Ray-Ray McCloud III had hamstring injuries. He also said that left tackle Ozzy Trapilo, who has yet to practice in full since being taken off the PUP list, is “right on track.” He also said that wide receiver Luther Burden III “looks 100% to me.” Patrick Finley of the Chicago Sun-Times shared that before the game, starting corner Jaylon Johnson, “who left practice Thursday after appearing to hurt his right arm/shoulder, is doing rehab work in the end zone, throwing a heavy ball and using stretching bands.” Running back Salvon Ahmed was kept out of the game with a minor injury, per Brad Biggs of the Chicago Tribune. Before we get into some more numbers, here are all the Bears who did not play against the Titans. And here is how the Bears started the day on both sides of the ball. Here are the Bears’ playing time breakdowns and a few individual stats. Offense Tyson Bagent played the entire first half, and he went 16 of 17 for 208 yards, 2 touchdowns, and a passer rating of 156.9, with 2 runs for 21 yards. He was credited with a fumble on a bad exchange with rookie Zavion Thomas on a jet sweep, but in his postgame presser, Thomas took full responsibility for it. Zavion had 5 catches for a game-high 140 yards, a 97-yard TD on the first play from the offense, plus a 39-yard kick return and a 22-yard punt return. Roschon Johnson led the Bears in rushing with 15 attempts, 52 yards, and a TD. Wideout Maurice Alexander led the Bears with 7 receptions for 50 yards and a TD. He also filled in at tailback when Brown left with a concussion, and he had 11 yards on 3 carries. Defense Rookie linebacker Wayne Matthews III led the defense with 6 tackles. Linebacker T.J. Edwards, one of the few starters for the Bears who played, had 5 tackles. Defensive end Jamree Kromah had 3 tackles, a tackle for loss, and a sack. UDFA defensive tackle Jayden Loving had 2 tackles, 2 TFLs, a sack, a forced fumble, and a pass defended. Corner Terell Smith had 2 passes defended. Special Teams *The above image has players who only played in the third phase. Cairo Santos was 3 for 3 on extra points, and he hit his only field goal (from 37). Tory Taylor had 2 punts and a 56 average (56 net), with 1 punt inside the twenty. Linebacker Antonio Grier, who was just signed this week, had 3 special teams tackles plus 3 more on defense. To check out the full Bears vs. Titans box score, ESPN has an easy-to-navigate site. All statistics, snap counts, and accompanying pictures are taken directly from the NFL’s Game Statistics and Information System.

title: 3 things we learned from the Bengals’ opening day 53-man roster
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals’ final roster cuts had some surprises but nothing too shocking. The main takeaway is that Zac Taylor and the front office put together a group of players who fit what the Bengals do, not one built on high upside or promise.  Here’s what we learned.  They like their tight ends Five tight […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OHIO - AUGUST 22: Dohnte Meyers #81of the Cincinnati Bengals runs with the ball while defended by Malik Muhammad #24 of the Chicago Bears during the preseason game at Paycor Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Cincinnati, Ohio. (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cincinnati Bengals’ final roster cuts had some surprises but nothing too shocking. The main takeaway is that Zac Taylor and the front office put together a group of players who fit what the Bengals do, not one built on high upside or promise. Here’s what we learned. They like their tight ends Five tight ends is a lot. But Taylor and offensive coordinator Dan Pitcher often feature multiple tight-end looks and even keep them on the field as fullbacks. Mike Gesicki is the starting-caliber receiving tight end. Erick All Jr. is superbly talented and needs to stay healthy. Drew Sample made his name as a blocker. Tanner Hudson has shown up as a receiver in the regular season. And Jack Endries gave us some splash plays in the preseason. It’s not hard to see why all five were retained. The focus is on the present The Bengals let Charlie Jones go, even though he was a fourth-round pick just in 2023 and, as Paul Dehner Jr. pointed out , the only NFL player with at least one return for a touchdown in each of the last three seasons. Cincinnati also released McKinnley Jackson, a talented third-round pick in 2024 who had yet to put it all together. In other words, they’re letting past production or unrealized potential be deciding factors. They want guys who are performing right now , this offseason. And that’s how Landon Robinson made it over Jackson and Dohnte Meyers, Colbie Young, and Ke’Shawn Williams made it over Jones. It’s a different mindset and one that is fitting for a team with Joe Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase, Tee Higgins, Dexter Lawrence, and only a few more years for that group to win a championship together. They want fighters This year’s roster is filled with inspiring stories, from Robinson, taken in the seventh round, to Meyers, a zero-star recruit who worked DoorDash until 3 AM to fund his NFL dream. Then there’s the undrafted Jacob Bayer and Swayze Bozeman. "This is just the beginning." pic.twitter.com/2q0j92paQM — Cincinnati Bengals (@Bengals) August 30, 2026 As Dehner Jr. wrote : Those are the types of players who build winning chemistry rather than tear it apart. There will be games this year when each of these players will be counted on to do a job or help a teammate do a job. There will be no doubt in their ability to do so or desire to do anything that helps the team win. The writer for The Athletic contrasted that with the players we’ve seen in the past who “you couldn’t say that about, whether it be staying out of trouble off the field, maintaining conditioning, knowing the playbook or, you know, showing up for stuff.” So the takeaway from all this is that the Bengals know who they are and what they want to accomplish. They’re no longer justifying decisions in their minds. They’re going with what they see on the field and maintaining a sense of urgency.

title: Bengals’ biggest 53-man roster surprises
summary: The preseason is over, and now we just need to wait two weeks until the Cincinnati Bengals take the field for the first time in a game that matters. Until then, though, there is still plenty to discuss. On Sunday, the Bengals announced their final 53-man roster. They made their cuts, and now they’ll prepare […]
full_text: Aug 28, 2026; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Ke'shawn Williams (12) celebrates his touchdown catch against the Philadelphia Eagles during the second half at Lincoln Financial Field. Mandatory Credit: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The preseason is over, and now we just need to wait two weeks until the Cincinnati Bengals take the field for the first time in a game that matters. Until then, though, there is still plenty to discuss. On Sunday, the Bengals announced their final 53-man roster. They made their cuts, and now they’ll prepare to put together their practice squad. Before we get to that, though, here are some guys that made the roster that may surprise some. Ke’Shawn Williams We all knew the Bengals were going to have to make some tough decisions at the bottom half of the wide receiver position. Ja’Marr Chase, Tee Higgins, and Andrei Iosivas were always going to be locks, but four guys were vying for the last three spots. Most thought the Bengals would either keep Jones or Tinsley, considering Jones is an accomplished return specialist, and Tinsley scored two touchdowns during last year’s regular season. That ended up not being the case, though. Instead, they opted for Williams, who caught seven passes for 81 yards and a touchdown. Jones and Tinsley combined for seven receptions. The decision to keep Williams likely stemmed from his comfort as both a return specialist and a receiver. Josh Newton Newton spent the vast majority of the preseason in the coach’s “ doghouse , “ but it appears as if his time chained up outside could be over. It could have been his performance on Friday night, which included an athletic pass breakup down the left sideline. Ja’Sir Taylor, who was placed on IR, was brought to Cincinnati as a free agent addition to the secondary on a one-year deal this offseason. The Bengals selected Tacario Davis in the third round of the draft, and he’ll join five other corners on the 53-man roster. Now the only corner on the roster the Bengals didn’t draft is Jalen Davis. PJ Jules Daijahn Anthony might be the better safety, but Jules made the roster because of what he does on special teams. Neither Jules nor Anthony would get a ton of snaps at safety—those will go to Bryan Cook and Jordan Battle. Special teams is a big deal, though, and it’s often the best way to sneak onto a roster. Jacob Bayer Guard Brian Parker II would have landed on the 53-man roster, but ended up on IR with Taylor instead. His spot went to Bayer, who played well this preseason, especially as a pass blocker. Hopefully he, along with the rest of the backup offensive linemen, isn’t called upon out of necessity. This is also a position the Bengals could address in free agency now that teams are making their final cuts. What players, if any, surprised you by making the Bengals’ 53-man roster? Sound off!

title: Bengals News: Plenty of roster movement still to come
summary: One of the most bittersweet days in professional sports is when NFL teams cut their rosters from 90 to the initial 53-man roster. The important word there is initial. An NFL roster is never truly final, as we will see today. Teams have practice squads they will fill with players who were cut. Teams also […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - FEBRUARY 25: General manager Duke Tobin of the Cincinnati Bengals speaks at the podium during the 2025 NFL Combine at the Indiana Convention Center on February 25, 2025 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images One of the most bittersweet days in professional sports is when NFL teams cut their rosters from 90 to the initial 53-man roster. The important word there is initial. An NFL roster is never truly final, as we will see today. Teams have practice squads they will fill with players who were cut. Teams also put in waiver claims to add anyone who was waived. If a team does get a player they put a request for from waivers, then they need to make a corresponding move by releasing a player who made the roster. There is almost nothing worse than making the roster only to be released the following day. Bengals News Bengals Pushed to Add $35 Million First-Round Pick Before Week 1 The Cincinnati Bengals are searching for a swing tackle after the team released veteran offensive lineman Cody Ford, who fulfilled that role last season. Regarding what he’s looking for out of a backup tackle, head coach Zac Taylor said, “Just trust that the backup tackle is going to go in and win the game, and we want to keep playing the way that we play. You’ve just got to be able to trust through the game. And so, I think there’s probably a competition there.” The pickup would certainly make sense. The Bengals love betting on pedigree, and obviously Willis has that. He couldn’t make the Bears squad a year after being nearly a year removed from a knee injury. Early returns from Dexter Lawrence are promising for Bengals “If he’s not making the play, it’s probably because there are four hands on him,” Montgomery told ESPN. “If there are four hands on him, there are people running free. So now you have other guys making plays and then building confidence as a defense.” This could quickly turn into a revenge season for Lawrence. He has looked every bit like a dominant interior rusher. Bengals impressively opt against complacency at their strongest position during final roster cuts The Cincinnati Bengals fully embraced competition at wide receiver this preseason. As a result, two players from last year’s Week 1 roster are now looking for other opportunities. It was admittedly surprising to see the team cut Mitchell Tinsley and Charlie Jones. Tinsley seems like he will easily catch on at another place and contribute. NFL News Packers RB Josh Jacobs placed on commissioner exempt list It means Jacobs will not be on the Packers’ 53-man roster and will not be able to practice or attend games. He will be paid and, with the team’s permission, may be at the facility for meetings, individual workouts, medical treatments, and other non-football activities. One of the bigger names at running back gets put on the exempt list while the NFL looks into his domestic violence case. NFL Network: Aaron Donald unretiring, coming back to play for Rams on one-year, $20 million deal “To be honest with you, it was on and off for a little while, but I think I knew this decision about two weeks [ago],” Donald said. “I know the world was saying all types of things and nobody knew what was going on, but I kind of knew for two weeks. I talked to Sean every single week, damn near every day. We stayed in contact. I’d give him all my updates of how I was feeling, how things was going. When has building a super team ever gone wrong? NFL roster cuts tracker: Team-by-team player moves ahead of 2026 season Around The NFL tracks roster cuts across the league as of Monday, Aug. 24, through the 53-man roster deadline on Aug. 30 as they are announced by teams or reported by NFL Network and ESPN. A look at all the players cut, as well as all the players now available after a day full of roster moves.

title: The Bengals should still be in the market for a linebacker following roster cuts
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals did so much to improve their defense this offseason. They went out and added quality defensive linemen across the board, as well as safety Bryan Cook. The one level of the defense they never meaningfully touched was the linebacker position. Well, they now at least will have a chance to add some proper depth […]
full_text: Duke Tobin, Director of Player Personnel for the Cincinnati Bengals, speaks at the 2023 NFL Combine on Tuesday, February 28, 2023. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Cincinnati Bengals did so much to improve their defense this offseason. They went out and added quality defensive linemen across the board, as well as safety Bryan Cook. The one level of the defense they never meaningfully touched was the linebacker position. Well, they now at least will have a chance to add some proper depth and maybe even an insurance policy if their second-year duo doesn’t pan out. And the Bengals could look like an appealing practice squad or roster to join as a linebacker, knowing you could be called up to play and that the guys aren’t exactly cemented in front of you. One of the big names is Tyler Dodson, whom the Miami Dolphins released a year after re-signing him to a two-year deal. He had 129 tackles last season. He started his career with the Buffalo Bills, so he has also played in some playoff games. He is the kind of guy who could come in and potentially compete for time on the field with the current group. In the same vein, the Pittsburgh Steelers cut veteran linebacker Elandon Roberts. He is going into Year 11 and has started 121 games. He has been an on-and-off contributor. He likely won’t take either job unless one falls through the cracks. There will also be a plethora of younger linebackers who failed to live up to expectations elsewhere that Cincinnati could be interested in adding. Sometimes they will lean on their scouting during the draft process to make those decisions. However, adding another young guy this late into the process certainly doesn’t scream insurance policy. Linebackers Barrett Carter and Demetrius Knight Jr. were rookies who started most of last season after Logan Wilson’s body couldn’t allow him to play at the level we are all used to. It didn’t go well, but then nothing for the defense did last season. However, the rookie duo ranked dead last among qualifying linebackers for Pro Football Focus last season. Now, those ratings are not the end-all, be-all, but having the bottom two in the NFL is simply terrible. The Bengals are banking too much on these guys being better after improving all around them. We are all rooting for them to play better, but banking on it without insurance is reckless.

title: 9 winners and 4 losers from the initial Bengals 53-man roster
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals have made their cuts and released the first version of their final roster on Sunday. They cut down from around 90 players to the 53 that will hopefully win the Bengals their first Super Bowl. Of course, the Bengals will look at who was cut by the other 31 teams, and odds […]
full_text: Aug 28, 2026; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Dohnte Meyers (81) catches a pass against the Philadelphia Eagles during the first quarter at Lincoln Financial Field. Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Cincinnati Bengals have made their cuts and released the first version of their final roster on Sunday . They cut down from around 90 players to the 53 that will hopefully win the Bengals their first Super Bowl. Of course, the Bengals will look at who was cut by the other 31 teams, and odds are they could make a waiver claim or two. Until that happens, though, here are some winners and losers from the Bengals’ initial 53-man roster. Starting with…. Winners Dohnte Meyers There might not be a cooler story this season than Meyers’. From getting no D1 offers out of high school and having to pay $100 to try out for a CFL team to making a 53-man roster at 26 years old is the kind of stuff they make movies about. Meyers earned his spot too, catching 11 passes on 13 targets for 121 yards. He led the team in receptions and receiving yards this preseason, and will now take his spot on the most talented wide receiver corps in the NFL. Landon Robinson You know those guys that you can’t help but like? You know, the ones that usually play for other teams that you always think, “Man, I wish that guy was a Bengal.” Robinson is officially that guy. The seventh-round pick had a multi-sack preseason and not only made the Bengals’ initial 53-man roster, but he appears primed to get some playing time early. Shemar Stewart Stewart is a winner because, despite a nasty-looking hyperextension of his knee at the start of training camp, he won’t be joining Brian Parker II and Ja’Sir Taylor on IR. That doesn’t mean he’s going to be ready to go by Week 1 (though it’s not out of the realm of possibility), but it means he ‘should’ be good to go before Week 5, when he would have been eligible to come off IR. Josh Newton Though Newton looked solid on Friday night against the Eagles in the Bengals’ third preseason game, he struggled through much of camp and was reportedly in the doghouse. It appeared as if he was on route to getting cut, but thanks to Ja’Sir Taylor being placed on IR (with designation to return) due to a hamstring injury. This opened the door for Newton to stick around. For now. These next four weeks are crucial for Newton’s chances of remaining on the roster. Play well, and he may very well remain there for the rest of 2026. Jalen Rivers The Bengals’ starting offensive line is set, and has been set since before the offseason even began. Rivers is one of four backup offensive linemen to make the first version of the Bengals’ final roster, but he wouldn’t be if it weren’t for the fact that Brian Parker II got placed on IR with Taylor with a knee injury. The Bengals may find a new offensive lineman among the many being cut throughout the league, but for now, Rivers is on the roster. Ke’Shawn Williams This was likely the biggest surprise addition to the Bengals’ 53-man roster. I would have thought Charlie Jones or Mitchell Tinsley would have the inside spot, but it was Williams who is the team’s WR6 and likely kick and punt returner. PFF gave him a score of 65.0 for kick returning and a 62.8 for punt returning compared to Jones’ 67.5 and 69.8, but he also caught seven passes to Jones’ four and Tinsley’s three. Tahj Brooks Brooks, the team’s third running back, didn’t do a lot to inspire confidence that, if the Bengals were to lean on him, he would be able to move the ball down the field. He only averaged 3.8 yards per carry on his 13 total rushing attempts. Kentrel Bullock and Jamal Haynes never really had much of a chance at cracking the 53-man roster, but it wasn’t for lack of trying. They both averaged more yards per carry, and both looked pretty solid on Friday night in Philly. That, and the Bengals were reportedly interested in Steelers running back Kaleb Johnson. But once Josh Jacobs was placed on the commissioner’s exempt list, the Packers got desperate enough to trade for Johnson. So for the time being, Brooks doesn’t have any real competition for his spot. Speaking of a lack of competition… Demetrius Knight and Barrett Carter Knight and Carter continue to have a stranglehold on their jobs after the Bengals opted to keep just two other linebackers on the roster: Oren Burks and Swayze Bozeman, neither of whom looks capable of pushing for a starting spot. Unless the Bengals make a trade or sign someone like Bobby Wagner, Knight and Carter are the starting linebackers for the foreseeable future. Let’s hope they’re ready to make a big jump from last year. Losers Charlie Jones/Mitchell Tinsley Jones and Tinsley were on the outside looking in when all was said and done on Sunday. Jones, a fourth-round pick in 2023, has been a solid return specialist in his time in Cincinnati, and Tinsley was one of the fun and exciting stories of the 2025 season. Unfortunately, they were outshone by the trio of Williams, Colbie Young, and Meyers. Ja’Sir Taylor Taylor is on IR, but that’s not why he’s on the losers list. He’s on this list because the four weeks he’ll miss could be the four weeks Newton needs to prove he does belong on the final roster and hold on to his spot — whether that be on the field on defense or on special teams. Taylor was signed in free agency on a one-year deal, and he was placed on IR with a designation to return. That return, at the earliest, would be in Week 5. Newton, on the other hand, is a former fifth-round draft pick of the Bengals who is under contract through 2027. In other words, there’s more incentive for the front office to keep Newton if this is a close battle. McKinnley Jackson Jackson struggled to get on the field in 2025, but the additions of Dexter Lawrence and Jonathan Allen really sealed his fate. Now that fate is official. The 2024 third-round pick is either going to the practice squad or playing elsewhere.
