title: The best Bengals players who didn’t make 53-man roster and could be practice squad candidates
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals’ 2026 roster is officially set, and while there were plenty of predictable decisions, there were also some genuinely difficult cuts. Cincinnati finished the preseason 3-0, capped by a 30-13 demolition of the Philadelphia Eagles, and that created something of a problem for Zac Taylor and Duke Tobin. Several players who performed well […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OH - SEPTEMBER 25: Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Charlie Jones (15) carries the ball during the game against the Los Angeles Rams and the Cincinnati Bengals on September 25, 2023, at Paycor Stadium in Cincinnati, OH. (Photo by Ian Johnson/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Cincinnati Bengals’ 2026 roster is officially set , and while there were plenty of predictable decisions, there were also some genuinely difficult cuts. Cincinnati finished the preseason 3-0, capped by a 30-13 demolition of the Philadelphia Eagles, and that created something of a problem for Zac Taylor and Duke Tobin. Several players who performed well throughout training camp and the preseason couldn’t fit into a 53-man roster that has considerably more depth than some recent Bengals teams. The Bengals ultimately kept all seven of their 2026 draft picks, five tight ends, six wide receivers, and 11 defensive linemen. That meant some talented players would inevitably be left out. Here are some of the best players who didn’t make Cincinnati’s initial 53-man roster but could be candidates for the 16-man practice squad. 1. Isaiah Foskey, DE This one hurts. Foskey wasn’t merely decent during the preseason. He was good. Really good at times. The former Notre Dame standout had a strong training camp and finished the preseason with 11 pressures and three sacks. In the preseason finale against Philadelphia, Foskey recorded 1.5 sacks in the first half and was one of the players Zac Taylor specifically mentioned when discussing the group that played virtually every defensive snap up front. And yet he didn’t make the roster. That’s the ultimate example of a “numbers game” cut. The Bengals had Boye Mafe, Myles Murphy, Cashius Howell and Shemar Stewart, among others, competing for edge snaps. Stewart’s knee situation ultimately helped Cincinnati keep him on the 53-man roster while he continues his rehabilitation. Foskey’s performance may also make him one of the more attractive players available on the waiver wire. 2. Charlie Jones, WR/returner Jones may be the most surprising offensive cut. For the past two seasons, he has been one of Cincinnati’s primary return specialists, and he entered the preseason with a legitimate argument to retain that role. He also played well in the preseason finale. Against Philadelphia, Jones returned three punts for 44 yards, including a 31-yard return, while catching two passes for 36 yards. But the Bengals ultimately decided that Ke’Shawn Williams could provide enough value as a returner while giving them a different skill set at receiver. Cincinnati’s official roster announcement confirmed that Williams would take over the return duties, while Jones was waived. That’s a significant decision because Jones wasn’t simply a fringe receiver. He had been Cincinnati’s primary kickoff returner and had established himself as one of the team’s more reliable special teams weapons. The Bengals clearly decided that the roster spot was better spent elsewhere. They could still attempt to bring Jones back if he clears waivers. 3. Josh Johnson, QB It’s hard to imagine Josh Johnson’s preseason going much better. Zac Taylor certainly thought so. After Cincinnati’s preseason finale, Taylor said: “Josh Johnson had a superb preseason. I really don’t know that he could have played much better.” That’s a strong endorsement from the head coach. Johnson completed 12 of 19 passes for 156 yards against Philadelphia and helped Cincinnati move the ball consistently in his first-half appearance. He had already thrown for 156 yards and two touchdowns against Chicago. The problem was that Cincinnati didn’t have room for him. Joe Burrow and Joe Flacco occupy the first two spots, and the Bengals decided that a third quarterback wasn’t worth using a 53-man roster spot on. Johnson was released as a vested veteran rather than waived, meaning he is free to sign with another team. Cincinnati could revisit the idea later, particularly if it wants a veteran quarterback in reserve. 4. Mitchell Tinsley, WR Tinsley’s story is particularly interesting because of how quickly things changed. A year ago, Tinsley was the Bengals’ preseason darling. His performance earned him a spot on the 53-man roster in 2025, and he remained in the conversation entering this year’s camp. But then Dohnte Meyers happened. And Colbie Young happened. Tinsley wasn’t necessarily bad this summer. He simply wasn’t as impressive as the players he was competing against. Cincinnati’s final receiver group became Chase, Higgins, Iosivas, Young, Meyers, and Williams. Tinsley could still be back in Cincinnati if he clears waivers, but other teams may have noticed what he did last year. 5. McKinnley Jackson, DT Jackson was a former third-round pick and had shown enough flashes during his first two seasons to make his release a tough pill to swallow for the front office. The ridiculous depth Cincinnati assembled along the defensive line helped lead to his release. The Bengals added Dexter Lawrence and Jonathan Allen during the offseason, retained B.J. Hill and T.J. Slaton, continued developing Kris Jenkins, and then watched seventh-round rookie Landon Robinson emerge as one of the biggest surprises of training camp. Jackson became the odd man out. Cincinnati reportedly received trade interest in Jackson before ultimately waiving him, but no deal materialized. He now gets an opportunity to find a new home. Jackson’s best NFL season came as a rookie in 2024, when he appeared in 13 games and recorded 15 tackles and a sack. Injuries and inconsistency slowed his development, but he’s still only entering his third NFL season. The fact that a former third-round pick with legitimate NFL experience couldn’t crack this defensive line says more about Cincinnati’s depth than it does about Jackson. 6. Shaka Heyward, LB Heyward is another player who appeared to have a legitimate argument for the 53. He had a strong preseason and was part of a linebacker competition that remained unsettled almost until the deadline. Ultimately, Cincinnati chose to carry four linebackers behind Barrett Carter and Demetrius Knight Jr., with Oren Burks and Swayze Bozeman rounding out the group. That decision squeezed Heyward out. Cincy Jungle’s roster tracker specifically identified Heyward as a surprise cut, noting that his performance had warranted consideration for a roster spot. The emergence of Bozeman is a major factor. Heyward could be an interesting practice-squad candidate if he clears waivers. 7. Antwaun Powell-Ryland, DE Powell-Ryland is another cut that demonstrates just how deep Cincinnati’s defensive front became. He made plays throughout the preseason and finished the Philadelphia game with a sack alongside Foskey. More importantly, Taylor specifically mentioned Powell-Ryland as one of the six defensive linemen who essentially had to play the entire game against Philadelphia because of Cincinnati’s limited numbers. The Bengals were comfortable enough with their other edge options that Powell-Ryland ultimately didn’t make the 53. That doesn’t mean he failed. It means Cincinnati had more players deserving of defensive-line jobs than it could accommodate. 8. Daijahn Anthony, S Anthony’s release is another interesting one because Cincinnati had previously invested in him as a developmental safety. The Bengals drafted Anthony in the seventh round of the 2024 draft, and he saw meaningful playing time as a rookie. But the safety room changed this offseason. Bryan Cook, Jordan Battle, and Kyle Dugger are established pieces, while P.J. Jules emerged strongly enough during camp to beat Anthony out for the final safety spot. The Bengals ultimately went with four safeties, leaving Anthony outside the 53. This is another case where the player wasn’t necessarily bad. Someone simply won the competition. 9. Cam Grandy, TE Grandy is perhaps less surprising than the players above, but his release is notable because…

full_text: Former third-round NFL pick and third-year defensive tackle McKinnley Jackson was waived Sunday afternoon by the Cincinnati Bengals . NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport broke the news, adding that Jackson was actually drawing trade interest, but the Bengals obviously did not make a deal with anyone. Entering his third season with the Bengals, Jackson was facing an uphill battle because of injuries and an extremely deep defensive line room this season. The former Aggie showed a bit of promise in his rookie season with a handful of solid plays, but never truly showed consistency. He never quite made it over the hump in Cincinnati. Despite struggling with a couple of injuries during his rookie season and this year during training camp, he still has quite a bit of upside, especially for teams searching for defensive line depth. Ultimately, Jackson’s best season was his rookie season when he played in 13 games, tallying 15 tackles and a sack. McKinnley Jackson could still have some interest around the league. title: Browns QB room: Decisions around the 4 QBs are and will be complicated
summary: Heading into the NFL season, most teams will carry two quarterbacks on their 53-man roster, with a third on the practice squad who can be called up when needed. With a limited number of roster spots available, teams have to balance their needs across every position group. This is why it is such an interesting choice for the Cleveland Browns to […]
full_text: Heading into the NFL season, most teams will carry two quarterbacks on their 53-man roster , with a third on the practice squad who can be called up when needed. With a limited number of roster spots available, teams have to balance their needs across every position group. This is why it is such an interesting choice for the Cleveland Browns to choose to keep four quarterbacks in their orbit. Dillon Gabriel was put on the IR with a back injury , while Deshaun Watson , Shedeur Sanders , and Taylen Green have all made the initial 53-man roster. It will be difficult to justify keeping four quarterbacks when Gabriel is healthy, when another roster spot could be better used on a player who fills a greater need. Gabriel and Green both proved their value in the final preseason game against the New England Patriots, so the team clearly views them as important assets. With a lot of questions around the play of both Watson and Sanders, it makes sense to keep other options on the roster that you trust. Additionally, the decisions made on the initial 53-man roster aren’t final. If a need arises at another position, the team has the flexibility to adjust its roster and address it accordingly. The fact that Gabriel is on Injured Reserve and doesn’t occupy an active roster spot also made the decision easier. Many felt as though a roster spot could be better used on someone like wide receiver Luke Floriea , who was very impressive during this year’s pre-season. The team likely feels confident it can bring him back to the practice squad and keep him in the organization in some capacity. With Gabriel on IR, the Browns have four game weeks to decide what they will do with their four quarterbacks. title: Browns roster comparison: 2026 initial 53-man roster versus the 2025 version
summary: The more things change, the more they stay the same… that has been true for the Cleveland Browns for quite a few seasons, but not anymore. Now, every year since GM Andrew Berry took over the team in 2020, the Browns roster has seen some changes here and there, but the massive overhaul that started […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NV - SEPTEMBER 29: Defensive end Myles Garrett #95 of the Cleveland Browns, long snapper Charley Hughlett #47, center Ethan Pocic #55, guard Joel Bitonio #75, cornerback Denzel Ward #21, and quarterback Deshaun Watson #4 stand on the sidelines prior to an NFL football game against the Las Vegas Raiders, at Allegiant Stadium on September 29, 2024 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The more things change, the more they stay the same… that has been true for the Cleveland Browns for quite a few seasons, but not anymore. Now, every year since GM Andrew Berry took over the team in 2020, the Browns roster has seen some changes here and there , but the massive overhaul that started in 2025 has taken another step ahead in 2026. So what happens when you compare the newly unveiled 2026 initial 53-man roster in Cleveland to the one the Browns started the 2025 season with? First, it is important to note that we already know how last year’s roster turned out. We are not comparing that roster on the day it was set to Sunday when this year’s roster was put in place. That doesn’t mean we can’t try the exercise anyway. It’ll be quite simple: a list of names from each year, and where it seems to be improved or diminished in talent compared to last year. Quarterback 2025: Joe Flacco, Dillon Gabriel, Shedeur Sanders 2026: Taylen Green, Shedeur Sanders, Deshaun Watson Verdict: Very, very uncertain. Flacco was terrible last year, as were the other two. Maybe a small improvement due to Green’s athletic ability? Running back 2025: Jerome Ford, Dylan Sampson 2026: Michael Burton (FB), Quinshon Judkins, Dylan Sampson, Raheim Sanders Verdict: Much improved. Obviously, things changed quickly in the RB room last year but this exercise is based on initial rosters. Wide receivers 2025: Jerry Jeudy, Cedric Tillman, Jamari Thrash, Gage Larvadain, Isaiah Bond, DeAndre Carter 2026: Isaiah Bond, Denzel Boston, KC Concepcion Jr., Malachi Corley, Jerry Jeudy, Tylan Wallace Verdict: Much improved. Next Tight ends 2025: David Njoku, Harold Fannin, Blake Whiteheart, Brenden Bates 2026: Harold Fannin Jr., Carsen Ryan, Blake Whiteheart Verdict: Diminished. Fannin was the top tight end last year, but Njoku was still a good blocker and had moments where he could make an impact in the passing game. Offensive line 2025: Jack Conklin, Dawand Jones, Cornelius Lucas, KT Leveston, Joel Bitonio, Wyatt Teller Teven Jenkins, Zak Zinter, Ethan Pocic, Luke Wypler 2026: Austin Barber, Parker Brailsford, Spencer Fano, Tytus Howard, Elgton Jenkins, Teven Jenkins, Zion Johnson, Dawand Jones, Luke Wypler, Zak Zinter Verdict: Has to be improved, right?! The starters will either all be new or four out of the five of them, from a line that was putrid last year, besides the now-retired Bitonio. Defensive line 2025: Myles Garrett, Alex Wright, Isaiah McGuire, Joe Tryon-Shoyinka, Cameron Thomas, Mason Graham, Maliek Collins, Mike Hall Jr, Shelby Harris, Adin Huntington 2026: Derek Barnett, Maliek Collins, Kalia Davis, Mason Graham, Mike Hall Jr., Adin Huntington, Isaiah McGuire, Julian Okwara, Jared Verse Verdict: Diminished. One of the easiest calls, sadly, in the roster comparisons. Cleveland is hoping that Verse plus some development from the young guys can offset Garrett’s departure and Wright’s injury. A lot to hope for. Linebacker 2025: Carson Schwesinger, Devin Bush, Mohamoud Diabate, Jerome Baker, Easton Mascarenas-Arnold 2026: Justin Jefferson, Easton Mascarenas-Arnold, Winston Reid, Carson Schwesinger, Quincy Williams Verdict: Some improvement. Williams can replace Bush, and Schwesinger should grow off his Rookie of the Year season. Defensive backs 2025: Denzel Ward, Greg Newsome II, Myles Harden, Cameron Mitchell, Dom Jones, Grant Delpit, Ronnie Hickman, Rayshawn Jenkins, Damontae Kazee, Donovan McMillon 2026: Mekhi Blackmon, Tyson Campbell, Michael Coats Jr., Grant Delpit, Myles Harden, Ronnie Hickman, Donovan McMillon, Emmanuel McNeil-Warren, Daniel Thomas, Denzel Ward Verdict: Slight improvement. The loss of some veteran depth at safety is offset by Campbell for Newsome, some development from the young guys, and the upside of EMW. Special Teams No changes Tabulating up the results: Improved : 5 (RB, WR, OL, LB, DB) Diminished : 2 (TE, DL) Too close to call: 2 (QB, ST) What say you? Where have they improved, diminished, or is it too close to call? Join the conversation! summary: The Cleveland Browns joined their NFL brethren on Sunday in cutting their roster down to the initial 53-man squad ahead of the NFL-mandated deadline. As everyone knows by now, the roster as it stands today is not the roster the Browns will take to Jacksonville in two weeks when they open the regular season against […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OH - AUGUST 27: Cleveland Browns quarterback Dillon Gabriel (6) on the field prior to the National Football League preseason game between the New England Patriots and Cleveland Browns on August 27, 2026, at Huntington Bank Field in Cleveland, OH. (Photo by Frank Jansky/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Cleveland Browns joined their NFL brethren on Sunday in cutting their roster down to the initial 53-man squad ahead of the NFL-mandated deadline. As everyone knows by now, the roster as it stands today is not the roster the Browns will take to Jacksonville in two weeks when they open the regular season against the Jacksonville Jaguars. Practice squads to be filled, waiver wires to be scoured for players, and a host of other roster manipulations will take place every week until the season comes to a close. But it is the roster the Browns have for the moment, so here are three quick observations about the work that general manager Andrew Berry did today. Our initial 53-man roster is set! 📰: https://t.co/6vlFfnOzlp | #DawgPound pic.twitter.com/c2sjQQln7A — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) August 30, 2026 Four quarterbacks … sort of There was much hand-wringing and discussion about whether or not the Browns would and should keep four quarterbacks on the initial roster. (Let’s set aside, for now, that it doesn’t really matter how many they keep since none are worthy of being QB1.) Berry ended up finding a way to keep all four – Deshaun Watson, Shedeur Sanders, Dillon Gabriel, and Taylen Green – in the building for the moment, but that comes with a caveat. While Watson, Sanders, and Green are on the roster, Gabriel will open the season on the injured reserve list with a back injury, meaning he will miss at least the first four games. When did Gabriel come down with this injury? Who knows! The last time anyone saw him in action, he lit up the New England Patriots for 186 passing yards and three touchdowns in one half of action in Thursday’s preseason finale. Browns QB Dillon Gabriel initially hurt his back during the preseason finale, had pain yesterday and underwent an MRI. The injury was notable enough to land him on injured reserve. https://t.co/LuIEFT1Iuk pic.twitter.com/IZ2NS9AxbL — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) August 30, 2026 The official word is that Gabriel hurt his back during the game and underwent an MRI on Saturday. So let’s go with that for now. In the end, it is a way for Berry to delay the decision about what to do with the quarterback room for a few more days or weeks. But it could be quite the risk if the Browns end up trading away a quarterback and Green is just one play away from seeing the field while Gabriel is unavailable. The 2026 Draft class shines All 10 members of the 2026 NFL Draft class made the initial roster, or at least survived being cut. The only member not to be on the active roster is tight end Joe Royer, who was placed on the reserve/non-football illness list. Royer has not been with the team all summer, and no one is saying when he might return. But for now, he is still a member of the team. As for the other nine selections, they all made the squad. Left tackle Spencer Fano, along with wide receivers KC Concepction and Denzel Boston, were always no-brainers. Safety Emmanuel McNeil-Warren looks to be a key member of the secondary, while offensive lineman Austin Barber may find himself in the starting lineup sooner rather than later. The rest of the class – center Parker Brailsford, linebacker Justin Jefferson, Green, and tight end Carsen Ryan – will all likely find a way onto the field at some point this fall. In past years, that would be seen as a sign of weakness or because Berry needs to prove he is the “smartest guy in the room.” But after the success of the 2025 draft class, it is another indication that the Browns may finally be on the right path. The dream is temporarily over for the man from Kent State It was always going to be hard for wide receiver Luke Floriea to find a roster spot, but that doesn’t make the news that he was cut any easier. Floriea was productive during the preseason, and everyone always likes a story of the local kid working his behind off when given the opportunity. Hopefully this is not the last we see of Floriea, as a practice squad spot should have his name on it. What do you say, Browns fans? Were you surprised by the initial roster? Happy? Frustrated? Let everyone know in the comments!

title: 5 reasons WR Luke Floriea missed the initial Browns 53-man roster
summary: To the disappointment, frustration, surprise, and maybe anger of a lot of Cleveland Browns fans, WR Luke Floriea is reportedly not making the team’s initial 53-man roster. As has been repeated over and over again, the initial 53-man roster is not the final 53-man roster. There are lots of reasons teams make moves in different […]
full_text: Cleveland Browns wide receiver Luke Floriea (81) catches a touchdown pass during day 12 of training camp, Aug. 11, 2026, in Berea, Ohio. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co To the disappointment, frustration, surprise, and maybe anger of a lot of Cleveland Browns fans, WR Luke Floriea is reportedly not making the team’s initial 53-man roster . As has been repeated over and over again, the initial 53-man roster is not the final 53-man roster. There are lots of reasons teams make moves in different orders, which could include bringing Floriea back either to the practice squad or to the main roster after some waiver claims go through. Many believe that the Mentor native had earned a spot on the team’s roster , especially with his performance in the third preseason game . In three preseason games, Floriea had six catches for 95 yards and three (almost four) touchdowns. A few reasons the preseason hero didn’t make the initial roster: Special Teams Limitations As noted many times, special teams matter when you are talking about the fifth and sixth wide receivers on a team. Not just in the return game, but also in coverage units. In three preseason contests, Floriea played just four special teams snaps while Malachi Corley , who might make the initial 53-man roster, played in 20 snaps and added two special teams tackles to his return totals. WR depth The additions of KC Concepcion, Denzel Boston , and Tylan Wallace , along with Isaiah Bond’s speed and Jerry Jeudy’s contract and veteran status, leave very little room for another receiver. Corley could make the roster, but that has not yet been determined, and the sixth receiver will likely be inactive most games until an injury happens. 4 QBs While it is possible Cleveland keeps six receivers, reports that the team will hold on to all four quarterbacks on the initial 53-man roster make that tenuous at best. Most teams keep three, at most, so a roster spot at another position must be sacrificed. Floriea, or another release, could be traced directly back to keeping all the quarterbacks. Preseason production does not equal talent Floriea was productive in preseason this year, but teams are generally not looking for production numbers when making back-of-roster decisions. Instead, traits and role are generally the higher priority. Could Floriea be the next undersized, hard-working, local-product-made-good story? Certainly, but a few touchdowns in preseason are not an indicator of that. Dorian Thompson-Robinson looked like an All-Pro for a few preseason games a couple of years ago, and we know how that ended. Low waiver claim risk Generally speaking, fans and media are much more worried about a player being claimed than actually happens. On average, about 1% of waived players are claimed. Those who are either play a vital position or have impressive physical traits that another team believes they can develop. Floriea is neither of those, making the risk of him being claimed pretty small. It is never zero, and that is a risk the Browns will take when this move becomes official. title: Browns fans weigh in on Todd Monken’s decision to start Deshaun Watson over Shedeur Sanders
summary: Cleveland Browns head coach made the unpopular decision this week to name Deshaun Watson as the team’s starting quarterback in Week 1 over Shedeur Sanders. We’ve heard a variety of things, including that since the team starts off with two road games, this gives the team to chance to see if Watson will deliver in […]
full_text: BEREA, OHIO - APRIL 21: Head coach Todd Monken and Deshaun Watson #4 of the Cleveland Browns watch a drill during a voluntary veteran minicamp at CrossCountry Mortgage Campus on April 21, 2026 in Berea, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images Cleveland Browns head coach made the unpopular decision this week to name Deshaun Watson as the team’s starting quarterback in Week 1 over Shedeur Sanders . We’ve heard a variety of things, including that since the team starts off with two road games, this gives the team to chance to see if Watson will deliver in those games prior to deciding what to do in front of the home crowd in Week 3. For this week’s Reacts poll, if I was to ask fans what they thought of Watson starting, I think it would have been 90% or higher toward the negative. Therefore, I tried to put a spin on things by framing your mindset towards head coach Todd Monken instead. The question asked, “Does Monken naming Watson the starter impact your view of the head coach?” 65% of fans still voted that it was a dumb decision by Monken (even though the language in the graphic to the left was edited to be nicer). The remaining 35% of fans said that they respect Monken’s decision (for now). It was a hot-button topic that lots of Browns fans weighed in on, if you go back and read the comments . Among the responses, one fan said: I cannot answer the survey because I don’t believe it was his decision. Spidey thinks Monken made the right call: From all indications, the players have Watson’s back. Heck, how many were here when the trade was made?!? They don’t carry any of the grudges the fans have And they don’t care about the 2027 QB or tanking. Therefore, put yourself in their shoes. You’ve seen both of them perform in training camp and preseason games. There’s not much difference in the results (TDs and INTs) and it certainly appears that Watson has better command in the huddle and LOS. If I’m a player and Monken made the decision based on the media and fans booing, I’d think less of the coach. Heck, I remember thinking less of my coaches in high school if I saw them hanging out with players’ parents or other fans with an interest in seeing one player over another. Monken has Watson on the team. The players have Watson as teammate. Those are the top two factors for Monken. And woe to the leader of men who bends to the whims of the outside world. Half Baked Again said: I have always wondered why we think the Ravens OC was a great hire. I mean that team lived by their defense and Lamar’s legs. They never had a working offense without Lamar. This decision tells me that the Browns are clearly tanking and I do not think Monkin will be here next year (he was set up to fail). Also, none of the QBs will be here next year. title: 7 surprise cuts from Cowboys 53-man roster
summary: The 2026 Dallas Cowboys are one step closer to being gameday ready, with their roster being trimmed down to 53 players at Sunday’s deadline. We kept track of it all right here, and will continue to do so as there is still potential for shakeups, and building the practice squad remains a work in progress. […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - JANUARY 04: Jaydon Blue #23 of the Dallas Cowboys celebrates a first quarter touchdown against the New York Giants at MetLife Stadium on January 04, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Ishika Samant/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 2026 Dallas Cowboys are one step closer to being gameday ready, with their roster being trimmed down to 53 players at Sunday’s deadline . We kept track of it all right here , and will continue to do so as there is still potential for shakeups, and building the practice squad remains a work in progress. It’s been several months on end now when Cowboys fans have been chattering about how different the player acquisition phase of this offseason felt, and roster cuts helped keep this theme going in a lot of ways. A large percentage of the Cowboys cuts came and went without much surprise at all, as Dallas did considerably more work in the offseason to bring in established players worthy of roster spots from the jump. This is especially true for a defense moving on from being one of the worst in franchise history just one season ago, with the only path forward being wiping out as much of the personnel responsible and starting fresh. This blew up, so let me clarify: 17 of the 26 players on the initial 53-man roster last year are not on 53-man rosters right now. 15 are unemployed, 2 are starting the season on PUP (Parsons, Liufau). https://t.co/w3KIm8YIE3 — Nick Harris (@NickHarrisFWST) August 31, 2026 We still have a list of seven surprising cuts below, and they favor Christian Parker’s new-look defense with four names on the list. On offense, the headline that all 11 starters return from 2025 became locked in on Sunday, but the position with the most room for change brought plenty of surprises at cut day, with Dallas going shorter than expected on the final roster at running back. Let’s get into the list. CB Reddy Steward Starting off with a mild surprise, Reddy Steward had a chance to be a rare carryover from that 2025 defense, but ultimately did not make the depth chart at cornerback. What most likely worked against Steward’s chances was the fact his best position is the nickel, where the Cowboys are expected to utilize first-round pick Caleb Downs plenty. There has been some concern about using Downs as just a matchup player in the slot and not using his versatility in the best way possible, but the Cowboys answered for this by also keeping Cobie Durant and Ameer Speed as capable players in this role. Speed came on strong as a special teams player and ultimately this was enough to beat out a player like Steward. Steward also did not have the draft pedigree of a player like Caelen Carson, who similarly had struggles throughout the preseason, but becomes a carryover player Dallas isn’t quite ready to give up on yet under new coaching as he also beat out Steward for a spot. RBs Phil Mafah, Jaydon Blue, Israel Abanikanda The Cowboys cuts at running back came one after another, after another, which is at least one more than anticipated for many fans. With Javonte Williams locked in as the starter, Jaydon Blue, Phil Mafah, Malik Davis, and Israel Abanikanda battled it out for the RB2 role, which Davis ultimately won – apparently in strong enough fashion to push the rest of his competition off the roster entirely. The Cowboys now have a pair of similar backs that are at their best pounding the rock between the tackles, passing on the chance to have more of a dynamic duo by pairing Williams with Blue. All three of these cuts will be candidates to watch for potential signings to the practice squad , where Dallas can still call on them come gamedays. After a balanced share out of the backfield in the preseason opener at the Seahawks, the Cowboys leaned on Blue to get them through the Cardinals game, and then saw Mafah lead them in carries against the Saints – a preseason finale that came and went without feeling like it had much impact on final roster decisions, especially on offense. Knowing how much this team prefers to keep the players they plan on using in the regular season on ice during exhibition season, the tea leaves here pointed to Davis earning the RB2 role. Opting to not have either Blue or Mafah as a RB3 with potential depending on the game plan to rise to RB2 any given week is still a surprise. Another thing the Cowboys showed against the Saints, and Cardinals the week before, is a desire to get in on the trend of multiple tight end usage this season. This offense may still trend towards the middle or bottom of heavy TE personnel usage due to having three receivers that demand to see the field a lot, but when they do, Williams and Davis are the best “no nonsense” backs to keep for these looks. Still, with the Cowboys having only Williams, Davis, and fullback Hunter Luepke on the roster out of the backfield, keep a close eye on how efficient they are in the short passing game as extensions of the run to make or break if moving on from a pair of second-year draft picks was the right decision. LB Sam Williams Back to another mild, or perhaps medium surprise, Sam Williams did not make the final roster of edge rushers. Rashan Gary, Donovan Ezeiruaku, Von Miller, and rookie Malachi Lawrence were four obvious choices on the depth chart here, and the other two spots went to players that flashed more than Williams this preseason, James Houston and Tyrus Wheat. The Cowboys defense obviously has many goals for this season, but an early one to officially move on from last year’s disaster is simply to play as a cohesive unit where all 11 players are on the same page and playing together. Far too many times, both in his previous stint with the team and in this preseason, Williams played out of line with this goal and cost the team with reckless play, penalties, or poor technique. The splash play potential in between these mishaps from Williams always gave him some chance to still make the team, but Dallas opted for players with more consistent rush integrity in Wheat and Houston. How much this group gets home to sack opposing quarterbacks is of course something to watch, especially if the Cowboys offense does what they’re expected to and piles on points to force opponents to play from behind. In more neutral situations and close games against top competition though, the Cowboys outside linebackers must do a better job than they have so far in setting a hard edge and not getting outflanked on the perimeter. Wheat and Houston may not be the first players that will help the defense here, but they are more capable than Williams while also having the speed to finish sacks in obvious pass situations. The team made a clear statement about just how much they value all of these things by leaving Williams off the team going into week one. DTs Jay Toia, Tommy Dunn Sticking with the defense to conclude our list, Jay Toia and UDFA Tommy Dunn are a package deal to make for a roster surprise when it comes to depth on the interior. Both players did not help themselves nearly as much as they could have on Friday night at home against the Saints, but prior to that had strong performances earlier in the preseason. If for nothing else, both Toia and Dunn should be commended for eating up snaps at a position where the Cowboys arguably had the most density of talent riding the bench all preseason, with Quinnen Williams, Kenny Clark, and Otito Ogbonnia just waiting for the Giants game. Joining these three presumed starters on the roster are veteran Jonathan Bullard and rookie LT Overton. Where Toia was a true nose tackle with little pass rush upside, and Dunn was a bit more of a hybrid player with way more juice as a run stuffer, Bullard and Overton both have the right mix the Cowboys are apparently looking for of pass rush upside and anchoring ability at the point of attack. With this pass rush potential from Bullard and Overton though comes concerns about how well Dallas can defend the inside run when the big…

title: Over half of last year’s Cowboys defenders are off the roster
summary: Roster cuts can be brutal, and it looks like they are especially brutal for players who played on the NFL’s worst defense last year. Nick Harris of the Star-Telegram did a quick check on the Cowboys defense, and found that 17 of the 26 defenders on the 2025 Week 1 roster are unemployed after yesterday’s […]
full_text: Roster cuts can be brutal, and it looks like they are especially brutal for players who played on the NFL’s worst defense last year. Nick Harris of the Star-Telegram did a quick check on the Cowboys defense, and found that 17 of the 26 defenders on the 2025 Week 1 roster are unemployed after yesterday’s final roster cuts. This blew up, so let me clarify: 17 of the 26 players on the initial 53-man roster last year are not on 53-man rosters right now. 15 are unemployed, 2 are starting the season on PUP (Parsons, Liufau). https://t.co/w3KIm8YIE3 — Nick Harris (@NickHarrisFWST) August 31, 2026 Harris corrected the number to 15, explaining that two of those 17 players were actually on IR. Here’s a look at the 2025 Week 1 roster for the defense, with the red cells indicating players that do not have a job right now, and the yellow cells marking players on IR: body .sbnu-legacy-content-table td, body .sbnu-legacy-content-table th, body .sbnu-legacy-content-table { border: 1px solid #000 !important; border-collapse: collapse !important; } body .sbnu-legacy-content-table td, body .sbnu-legacy-content-table th { padding: 0px 6px !important; } 2025 Week 1 roster – Base 4-3 D POS Starter 2nd 3rd LDE Sam Williams Donovan Ezeiruaku NT Kenny Clark Mazi Smith Jay Toia DT Osa Odighizuwa Solomon Thomas Perrion Winfrey RDE Dante Fowler Marshawn Kneeland (RIP) James Houston WLB Jack Sanborn Shemar James MLB Kenneth Murray Marist Liufau (IR) SLB Damone Clark (IR) Buddy Johnson SS Malik Hooker Markquese Bell FS Donovan Wilson Juanyeh Thomas RCB Kaiir Elam C.J. Godwin (retired) Trikweze Bridges LCB DaRon Bland Trevon Diggs Reddy Steward IR/PUP DeMarvion Overshown, Shavon Revel Jr., Caelen Carson Of the 27 players on the opening-day roster against the Eagles in 2025, 15 are currently without a team, even if that may not last more than a few hours in some cases. Rosters in the NFL churn about 30% each year, so some degree of change can be expected from year-to-year, especially among backups and down-roster players. But five of last year’s starters are also without a team right now, which seems pretty high, but is probably indicative of the quality of those former starters. Jerry Jones opened the press conference following Day 2 of the draft by pointing out the changes made to the defense . “We have been able to, as of right now, rebuild this defense. I think the fact that we put a new newness to the system and coaching staff, and new faces that we’ve added, we’ve changed this defense.” Jones also pointed out that the changes made were not just a reaction to last year, but a “product of 3, 4, 5 years, maybe more, where we ultimately didn’t get to where we were trying to go and be a contender.” If you look closely at the table above, you’ll also notice that the 2026 Cowboys are only returning seven defensive players from last year’s week one roster (plus Marist Liufau on IR). Eight out of 27. That’s a roster churn of 70%. A change of this magnitude is not just unusual, it’s unprecedented for a team like the Cowboys that likes to keep things comfortable and is generally averse to change. But judging by how last year’s players fared with other teams around the league, those changes were absolutely necessary.

title: 10 thoughts on the Cowboys initial 53-man roster
summary: The Dallas Cowboys’ 53-man roster is set. For now, that is. Expect more shuffling as they work out the little things with players still being claimed off waivers. This group is a good start and will make up most of the cast of characters we’ll be rooting for this upcoming season. Most of it was […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - AUGUST 15: Noah Igbinoghene #17 of the Seattle Seahawks lines up against Camden Brown #6 of the Dallas Cowboys during the second quarter during the NFL preseason game at Lumen Field on August 15, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Jack Compton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys’ 53-man roster is set. For now, that is. Expect more shuffling as they work out the little things with players still being claimed off waivers. This group is a good start and will make up most of the cast of characters we’ll be rooting for this upcoming season. Most of it was as expected, but there were surprises. Here are our 10 thoughts on the team’s initial roster. 1. Camden survives Fans were on pins and needles about whether the team would carry six wide receivers, with one being undrafted free agent and camp sensation, Camden Brown. Well, we got our answer. Brown started turning heads in camp with amazing catches, and he continued such in the preseason. His quick acceleration and elite contested-catch ability were too good to leave off the roster. 2. Three’s company Whether it was their intentions all along, or the final preseason game sealed the deal, the Cowboys are keeping three quarterbacks. This gives them some flexibility between Joe Milton III and Sam Howell, as one offers some nice upside while the other provides a safe floor. Hopefully, we’ll never find out which the team prefers, but at least they’ll have options if that time comes. 3. Short at RB It seemed as if we knew what was going on at running back based on who played (or didn’t play) in the final preseason game, but the team pulled a fast one on us by releasing their fast one. Jaydon Blue, the team’s fifth-round pick last year, was a surprise release. He’s looked better this year, but the coaches don’t feel comfortable keeping him. With all the backups not named Malik Davis released, the team hopes they can get a couple of them back on the practice squad. 4. Tackle trades The offensive tackle position saw a huge shakeup over the last 24 hours with two trades. On Saturday, the Cowboys traded with the Pittsburgh Steelers to acquire former first-round pick Broderick Jones . The move signaled the end for third-year tackle Nate Thomas, but the team at least got something in return by trading him to the Houston Texans on Sunday. They worked the phones to get a swing tackle upgrade. Fingers crossed it works out. 5. Familiar approach Not only did the Cowboys bring in a new guy they like and trade away a third-year player they have given up on at the last second, but they also kept a developmental guy who clearly wasn’t ready. Fourth-round rookie Drew Shelton survived roster cuts, giving the team more time to work with him. This approach looks very familiar to last year, but they pulled off something similar. 2025 – Outside acquisition (Hakeem Adeniji), develop a rookie (Ajani Cornelius), and trade (Asim Richards) 2026 – Outside acquisition (Broderick Jones), develop a rookie (Drew Shelton), and trade (Nate Thomas) Enter the Biff’s “There’s something very familiar about this” meme. 6. Light in the interior The interior offensive line took a bigger hit than expected. While we were waiting to see who survived between Nick Leverett and Trevor Keegan, the team surprised people by not choosing either of them. They still have T.J. Bass and last year’s development tackle-turned-guard, Cornelius, but they still seem a bit light. The good news is that at least one (if not both) of Leverett and Keegan should make it through waivers to the practice squad. Or the Cowboys may opt to claim an interior lineman who’s been released? 7. Hard work rewarded Both Tyrus Wheat and Alijah Clark have made the roster before, so it shouldn’t be a complete shocker, but many felt their chances were slim because they were stuck in crowded position groups. The Von Miller signing created little room at outside linebacker, but Sam Williams’ release and Marist Liufau’s injury opened up just enough room for Wheat. Clark wasn’t given those same breaks, so he had to make his own luck and force the team to go long at safety. Both guys show relentless effort and are key contributors on special teams, which proves that we must not overlook these details when filling out the roster. Note – Liufau was placed on IR, designated to return. 8. No more room in the middle The Cowboys have completely remodeled their defensive tackle position as all five of the guys selected just completed their first training camp with the team. All of them. With four savvy veterans and one fourth-round rookie, this group looks stout, but it didn’t leave room for either Jay Toai or Tommy Dunn, both of whom flashed in preseason action. 9. The need for Speed Cornerback depth after the first three was a big question for the Cowboys. Caelen Carson made the cut despite being picked on some in preseason action, but the biggest surprise was hanging on to UFL’er Ameer Speed. He’s had a good camp and only allowed one reception across 77 defensive snaps this preseason. Rookie corner Devin Moore was placed on IR, designated to return. 10. Good use of a Day 3 pick Dee Winters made the team! Okay, that’s not a surprise to anyone, but it’s worth pointing out that the fifth-round pick the team traded to the San Francisco 49ers to get him did not. Tight end Justin Joly, taken 152nd overall, was released on Sunday. It’s a friendly reminder that Day 3 picks have low-chance returns, so anytime you can exchange that for a sure-thing contributor, it’s a good move.
author: Dan Rogers

title: Cowboys news: Takeaways and analysis of Dallas’ 53-man roster
summary: Football is now two weeks away, preseason football is in the books, and Dallas now has a finalized 53-man roster. Players like Jaydon Blue and Michael Trigg unfortunately did not make the cut, while names like Camden Brown and both Sam Howell and Joe Milton are on the team. The last piece of the puzzle […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TEXAS - AUGUST 28: Head coach Brian Schottenheimer of the Dallas Cowboys watches action prior to an NFL Preseason 2026 game against the New Orleans Saints at AT&T Stadium on August 28, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) | Getty Images Football is now two weeks away, preseason football is in the books, and Dallas now has a finalized 53-man roster. Players like Jaydon Blue and Michael Trigg unfortunately did not make the cut, while names like Camden Brown and both Sam Howell and Joe Milton are on the team. The last piece of the puzzle is finding out who is going to clear waivers and can make it back on the practice squad. It may not be the end of the road for guys like Blue and Trigg in Dallas if they can bring them back. Cowboys release initial 53-man roster for 2026 season- Tommy Yarrish, DallasCowboys.com There are still moves Dallas can make with their roster. Especially with two weeks to go, it would be surprising if these were the 53 men on the roster come week one. The initial 53-man roster is just the starting point of Dallas’ personnel taking full shape, as they’ll also work to create their practice squad and with two weeks until the season opener, could see different personnel transactions from now until kickoff on Sunday night in East Rutherford. Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer said the cut down decisions this season will be more difficult because Dallas is a “deeper, better, more talented football team,” and he and his staff had difficult decisions to make. Cowboys 53-man roster analysis: Dallas keeps 3 QBs, cuts a notable veteran and more- Joseph Hoyt, DMN One of the more notable cuts in Michael Trigg is a gamble. Because Trigg is not ready to be a consistent contributor on the team, but he did flash enough to believe he could do so down the line. Now Dallas has to hope he clears waivers. The Cowboys decided to not have their highest-paid undrafted free agent on the initial roster , contradicting a common theme they’ve had in the past. They hope Trigg can make it through waivers and return to the practice squad, where he can continue his development under tight ends coach Lunda Wells. Full details as Cowboys somehow convince Texans to trade for Nate Thomas- Jerry Trotta, The Landry Hat Amid the shuffle of cuts, the Cowboys pulled off a last-minute trade, sending Thomas to Houston. Since Thomas was far from a lock to make the roster in the first place, Dallas getting a seventh-round pick in return was a win. Here’s a snapshot of what the Cowboys have acquired and lost in the Broderick Jones and Nate Thomas trades. Gained: Broderick Jones 2027 fourth-round pick 2027 seventh-round pick Lost: 2027 third-round pick 2027 sixth-round pick Nate Thomas Five most surprising cuts that the Dallas Cowboys made on Sunday – Nick Harris, FWST In addition to Blue, Dallas had to part ways with several names that had been contributors as recently as last season. While unfortunate, this is a good sign, the roster is stronger and players that were relied on last year aren’t even among the 53 best names in 2026. Sam Williams The 2022 second-round pick at the outside linebacker spot was brought back in the offseason on a one-year, fully guaranteed $2 million contract in hopes that the new scheme would benefit his progression, but the staff decided to cut ties after seeing him in training camp and in the preseason. Dallas Cowboys’ Perfect Answer at LB Just Fell Into Their Lap With NFL Roster Cuts- Randy Gurzi, Sports Illustrated Don’t forget that 31 other teams also trimmed down their rosters on Sunday, which means there is a whole batch of new talent on the free agency market. Dallas would be wise to look around, especially at impressive vet Tyrell Dotson. While they’re surely going to keep an eye on every player who is waived as teams trim their rosters to 53 players , the Cowboys might have already been gifted the answer to their concerns. On Sunday, it was announced that the Miami Dolphins are releasing linebacker Tyrel Dodson, and since he’s a vested veteran, he will immediately become a free agent. 4 burning questions after Cowboys cut down to 53- LP Cruz, Blogging The Boys While we now have a significantly clearer picture of what the roster will look like heading into next season, there are still outstanding questions. This are still holes that could be addressed and talent that could fill them. Is there a backup nose tackle? Tommy Dunn, the Kansas UDFA, produced enough positive snaps to make a case as the reserve nose. The Cowboys disagreed and cut him, along with Jay Toia (who showed flashes against Arizona but struggled against the Saints). Daily discussion question: What do you make of the initial 53-man roster?

title: 4 burning questions after Cowboys cut down to 53
summary: As of now, the Dallas Cowboys have trimmed their roster to 53 players following the preseason. Many fans breathed a sigh of relief when standout receiver Camden Brown made the team. The Cowboys also released Sam Williams along with several others at one key position. Surprisingly, Dallas held on to both Joe Milton and Sam […]
full_text: FRISCO, TEXAS - AUGUST 25: Head coach Brian Schottenheimer of the Dallas Cowboys gives instruction during practice at The Star in Frisco on August 25, 2026 in Frisco, Texas. (Photo by Sam Hodde/Getty Images) | Getty Images As of now, the Dallas Cowboys have trimmed their roster to 53 players following the preseason. Many fans breathed a sigh of relief when standout receiver Camden Brown made the team. The Cowboys also released Sam Williams along with several others at one key position. Surprisingly, Dallas held on to both Joe Milton and Sam Howell. For the Cowboys, the job isn’t complete. Sunday’s cuts provided clarity in some areas but ushered in more questions in others. Here are four remaining questions after Dallas’ roster cuts. Who is RB3? The Cowboys stunned observers by releasing fifth-rounder Jaydon Blue, who possessed electric speed and was firmly in the mix for the RB2 job behind Javonte Williams. Blue led the team in rushing against Arizona and sat out the preseason finale—moves that typically signal roster security. Instead, Dallas trimmed the backfield hard, also cutting Phil Mafah and Israel Abanikanda. Malik Davis has been the most consistent backup all offseason and now sits as RB2. Hunter Luepke can handle short-yardage and fullback duties, but he is not a traditional runner. Dallas currently lacks a reliable third running back. Cutting three backs only makes sense if the team plans to add one from the waiver wire or free-agent market—and that addition is clearly needed. Do they add an outside cornerback? The initial 53-man roster carries five cornerbacks, with Caleb Downs listed as a defensive back. Ameer Speed is mainly a special-teams player, and Caelen Carson failed to impress in camp or the preseason. Devin Moore is on injured reserve; Reddy Steward and Josh Butler were released. DaRon Bland’s durability remains a concern, and Shavon Revel still need to prove he can do it when the games count. The Cowboys have already shown interest in veteran Adoree’ Jackson (a natural fit under Christian Parker) and have been linked to bigger names such as Christian Gonzalez. Dallas must improve the cornerback room. Standing pat leaves the secondary vulnerable. Is there a backup nose tackle? Tommy Dunn, the Kansas UDFA, produced enough positive snaps to make a case as the reserve nose. The Cowboys disagreed and cut him, along with Jay Toia (who showed flashes against Arizona but struggled against the Saints). The Cowboys could rotate starters Kenny Clark, Otito Ogbonnia, and Quinnen Williams through different positions. No one else on the current roster is a natural fit as a 0-tech backup. This is a clear, under-addressed need that Dallas still has not solved. They may use practice squad callups to augment the room during the season. Are they thin at inside linebacker? The top of the depth chart is strong: Dee Winters is productive, Shemar James is progressing in Year 2, DeMarvion Overshown is a playmaker, and rookie Jaishawn Barham has exceeded expectations. Carrying only four linebackers at such a physical position is a calculated risk. Overshown’s injury history and Barham’s inexperience leave the group exposed. The Cowboys have long been connected to veteran additions. They cut Curtis Robinson, Justin Barron and Langston Patterson. Keeping just four is a deliberate choice that could prove costly once the season’s attrition begins. The saving note is that Robinson intends to re-sign with the practice squad. What are your big questions around the initial roster?

While the Cowboys have a final (ongoing) 53-man roster, they also have to put together a practice squad. Some FAQ topics answered regarding an NFL practice squad: NFL teams are allowed to have 16 players and can carry a 17th if the extra is from the league’s International Pathway Program. A maximum of six players on the squad can have NFL experience. Each Tuesday of the season the league can “protect” four of them so that they cannot be poached. Every week the Cowboys (or any NFL team) can promote two players from the squad to their active roster but only three times maximum. Beyond that the player must be a member of the active roster. title: Cowboys countdown to kickoff: Top 100 iconic games – Day 14
summary: It is Day 14 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like […]
full_text: MIAMI, FL - JANUARY 21: Head Coach Tom Landry of the Dallas Cowboys stands with his team prior to playing the Pittsburgh Steelers in Super Bowl XIII on January 21, 1979 at the Orange Bowl in Miami, Florida. The Steelers won the Super Bowl 35-31. (Photo by Focus on Sport/Getty Images) | Getty Images It is Day 14 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like how big the game was for the organization, how memorable the game was, games that had unusual events take place, games that are a part of NFL lore, Cowboys firsts, and games where the Cowboys just plain dominated. Variety is the spice of life and we have all different kind of Cowboys games to review. At the bottom, we’ll link each day of the countdown so you can go back and check out any you missed. We give you Day 14 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff, when we revisit perhaps the ultimate heavyweight fight of the NFL’s 1970s era. The defending champion Cowboys met the Pittsburgh Steelers in the first Super Bowl rematch, and a game loaded with Hall of Fame talent delivered on the hype. Sunday, January 21, 1979 Miami Orange Bowl, Miami, Florida Final Score: Pittsburgh Steelers 35, Dallas Cowboys 31 Pittsburgh struck first when Terry Bradshaw found John Stallworth for a 28-yard touchdown. Dallas answered when Roger Staubach hit Tony Hill for a 39-yard score, and the Cowboys then moved ahead 14-7 when linebacker Mike Hegman stripped Bradshaw and returned the fumble 37 yards for a touchdown. The advantage disappeared quickly. Bradshaw responded with a 75-yard touchdown to Stallworth, then found Rocky Bleier from seven yards out late in the second quarter. Pittsburgh carried a 21-14 lead into halftime after a frantic opening half in which both teams repeatedly produced game-changing plays. Dallas had a golden opportunity to tie the game during the third quarter. Staubach found veteran tight end Jackie Smith completely open in the end zone on third down, but Smith went to the ground and could not secure the pass. Instead of a touchdown, the Cowboys settled for Rafael Septién’s 27-yard field goal and remained behind 21-17. It became one of the most painful missed opportunities in franchise history. The game swung decisively during the fourth quarter. A controversial 33-yard pass-interference penalty against Cowboys cornerback Benny Barnes helped Pittsburgh move deep into Dallas territory. Two plays later, Franco Harris broke through for a 22-yard touchdown to make it 28-17. Disaster followed on the ensuing kickoff. Randy White fumbled the bouncing kick and Pittsburgh recovered. Bradshaw immediately capitalized by hitting Lynn Swann for an 18-yard touchdown, suddenly stretching the margin to 35-17. In a matter of moments, a four-point game had become an 18-point deficit. Dallas still refused to go away. Staubach directed an 89-yard drive and found Billy Joe DuPree for a seven-yard touchdown with 2:27 remaining. Dennis Thurman then recovered the Cowboys’ onside kick, giving Staubach another opportunity. Dallas drove 52 yards and scored again when Butch Johnson caught a four-yard touchdown pass with just 22 seconds left. Suddenly, Pittsburgh’s lead had been reduced to 35-31. The Cowboys attempted another onside kick, but Bleier recovered it and finally ended the comeback. Dallas had scored 14 points in barely two minutes, but the earlier missed opportunities proved too much to overcome. This game belongs on the countdown because few games better represent what the Cowboys were during the 1970s. Dallas and Pittsburgh were two of the NFL’s defining powers, and Super Bowl XIII placed them against each other with a championship at stake for the second time in four seasons. The Cowboys lost, but their furious comeback helped turn the game into one of the defining Super Bowls of the era. #Cowboys vs #Steelers 1978 Super Bowl XIII Final Score: Pittsburgh Steelers 35, Dallas Cowboys 31 #DallasCowboys #NFL (📽️: @nfl ) pic.twitter.com/iLWlCvOHR3 — Mike Poland (@kenfigkowboy) August 29, 2026 Interesting Facts About the Game Super Bowl XIII was the first rematch in Super Bowl history. Pittsburgh had also defeated Dallas 21-17 in Super Bowl X three years earlier. full_text: DENVER, CO - AUGUST 28: Sam Ehlinger #4 of the Denver Broncos throws a pass during the second quarter against the Minnesota Vikings in a preseason game at Empower Field at Mile High on August 28, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images One of the bigger questions heading into the roster cut deadline was whether or not the Broncos will keep three quarterbacks on their 53-man roster. Last season, they released Ehlinger, but despite reportedly having backup opportunities out there for him, the former Texas star quarterback agreed to sign on to the Broncos’ practice squad. But would they risk that again this year? The answer is no. Before the cut deadline, it was reported that the Broncos would keep three quarterbacks on their 53-man roster, which meant third-string QB Sam Ehlinger made the team. George Paton said Sam Ehlinger's third preseason game convinced them they needed to keep him. — Zac Stevens (@ZacStevens) August 30, 2026 After the preseason finale on Friday, I wrote that it is tough to figure out what from that game mattered and what didn’t. For instance, Justin Joly has an 88-yard touchdown and is later waived. The same goes for Jaleel McLaughlin, who scored a touchdown from QB Sam Ehlinger but was also cut. Well, Ehlinger’s performance mattered and convinced the Broncos to keep him on their 53-man roster. Broncos GM George Paton told reporters, “Sam obviously played great. If we were thinking anything there, that certainly confirmed keeping Sam”. He added that Ehlinger is “a big part of this quarterback room and they felt they would have lost him if they let him go this time around. “We love the quarterback room. We stated that a lot. [QB] Sam [Ehlinger], ‘Stiddy’ (QB Jarrett Stidham), we thought they both had really good offseasons, really good training camps and in the games. Sam is a big part of this quarterback room. We didn’t want to lose him, and we felt we were going to lose him. He’s too important to our team and just didn’t want to risk doing that. Obviously the game he played the other night was outstanding. We love the room. We’re going to keep the room together.” Since being signed to the team, the Broncos have been very vocal about what Ehlinger meant to this team on and off the field. Sure, he might just be a third-string quarterback who hopefully doesn’t play this season, but he’s important to the locker room and, specifically, that quarterback room. One example was this offseason, when Ehlinger and Nix planned an offseason throwing session in Austin, Texas (they love Ehlinger down there), and Broncos wide receiver Troy Franklin added that Ehlinger set up a boat trip for the players during their time there . The coaches love him, the players seem to love him, and he gives the Broncos talented quarterback depth. Does he stay on the 53-man roster all season? That remains to be seen, but in the short-term, he’s on the 53-man roster and the Broncos love their quarterback room.

title: Jonah Elliss and Que Robinson will step into big roles on the Broncos’ defense
summary: It was announced on Sunday that starting outside linebacker/edge rusher Jonathon Cooper would be placed on the Commissioner’s Exempt List and be sidelined for the foreseeable future. As we know, he is dealing with a serious legal matter off the field, and this was simply part of the process. General Manager George Paton told reporters […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - JANUARY 25: Jonah Elliss #52 and Que Robinson #51 of the Denver Broncos celebrate during the first quarter of the AFC Championship game against the New England Patriots at Empower Field At Mile High on January 25, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images It was announced on Sunday that starting outside linebacker/edge rusher Jonathon Cooper would be placed on the Commissioner’s Exempt List and be sidelined for the foreseeable future. As we know, he is dealing with a serious legal matter off the field, and this was simply part of the process. General Manager George Paton told reporters that they continue to take this matter very seriously and will monitor all legal developments and support Cooper. He added that Cooper has worked very hard to better himself, and he believes it will be good to have him inside the building and simply be part of the team. Yes, in regards to [OLB] Jonathon [Cooper] being placed on the Commissioner’s Exempt list, it’s part of the process. We continue to take this very seriously. We’re going to monitor all the legal developments and continue to support Jonathon. Jonathon’s worked very hard to better himself, and it’ll be good to have him in the building, be in meetings and just be a part of the team”. However, while Cooper is sidelined, the Broncos are going to need to replace him on the field. He was a key starter in their league-leading pass rush unit and will need to be replaced if they want to be the league’s best pass rush unit again this season. Thankfully, the Broncos are deep at edge rusher and have two young and talented players ready to step up. George Paton on the OLB room without Jonathon Cooper: "These guys have all played in games. Big games" "All these guys can play" Gave a shoutout to Que Robinson and how he came on late down the stretch last year "We feel really good about him" — Zac Stevens (@ZacStevens) August 30, 2026 Third-year edge rusher Jonah Elliss is expected to replace Jonathon Cooper in the Broncos’ starting lineup. He has flashed real talent during his first two years with the team and now will have an opportunity to shine as a starter. However, don’t sleep on second-year edge rusher Que Robinson. He looked like a future starter last season, according to Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph, and has all the tools to be a 10+ sack guy for the Broncos defense this upcoming season. GM George Paton told reporters that “all these guys can play” and singled out Que Robinson as someone they feel really good about moving forward. He added they like their depth, but will be looking around because “You can never have enough pass rushers.” “These guys have all played in big games and done well. All these guys we feel like can play. We like the depth there. We led the league in sacks the last two years, and these guys were all a part of that. [OLB] Que [Robinson] coming on late. I think you saw what Que did in the New England game late in the season, even the Houston game last year and some of the things he did. Then you watched him in training camp and the games this year. We feel really good about him. Then [OLB] Jonah [Elliss] and obviously ‘Tilly’ (OLB Dondrea Tillman) and [OLB] Nik [Bonitto], these guys have played and have done well. Depth-wise, we’ll be looking a little bit, looking on the practice squad and we’ll be looking around. You can never have enough pass rushers, so we’ll kind of see how that goes.” Jonah Elliss was a standout player throughout camp, but so was Que Robinson. Both have pass rush potential and should see significant snaps moving forward. I am personally a big Que Robinson fan and believe he is a big-time breakout candidate. He looks like a legit pass rusher off the edge. He has the size, length, athleticism, bend, and explosive first step you look for, and he could thrive opposite Nik Bonitto. He was making plays throughout the preseason, and I believe that will continue into the season. Simply, the Broncos will need these two players to step up and play well quickly. Their schedule on paper looks tough, starting the year with an opening-week road game in primetime at Arrowhead, a home game vs. the Jaguars (the only team that truly beat the Broncos last season), and games vs. the Rams, 49ers, Chargers, and the reigning champions, the Seattle Seahawks. They cannot afford their pass rush to take a step back early on, so Elliss and Robinson will really need to step up for the Broncos. I think they will, and the team seems confident that they will. Offenses will be focusing on All-Pro’s Nik Bonitto and Zach Allen while players like Malcolm Roach and Eyni Uwazurike also get after the passer. So, both Elliss and Robinson should have opportunities to thrive in Vance Joseph’s defense this season.

title: Broncos GM George Paton explains their decision to go with Tyler Badie over Jaleel McLaughlin
summary: One of the Broncos’ more noteworthy roster cuts on Sunday was running back Jaleel McLaughlin. The former undrafted free agent made the team as a rookie after a standout performance during the preseason and became a key member of the Broncos’ offense for a period of time. Despite being undersized, McLaughlin ran well between the […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - AUGUST 28: Tyler Badie #28 of the Denver Broncos runs with the football during the first quarter against the Minnesota Vikings in a preseason game at Empower Field at Mile High on August 28, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images One of the Broncos’ more noteworthy roster cuts on Sunday was running back Jaleel McLaughlin. The former undrafted free agent made the team as a rookie after a standout performance during the preseason and became a key member of the Broncos’ offense for a period of time. Despite being undersized, McLaughlin ran well between the tackles and had some big plays for the team. However, the tide started to turn last season when McLaughlin was inactive for several games prior to the injury to veteran running back JK Dobbins. He did see some late-season action, but struggled to really get anything going on the ground. Jaleel would re-sign on a one-year deal with the Broncos this offseason, but the selection of standout rookie Jonah Coleman in the draft really put his roster spot in danger. Ultimately, McLaughlin played behind Coleman throughout the summer, and the writing appeared to be on the wall when McLaughlin played well into the fourth quarter of the preseason finale. Still, this was a tough cut for the Broncos. McLaughlin was a favorite in that locker room, and General Manager George Paton called McLaughlin the “toughest cut” they had to make at the roster deadline this year. Broncos GM George Paton noted that Jaleel McLaughlin was the "toughest" cut this year at the roster deadline, with Tyler Badie nabbing the RB4 spot. "Yeah, I mean that was really tough. Really all three of those runners, you know, they're all really good runners. They're all… pic.twitter.com/4J64EpsEwI — Andrew Mason (@MaseDenver) August 31, 2026 When asked what went into the decision to keep Tyler Badie over Jaleel McLaughlin, Paton said it was tough, but special teams and third-down ability played into it. “Yes, that was really tough. Really, all three of those runners, they’re all really good runners; they’re all different. A lot goes into it, obviously. [RB] Jaleel [McLaughlin], he’s something else. He was really important to this team- the passion, everything he brings. They have two different skill sets, without going into too much detail. So without getting into details, it was a really hard decision. Obviously, special teams are involved, third-down ability. There’s a lot involved, but that was probably the last decision we made, this fourth runner.” The special teams and third-down ability part is what ultimately mattered here. McLaughlin is a better running back than Tyler Badie; however, Badie offers a lot more as a pass blocker and on special teams. When you’re the RB4 on the roster, those are two things you need to excel at, and that is where Tyler Badie had the edge and is the same reason why he was active over McLaughlin last season. Heading into Week 1, the Broncos’ running back room looks pretty good on paper. Veteran JK Dobbins was among the league leaders in rushing prior to his injury, and if he can stay healthy, he will be a big part of this offense this season. Then you have the pass-catching specialist RJ Harvey, who has great speed and can pop off a big run at any moment and make some big plays in the passing game. He is coming off a 12-touchdown rookie year and will look to repeat that again this season. Then you have impressive rookie Jonah Coleman, who should factor into this backfield right away. He’s a powerful back with good short-area quickness who can pass block and catch passes out of the backfield. Coleman has the makings of a future impact starter. Finally, you have Badie, who could be inactive most weeks, but he offers some running and pass-catching ability and is mostly on the roster for his pass-blocking and special-teams ability. We shall see where Jaleel McLaughlin lands today. Will he be claimed, sign to the Broncos’ practice squad, or start fresh somewhere else and continue his NFL career?
