title: Thoughts and analysis on Broncos’ initial 53-man roster
summary: The Denver Broncos have assembled their initial 53-man roster for the 2026 season. Given the roster’s continuity from last season, there weren’t many spots up for grabs. However, there were a few mild surprises which we will delve into. There are a lot of moves to unpack, so here are some of my early thoughts […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - JANUARY 17: Detail view of the Denver Broncos logo prior to an NFL divisional playoff football game between the Buffalo Bills and the Denver Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High on January 17, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos have assembled their initial 53-man roster for the 2026 season. Given the roster’s continuity from last season, there weren’t many spots up for grabs. However, there were a few mild surprises which we will delve into. There are a lot of moves to unpack , so here are some of my early thoughts and analysis on what we know thus far. Jonathon Cooper heads to the NFL commissioner’s exempt list The first big domino to fall this afternoon was the news that edge rusher Jonathon Cooper would be placed on the NFL commissioner’s exempt list. Cooper’s arraignment for five different domestic violence related charges is tomorrow. As the legal process plays out, there is a strong likelihood he will end up being suspended at some point in time in the future. But for now? He won’t count against the Broncos’ 53-man roster and will be sidelined away from the team to start the season. This signifies third-year edge rusher Jonah Elliss and second-year edge rusher Que Robinson will be in line for extended reps early on in the season. While losing Cooper is a blow to the team’s pass rush, Elliss and Robinson have flashed with their ability to get after the quarterback. Dondrea Tillman will also be in the mix. For whatever it’s worth, I think four edge rushers is a tad light to start the season. There are still a few weeks until the season opener. Given that, perhaps this is an area they try to find another player, perhaps a waiver wire pickup or veteran. If not, they could always elevate someone from the practice squad if necessary. Broncos opt to carry three quarterbacks to start the season I don’t particularly see the need for the Broncos to carry three quarterbacks on the active roster. However, the Broncos’ brass obviously felt differently . Sam Ehlinger’s performance against the Vikings earned him a spot. Both Head Coach Sean Payton and Offensive Coordinator Davis Webb have given him high praise throughout the offseason. Quarterback is the NFL’s most valuable position for certain. Denver’s coaching staff and front office believes has untapped potential. Keep in mind, this is the last year of Jarrett Stidham’s deal. Therefore, Ehlinger being a top backup next season remains a strong possibility. Yesterday after the roster was finalized, General Manager George Paton discussed their reasoning for keeping three signal callers. “Sam is a big part of this quarterback room. We didn’t want to lose him, and we felt we were going to lose him. He’s too important to our team and just didn’t want to risk doing that. Obviously, the game he played the other night was outstanding. We love the room. We’re going to keep the room together,” stated Paton. Denver waives a trio of their 2026 NFL Draft class It’s not unusual for Day 3 picks to wind up being waived. Especially for teams like the Broncos who have a strong roster. That being said, I consider rookie tight end Justin Joly being waived as one of the biggest surprises. Adam Trautman, Evan Engram, and Nate Adkins are Denver’s top three. However, waiving a fifth-round selection at a position group that needed long-term help was an interesting development. It’s tough for tight ends to make the jump and acclimate to the pros. Nevertheless, I thought Joly’s upside as a potential heir to Engram at move tight end was worth carrying him on the roster. The coaches clearly valued Dallen Bentley’s future potential a bit more as an inline ‘Y’ tight end. Here is what Paton had to say on that decision. “Justin is a talented player. We knew it when we drafted him. We knew he was raw. We still like the player. He was coming on towards the end of training camp. Tight end position is a tough position for a rookie. He missed a lot of the offseason, just a little bit behind. We wish we had another game or two. We still like the player. We think he’s going to have a nice career. You just have to make tough decisions to build the best 53 you can make.” The waiving of Red Murdock was also something I didn’t envision. He earned a lot of praise from Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph over the past few months. Given his extended run in the preseason, I believed he would make the team. This move means the Broncos have confidence in Karene Reid and Jordan Turner. Those two who have a much better grasp of the playbook and more time in the system to be the ‘next man up’ if called upon. Last but not least, the team parted ways with seventh-round defensive back Miles Scott. That wasn’t too unexpected. Tycen Anderson, one of the only outside free agent signings, is the team’s fifth safety. We’ll see if the Broncos are able to get Joly, Murdock, or Scott back on their 16-man practice squad. If so? No worries on these moves. Jonah Coleman, Kage Casey, and Dallen Bentley were the three of Denver’s six Day 3 choices to make the roster. Coinciding with this, I’ll offer this up for discussion: Perhaps with extra selections in next year’s draft, the Broncos would be wise to consider packaging some of those late-round picks to move up and target highly ranked players on their board they believe can contribute Year 1. Other miscellaneous tidbits on the initial 53-man roster: The team keeping six wide receivers isn’t too out of pocket. Though it’s noteworthy that Troy Franklin nor Lil’Jordan Humphrey are special team contributors. Usually, your backend wide receivers offer that. Marvin Mims Jr. is the only contributor in the group who does. But I’d wager the coaching staff will occasionally utilize Humphrey in ways they do Evan Engram from time to time. I don’t doubt Tyler Badie’s ability as the team’s best pass blocking back. Like carrying three quarterbacks, I just don’t see the need to carry a fourth running back on the roster. It’s basically a tell for defenses the Broncos are going to pass the ball whenever Badie is on the field. I thought Matt Peart would have been a cut. But with Frank Crum heading to IR, the Broncos opted to keep a battle-tested veteran who has flexibility at tackle and guard. It’ll be curious what happens once Crum is available to return in Week 5 from IR. Mitchell Fabroni, the team’s long-snapper, didn’t make the final roster, but will be eligible to play as a practice squad call-up for the first three games. My question is what roster positions do they shed down from once his elevations are over and he has to be on the 53-man roster?

title: Acclimating to the 2026 Denver Broncos 53-man roster
summary: On Sunday, the axe came down on 27 preseason participants and left behind the 2026 Denver Broncos. As there seems to be every year, a few surprises stood out looking at the list. Here is what you need to know. In all the models and guesses about who would and who wouldn’t make the final […]
full_text: Dec 10, 2023; Inglewood, California, USA; Denver Broncos left safety Mitchell Fraboni (48) during pregame in a game against the Los Angeles Rams at SoFi Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Yannick Peterhans-USA TODAY Sports | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Con On Sunday, the axe came down on 27 preseason participants and left behind the 2026 Denver Broncos. As there seems to be every year, a few surprises stood out looking at the list. Here is what you need to know. Justin Joly was the No. 152 pick overall. I believe that makes him the highest pick waived by the Broncos at the roster deadline as a rookie since Maurice Clarett in 2005 (No. 101). — Andrew Mason (@MaseDenver) August 30, 2026 In all the models and guesses about who would and who wouldn’t make the final 53, there were none, at least that I’m aware of, that had Joly on the outside looking in. When you look back at Clarett and how little he participated in training camp and the preseason back in 2005, it’s telling just how poorly Joly performed. Against Atlanta he had 1 reception for 0 yards. Against Green Bay, he had 2 receptions for 10 yards. His breakout performance against Minnesota, 2 receptions for 96-yards and a touchdown wasn’t enough to overcome whatever it was that ultimately kept him off the team. There is clearly more to this story. The Broncos don’t just Clarett a third round pick unless it’s dutifully earned. It’s really weird to see all the roster chicanery regarding the practice squad, elevation on gamedays, and everything in between. What do I mean? As of right now, the Broncos don’t currently have a fullback or long snapper on the roster. It's the annual Fullback Games. As they have done in past, #Broncos are releasing fullback Adam Prentice source confirms with idea of elevating him from PSquad first 3 games and likely promoting him to 53-man roster by game 4. Don't have to guarantee his $1.215M salary this way… — MikeKlis9NEWS (@mikeklis9news) August 29, 2026 Broncos do not have a long snapper after releasing Mitchell Fraboni. George Paton said he'll sign to the practice squad. Added it provides roster flexibility. — Zac Stevens (@ZacStevens) August 30, 2026 Veteran tight end Lucas Krull is also caught up in this weird maneuver, but, like the others, is expected to join the practice squad in the coming hours. It’s got to be an added aggravation to have to go through this process if you’re the player. Jonathon Cooper wasn’t cut, nor is he on the Broncos 53. Due to two offseason instances of alleged profound stupidity, Cooper will be starting the season on the Commissioner’s Exempt List. There is no telling how long Cooper will be in NFL purgatory, but estimates project at least two games, but could potentially extend the entire season, especially if his legal defense stalls out in court. You should should also know, citizens of Broncos Country, that Bo Nix, Jaylen Waddle, Nik Bonitto, and all the marquee Broncos you’ve come to know and love this preseason (Sorry, Manjack and Murdock. It just wasn’t meant to be) will suit up in two weeks to face Kansas City to begin the effort to return to the AFC Championship game and beyond. It’s going to be an awesome season and it’s nearly here. Now, just who will join the Broncos practice squad? Make sure to check this page out throughout the day for practice squad rumors and signings.

He was picked up by then-New Orleans Saints head coach Sean Payton and remained with the team through 2023. He bounced around before rejoining Payton in Denver in 2024. […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MO - DECEMBER 25: Calvin Throckmorton #76 of the Denver Broncos runs out of the tunnel prior to an NFL football game against the Kansas City Chiefs at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium on December 25, 2025 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos have announced they released offensive lineman Calvin Throckmorton today. Throckmorton entered the league as an undrafted free agent after the 2020 NFL Draft. He was picked up by then-New Orleans Saints head coach Sean Payton and remained with the team through 2023. He bounced around before rejoining Payton in Denver in 2024. He’s been a versatile lineman and even filling in as center this preseason due to various injuries. We thought he could compete for a roster spot , but it would be unlikely: Calvin Throckmorton should be attempting to take over a role as the extra blocker, but that seems like it may be unlikely. However, securing an active roster spot seems more probable this year than it did the last. The addition of Kage Kasey in the draft likely spelled doom for Throckmorton’s 53-man roster hopes. We’ll see where the 30 year old offensive lineman ends up from here.

title: Grading the 2026 Detroit Lions initial 53-man roster
summary: It took some time, but the Detroit Lions eventually established their initial 53-man roster—and yes, they could count to 53 this year! Amid a flurry of unexpected roster moves, the Lions are now poised for their Week 1 tilt versus the New Orleans Saints on September 13. Detroit will have two weeks to ramp up […]
full_text: Detroit Lions quarterback Jared Goff (16) practices during training camp at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Monday August 17, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co It took some time, but the Detroit Lions eventually established their initial 53-man roster —and yes, they could count to 53 this year! Amid a flurry of unexpected roster moves, the Lions are now poised for their Week 1 tilt versus the New Orleans Saints on September 13. Detroit will have two weeks to ramp up their roster, make tweaks to the game plan, and try to put their best foot forward. There is plenty of hope but an equal amount of doubt. Is this the roster that can win the NFC North, the NFC, and the Super Bowl? Let’s grade the 53-man roster that Detroit has put together. Quarterbacks (2) Starter: Jared Goff Depth: Joshua Dobbs I do not think there will ever be a consensus on how good Goff is compared to his peers, but here in Detroit, we are fortunate to have him leading the offense. He won’t wow you with athleticism, but he is as steady as them come—you know what you are getting from Goff. He can air it out when needed or take what is given to him. With a rekindled offensive scheme, perhaps this is the year that he garners league-wide respect for his play. As for the backup spot, the Lions are rolling with just one quarterback. Luke Altmyer had a competitive preseason and impressed considering his undrafted status. However, once Dobbs got settled in, he quickly took control of the quarterback competition. He has the football IQ to be an asset in the film room, the experience to be a worthwhile substitute if called upon, and the athletic ability to do damage through the air or on the ground. Considering the Lions signed Dobbs just days before the first preseason game, I feel pretty satisfied with him as a backup. Grade: A Running backs (5) Starter: Jahmyr Gibbs Depth: Isiah Pacheco, Sione Vaki, Jacob Saylors, Jabari Small We all know who Gibbs is at this point: one of the most electric players in the NFL. The biggest question is surrounding his supporting cast. How large of a role will Gibbs fill in this offense, and when he needs time off, who will step in—and how well? Pacheco should be the top reserve behind Gibbs, but he has rarely been healthy in training camp. That leaves three unknowns to fill in. Vaki is unproven as a running back, and he is more so a special teams ace at this point in his career. Saylors was downright dominant in preseason, but his resume is miniscule—is he ready to take RB2 duties? As for Small, him making the 53-man roster was a shock to begin with, as he has gotten injured nearly every week. I think there is some upside with the depth, but as a whole, it is a step down from David Montgomery. Gibbs really elevates this group. Grade: B+ Wide receivers (4) Starters: Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams, Isaac TeSlaa Depth: Tay Martin The release of Greg Dortch is downright stunning. A player that seemingly had a lock on the WR4 role now hits free agency. That leaves the Lions with St. Brown and Williams, arguably the league’s best receiving duo, atop the depth chart. A lot is to be expected of Isaac TeSlaa going forward—not only is he the WR3 in a potent offense, he is the unchallenged WR3. TeSlaa has had a poor training camp and preseason, so the Lions are really betting on him rising to the occasion. As for Martin, he is somewhat of an unknown factor. He likely made this team for his special teams ability, but can he be relied upon to be WR4? While his stock skyrocketed in camp and preseason, he still only finished with six catches for 46 yards and a touchdown—this doesn’t scream instant contributor. I am fairly concerned about the receiver depth, and I would be surprised if it is not addressed in the near future. Yet much like at running back, the starters do a lot of the heavy lifting for this grade. Also… who will return punts? Grade: B- Tight ends (3) Starter: Sam LaPorta Depth: Brock Wright, Jackson Meeks The answer for who will be WR4 is likely in the tight end group. LaPorta will obviously be an important part going forward, likely third in the receiving pecking order. LaPorta has battled injuries but is still an elite player when healthy, contributing both as a receiver and a blocker. Expect him to see the field often. As for the depth, the Lions surprisingly released Tyler Conklin, leaving just Wright and Meeks on the roster. Wright is a steady reserve, but there was some hope that Conklin would have been an upgrade over him at TE2. Instead, the Lions opted to keep Meeks, the former wide receiver. Meeks has obvious upside as a receiving threat, but his inline ability is still a project. If he is active on game days, the Lions will likely try to use him in passing situations, but I am still skeptical of how well they can run 13 personnel with this trio. Re-signing Conklin to the practice squad would ease some of my worries, but it is nonetheless a group that I wish I had more faith in. Grade: B- Offensive linemen (9) Starters: Penei Sewell, Christian Mahogany, Tate Ratledge, Blake Miller, Juice Scruggs Depth: Larry Borom, Ben Bartch, Miles Frazier, Seth McLaughlin IR: Cade Mays NFI: Giovanni Manu This unit will obviously miss Mays during their first four games, but I am actually cautiously optimistic—normally a rarity when it comes to offensive line depth. Sewell is obviously an All-Pro talent, but I think Ratledge and Miller have a chance to shine over on the right side of the line. Scruggs slots in at center in the meantime, and while he is a below-average starter, that still makes him an above-average backup in the NFL—the Lions could do far worse than him. The biggest question mark is Mahogany, but I am still a believer in his potential. Is this the best offensive line depth that the Lions have had in a decade? Borom is a high-end swing tackle that could reasonably start on a few teams around the league. Bartch has battled injuries, but could also be a starting-caliber player when healthy. As for Frazier and McLaughlin, the Lions have themselves two high-upside reserves. We will see if McLaughlin sticks around when Mays comes back. Grade: A Defensive tackles (5) Starters: Alim McNeill, Tyleik Williams Depth: Levi Onwuzurike, Skyler Gill-Howard, Mekhi Wingo McNeill has looked dominant in camp, now over a year removed from his ACL tear. Tyleik Williams looks primed for a big Year 2 jump and has impressed in camp, but he is still classified as an unknown commodity. I am hopeful but cautious. If these two play to their ceilings, it could be a very formidable interior, both in terms of run defense and shrinking the pocket. As for the depth, there was some nervousness regarding Onwuzurike’s roster spot, but the former second rounder stayed aboard the 53. Perhaps most interestingly is that of their depth tackles, all of them are undersized with pass rushing prowess. Gill-Howard turned himself in a roster lock with an outstanding preseason. His play largely overshadowed Wingo given their similar skill sets, but the Lions still kept Wingo on the team as well. Ideally, it would be nice if Detroit had another nose tackle, but they do benefit from both McNeill and Williams being capable at that spot. Plus, Chris Smith is a likely candidate for the practice squad as insurance. Grade: B+ Edge defenders (6) Starters: Aidan Hutchinson, DJ Wonnum, Tyler Lacy Depth: Derrick Moore, Ahmed Hassanein, Eric O’Neill Pass rush was a problem for the Lions in 2025, and they have seemingly revamped the group in just one offseason. Hutchinson is among the league’s best and needs little discussion, but Wonnum should not be forgotten about. He has a chance to be an reliable rotation piece for the Lions. Sprinkle in Moore coming off the edge, and the Lions have some guys capable of crushing the pocket. Add in Lacy at big end, and they aren’t too bad at run defense either. The top four of this group were a given from the start of camp, with Hassanein…
author: John Whiticar

title: Key takeaways: Detroit Lions finalize initial 53-man roster
summary: Following the quick turnaround from the final preseason game, general manager Brad Holmes and head coach Dan Campbell have finalized the Detroit Lions’ initial 53-man roster. Below are my three key takeaways. Jahmyr Gibbs: Offensive Weapon The Lions surprisingly cut down to only 4 wide receivers while keeping five running backs on the initial roster. […]
full_text: Following the quick turnaround from the final preseason game, general manager Brad Holmes and head coach Dan Campbell have finalized the Detroit Lions’ initial 53-man roster. Below are my three key takeaways. Jahmyr Gibbs: Offensive Weapon The Lions surprisingly cut down to only 4 wide receivers while keeping five running backs on the initial roster. My biggest takeaway is that this may signal the Lions are finally cashing in on the Brad Holmes “Jahmyr Gibbs Offensive Weapon” promise. “We thought he was a multiphase, elite, explosive position-less weapon.” Of course, the practice squad has yet to form, and the staff could choose to have five wide receivers active on gamedays by way of elevation, but the unexpected release of gadget wide receiver Greg Dortch gives evidence to the idea that any non-Amon-Ra St. Brown slot snaps are already accounted for. No disrespect to Dortch or any of the other wide receivers competing for a roster spot this training camp, but the reality is that Gibbs presents a far greater matchup problem in the slot than anyone else. Offensive coordinator Drew Petzing explained , “Because the key is the matchups. When you have guys that can do a lot of different things, you can start to dictate things based on what the defense wants to do.” If true, the utilization of a position-less Gibbs could pay dividends with and without the football by dictating defensive personnel and matchups. All-in on a movement-centric defensive line I like the way you move. The Lions opted not to carry a single true nose tackle on the roster after waiving DT Chris Smith. The decision leaves the defense with a group of versatile, athletic pieces to use along the front. While surprising, t he breadcrumbs have been leading in this direction all offseason . The interior of the defensive line now consists of Alim McNeill, Tyleik Williams, Levi Onwuzurike, Skyler Gill-Howard, and Mekhi Wingo. All five linemen possess the versatility to play multiple roles, but more importantly, have the athleticism to execute movement games through stunts and stems. Defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard appears to have made this a focal point of his vision for the defense this season. The dynamic traits of the defensive line also help in the pass rush game through designed stunts. Most notably, Wingo was used in multiple unique ways this preseason. I like fun ways to generate pressure. pic.twitter.com/fAyPLJZ3b3 — Jeremy Reisman (@DetroitOnLion) August 30, 2026 Above, as Jeremy Reisman breaks down, Wingo (94) in the 4i- technique over the Indianapolis Colts’ right tackle stunts all the way across to pick the left guard, as the Lions’ opposite end Eric O’Neill loops inside to generate the pressure. Below, Wingo is asked to flash his rush, then drop into coverage. This holds the center’s attention enough to give Skyler Gill-Howard space for an inside rip through the left guard and to the quarterback for a sack. Sky LOCO 😤 pic.twitter.com/53huI3Foac — Detroit Lions (@Lions) August 29, 2026 The new style of defensive front has already shown some positive results this preseason. How Sheppard opts to utilize this skill set will be something to track over the course of the season. Passion plus perseverance pays off Dan Campbell put it best in his postgame presser in Indianapolis after the last preseason game: “It’s an exciting time and it’s also kind of a somber time.” For my final takeaway, I want to focus on the former and put a spotlight on this exciting time for two players in particular. Those guys are defensive end Ahmed Hassanein and tight end Jackson Meeks. Both Hassanein and Meeks are excellent examples of “grit” and why they are perfect for Dan Campbell’s Detroit Lions. First, Hassanein had a rough start to his rookie year after tearing his pectoral muscle, which led to an injury settlement after he was waived, with the expectation that he would sign to the practice squad once healthy. From that point forward, Hassanein appeared to be on a mission , ultimately leading to a transformative offseason where he dropped his body fat from 35 percent to 18 percent . Now, Hassanein is not only the first Egyptian-born athlete to be drafted in the NFL, but he’s the first Egyptian to make an active 53-man NFL roster. Jackson Meeks also deserves his moment. Meeks started his NFL career as an UDFA wide receiver in 2025. But while on the practice squad late in the 2025 season, the Lions started trying Meeks at tight end. From the 213 pounds he was listed at in his NFL draft profile, Meeks has transformed himself into a tight end weighing in at 235 pounds entering training camp. His growth this offseason and effort on special teams earned him a spot on the roster. Hassanein and Meeks are hardly the only players on this Lions team with passion and perseverance. In fact, the team is full of these stories, and that is no accident. Ultimately, the NFL is a game of attrition. A season of highs and lows. When a team is led not only by the likes of Penei Sewell and Amon-Ra St. Brown, but is bookended by Ahmed Hassanein and Jackson Meeks, its identity is one of extreme passion and perseverance. It’s a team that takes on the identity of this city. It’s a team this fan base can be proud of. Sound familiar?

title: Discussion: What was the Detroit Lions’ most surprising roster decision?
summary: The Detroit Lions have set their initial 53-man roster, and it has a fair number of surprises. From unexpected veterans getting cut to players beating the odds and making the team, the Lions made cut-down day entertaining as usual (albeit very delayed—please be quicker with your roster announcement next time!). There is no shortage of […]
full_text: The Detroit Lions have set their initial 53-man roster, and it has a fair number of surprises. From unexpected veterans getting cut to players beating the odds and making the team, the Lions made cut-down day entertaining as usual (albeit very delayed—please be quicker with your roster announcement next time!). There is no shortage of stunning moves that Detroit made , but which decision surprised you the most? Today’s Question of the Day is: What was the Detroit Lions’ most surprising roster decision? My answer: Keeping Jabari Small on the 53-man roster. I will credit Small for making an impact in camp, but that sadly never materialized in preseason. He missed the first preseason game with a knee injury. After just three carries, he suffered a concussion in the second preseason game. In the third and final preseason game, he was knocked out of the game on a kickoff return. It is an unfortunate circumstance for a player who was reportedly neck-and-neck with Jacob Saylors , but the writing was seemingly on the wall for Small. His staying on the roster tells me three things. Firstly, his injury is not severe enough to warrant a stint on the Injured Reserve—the Lions only used one of their two IR-to-return slots on cutdown day (Cade Mays). Second, the team clearly liked him a lot despite his preseason absences. As a shifty player who can contribute as a pass catcher and on special teams, it’s not hard to envision why the Lions would want to keep him around. Finally, you have to wonder about the status of Isiah Pacheco for Week 1 if the Lions are keeping five running backs on the initial roster. While I am still scratching my head about keeping Small over, say, Nick Whiteside, I am happy for Small and excited to see what he can bring to the offense. So, what Lions’ decision was the most surprising to you? Let us know in the comments.

title: Detroit Lions 53-man roster: 6 stunning choices
summary: The Detroit Lions dropped their initial 53-man roster for the 2026 season—see it here—and there were plenty of big surprises in their choices. Now, the Lions are likely to make some tweaks over the next 48 hours, so it’s important not to overreact until they truly settle on a Week 1 roster. But here are […]
full_text: ALLEN PARK, MICHIGAN - JULY 29: Jabari Small #26 of the Detroit Lions look on during Detroit Lions Training Camp at Detroit Lions Meijer Performance Center on July 29, 2026 in Allen Park, Michigan. (Photo by Nic Antaya/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Detroit Lions dropped their initial 53-man roster for the 2026 season—see it here—and there were plenty of big surprises in their choices. Now, the Lions are likely to make some tweaks over the next 48 hours, so it’s important not to overreact until they truly settle on a Week 1 roster. But here are 6 shocking decisions the Lions front office made with this initial roster. Five running backs A few weeks ago, Dan Campbell noted that the RB4 competition between Jacob Saylors and Jabari Small was neck-and-neck. However, since then, it’s been almost all Saylors. He finished the preseason with more scrimmage yards than any other player in the NFL, while Small failed to stay on the field. Small missed the first preseason game with an injury, left Game 2 with a concussion, and left Game 3 with another injury. Yet the Lions liked enough of what they saw in Small to give him a coveted roster spot. That is perhaps the most shocking decision of all. Four receivers and no punt returners? Not far behind was Detroit’s decision to only keep four receivers. While everyone had Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams, Isaac TeSlaa, and Tay Martin on their 53-man roster predictions, a fifth almost seemed necessary and certain. Greg Dortch is a trusted veteran who looked great as a punt returner all August and had experience with offensive coordinator Drew Petzing. When it was revealed that Dortch was being released, it was certainly Tom Kennedy who won the spot, right? Nope, he was released in the final cuts as well. So…. what is the Lions’ plan at punt returner? Just a few weeks ago, special teams coordinator Dave Fipp said the competition was between Dortch and Kennedy. So, either one (or both) is coming back to the practice squad (or 53-man roster), or some unknown player on the roster will step up. But in all honesty, I don’t have the faintest of clues who on the current roster could take over those duties. Meeks over Conklin Not many questioned whether Tyler Conklin’s spot on the roster was in jeopardy. He frequently repped ahead of Jackson Meeks, and looked just fine in his role as TE3 behind Sam LaPorta and Brock Wright. For as many two- and three-tight end formations the Lions are expected to use, having an experienced veteran like Conklin seemed like a no-brainer—especially after the struggles they went through last year when LaPorta and Wright went down with injuries. And while many of us had Meeks on the roster as TE4, trusting him as the team’s TE3 is a risky move for a player who is still learning the nuances of the position. That said, Meeks earned it on special teams, and that’s where his initial role will be. One final thing to keep in mind: as a vested veteran, Conklin’s salary would have been fully guaranteed if he was on the active roster in Week 1, and this could be their way of circumventing that rule. If they add him to the practice squad, they could elevate him in Week 1, then re-sign him to the active roster in Week 2. Lions go pass-rush over size EDGE Eric O’Neill: 6-foot-2, 250 EDGE Ahmed Hassanein: 6-foot-2, 275 DT Skyler Gill-Howard: 6-foot, 280 DT Mekhi Wingo: 6-foot, 282 These four players who made the 53 shined in the preseason predominantly because of their pass rush, while their abilities as run defenders are still a work in progress. Meanwhile, these players: EDGE Anthony Lucas: 6-foot-5, 265 DT Chris Smith: 6-foot-1, 310 DT Ben Stille: 6-foot-4, 296 None of them made it. This represents a pretty clear shift in the preferences of their defensive linemen, with a newfound lean into getting to the quarterback. That isn’t to say they don’t have size on the roster. Alim McNeill (6-foot-2, 310), Tyleik Williams (6-foot-3, 325), Levi Onwuzurike (6-foot-3, 304), and DJ Wonnum (6-foot-5, 262) are all big for their positions. But it appears they want some juice with their reserves. Jimmy Rolder avoids IR Maybe not the biggest shock, considering Rolder himself told the media that he believes he’s close to a return. But when the injury happened, it appeared the Lions’ fourth-round rookie was going to miss significant time. Instead, the Lions believe his development is important enough to stay on the roster and avoid a four-week absence on IR. Detroit had enough linebacker reserves that they would’ve been fine if Rolder went on IR, but they clearly believe in Rolder’s health and ability to make a difference early this season. No Nick Whiteside Through a few weeks of training camp, there was no better story than Nick Whiteside. He had worked his way up from the bottom of the depth chart to sharing some first-team defense reps at cornerback. He played a physical style of game that seemed like a great fit. And while he admittedly cooled down a bit toward the end of training camp, some of that was simply due to him having to cover the safety position that was plagued by injuries. I thought flashing that versatility would only strengthen his case for the 53-man roster. Instead, Detroit favored guys like Ennis Rakestraw, who has more potential, and Khalil Dorsey, who is one of the team’s best special teamers.

title: Lions to place Brian Branch, Kerby Joseph on reserve/PUP, both to miss 4 games
summary: As part of their roster cutdowns on Sunday, the Detroit Lions placed both starting safeties Kerby Joseph and Brian Branch on the reserve/Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) list per several reports. That means both players won’t count against the 53-man roster, but both are now ineligible to play in Detroit’s first four games of the […]
full_text: Detroit Lions safety Kerby Joseph (31), left, and safety Brian Branch (32) walk off the field after practice during mini camp at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Wednesday, June 17, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co As part of their roster cutdowns on Sunday, the Detroit Lions placed both starting safeties Kerby Joseph and Brian Branch on the reserve/Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) list per several reports. That means both players won’t count against the 53-man roster, but both are now ineligible to play in Detroit’s first four games of the season. Joseph is still dealing with a knee injury, suffered last year, that he has been unable to shake. The injury cost Joseph the final 11 games of last season, and he’s been looking for ways to manage it. We’ve seen him do some intense workouts at training camp, but for the past couple of weeks, he’s been away from the facility with a “personal issue.” Branch is still recovering from a torn Achilles suffered in the first week of December last year. He has been at the Lions facility this training camp, and coach Dan Campbell noted that it’s possible he returns to practice as soon as late August, but it appears he didn’t quite hit that milestone. That said, Campbell has remained optimistic about each player’s progress. “Both of those guys are doing well right now,” Campbell said on Thursday. The good news for both players is that if they are nearing a return to practice, a new NFL rule will allow both players to start practicing just two weeks into their stint on PUP. That could give either or both players enough ramp-up time to be ready to play in Week 5 against the Arizona Cardinals. That said, Detroit does have a Week 6 bye, so it’s possible Detroit holds both out until Week 7 against the Green Bay Packers. The first four games of the season they will definitely miss are: vs. Saints, at Bills, vs. Jets, and at Panthers. In their place, the Lions will likely rely on veterans Chuck Clark and Avonte Maddox to start at safety, with Thomas Harper and Christian Izien set to back up the position. That said, Maddox, Harper, and Izien are all currently dealing with injuries with unknown timelines, so it’s possible the Lions may try to add to the position before Week 1 begins in two weeks .

title: Detroit Lions make decision on backup QB job, waive Luke Altmyer
summary: The Detroit Lions officially have a winner for the backup quarterback job. According to Tom Pelissero, the Lions are waiving undrafted rookie quarterback Luke Altmyer, and veteran Josh Dobbs will back up Jared Goff this season. Mandatory Credit: Robert Goddin-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Detroit Lions officially have a winner for the backup quarterback job. According to Tom Pelissero, the Lions are waiving undrafted rookie quarterback Luke Altmyer, and veteran Josh Dobbs will back up Jared Goff this season. While Altmyer had an impressive training camp for an undrafted rookie, the writing for the backup job seemed on the wall after the final preseason game. Dobbs played a near-perfect game in two quarters of work, completing 15-of-19 passes for 128 yards and two touchdowns. Meanwhile, Altmyer turned the ball over twice and led just one scoring drive over the other two quarters against the Colts. title: Detroit Lions waiving CB Nick Whiteside
summary: In another move few saw coming, the Detroit Lions are reportedly waiving cornerback Nick Whiteside, per Nolan Bianchi Early in camp, Whiteside was one of the best cornerbacks on the field. He went from the bottom of the depth chart to earning some reps with the first-team defense, and he didn’t look out of place. […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - NOVEMBER 16: Nick Whiteside #38 of the Detroit Lions runs downfield during the second quarter against the Philadelphia Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field on November 16, 2025 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images In another move few saw coming, the Detroit Lions are reportedly waiving cornerback Nick Whiteside, per Nolan Bianchi Early in camp, Whiteside was one of the best cornerbacks on the field. He went from the bottom of the depth chart to earning some reps with the first-team defense, and he didn’t look out of place. However, some of that momentum slowed toward the end of training camp. In recent days, Whiteside had dropped back to safety to help out a very injured back end of the roster. However, that versatility wasn’t apparently enough to win him a spot on the initial 53-man roster. Whiteside failed to make Detroit’s 53-man roster last year, as well. But he ended up spending most of the year on the team’s practice squad before getting the call-up—and shining—in the team’s “Legion of Whom” win over the Tampa Buccaneers. It will be interesting to see how the Lions approach their cornerback room in the upcoming days. After cutting Terrion Arnold earlier this offseason, the depth of the room doesn’t look particularly strong, with D.J. Reed and Rock Ya-Sin holding down the starting positions. Behind them are 2024 second-round pick Ennis Rakestraw, veterans Roger McCreary and Khalil Dorsey, as well as rookie Keith Abney—amongst other late additions. Whiteside will hit the waiver wire, and if he clears, he could return to the practice squad. Check all of the latest roster moves with our 2026 Detroit Lions roster cuts tracker.

full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - AUGUST 29: Greg Dortch #8 of Detroit Lions runs with the ball while defended by Rob Carter Jr. #39 of the Indianapolis Colts at Lucas Oil Stadium on August 29, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) | Getty Images In the biggest surprise of early announced cuts, the Detroit Lions are apparently parting ways with veteran receiver Greg Dortch, per Tom Pelissero. For most of training camp and the preseason, Dortch was the presumed WR4 behind the starting three receivers. Because of his history alongside Lions offensive coordinator Drew Petzing and his strength as a kick and punt returner, most assumed his spot on the roster was safe. However, it’s worth noting he was often repping second in punt return order. Who was first? Veteran receiver Tom Kennedy. It’s not yet known whether Kennedy will make the team’s 53-man roster, but this is certainly a promising sign for his chances. The 30-year-old receiver is one of the most trusted players on the roster, capable of playing any of the receiver positions in Detroit. He was also the only one in competition for the punt returner job with Dortch, per special teams coordinator Dave Fipp. “You have the returner position with Kennedy and Dortch really at punt returner,” Fipp said. “(Dominic) Lovett fitting into that a little bit, but really probably Kennedy and Dortch right now in my opinion.” We’ll see if there’s any way the Lions opt to bring Dortch back—as he’s a veteran not subject to waivers. But as of now, this is the Lions’ most surprising cut. See all of Detroit’s roster cuts with our 2026 Lions 53-man roster tracker.

title: Who will be the Packers’ third quarterback?
summary: The Green Bay Packers don’t have a third quarterback, and that’s weird. Half of the NFL kept three players at the position (four of them kept four, if you can believe it) at the cutdown deadline, when rosters shrank from 91 to 53 on Sunday. So for the Packers to have only rostered two players […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - AUGUST 29: Miller Moss #16 of the Chicago Bears looks to pass during the second half of a pre-season game against the Tennessee Titans at Nissan Stadium on August 29, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Justin Ford/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Green Bay Packers don’t have a third quarterback, and that’s weird. Half of the NFL kept three players at the position (four of them kept four, if you can believe it) at the cutdown deadline, when rosters shrank from 91 to 53 on Sunday. So for the Packers to have only rostered two players at the position and have no internal option to even add to the practice squad sticks out like a sore thumb, but that’s the offset when the Miami Dolphins are willing to give you a draft pick for a guy you signed off the street in January . I’m sure a lot of you are thinking, “Wait, who am I going to see under center if Jordan Love or Tyrod Taylor ever go down, God forbid?” I don’t know the answer to that, but I’m going to throw a couple of options out for you today. Bring back Kyron Drones This is probably the least inspired of our options. The Packers signed Kyron Drones to a deal worth $5,000 guaranteed as an undrafted free agent this offseason, and he was beat out for the QB3 job (at least in the summer) by Kyle McCord (who, again, is now a Dolphin). Drones was outright waived by the team — with the Packers not even needing to fill his roster spot for several days — after a four-dropback performance against the Pittsburgh Steelers in the preseason opener. Drones was sacked on three of those plays, including a screen. It seemed like they were just over the experience. Sign a player who was just cut Alright, here’s where I did a lot of legwork. We’re going to have to use different fonts to mean different things, because I want you to be able to take one glance and understand the full landscape at the position. Players whose names are bolded were cut from teams that kept three or more quarterbacks. These are the players who are most likely to be available for the Packers, as these teams are less likely to need a practice squad arm for the scout team. Players who are italicized come from teams that have only two quarterbacks on the 53-man roster, but there were multiple quarterbacks cut on Sunday. These teams will likely try to re-sign one of them on the practice squad, but not both quarterbacks. Players who are not bolded or italicized come from teams that only kept two quarterbacks on the roster but only released one on Sunday, meaning they’re more likely to be retained by their original team’s practice squad as a camp arm. Given the option, quarterbacks in the #3 spot in the pecking order tend to return to their original club on the practice squad. Below is a full list of all of the quarterbacks cut league-wide (without an injury designation) on Sunday. ARZ: Kedon Slovis BAL: Austin Reed BUF Shane Buechele CAR: Kyle Trask CHI: Miller Moss CIN: Sean Clifford DET: Luke Altmyer HOU: Brett Rypien IND: Easton Stick JAX: Nick Mullens and Joey Aguilar LV: Jacob Clark LAC: DJ Uiagalelei MIA: Mark Gronowski and Cam Miller NO: Hunter Dekkers NYG: Brandon Allen and Jake Haener NYJ: Bailey Zappe and Brady Cook SF: Adrian Martinez TB: Jake Browning and Connor Bazelak TEN: Will Levis and Hendon Hooker WAS: Sam Hartman This draft cycle, I reported that scouting sources told me the Packers were interested in Kyron Drones, Haynes King and Mark Gronowski as potential pickups. Drones had his stint in Green Bay, while Gronowski ended up in Miami (where he took a pre-draft visit) and King actually made Carolina’s 53-man roster as a UDFA (good for him). For perspective, King signed for $210,000 guaranteed compared to Drones’ $5,000. Ultimately, King was just in a different market than Drones when they were both free agents post-draft. So Gronowski is a good start for a watch list, but Miami might retain him. If they do, though, that will likely free up Cam Miller, who was a sixth-round pick in the 2026 draft. Maybe he’s an option, too. Along with King, Jalon Daniels and Jack Strand were UDFA quarterbacks who received large guarantees this offseason and ended up making their team’s initial 53-man roster. A couple who were just cut, though, are Luke Altmyer, Joey Aguilar and Miller Moss. Altmyer, who the Packers had a pre-draft virtual meeting with, will likely be kept by the Detroit Lions, as they only have two quarterbacks on their roster. Aguilar could be available, as the Jacksonville Jaguars have two quarterbacks and released two today. Moss will almost certainly be available, as the Chicago Bears kept three quarterbacks on their 53-man roster. I’m not sure that Will Levis will pass through waivers unclaimed, but if he does, I think his addition would make a lot of sense for the Packers. It seems like both he and the Titans just want to move on, and that he won’t be brought back to Tennessee. If for whatever reason he does return to the Titans, though, that means that they (probably) won’t be bringing back Hendon Hooker, who was a pre-draft visitor with Green Bay before his selection at 68th overall in 2023 by the Detroit Lions. He’s another option that makes some sense. I have no idea how Kedon Slovis (outside of his game against the Packers on Friday) or Adrian Martinez played this preseason, but both of them played in “LaFleur-like” offensive systems, so maybe there would be less friction for them to hit the ground running than a typical outside signing to the practice squad. Those are just a couple of names that I think are realistic right now. A street signing The Packers worked out quarterback Seth Henigan, a UDFA from the class of 2025, this offseason. Green Bay didn’t do a lot of workouts since the start of camp, but they brought him in once, so that’s one possibility. Some veterans are out there, like Jimmy Garoppolo, but it seems highly unlikely that they’d be interested in a practice squad opportunity. I just wouldn’t hold my breath on experience at QB3 this year. Tyrod Taylor has taken care of us in that department. — There’s probably no great answer to QB3 right now, but which of these options do you like better? Let us know in the comments section. My opinion: I think they just grab a scout team arm for now, but if there’s ever a serious injury, I bet they go the veteran route and start looking at Garoppolo and co. on the 53-man roster. title: NFL Cutdowns: Former Packers pre-draft visitors released on Sunday
summary: I’ll keep this one short: The Green Bay Packers target their pre-draft visitors at a high clip, whether it’s the draft, as initial undrafted free agents or further down the line. For example, last cutdown cycle the team traded a pick for offensive linemen Darian Kinnard and picked up tight end Josh Whyle to the […]
full_text: CANTON, OHIO - AUGUST 06: Trevin Wallace #32 of the Carolina Panthers looks on during the first quarter of the 2026 Pro Football Hall of Fame Game against the Arizona Cardinals at Tom Benson Hall Of Fame Stadium on August 06, 2026 in Canton, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images I’ll keep this one short: The Green Bay Packers target their pre-draft visitors at a high clip, whether it’s the draft, as initial undrafted free agents or further down the line. For example, last cutdown cycle the team traded a pick for offensive linemen Darian Kinnard and picked up tight end Josh Whyle to the practice squad. Whyle eventually ended up winning a roster spot and made this year’s initial 53-man roster . So, who was just made available to the Packers? Good question. So far, these are the players who just hit the market and were brought to Green Bay during their draft cycle (since 2022, when the team started targeting more draft picks). Quarterback Hendon Hooker, Titans Sean Clifford, Bengals Can I interest anyone in Sean Clifford as a QB3 again? Running Back Velus Jones Jr., Seahawks Evan Hull, Cardinals Lew Nichols, Steelers Damon Bankston, Giants The one I’m most interested here is rookie Damon Bankston, who received eight times the guarantees to sign with the New York Giants than the Packers’ UDFA signing Jaden Nixon got this cycle . If Green Bay is pivoting to a more outside zone-based scheme, which has been the indication, I think Bankston fits really well. With that being said, he would probably be a practice squad signing immediately, not a 53-man roster guy. Receiver Anthony Smith, Cowboys Samori Toure, Eagles I don’t think the team wants to go down the Samori Toure path again, but rookie receiver Anthony Smith is interesting. Smith was taken two picks after Packers kicker Trey Smack. The seventh-round pick did not make it on the Dallas Cowboys’ roster. He ran a 4.45-second 40-yard dash at 6’2” and 197 pounds. The guy is a speedster. Tight End None Offensive Line Kiran Amegadjie, Bears Esa Pole, Chiefs Both Kiran Amegadjie and Esa Pole are players I could see the Packers adding to the bottom of their offensive line unit. Amegadjie was a third-round pick out of Yale for the Chicago Bears back in 2024, but he never caught on with the team. Esa Pola is a second-year former UDFA who was working with the first-team unit as the team’s left tackle in Kansas City at points this summer, but the Chiefs traded for Diego Pounds right before the cutdown deadline. Defensive Line Eric Johnson II, Falcons With seven interior defensive linemen on the 53-man roster, I’m not sure the Packers even need a practice squad defensive lineman right now. Edge Defender Sam Williams, Cowboys Sam Williams was arrested for felony sexual battery at Ole Miss, but the charges were later dropped. I know now this isn’t a great time to say this , but the Packers bring in a lot of prospects with “off-field” red flags for visits, and they generally do it to rule them out completely. I do not expect Williams to be on Green Bay’s short list. Off-Ball Linebacker Trevin Wallace, Panthers Here’s an interesting one: Trevin Wallace, the 2024 third-rounder who made 12 starts in 12 games played last year for the Carolina Panthers, was waived by the Panthers today. In total, he played 25 games (20 starts) for Carolina over two regular seasons. I could see the team taking a swing on him. Cornerback D’Arco Perkins-McAllister, Chiefs D’Arco Perkins-McAllister actually started his college career off as a fairly big recruit, but wound up bouncing around schools after two years at TCU. He ended up at New Mexico, UT-Chattanooga and Louisiana-Monroe after that. He was waived by the Kansas City Chiefs, and it’s not like the Packers’ third-team defensive backs played well in the preseason. Maybe they change things up. Safety Jammie Robinson, Falcons Chris Edmonds, Browns Safety is a position that will probably be more impacted on the practice squad level, if anything, than on the 53-man roster level, but two were made available today. Chris Edmonds has played almost exclusively as a special teamer when he’s been active in NFL games in his career, while Jammie Robinson, a former fifth-round pick, is looking to catch on with his sixth team in four years. He’s been available before, and the Packers haven’t added him, so I’m not sure the 25-year-old is going to be a priority for them now.

title: Packers trade for RB Kaleb Johnson at cutdown deadline
summary: The Green Bay Packers have added depth to their running back room on Sunday, as they’ve traded for former Pittsburgh Steelers running back Kaleb Johnson. Johnson, a 23-year-old, was a third-round pick for the Steelers coming out of Iowa last season. Johnson ended up buried on Pittsburgh’s dept chart, though, following the team’s signings of […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - DECEMBER 15: Kaleb Johnson #20 of the Pittsburgh Steelers runs prior to an NFL football game against the Miami Dolphins at Pennsylvania on December 15, 2025 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Green Bay Packers have added depth to their running back room on Sunday, as they’ve traded for former Pittsburgh Steelers running back Kaleb Johnson. Johnson, a 23-year-old, was a third-round pick for the Steelers coming out of Iowa last season. Johnson ended up buried on Pittsburgh’s dept chart, though, following the team’s signings of Rico Dowdle and Travis Homer behind starter Jaylen Warren. As a rookie, the former All-American carried the ball just 28 times for 69 yards (2.5 yards per attempt) in the regular season, good for the third-most attempts on the team behind Warren and Kenneth Gainwell. Funny enough, he was actually fourth on the Steelers in rushing yards last year, as tight end Jonnu Smith had nine carries for 70 yards and a touchdown. Smith, who previously played for head coach Matt LaFleur when LaFleur was an offensive coordinator for the Tennessee Titans, was signed by the Packers earlier this week . Johnson played 11 snaps of special teams in 10 games, with 8 of those snaps being kickoff returns on which he got his hands on the ball. It doesn’t seem like he has much of a background on teams other than as a kickoff returner, something that will probably go to receivers Skyy Moore and Savion Williams during the regular season. He had a long of 29 yards on his eight returns last year. The Packers have released running back Pierre Strong Jr., according to the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel ’s Tom Silverstein. It looks as though Green Bay will enter the regular season with four backs on its roster: Josh Jacobs, MarShawn Lloyd, Chris Brooks and Johnson. So far, there have been no reports on the compensation that the Steelers will receive for Johnson, be it a player or draft pick. Update: NFL insider Adam Caplan is now reporting that the expected compensation for the Johnson trade is a future sixth-round pick . Update #2: #Packers are giving a 2028 sixth-round pick to the #Steelers for running back Kaleb Johnson, according to a source. The pick is their own and not the one they obtained from Miami. — Tom Silverstein (@TomSilverstein) August 30, 2026 So, the Packers functionally traded QB Kyle McCord for RB Kaleb Johnson. — Update #3: It’s a 7th for Kaleb Johnson. Not a 6th. Even better! pic.twitter.com/iBp4Yat0Id — Andy Herman (@AndyHermanNFL) August 31, 2026 It is actually a seventh-round pick that was given up in the trade, not a sixth-round pick. This is interesting, since both the Packers and Steelers claimed it was a sixth-round pick, not a seventh-round pick. It’s possible this is an error on the league’s part.

summary: After much debate, the Green Bay Packers announced their first 53-man roster of the 2026 season after a day full of news. We’ll go position by position, showing you who made the team and the big information of the day. Quarterback Earlier today, the Packers traded third-string quarterback Kyle McCord to the Miami Dolphins for […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - AUGUST 28: Anthony Campbell #60 of the Green Bay Packers tries to block a pass from Kedon Slovis #12 of the Arizona Cardinals during the fourth quarter of a preseason game at Lambeau Field on August 28, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Geoff Stellfox/Getty Images) | Getty Images After much debate, the Green Bay Packers announced their first 53-man roster of the 2026 season after a day full of news. We’ll go position by position, showing you who made the team and the big information of the day. Quarterback Jordan Love Tyrod Taylor Earlier today, the Packers traded third-string quarterback Kyle McCord to the Miami Dolphins for their sixth-round pick in 2028 . Running Back MarShawn Lloyd Chris Brooks Kaleb Johnson Starting running back Josh Jacobs has been placed on the Commissioner Exempt list , which doesn’t count against the 53-man roster. Prior to that news, Kaleb Johnson was traded for by the Packers for Green Bay’s original sixth-round pick in 2028 . Reciever Christian Watson Matthew Golden Jayden Reed Bo Melton Skyy Moore J. Michael Sturdivant Receiver Savion Williams is dealing with an ankle injury and will start the season on the injured reserve, meaning that he’ll miss the next four weeks of action. Undrafted rookie J. Michael Sturdivant got the nod over Isaiah Neyor and Will Sheppard, who had also been working with the second-string offense this summer. Tight End Tucker Kraft Jonnu Smith Mark Redman Josh Whyle Coming into today, I don’t think anyone had the Packers carrying four tight ends into the season, since Luke Musgrave was still on the PUP list. That changed when Green Bay traded a seventh-round pick in 2028 to the Los Angeles Rams for Mark Redman , a blocking tight end who had a nice preseason. Musgrave remains on the PUP list. Offensive Line Zach Bako-Bewele Sean Rhyan Jordan Morgan Aaron Banks Jacob Monk Jager Burton Anthony Belton John Williams Donovan Jennings Travis Glover Travis Glover, the forgotten man in Green Bay, finally displaced Darian Kinnard, who was the Packers’ sixth offensive lineman at times during the 2025 season, with the second-team offense in the final preseason game. Before then, Glover had been working with the second-team unit all summer. No returning player fell down the depth chart more than Kinnard in 2026. Defensive Line Devonte Wyatt Karl Brooks Javon Hargrave Chris McClellan Warren Brinson Jonathan Ford Anthony Campbell Green Bay found the room to keep all seven interior defensive linemen on the 53-man roster, even though it’s highly likely that the team will have to make one a healthy scratch at the start of the regular season. With only 48 bodies available on gamedays, it’s very hard to justify all seven dressing down for game action — especially when Karl Brooks is really the only special teams contributor among the bunch. Jordon Riley remains on the PUP list. Edge Defender Lukas Van Ness Barryn Sorrell Brenton Cox Jr. Dani Dennis-Sutton Surprisingly, the Packers only kept four edge defenders at the position, as Collin Oliver was placed on the injured reserve with a return designation. The backups in this unit usually have to play a lot of special teams for Green Bay, but maybe carrying four tight ends will help the Packers with a similar body type. Brenton Cox Jr. has played very few special teams reps in the past (notably, edge defenders are usually the protection unit on punts), while Dani Dennis-Sutton is a rookie who has played all of one preseason game. Keep an eye out here. Yes, Micah Parsons is going to be out for the first four weeks of the year (at least) on the PUP list. Off-Ball Linebacker Zaire Franklin Edgerrin Cooper Isaiah McDuffie Ty’Ron Hopper Nick Niemann This is a copy-paste of last season, with Zaire Franklin replacing Quay Walker as the Mike linebacker. This is what we expected going into camp and coming out of it. Cornerback Keisean Nixon Carrington Valentine Brandon Cisse Benjamin St-Juste Kamal Hadden The Packers technically list Kamal Hadden as a cornerback, so we’re just going to have to roll with it. Hadden has recently been practicing with the safeties, as he’s really a slot defender, neither an outside cornerback or safety at the moment. In both of his preseason games, Hadden played exclusively in the slot for Green Bay. He made the roster by winning the backup job behind safety Javon Bullard following Jonathan Baldwin’s season-ending injury. Safety Xavier McKinney Evan Williams Javon Bullard Kitan Oladapo Like linebacker, this is basically the same unit as last season with one alteration. This time, Zayne Anderson isn’t on the team, as he signed a deal with the Miami Dolphins and his former defensive coordinator Jeff Hafley this offseason. Safety Trey Dean III was waived with an injury designation. If he passes through waivers, he will go back to Green Bay on the injured reserve. From there, the team can decide whether or not to give him an injury settlement or pay him out his entire 2026 roster to remain on the IR. Kicker Trey Smack IT’S UP. IT’S GOOD. He was the only kicker on the roster, and he was perfect in the preseason. Punter Daniel Whelan He was also the only punter on the roster. Long Snapper Matt Orzech Despite Cal Adomitis playing the long snapping position for all of Trey Smack’s perfect streak in live action, the Packers activated Matt Orzech, their returning starter, from the PUP list on Sunday.

title: Packers Roster Cut Tracker 2026
summary: Sunday, August 30th is a big day for the NFL this year. In 2026, the league has set the deadline for teams to cut their rosters down from 90 players to 53 for Sunday at 6:00 PM Eastern Time (5:00 Central), an odd time compared to recent deadlines. Recent years have seen the league require […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WI - AUGUST 02: Green Bay Packers head coach Matt LaFluer and General Manager Brian Gutekunst look on during the annual Green Bay Packers Family night practice at Lambeau Field on August 2nd, 2025 in Green Bay, WI. (Photo by Larry Radloff/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Sunday, August 30th is a big day for the NFL this year. In 2026, the league has set the deadline for teams to cut their rosters down from 90 players to 53 for Sunday at 6:00 PM Eastern Time (5:00 Central), an odd time compared to recent deadlines. Recent years have seen the league require cuts come in on the Tuesday following the final week of preseason games, giving front offices a few extra days. This year, however, the league’s decision to hold a game in Australia in week one led it to push the cutdown date a bit earlier. Green Bay Packers general manager Brian Gutekunst revealed that in a press conference earlier this week, noting that while not a fan of the shift, there’s not really anything he or the other 31 GMs around the league can do about it. That means that the Packers will have a little less than 48 hours from the completion of their final preseason game (around 10 PM Central on Friday night) to the cut-down deadline. Here at Acme Packing Company, we will be following along with all of the Packers’ moves to get from 90 to 53, which will include releases, players going on the reserve/PUP list, and more. The Reserve/Physically Unable to Perform list is one mechanism for teams to keep players on their roster in a reserve role if they failed a physical exam before training camp, went on the active/PUP list to start camp, and stayed there all summer long. Players who go on reserve/PUP to start the regular season do not count against the 53-man limit, but they may not be activated until after their team’s fourth regular season game, though they can start practicing after two games have passed. The Packers have four players still on the active/PUP who are eligible for the reserve/PUP to start the season: Luke Musgrave, Matt Orzech, Micah Parsons, and Jordon Riley. Parsons has generally been targeting the Packers’ Week 6 game against his old team, the Dallas Cowboys, for his return. Perhaps surprisingly, he is not seen as one of the favorites to win the NFL’s Comeback Player of the Year award; FanDuel sportsbook has his odds at just +3500 , good for 10th in the NFL. That slots in behind teammate Tucker Kraft (7th, +2700), while a host of quarterbacks like Patrick Mahomes, Kyler Murray, and Jayden Daniels lead the way. Stay tuned here for news on the Packers’ roster as it is revealed. Players to be waived RB Pierre Strong Jr . title: Packers Practice Squad Tracker 2026: Follow all the reports & signings
summary: A 53-man roster isn’t the only thing that NFL teams need to decide on this week. The league’s cutdown deadline from 90 to 53 will come and go on Sunday afternoon, and on Monday it will be time for teams to begin assembling the other major piece of their rosters: the practice squad. Over the […]
full_text: DETROIT, MI - NOVEMBER 27: Green Bay player's helmets sit on the turf during an NFL regular season Thanksgiving Day football game between the Green Bay Packers and the Detroit Lions on November 27, 2025 at Ford Field in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Scott W. Grau/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images A 53-man roster isn’t the only thing that NFL teams need to decide on this week. The league’s cutdown deadline from 90 to 53 will come and go on Sunday afternoon, and on Monday it will be time for teams to begin assembling the other major piece of their rosters: the practice squad. Over the last several years, this component of the roster has expanded greatly in significance. Not long ago, teams could carry a maximum of 8 players on the practice squad, but that number has gradually increased, now doubling to 16 (plus an additional 17th spot if a team signs a player with an international roster exemption). Furthermore, a player can be elevated from the practice squad to the active gameday roster a few times per year without a full promotion to the 53, making the unit a more functional squad of backups and injury replacements. As a result, the NFL has expanded the eligibility rules for practice squads over the years as well. Now, a team can sign players with any level of experience to the squad. At least ten of the 16 spots must be taken up by players with two or fewer years of accrued NFL experience, but that leaves up to six slots that can be filled by players of any experience level. Notably, teams cannot begin signing players to the practice squad until the league’s post-roster cut waivers are processed. That will take place at 12 Noon Eastern on Monday, when waiver claims will be awarded. After that, any players who clear waivers become free agents and are eligible to sign with any team, either to a full 53-man roster spot or to a practice squad. Still, there will be reports during cutdown day on Sunday of players whom the Packers would like to bring back for the practice squad if they do clear waivers. Here, APC will keep track those reports through Sunday, followed by the actual signings on Monday afternoon. The Green Bay Packers have used the practice squad heavily in recent years as rules have changed, often promoting players to the gameday roster to fill in for injured players or to contribute on special teams. As such, today is an important day for general manager Brian Gutekunst and his staff, who will surely be working hard to bring back several individuals whom the Packers waived as part of Sunday’s cutdown. Building out a deep squad can have a major impact on a team’s ability to withstand challenges over the course of the season, and the quality of players on that unit could be the difference between the Packers going over or under their projected win total of 9.5, which is the current number on FanDuel sportsbook . Keep it here throughout the next day or two as the squad fills out. Reported Practice Squad Targets The Packers are releasing the following players on Sunday, but the reports of their release has indicated that the Packers intend to or are interested in bringing them back for the practice squad if they clear waivers. OL Dylan Barrett OL Dalton Cooper DT Jaden Crumedy RB Jaden Nixon S Murvin Kenion III S Mark Perry S Jaylin Simpson LB Kristian Welch

title: Packers RB Josh Jacobs placed on the NFL’s commissioner exempt list
summary: ESPN’s Adam Schefter is reporting that Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs is being placed on the NFL’s commissioner exempt list, which means that he will not start on the team’s 53-man roster to open the season. At the time, there is no timeframe for a Jacobs suspension following the news earlier this week […]
full_text: ASHWAUBENON, WISCONSIN - JUNE 09: Josh Jacobs #8 of the Green Bay Packers participates in drills during the Green Bay Packers mandatory minicamp at Don Hutson Center on June 09, 2026 in Ashwaubenon, Wisconsin. (Photo by John Fisher/Getty Images) | Getty Images ESPN’s Adam Schefter is reporting that Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs is being placed on the NFL’s commissioner exempt list, which means that he will not start on the team’s 53-man roster to open the season. At the time, there is no timeframe for a Jacobs suspension following the news earlier this week that he was charged with battery and criminal damage to property after an incident that involved his girlfriend at his residence . After the preseason finale, head coach Matt LaFleur stated that he fully anticipated Jacobs to be on the roster, but was not willing to say one way or another if Jacobs was going to be on the field on Week 1. “I can’t really comment on that, because I don’t know,” were LaFleur’s final words about the subject. He was not asked whether or not the team or league has seen the alleged video that police received from the surveillance camera on the property, which the police report states shows “ the altercation .” The Packers did not speak to the media on either Saturday or Sunday, and they won’t on Monday, either. The first time that anyone in Green Bay’s organization will have a press conference following LaFleur’s post-game presser will be on Tuesday, when the media will be allowed to do a headcount during the stretching and individual periods of Packers practice. Earlier today, Green Bay traded for running back Kaleb Johnson from the Pittsburgh Steelers . The assumption is that the team will roll into the regular season with MarShawn Lloyd, Johnson and Chris Brooks at the position. Update: Jacobs’ representation dropped the following statement, via ESPN/NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport . “Josh Jacobs has been placed on the Commissioner’s Exempt List, which is an administrative procedure used by the NFL while a matter is being reviewed. It is not a final determination. Josh respects the NFL process, the Packers, and his Coaches and Teammates. He looks forward to his return to the team and the NFL.” Update #2: The most recent case of a player landing on the commissioner's exempt list was Jimmie Ward, who stayed on for 27 days (8/26-9/22) last year. In 2024, Michael Hall Jr. (35 days), Jabrill Peppers (47 days), and Tashaun Gipson (4 days, after a PED suspension) wound up on it. https://t.co/YQyCAnhpGO — Albert Breer (@AlbertBreer) August 30, 2026

title: Green Bay Packers officially win the Zaire Franklin-Colby Wooden trade
summary: Earlier this offseason, the Green Bay Packers traded defensive lineman Colby Wooden, who was going into the final year of his rookie contract, for then-Indianapolis Colts linebacker Zaire Franklin. Since joining the Packers, Franklin has been the team’s starting Mike after Quay Walker signed with the Las Vegas Raiders in free agency, received a new contract and was […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - NOVEMBER 10: Colby Wooden #96 of the Green Bay Packers takes the field prior to an NFL football game against the Philadelphia Eagles at Lambeau Field on November 10, 2025 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Earlier this offseason, the Green Bay Packers traded defensive lineman Colby Wooden, who was going into the final year of his rookie contract, for then-Indianapolis Colts linebacker Zaire Franklin. Since joining the Packers, Franklin has been the team’s starting Mike after Quay Walker signed with the Las Vegas Raiders in free agency, received a new contract and was even named a team captain in the team’s preseason opener. Apparently, though, the Colts’ end of the bargain hasn’t been going so well. On Sunday, ESPN/NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport announced that Indianapolis will be waiving Wooden , who started as Green Bay’s out-of-place nose tackle in 2025 — following Kenny Clark’s inclusion in the Micah Parsons trade. Wooden will have a new home, be it as a free agent or as a waiver claim. Considering the Packers’ depth at the position, it seems unlikely that he’d return to Green Bay on his one-year deal, unless the team thinks he’s a better 3-4 nose tackle prospect than Jonathan Ford, who has been the team’s “starter” in their base looks — which should make up about one-third of their defensive snaps this season. With that being said, I don’t think it’s a coincidence that the team’s move to a 3-4 defense came with the team moving on from their 2025 nose tackle, who was just 273 pounds coming out of college — though he’s visibly bulked up since 2024, even though his listed weight on rosters hasn’t changed. Wooden shortly after being traded from GB to Indy in March: "Last year I played out of position a little bit … For coach to come get me and told me that I'm going to be playing in a scheme that fits me better and I'll be doing something that I know how to do." https://t.co/KdvXmolp77 — Rob Demovsky (@RobDemovsky) August 30, 2026 Best of luck to Wooden, wherever he ends up. Not many players can say that they started off sub 280 pounds and were able to get NFL starts for a playoff team at nose tackle. He wasn’t always put in the best positions, but he didn’t flinch when asked to step up.

title: This isn’t how the Colts wanted Keenan Allen to make headlines
summary: What a debut. Keenan Allen’s name is circulating all around the Circle City, and he has only been in town for a week. Unfortunately, it has nothing to do with his performance in the Indianapolis Colts’ third preseason game. What should have been a forgettable weekend for Allen has turned into front page news. Early […]
full_text: WESTFIELD, IN - AUGUST 20: Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Keenan Allen (10) runs through a drill during the Indianapolis Colts and Atlanta Falcons joint training camp practice on August 20, 2026 at the Grand Park Sports Campus in Westfield, IN. (Photo by Zach Bolinger/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images What a debut. Keenan Allen’s name is circulating all around the Circle City, and he has only been in town for a week. Unfortunately, it has nothing to do with his performance in the Indianapolis Colts’ third preseason game. What should have been a forgettable weekend for Allen has turned into front page news. Early Sunday morning, Allen was arrested for allegedly operating a vehicle while intoxicated. This is a decision that is inadvisable for anyone, not just NFL players. Lives are at risk and serious injury or death could occur. On the lesser side of importance is the fact that a professional athlete finds themselves in any situation like this. It happens way too frequently. For people with millions of dollars, the prevailing question is always, why not call for a ride or have one lined up? For the personal reasons alone, it seems you wouldn’t want to do anything to jeopardize your career. Allen was brought in to be a veteran presence, on and off the field. This is not the example the Colts were hoping he would set out of the gate. Not only is it a terrible look, it could set his team at a disadvantage to start the year. Allen could be looking at a potential three-game suspension. He hurt his team and his reputation, and he could have potentially hurt someone. That is a rough first week on the job. It’s not the type of week most of us would be able to afford. Employment would be on the line in most cases. There’s a good chance this doesn’t affect his job security with the Colts. At the same time, Colts head caoch Shane Steichen isn’t afraid to send a message. Can he afford to though with his job on the line? This sets up an uncomfortable situation for the Colts heading into the season in just a few weeks. Not downplaying what could have been, but it is fortunate no one was seriously hurt. What could be hurt now is Keenan Allen’s image and his new team. No one knows what Allen has to offer the Colts, but they were banking on some production. That production may have to wait a little bit longer.
