title: Colts announce official initial 53-man active roster
summary: The Indianapolis Colts have officially announced their initial active 53-man roster, and here’s one of the first looks, as they trimmed down their group from 90 players at the league’s 6 PM EST deadline: OFFENSE DEFENSE Defensive Line: The Colts pair of ‘Day 3’ rookie edges: George Gumbs Jr. and Caden Curry both made the […]
full_text: WESTFIELD, INDIANA - AUGUST 19: A detailed view of a Indianapolis Colts helmet on the field during the joint practice with the Atlanta Falcons at Grand Park Sports Campus on August 19, 2026 in Westfield, Indiana. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Indianapolis Colts have officially announced their initial active 53-man roster, and here’s one of the first looks, as they trimmed down their group from 90 players at the league’s 6 PM EST deadline: our initial 53-man roster. pic.twitter.com/RIXIx4uhUj — Indianapolis Colts (@Colts) August 30, 2026 OFFENSE Quarterback: No surprises here, as the Colts will go with the quarterback trio of Daniel Jones, Anthony Richardson Sr., and Riley Leonard—presumably in that order, as backup Easton Stick was cut on Sunday. Running Back: Rookie Seth McGowan has ascended to the 2nd-string backup behind star workhorse Jonathan Taylor, but it looks like 2nd-year running back DJ Giddens held off Ulysses Bentley IV for the third running back spot, despite being largely limited throughout training camp with a hamstring injury and still needing some work in pass protection. He presumably got the edge for his rushing ability. Wide Receiver: Based on preseason playing time allocation, it seemed like the Colts wide receiver group of Alec Pierce, Keenan Allen, Josh Downs, Ashton Dulin, and Laquon Treadwell was pretty well set, but Indy elected to keep rookie 7th round Deion Burks on the roster, with Coleman Owen going to the injured reserve with a concussion suffered on Saturday. That means Nick Westbrook-Ikhine was the odd man out here, which he may have become a bit redundant with the late offseason addition of veteran Keenan Allen. Special teams returnman and wide receiver Anthony Gould also went to the cutting block. It’s worth noting that fellow wideout D.J. Montgomery was placed on injured reserve. Tight End: The Colts went with Tyler Warren, Drew Ogletree, and veteran Mo Alie-Cox, but backup Will Mallory (thumb) was placed on injured reserve with a designation to return, meaning he’ll still be with the Indianapolis organization but will miss at a minimum, the first four games of the 2026 regular season. Offfensive Line: The big news of the day came when the Colts acquired backup center Sedrick Van Pran-Granger from the Buffalo Bills, which meant Dalton Tucker would transition back to guard (presumably at the expense of Josh Sills) for the other backup interior offensive line job along with rookie Jalen Farmer. Backup offensive tackle Luke Tenuta was surprisingly not listed, but will serve as a backup offensive tackle for at least Week 1, when cornerback Cam Taylor-Britt serves his one game suspension. Also of note is that the Colts finally pulled the plug on 2023 4th round pick Blake Freeland, who despite being an impressive athlete, never had that translate onto the field to consistently be a very effective blocking offensive tackle. DEFENSE Defensive Line: The Colts pair of ‘Day 3’ rookie edges: George Gumbs Jr. and Caden Curry both made the active 53-man roster after impact preseason showings, which is an encouraging initial sign. Colts kept 2025 6th round pick Tim Smith which isn’t all that surprising given that Indy had to keep at least one natural backup interior defensive lineman, but what is, regards veteran Jerry Tillery, who didn’t perform all that well in preseason. The Colts cut Colby Wooden, who they acquired from the Green Bay Packers for Zaire Franklin. Linebacker: Rookies CJ Allen and Bryce Boettcher were locks to make it along with veteran Akeem Davis Gaither, as well as Jaylon Carlies and Austin Ajiake. Undrafted rookie Tahj Chambers out of Ole Miss earns the last linebacker spot among the group and should be an immediate special teams contributor. Cornerback: Not surprising, Sauce Gardner, Charvarius Ward, Justin Walley, and Cam Taylor-Britt all make the active roster—with Taylor-Britt having to serve a suspension in Week 1. Despite a rough preseason showing, backup cornerback Johnathan Edwards hangs on for his special teams work. Surprisingly, Jaylon Jones also is a holdover, as he played decently well in preseason, but the former starter doesn’t seem to be as natural a fit in Colts defensive coordinator Lou Anarumo’s defensive scheme. Safety: The Colts only roll four deep here with veteran starter Cam Bynum, projected rookie starter AJ Haulcy, and then a pair of backups: Hunter Wohler and Jonathan Owens. It means that one of the Colts free agent signings earlier this offseason, Juanyeh Thomas, didn’t crack the Colts initial active 53-man roster. Also worth noting that fellow safety Daniel Scott, who’s struggled staying healthy in Indianapolis, was among the recent cuts. The former 2023 5th round pick had spent the past three seasons in Indianapolis, and they had initial high hopes. SPECIAL TEAMS Kicker: Obviously, no surprises at punter regarding longtime special teams fixtures: contract extended punter Rigoberto Sanchez and long snapper Luke Rhodes, but it was reported earlier on Sunday that returning placekicker Spencer Shrader beat out fellow kicker Blake Grupe, after the former had a strong preseason showing, especially from long distance. Shrader had some initial rust in training camp, returning from 2025 season-ending knee tears, but proved to be the stronger performer when the lights came on during preseason.

title: Evaluating Anthony Richardson’s Preseason: What does AR’s future look like in Indy in 2026?
summary: Anthony Richardson’s tenure with the Colts has been nothing but mundane. A rollercoaster that produced some jaw dropping highs, but also some really embarrassing and painful lows. Year 3 was essentially a redshirt year for Anthony Richardson, a bit backwards in terms of standard development, but I do think it gave him a chance to […]
full_text: Anthony Richardson’s tenure with the Colts has been nothing but mundane. A rollercoaster that produced some jaw dropping highs, but also some really embarrassing and painful lows. Year 3 was essentially a redshirt year for Anthony Richardson, a bit backwards in terms of standard development, but I do think it gave him a chance to take a much needed step back– even if his year on the bench was interrupted by a freak eye injury. Anthony Richardson is often described as inconsistent. But if he’s consistent with anything, it’s how often his film looks so inconsistent. The 2026 film is yet another rollercoaster, and now we’re wondering if any team wants to hop on the ride. WHAT HAS IMPROVED? Anthony Richardson is certainly getting better at making layups look more like layups. That’s the most notable improvement that almost anyone who has watched him in his career could tell you. Anthony Richardson rolling out to the opposite side of his throwing arm and making an easy completion look very easy. pic.twitter.com/y4vXUzxPlq — Colts Film Room (@ColtsFilmRoom) August 30, 2026 I think particularly on speed outs he has a more relaxed throwing motion, in an effort to take a bit of gas off of some of his throws. It’s definitely helped him make shorter throws look a lot easier. Anthony Richardson Speed Out Week 3 2024 vs. PRE Week 2 2026 pic.twitter.com/ai1g3IOhfs — Colts Film Room (@ColtsFilmRoom) August 24, 2026 This is a side by side from AR throwing a speed out vs. a corner in off coverage. It’s a very easy throw obviously, but in 2026 these seem to be actually easy for Anthony Richardson. Anthony Richardson really does look more relaxed back there. The Colts haven't ran a ton of under center with AR (for good reason) but his drops this preseason have much more tempo to them instead of the twitchy, explosive and erratic drops early in his career. pic.twitter.com/81R55ODrRH — Colts Film Room (@ColtsFilmRoom) August 30, 2026 If you’re looking for a rep to hang onto and point to AR’s improvement, there is none better than this rep vs the Lions. Anthony Richardson recognizing Cover 0, changing the protection by bringing in a TE to block, signaling to the WR to get to a zero beater… And then mitigating a bad snap without panicking and throwing the flat route on time. Things that weren't happening in Year 1 or 2. pic.twitter.com/uROYZAiqWG — Colts Film Room (@ColtsFilmRoom) August 30, 2026 He recognizes Cover Zero, meaning the Lions will be blitzing one more guy than the Colts can block. So Anthony Richardson brings the Tight End in to block on this play. Now the Colts have 7 blockers to counter the 7 guys in the box that are going to bliz. If the Lions want to blitz the safety as the extra rusher that’s 12 yards from the line of scrimmage, then so be it. Next he signals to NWI and Anthony Gould to change the play to a Cover Zero beater. In Cover Zero, DBs will be inside leveraged because they have no safety help and want to funnel plays to the sideline. So the Colts run Anthony Gould on a flat route to beat the coverage. After ALL OF THAT, the snap is atrocious and throws the timing off of the play. But without panicking AR gets this ball out on time for a completion. High level QB play. I think his footwork is more calm (on certain plays). WHAT HAS NOT? Consistency and mental errors. A very nice release from Treadwell vs. Ennis Rakestraw Jr. Definitely a miscommunication on a route conversion vs. press. A shame because this should be a touchdown every single time pic.twitter.com/CF0cxnaOZh — Colts Film Room (@ColtsFilmRoom) August 30, 2026 This play stands out in particular to me. Versus press coverage, a lot of routes “convert”, because if a corner is in your hip pocket from the line of scrimmage, you can’t threaten their leverage or take advantage of space. I would bet vs. single high press, this route converts to a Go. You can see Treadwell dust the DB off the line and put his hand up. But Anthony Richardson throws this like he’s expecting the original route (guessing a comeback) to still be on. While I think Anthony Richardson has made some noticeable strides.. There's still a lot of the same problems that's plagued him since he's been in the league. Very poor ball placement that's caused by sloppy mechanics. pic.twitter.com/aKLFS0iLAb — Colts Film Room (@ColtsFilmRoom) August 30, 2026 I still think there needs to be way more consistency. The layups are starting to look like layups, but this is also a ball that needs to be completed. Everyone will have a miss every so often, but there are throws like these that leave you incredibly frustrated because the WR has no chance. Look at where Anthony Richardson is lined up vs. where he's trying to throw this ball. pic.twitter.com/UXC7Sq5F4J — Colts Film Room (@ColtsFilmRoom) August 30, 2026 Also, when you’ve put the ball on the ground a plethora of times in your career, you can’t afford to it in a glorified tryout for NFL teams. Unfortunately the fumble in New England is not going to help him put that narrative to bed. Excellent job by K.J. Britt to knock this out and a great recovery by Isaiah Iton Anthony Richardson HAS to hold onto that football smdh pic.twitter.com/DtqLBOrczQ — Ben Brown 🌻 (@BennyGIFs) August 14, 2026 BOTTOM LINE Full transparency, I’ve had this article written already, but have been holding out to see if the Colts would make a move prior to the 6 PM deadline. It appears he’s made the initial 53 man roster, likely as the QB2? I would be kind of shocked if Anthony Richardson is on the roster for the entire year and then just walks in free agency while the Colts get nothing in return. I’d also be shocked if Anthony Richardson doesn’t request his release at some point in the year. He’s a guy who’s desperate for a fresh start. All along it’s felt like the best thing for both sides was to orchestrate a trade. I am surprised it has not happened. If Anthony Richardson is the Colts QB2 this year, you could certainly do much worse. I also think he’s more of an option for a team who wants to develop him into someone who could compete for a job in the future, not someone like the Colts who need a reliable option that could win them a game today.

title: Colts have reportedly made a decision regarding offseason kicking competition
summary: According to NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo, the Indianapolis Colts are releasing kicker Blake Grupe, as returning kicker Spencer Shrader has won their kicking job after a strong preseason showing, especially from long distance: While Grupe, who kicked in relief of Shrader last season after his season-ending injury, was close to automatic in training camp, he […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - AUGUST 29: Rigoberto Sanchez #8 of the Indianapolis Colts celebrates with Spencer Shrader #3 after Shrader made a field goal against the Detroit Lions during the preseason game at Lucas Oil Stadium on August 29, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) | Getty Images According to NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo, the Indianapolis Colts are releasing kicker Blake Grupe, as returning kicker Spencer Shrader has won their kicking job after a strong preseason showing, especially from long distance: The #Colts are releasing K Blake Grupe. Spencer Shrader wins the job after hitting his second 60+ field goal of the preseason. Grupe had a 90% make rate in camp. A close battle, with Shrader just barely edging Grupe out. pic.twitter.com/HzaKbgKb30 — Mike Garafolo (@MikeGarafolo) August 30, 2026 While Grupe, who kicked in relief of Shrader last season after his season-ending injury, was close to automatic in training camp, he surprisingly struggled during the preseason. Specifically, Grupe missed a 61-yard attempt wide right against the Patriots in Preseason week 1, a 36-yard field goal attempt wide right against the Falcons (Week 2), and while he was a perfect 2 for 2 against the Lions (Week 3), his 46-yard attempt was only good after doinking off the upright and barely breaking the field goal cross bar. Meanwhile, Shrader really turned it on when the preseason lights came on, going 2 for 2 against the Patriots in Week 1 of preseason (including makes of 46 and 61 yards), versus the Falcons (featuring makes of 48 yards and 53 yards), and most recently, the Lions respectively (converted from 60 yards). Looking at both kickers in training camp even up close, Shrader comes in at 6,2”, 201 pounds compared to Blake Grupe’s 5,‘7”, 156 pounds, and while size clearly isn’t everything for a kicker, it appears as though he may have the bigger leg as of late, and it may have just taken him some additional time to come back from the season-ending tears of his ACL and MCL after showing some initial rust in training camp. One thing to note too that I would be curious about, and which was never revealed publicly but I’m sure the Colts were tracking is which kicker’s ball was traveling with the most velocity, RPMS, or whatever you want to call it. I would think you would want a kicker who drives the ball on his kicks, so it’s not susceptible to being as impacted by the weather elements—as the Colts only play half their games indoors. Having watched a lot of Colts football, there was a clear difference in say, Adam Vinatieri’s field goal kicks than Rodrigo Blankenship’s for instance, the latter’s whose kicked football tended to float and hang up in the air, but again, that’s just my opinion. At any rate, congratulations to Shrader for working his way back from a tough injury suffered early last season when he was having such a promising kicking campaign and showing perseverance to win the Colts’ placekicker job again.
author: Luke Schultheis

title: NFL waiver wire rules and order for Colts fans

full_text: WESTFIELD, INDIANA - AUGUST 04: The Indianapolis Colts helmets are seen on the field during the Indianapolis Colts Training Camp at Grand Park Sports Campus on August 04, 2026 in Westfield, Indiana. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images As NFL team’s trim their active rosters down to the final 53-man requirement, there will be a number of players that will be hitting the league’s waiver fire and thus, subject to potential claim (or even signing) by the Indianapolis Colts. Specifically, with the acquisition of backup center Sedrick Van Pran-Granger earlier Sunday morning, the Colts still project to be very active at offensive tackle, defensive tackle, and cornerback among other potential positions. The multi-step cutdown format from recent offseasons is no longer in effect, as NFL teams make their final wave of releases all at once after the preseason concludes. Waiver Wire Rules Under Four Accrued Seasons: Players with four or fewer accrued NFL seasons are placed on league waivers when released. Other teams can claim them in reverse order of the previous year’s NFL draft standings, which we have denoted below. Claims must be submitted by Monday at 1:00 p.m. ET. Vested Veterans: Players with four or more accrued seasons bypass waivers entirely and become immediate unrestricted free agents, and are available to sign with any interested league suitor, without further restriction. Here’s the NFL’s waive wire order headed into final 53-man roster cuts, where the Colts are exactly in the middle at 16th in league claim priority: Las Vegas Raiders New York Jets Arizona Cardinals Tennessee Titans New York Giants Cleveland Browns Washington Commanders New Orleans Saints Kansas City Chiefs Cincinnati Bengals Miami Dolphins Dallas Cowboys Atlanta Falcons Baltimore Ravens Tampa Bay Buccaneers Indianapolis Colts Detroit Lions Minnesota Vikings Carolina Panthers Green Bay Packers Pittsburgh Steelers Los Angeles Chargers Philadelphia Eagles Jacksonville Jaguars Chicago Bears Buffalo Bills San Francisco 49ers Houston Texans Los Angeles Rams Denver Broncos New England Patriots Seattle Seahawks

title: Colts announce trade with Bills for much needed backup center
summary: On Sunday morning, the Indianapolis Colts announced a trade with the Buffalo Bills, in which the Colts will send 2027 6th round pick and receive Bills backup center Sedrick Van Pran-Granger and a 2027 7th round pick: This is one, where at the very least, everyone reasonably expected Indianapolis to be very active on the […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - JANUARY 4: Sedrick van Pran-Granger #62 of the Buffalo Bills waits to snap the ball against the New York Jets at Highmark Stadium on January 4, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Timothy T Ludwig/Getty Images) | Getty Images On Sunday morning, the Indianapolis Colts announced a trade with the Buffalo Bills, in which the Colts will send 2027 6th round pick and receive Bills backup center Sedrick Van Pran-Granger and a 2027 7th round pick: 🚨TRADE🚨 we have acquired C Sedrick Van Pran-Granger and a 2027 seventh-round draft pick from the @BuffaloBills . — Indianapolis Colts (@Colts) August 30, 2026 This is one, where at the very least, everyone reasonably expected Indianapolis to be very active on the league waiver wire regarding final cuts, looking for a competent 2nd-string center behind starter Tanor Bortolini. With Van Pran-Granger likely on the roster bubble with the Bills, the Colts jumped the waive wire order and were able to land a young player, who they believe can be a decent backup center, at a very minimal cost of draft capital for next year. The need for a backup center only heightened after yesterday, when in Saturday’s preseason finale, Colts transitioning 2nd-string center Dalton Tucker struggled snapping out of shotgun, with several errant snaps. Tucker would figure to transition solely back to backup offensive guard after this latest center acquisition. Regarding Van Pran-Granger, the former 2024 5th round pick of the Bills stands at 6,’4”, 315 pounds, and was a former First-Team All-SEC and 2x CFP National Champion with the Georgia Bulldogs. Over the past two seasons for Buffalo, he’s appeared in 31 career games, making 2 starts. While he didn’t receive enough snaps to qualify, with just 97 total offensive snaps, per PFF, he received a +58.6 overall grade last season, but that was highlighted +85.1 pass blocking grade. It’s hard to disagree with this pickup, given how dire the backup center situation was for the Colts previously and the relative low cost of draft capital surrendered for Van Pran-Granger, who’s very much still a young center with some developmental upside coming out of their 2nd unit.

[Doug Engle/Florida Times-Union] | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co With roster cuts beginning for the Jacksonville Jaguars and every other NFL team, practice squad invitations will be sent out shortly. Here’s a brief primer from our friends at Field Gulls . Keep track of who the Jags add to their practice squad below! Practice squad formation rules Teams can begin forming their practice squads after the waiver period expires at 1 p.m. ET on Monday, August 31. The NFL will send a subsequent Personnel Notice confirming the results of the waiver process, and teams can begin signing practice squad players after receiving that notice. A player claimed off waivers cannot go directly to a practice squad. A successful waiver claim means that player goes onto the claiming team’s 53-man roster. The player must first clear waivers before becoming eligible to sign with a practice squad. A standard practice squad consists of 16 players. Teams can have a 17th player if that player qualifies for and is designated under the NFL’s International Player Pathway Program (Jacksonville may keep OL Kilian Zierer in this spot). Players who are not subject to waivers can immediately sign with another team or join a practice squad. Players with four or more accrued seasons are unrestricted free agents when released and are not subject to waivers. Players with three or fewer accrued seasons are subject to the waiver process. title: Chiefs practice squad and waiver wire tracker
summary: The Kansas City Chiefs have determined the initial 53-man roster. Now, the next step is building out a 16-man practice squad. At noon Arrowhead Time on Monday, players unclaimed on the waiver wire will be available to sign to NFL practice squads. Most players who will fill the practice squad will have previously been waived […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA - FEBRUARY 09: The helmet of Trey Smith #65 of the Kansas City Chiefs seen in the locker room prior to Super Bowl LIX against the Philadelphia Eagles at Caesars Superdome on February 09, 2025, in New Orleans, Louisiana. The Eagles defeated the Chiefs 40-22. (Kara Durrette/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs have determined the initial 53-man roster. Now, the next step is building out a 16-man practice squad. At noon Arrowhead Time on Monday, players unclaimed on the waiver wire will be available to sign to NFL practice squads. Most players who will fill the practice squad will have previously been waived from the Chiefs’ 90-man roster. Up to six of the 16 players each team can carry on its practice squad may have any amount of league experience. So it’s possible the Chiefs could sign some practice-squad players from the pool of veteran players just released by other teams — who will not have to go through waivers — before Monday’s deadline. The Chiefs are eighth in the waiver order, so the front office has an opportunity to claim a player and bring them onto the 53-man roster at the expense of a player who initially made it. The Chiefs have relied on practice-squad call-ups throughout their era of three Super Bowl titles. This year, Kansas City is tied for the fifth-lowest odds (+1700) to win Super Bowl LXI among all NFL teams, according to FanDuel Sportsbook . Chiefs practice squad news & rumors The Chiefs hope to bring left tackle Esa Pole back to the practice squad, but there is outside interest, according to Sam McDowell of The Kansas City Star . There is a possibility that undrafted rookie wide receiver Jacob De Jesus lands on the practice squad should he clear waivers, per Pete Sweeney of The Kansas City Star .

title: Chiefs Preseason Week 3 snap count analysis: Marcus Harris earned roster spot
summary: Welcome back to Arrowhead Pride’s weekly snap-count analysis! During the preseason, we will shorten the analysis, as it is difficult to make definitive statements based on the raw snap-count data. Still, let’s see what we can figure out about the Kansas City Chiefs when taking a closer look at playing time during the 9-9 tie […]
full_text: ST. JOSEPH, MO - JULY 29: Peter Woods #99 and Marcus Harris #68 walk to the field during the Kansas City Chiefs training camp on Aug 11, 2026 at Missouri Western State University in St. Joseph, MO. (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Welcome back to Arrowhead Pride’s weekly snap-count analysis! During the preseason, we will shorten the analysis, as it is difficult to make definitive statements based on the raw snap-count data. Still, let’s see what we can figure out about the Kansas City Chiefs when taking a closer look at playing time during the 9-9 tie against the Seattle Seahawks last Friday. Starters (offensive): LT Jaylon Moore, LG Kingsley Suamataia, C Creed Humphrey, RG Trey Smith, RT Kahlil Benson, QB Garrett Nussmeier, WR Rashee Rice, WR Xavier Worthy, RB Kenneth Walker, TE Travis Kelce and TE Noah Gray Starters (defensive): DE George Karlaftis, DT Chris Jones, DT Khyiris Tonga, DE Felix Anudike-Uzomah, LB Nick Bolton, LB Jeffrey Bassa, LB Cooper McDonald, S Christian Roland-Wallace, CB Nohl Williams, CB Mansoor Delane, S Jaden Hicks Did not play: QB Patrick Mahomes, QB Justin Fields, QB Chris Oladokun (Concussion), RB Kenneth Walker, WR Jimmy Holiday, LT Josh Simmons (Back), S Chamarri Conner, LB Drue Tranquill (Back spasms), LB Jack Cochrane (Knee), DE Ashton Gillotte (Hamstring), S Alohi Gilman (Low-back spasms), WR Jeff Caldwell (Hyperextended knee), DE Tyreke Smith (Hamstring), G C.J. Hanson, OL Joshua Ezeudu, DE Niles King, DT Omarr Norman-Lott (PUP) The big takeaway Before he made the 53-man roster on Sunday, second-year defensive tackle Marcus Harris was the team’s leader in defensive snaps (42) against Seattle, and he made a big impact in his time on the field. Harris finished the game as the leading tackler, including multiple stops towards the end of the game that preserved the tie. Harris was putting on a strong performance during training camp and the preseason prior to Friday’s finale, but he put the cherry on top of his ascension to the roster against the Seahawks. As things stand right now, he will be the team’s fourth defensive tackle through at least the first four weeks of the season. The Offensive takeaway Over 13 pass-play snaps against Seattle, rookie wideout Cyrus Allen aligned in the slot 100% of the time, according to Pro Football Focus. He caught just one of the two passes thrown to him, but the usage of Allen in the slot is a continuation of a trend from his time at the University of Cincinnati. In 2025, Allen was in the slot for over 90% of the pass plays in the Bearcats’ offense. In camp, Allen has shown a more well-rounded skill set, but in his rookie year, the offense may focus on using the preseason standout where he is most comfortable and experienced while he develops long-term. The Defensive takeaway Veteran cornerback L’Jarius Sneed took the field on the first possession of the game with the starting defense, manning the slot in the team’s Nickel defense. Over six snaps played, Sneed was in the slot for five of them. For most of the preseason, safety Christian Roland-Wallace has aligned as the Nickel defender with the first-team unit. He shifted to a traditional safety role for the preseason finale with injuries to starting safeties Alohi Gilman (Low-back spasms) and Chamarri Conner. It remains to be seen whether Sneed or Roland-Wallace will be the first-team Nickel defender when everyone is healthy, hopefully by Week 1, but it’s clear that the coaching staff trusts Sneed to play multiple roles in the defense; in camp, he was mostly playing outside cornerback while rookie Mansoor Delane was recovering from the shoulder injury. Editor’s Note : Arrowhead Pride will present charts with updated snap-count data in this weekly post during the regular season.

title: Chiefs News: It’s time to form the practice squad
summary: The latest On Sunday, the Kansas City Chiefs revealed the initial 53-man roster, subject to change by the time Week 1 arrives. On Monday, after Noon Arrowhead time, waived players who were unclaimed will become eligible to sign to the practice squad. The Chiefs have 16 spots to fill. Andrew Armstrong and 8 more roster […]
full_text: Kansas City Chiefs general manager Brett Veach, left, and head coach Andy Reid speak while observing players during practice at Chiefs training camp on July 17, 2024, in St. Joseph, Missouri. (Emily Curiel/The Kansas City Star/Tribune News Service via Getty Images) The latest On Sunday, the Kansas City Chiefs revealed the initial 53-man roster, subject to change by the time Week 1 arrives. On Monday, after Noon Arrowhead time, waived players who were unclaimed will become eligible to sign to the practice squad. The Chiefs have 16 spots to fill. Andrew Armstrong and 8 more roster cuts the Kansas City Chiefs should bring back on the practice squad for 2026 | A to Z Sports WR Andrew Armstrong The good news about the Chiefs’ release of Armstrong is that it’s rare for wide receivers to be claimed during 53-man roster cuts. It’s disappointing because it felt like he really earned a roster spot through his play on the field. He led the team in the preseason with 7 receptions for 85 yards. His blocking was about as impressive as it gets. Plus, he’s just a different style and body type than anything else on the roster. Chiefs roster cuts: Five notable players who did not make the team | KMBC 9 Emari Demercado, RB: Demercado is the odd man out in a suddenly crowded running back room. He signed a one-year deal during the offseason, but rookie running back Emmett Johnson and second-year running back Brashard Smith were able to beat him out for roster spots. The Chiefs also kept Remigio, who is mainly used as a returner, closing perhaps another door for Demercado to make the team. Chiefs cut offensive lineman who started four games for them last season | The Kansas City Star Pole played with the second unit during training camp, and actually received snaps with the first team as recently as this summer during organized team activities. The release came Sunday. But the shaky ground came a day earlier. The Chiefs traded a 2028 conditional sixth-round pick to the Ravens for tackle Diego Pounds, a 23-year-old undrafted free agent. His addition left Pole as the odd man out. The Chiefs cut Pole out of training camp a year ago as an undrafted free agent — but they later added him back to their roster. He started the final four games of the season. Three shocking omissions from the Chiefs final 53-man roster announcement | FanSided Kader Kohou I largely expected Kohou not to make the team over the past few weeks. The coaches didn’t seem too interested in putting him in the preseason games until very late, and when in, Kohou failed to separate himself. His role was meant to be the starting slot corner when the Chiefs signed him. But this summer has brought multiple names up in the conversation for the same role. Kohou, who is still recovering from a torn ACL last season, never realized the opportunity in front of him and sadly may have left his most meaningful football behind. Projecting Chiefs Depth Chart After Initial 53-Man Roster Revealed With Several Surprises | Heavy Sports The Chiefs also placed wide receiver Jimmy Holiday on injured reserve and defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott on the physically unable to perform list. Changes can still come through waiver claims and additional moves, something general manager Brett Veach made clear before the deadline when he described Kansas City’s roster as not yet a “finished product.” For now, however, the initial 53 provides enough information to project how Andy Reid’s depth chart could look. Around the NFL Aaron Donald back: Three-time Defensive Player of the Year returning to Rams for 2026 season | CBS Sports “If the wife wasn’t happy it wasn’t gonna get done,” Donald said after signing. “My wife was on board and she was with me 100%.” The comeback is now firmly in motion with Donald set to join forces with Garrett in a defensive front that, on paper, is as formidable as any in recent years. Sean McVay wouldn’t commit to Donald playing in Week 1. Packers RB Josh Jacobs placed on commissioner exempt list | ESPN The move comes three days after Jacobs was formally charged with two misdemeanors stemming from an alleged incident with a woman in May. It means Jacobs will not be on the Packers’ 53-man roster and cannot practice or attend games. He will be paid and, with the team’s permission, is allowed to be at the facility for meetings, individual workouts, medical treatments and other non-football activities. Broncos’ Jonathon Cooper placed on NFL commissioner exempt list after June arrests | The Athletic Cooper will be paid his full salary while on the exempt list, but he can’t play in games or practice with the team. He will be allowed to attend meetings and receive treatment at the team facility. Commissioner Roger Goodell has sole discretion to place a player on the list or remove them from it. The exemption is typically used for players who have pending legal cases and/or are still under investigation by the league. The duration of time players spend on the exempt list has ranged from a few days to an entire season, and there’s no indication yet as to how long Cooper could remain on the list. He could still be subject to a suspension by the NFL. In case you missed it on Arrowhead Pride Chiefs’ Omarr Norman-Lott to begin 2026 season on PUP list Harris has arguably earned the spot regardless of Norman-Lott’s health. He finished the preseason with a standout performance against the Seattle Seahawks, stifling multiple handoffs in the backfield and forcing a lengthy field-goal attempt that was ultimately missed. Once Norman-Lott is healthy, it will be interesting to see how the rotation adjusts to welcome him back. For now, Harris looks to compete for snaps with rookie Peter Woods behind defensive tackles Chris Jones and Khyiris Tonga. summary: As we await the Kansas City Chiefs‘ final 53-man roster for the 2026 season, or even the initial 53-man roster as of the cutdown deadline at 5:00 p.m. on Sunday, reports have leaked out about who the front office and coaching staff plan to keep. ESPN’s Nate Taylor reported that second-year defensive tackle Marcus Harris […]
full_text: ST. JOSEPH, MO - JULY 29: Omarr Norman-Lott #55 walks to the field during the Kansas City Chiefs training camp on Aug 11, 2026 at Missouri Western State University in St. Joseph, MO. (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images As we await the Kansas City Chiefs ‘ final 53-man roster for the 2026 season, or even the initial 53-man roster as of the cutdown deadline at 5:00 p.m. on Sunday, reports have leaked out about who the front office and coaching staff plan to keep. Marcus Harris has made the Chiefs’ initial 53-man roster, per source. Harris, who entered the NFL as a 7th-round pick with the Texans in the 2024, had plenty of strong moments in the preseason. Omarr Norman-Lott will start the season on the PUP list, missing the first 4 games. — Nate Taylor (@ByNateTaylor) August 30, 2026 ESPN’s Nate Taylor reported that second-year defensive tackle Marcus Harris will be one of the players going to bed happy on Sunday evening. He will make the team’s initial 53-man roster , but Taylor’s report is tagged with confirmation of second-year defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott’s (Knee) injury status. Norman-Lott will begin the season on the Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) list, meaning he will miss at least the first four games of the season. The second-round pick from last year’s draft is still recovering from tearing his ACL during the Week 7 game against the Las Vegas Raiders last season. Harris has arguably earned the spot regardless of Norman-Lott’s health. He finished the preseason with a standout performance against the Seattle Seahawks , stifling multiple handoffs in the backfield and forcing a lengthy field-goal attempt that was ultimately missed. Once Norman-Lott is healthy, it will be interesting to see how the rotation adjusts to welcome him back. For now, Harris looks to compete for snaps with rookie Peter Woods behind defensive tackles Chris Jones and Khyiris Tonga.

title: Chiefs Analysis: What to make of the two trades for offensive linemen
summary: The NFL season kicks off in two weeks, and the Kansas City Chiefs wrapped up the preseason on Friday night. Final moves to trim rosters from 90 players down to 53 are due at 5:00 p.m. Arrowhead time on Sunday, August 30th. Late last week, the Chiefs traded for offensive lineman Joshua Ezeudu from the […]
full_text: Munich, Germany - November 10: Joshua Ezeudu of New York Giants looks on during the NFL Munich Game 2024 between New York Giants and Carolina Panthers at Allianz Arena on November 10, 2024 in Munich, Germany. (Photo by Mario Hommes/DeFodi Images via Getty Images) | DeFodi Images via Getty Images The NFL season kicks off in two weeks, and the Kansas City Chiefs wrapped up the preseason on Friday night. Final moves to trim rosters from 90 players down to 53 are due at 5:00 p.m. Arrowhead time on Sunday, August 30th. Late last week, the Chiefs traded for offensive lineman Joshua Ezeudu from the New York Giants in exchange for a 2028 7th-round pick. Ezeudu was present on the sideline Friday night in Kansas City, but did not dress. Saturday afternoon, the Chiefs struck another deal to acquire offensive tackle Diego Pounds from the Baltimore Ravens in exchange for a 2028 conditional sixth-round pick. Both moves come at an interesting time: the Chiefs have been looking to bulk up the depth of their offensive line, and Josh Simmons is seeking additional opinions on a back injury that has sidelined him in camp for close to two weeks. Multiple factors may be at play in these trades, but let’s take a look at Ezeudu and Pounds to figure out what they can bring to Kansas City. Joshua Ezeudu A former top-100 selection, Ezeudu has started ten games through his career at guard and tackle. Josh Ezeudu LT Quick out of his stance into his drive and catch; meets the edge at the bend point on the arc and washes him past the QB. Good pass set path and good quickness to get there. pic.twitter.com/axAyHFEqJE — Caleb James (@CJScoobs) August 26, 2026 During the preseason, Ezeudu played the first week fully at tackle, but in the second week he slid inside to guard, which may be a more natural fit for him. Good help snap from Ezeudu at RG. Helps the C secure the NT, and then, when the edge tries to swim inside, he closes the door and delivers contact. pic.twitter.com/WlVsX8UfvW — Caleb James (@CJScoobs) August 30, 2026 At 6 feet 4 inches tall and 310 pounds, he is a bit undersized as a traditional guard, but his quickness off the snap and leverage help him to win by beating defenders before they can get a chance to get going. At tackle, he struggled to anchor when edge rushers would line up wide and go from speed to power. At guard, he can use quick sets to take away the defenders’ build-up, and this plays much better to his strengths. Ezeudu with a physical set here. Delivers some force with his inside hand, drives his feet, and moves the 3-tech out of the pocket, and puts him on the ground. pic.twitter.com/qnVYpGirBs — Caleb James (@CJScoobs) August 30, 2026 Although he did not live up to his draft status in New York, the Chiefs needed a player with live NFL experience at both tackle and guard. Diego Pounds An undrafted free agent, Pounds was a natural fit for Baltimore out of Ole Miss. At 6 feet 6 inches tall and 330 pounds, with solid athletic ability , he had the frame to develop into a road-grading run blocker and had the size and strength to excel as a jump setter in the passing game that Baltimore has historically used in their scheme. Pounds gains depth and width with his first step. He aims well to reach the edge, and his hands and feet meet at the same time. Good fundamental blocking to help set up the zone run. pic.twitter.com/qgPlbQa5zn — Caleb James (@CJScoobs) August 30, 2026 Despite his physical gifts, he was listed as a third stringer on the Ravens depth chart for most of camp and the preseason. Pounds was solid in the preseason, but stuck in a deep unit, which would have made him a bubble candidate to make the Ravens’ roster. While his game needs work overall, he has natural mechanics in pass protection and a bulldog mentality that were bound to ensure that he would find an active roster spot- whether it was with Baltimore or not. Pounds has a good drive off his inside foot to get into his pass pro set. Could stay more vertical initially, but he does a good job of using the outside hand to stab the edge rusher, then locks on and mirrors to end the play. pic.twitter.com/5Uwfm89inY — Caleb James (@CJScoobs) August 30, 2026 It appears that the Chiefs were watching from afar, and, as they have many times in the past, the team is betting on a large man who can move in space. Linemen who can move in space and land big blocks have tended to work out in KC. Pounds gets in space on the pin and pull and lays down a DB. The pin man didn't do a good job on 53. pic.twitter.com/WNfWf9NFk2 — Caleb James (@CJScoobs) August 30, 2026 Pounds has traits that cannot be taught, and his overall game is further along than many undrafted players at the same position. Why make the moves? Listed as day-to-day, starting left tackle Josh Simmons’ current status is unclear, as he missed the second half of the preseason with a back injury. Speculation has swirled about the extent of his injury, and now the big question is whether the Chiefs made these moves expecting him to miss more time than they initially thought. There is no clear answer, but in short: yes, and no. If Simmons has to miss significant time, the Chiefs are in trouble. Adding as much depth as possible to prepare for the worst-case scenario could be in the cards, but it could also be an attempt to add overall depth to the roster. A week ago, the trio of Jaylon Moore, Kahlil Benson, and Esa Pole struggled greatly against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers ‘ edge rushers. While they rebounded this week, the struggles against starting-caliber players for Tampa could have raised concerns. It could also say something about the Chiefs’ depth on the interior offensive line. The Chiefs have lacked quality interior depth since Nick Allegretti departed for free agency after the 2023 season, and Mike Caliendo has filled in with mixed results over the past few seasons. The team has tried to let Hunter Nourzad take the reins, but it has not worked out. Benson took first-team snaps at right guard when Trey Smith missed time earlier in the preseason, and undrafted rookie Pete Nygra has also filled in with the second team. Ezeudu will inject an immediate dose of interior experience and can slide to tackle as needed. Pounds only played left tackle at Ole Miss, and has only played tackle so far in the NFL, but with his frame and strength, he could be a prime candidate for the Chiefs to eventually work into guard. The bottom line The Chiefs brass has clearly not been satisfied with the quality of depth on the offensive line, and the front office has now made moves to ensure the offense has enough bodies to either prepare to be without their left tackle for some time or solidify the swing tackle and interior offensive line spots. The room has suddenly gotten much more crowded with the roster cutdown deadline drawing near. This has likely dashed some players’ hopes of making the roster and placed some players who might have been “safe” on the bubble. Ezeudu and Pounds will need to be brought up to speed quickly, but it seems they will both be a part of the plans for 2026.

title: Chiefs final cutdown tracker: Reports and rumors ahead of Sunday’s deadline
summary: By 5:00 p.m. (Arrowhead Time) on Sunday, the Kansas City Chiefs must reduce their 90-man active roster by 38 players in order to get it down to the in-season limit of 53 players. The team will eventually release a complete list of all of its moves — but until then, news about some of them […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - AUGUST 15: General Manager Brett Veach of the Kansas City Chiefs watches from the sidelines prior to the preseason game between the Los Angeles Rams and the Kansas City Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium on August 15, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images) | Getty Images By 5:00 p.m. (Arrowhead Time) on Sunday, the Kansas City Chiefs must reduce their 90-man active roster by 38 players in order to get it down to the in-season limit of 53 players. T he team will eventually release a complete list of all of its moves — but until then, news about some of them will trickle out. Here, we’ll track all the roster moves Kansas City is reported to have made. With each new report, we’re also updating our Chiefs roster page , so you can easily see how many players are left in each position group. We’re awaiting the 53-man roster that will attempt to bring the Chiefs back to the postseason. Currently, Kansas City has (-176) odds to make the playoffs, according to FanDuel Sportsbook . Reported Chiefs roster moves Sunday, August 30 The Chiefs have officially released their list of roster moves to meet the mandatory 53 player limit. Defensive tackle Damon Payne was waived, according to The Kansas City Star ’s Sam McDowell . Defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott to be placed on the Reserve/Physically-Unable-to-Perform (PUP) list, according to ESPN ’s Nate Taylor . Defensive tackle Marcus Harris has made the Chiefs’ initial 53-man roster, according to ESPN ’s Nate Taylor . Tight end Mason Pline was waived, according to The Kansas City Star ’s Sam McDowell . Linebacker Kam Arnold was waived, according to Chiefs Digest ’s Matt Derrick . Offensive tackle Esa Pole was waived, according to The Kansas City Star ’s Sam McDowell . Defensive end Emmanuel Ogbah was released, according to ESPN ’s Adam Schefter . Wide receiver Jacob De Jesus was waived, according to The Kanas City Star ’s Pete Sweeney . Defensive end Ethan Hurkett was waived, according to The Kansas City Star ’s Pete Sweeney . Center Pete Nygra was waived, according to NFL insider Jordan Schultz . Tight end Jake Briningstool has made the Chiefs’ initial 53-man roster, according to ESPN ’s Nate Taylor . Cornerback D’Arco Perkins-McCalister was waived, according to Houston reporter Aaron Wilson . Tight end Tre Watson was waived, according to ESPN ’s Adam Schefter . Cornerback Kaiir Elam was released, according to NFL insider Jordan Schultz . Wide receiver Xavier Loyd (a Blue Springs native) was waived, according to The Atheltic ’s Jesse Newell . Saturday, August 29 Cornerback Zelmar Vedder was waived, according to Houston reporter Aaron Wilson . The Chiefs struck a deal with the Baltimore Ravens to acquire rookie left tackle Diego Pounds . Linebacker Wesley Bissainthe was waived, according to ESPN’s Adam Schefter . How roster changes are made When players with fewer than four accrued seasons are cut, they have been waived . (Players acquire an accrued season when they are on a team’s active roster, its Reserve/Injured list, or its Reserve/PUP list for at least six games in a given season). When players with at least four accrued seasons are cut, they have been released . They immediately become free agents. Waived players may be claimed by another team, which then assumes the balance of their contract. The team that had the most recent draft’s first pick has precedence over waiver claims from all other teams. The team with the most recent draft’s 32nd pick has precedence over waiver claims from no other teams — and so on. If a waived player isn’t claimed by noon on Monday, they become free agents. Players can also be waived with an injury designation — commonly referred to as waived/injured . If these players go unclaimed, they automatically revert to the team’s Reserve/Injured list. This has already happened with prior cuts of tackle Matt Waletzko and wide receiver Jeff Caldwell. That is one of three Reserve lists that do not count against the 53-man limit. The other two are the Reserve/PUP (physically-unable-to-perform) and Reserve/NFI (non-football-injury) lists. Players on the latter two lists at the final cutdown must miss at least four regular-season games before being activated to the roster, which occurs when they pass a physical. Defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott — who missed all of training camp recovering from a torn ACL from 2025 — is the only player eligible for the Reserve/PUP list. The salaries for players on a team’s Reserve/PUP and Reserve/Injured lists count against the salary cap. Outside of first- and second-round picks, most players without veteran status can see their base salary cut in half while on reserve lists at the discretion of the team. Salaries for players on Reserve/NFI are not paid (unless a contract provision specifies otherwise). Players placed on Reserve/Injured in the offseason (up through the final cutdown day) must miss the whole season. If a player is placed on Reserve/Injured after the final cutdown day, they may be designated for return after they have missed at least four games. But on final cutdown day, a team may declare up to two players being placed on its Reserve/Injured list as being eligible to be treated as if they are placed on Reserve/Injured after the final cutdown. Teams may make only eight designations for return during a given season — a limit that is extended to 10 if the team appears in the postseason. If a team labels a player as eligible for return at the final cutdown, it counts against this limit — even if the player is never actually designated for return. Players designated for return from Reserve/Injured are eligible to practice with the team for up to 21 days. At any time during that period, they may be activated to the roster. If they are not, they must remain on the Reserve list for the remainder of the season. Finally… players may be removed from the roster by being traded to another team. Just like with a waiver claim, the player’s new team assumes their existing contract, which counts against their cap. But any money that has already been paid to the traded (or waived) player (such as signing and workout bonuses) must be carried against the original team’s cap. Roster change s ummary Current roster size: 53 Released: LB Cole Christiansen, CB Kaiir Elam, CB Kader Kohou, DE Emmanuel Ogbah Waived: DE Vincent Anthony, LB Kam Arnold, WR Andrew Armstrong, LB Wesley Bissainthe, DT Cole Brevard, WR Jason Brownlee, WR Jacob De Jesus, RB Emari Demercado, OT Ethan Driskell, WR Omari Evans, OT Chukwuebuka Godrick, DE Ethan Hurkett, LB Cam Jones, DE Niles King, WR Xavier Loyd, S Tanner McCalister, DT Amari McNeil, C Pete Nygra, RB Jadyn Ott, DT Damon Payne, CB D’Arco Perkins-McCalister, TE Mason Pline, OT Esa Pole, S De Shon Singleton, CB Melvin Smith, DE Tyreke Smith, G Josh Thompson, CB Zelmar Vedder, TE Tre Watson, WR Jeff Weimer Waived/injured: G CJ Hanson, QB Chris Oladokun, RB EJ Smith Traded: None Free agents signed: None Acquired through trade: OT Diego Pounds Placed on Reserve/Injured: WR Jimmy Holiday Placed on Reserve/NFI: None Placed on Reserve/PUP: DT Omarr Norman-Lott

title: Los Angeles Chargers 53-man roster: Analyzing the initial team, including 2 UDFAs who made it
summary: The Chargers announced their initial 53-man roster around 6:00 p.m. Sunday evening. It came with several notable surprises, including having only two specialists and 11 total offensive linemen. Below is a complete breakdown of the roster along with some analysis on each room. Quarterback (2): Justin Herbert, Trey Lance Even as someone who believes D.J. […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CA - AUGUST 27: Jacob Spomer #60 of the Los Angeles Chargers on the sidelines during an NFL preseason game between the Los Angeles Rams and the Los Angeles Chargers on August 27, 2026, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Greg Fiore/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Chargers announced their initial 53-man roster around 6:00 p.m. Sunday evening. It came with several notable surprises, including having only two specialists and 11 total offensive linemen. Below is a complete breakdown of the roster along with some analysis on each room. Quarterback (2): Justin Herbert, Trey Lance Even as someone who believes D.J. Uiagalelei outplayed Lance during the preseason by a decent margin, the Chargers were always going to keep Lance as their backup due to his larger pool of experience in the NFL, on top of his familiarity with the Shanahan-influenced offense that Mike McDaniel wants to run (even if he’s not the best at executing it himself). Uiagalelei is expected to return on the team’s practice squad for another year, but the Chargers would be wise to still look elsewhere for an upgrade at backup behind Herbert. Former 49ers quarterback Nick Mullens was released and he has even more experience in running this style of offense than Lance during the former’s time with the 49ers. Running back (3): Omarion Hampton, Keaton Mitchell, Kimani Vidal Both Amar Johnson and Greg DesRosiers Jr. performed well enough to make the final roster, but positional needs elsewhere forced the Chargers to keep this group nice and tight. Hampton will rightfully lead the team in carries while Mitchell’s speed and complementary skillset gets rotated in given the situation. Vidal rushed for over 100 yards three times in 2025 and had another game with 95. His skillset fits well enough as a north-south runner who can eek out extra yards through contact. It also helps that he showed the ability to be a lead rusher behind that abomination of a 2025 offensive line. Fullback (1): Alec Ingold No surprises here. The Chargers got the perfect fullback for Mike McDaniels’ offense and I’m actually thoroughly excited to see Ingold in action this season. He’ll be pivotal in unlocking Hampton into one of the league’s best ball-carriers. Wide Receivers (6): Ladd McConkey, Quentin Johnston, Tre’ Harris, Brenen Thompson, Derius Davis, KeAndre Lambert-Smith The Chargers chose to keep KeAndre Lambert-Smith after another sollid preseason where he showed good rapport with the Chargers’ backup quarterbacks. KLS is a NFL wide receiver and you could do far worse for the team’s WR5. Davis makes the team as the presumed return man. He was used on an end-around against the Rams that went for a big gain so there may be a chance he gets back into the offense thanks to McDaniel. However, there’s still so many mouths to feed in this offense and rookie Brenen Thompson — who has comparable speed — is a much better overall wideout than Davis. The biggest question here is how the top three will shake out in terms of usage. I think the safe bet is McConkey will be “the guy” but Harris has looked phenomenal this summer while also being the best run blocker at receiver. He’ll potentially lead the whole position in snaps played if McDaniel is truly a believer in “no block, no rock.” Tight End (3): Charlie Kolar, David Njoku, Oronde Gadsden II Kolar caught two passes this preseason while playing amongst the starters who overall got single-digit snaps together as a group. That’s good efficiency for a guy labeled as the “blocking tight end” when they first signed him. He’s a sneaky pick to lead this group is receptions, even with Gadsden and Njoku in the same room. Both Gadsden and Njoku also have to become more consistent as run blockers, as well. Neither player looked comfortable blocking on the move this preseason and they were directly related to why their only drive against the Niners was a three-and-out. Offensive Line (11): Rashawn Slater, Joe Alt, Jake Slaughter, Cole Strange, Kayode Awosika, Trey Pipkins, Jacob Spomer, Travis Burke, Logan Taylor, Alex Harkey, Trevor Penning The Chargers held on to several players here that I do no agree with, but the placement of Branson Taylor on IR designated to return left them an extra spot. But they kept three (3) names here I did not expect them to hold onto. We all know what Penning is. It was not a successful move when they traded for him at the deadline last season. Harkey and Taylor both did not standout in the preseason, but Taylor at least spent most of the time at tackle which is the position we did not expect him to play in the NFL. He was the one of the three I expected to be kept, if any of them. Plenty of players they cut would have been preferred over either of Penning or Harkey. I don’t get it. Interior Defenders (5): Teair Tart, Dalvin Tomlinson, Jamaree Caldwell, Justin Eboigbe, Nick Barrett After a standout preseason, the Chargers chose to get some worth out of TeRah Edwards whom they did not expect to be kept on the final 53. He was sent to the Panthers for a sixth-round pick in 2028. This group is otherwise as expected. You have the starters, the veteran free-agent signing, and the rookie. Good depth and a solid group overal. Edge Rushers (4): Khalil Mack, Tuli Tuipulotu, Bud Dupree, Akheem Mesidor After neither Nadame Tucker and Kyle Kennard impressed enough to force their way here, the Chargers are moving ahead with their best four. No frills here. Just a strong group with high expectations, especially for their first-rounder in Mesidor. Linebackers (5): Denzel Perryman, Daiyan Henley, Troy Dye, Marlowe Wax, Del’Shawn Phillips Marlowe Wax was phenomenal in August and that stamped his ticket to the active roster. Phillips obviously makes the team after a Second-Team All-Pro honor as a special-teamer. This group is nothing flashy, but it’s solid and has been what the defense has needed to be a top-five unit each of the past two seasons. Cornerbacks (5): Donte Jackson, Tarheeb Still, Cam Hart, Deane Leondard, Rodney Shelley With a ton of competition past the top four cornerbacks, Shelley was the guy who came out on top to make the roster as CB5. Avery Smith, whom many thought was a roster lock, was shipped to the Seahawks for a 2027 sixth-round pick. I truly hope the Chargers don’t regret that decision. He seemed like a potential future starter when Jackson’s time with the team was done. Safeties (6): Derwin James, Elijah Molden, Tony Jefferson, R.J. Mickens, Genesis Smith, Kendall Williamson Williamson was always going to be kept due to his contriutions on special teams. That made it tough for the Chargers not to keep six players at safety. Since James has been the teams primary nickel defender, it made it more palatable to keep five cornerbacks. Mickens remains a special teams contrubutor, as well, and Smith was one of their fourth-round picks. They round out a solid group with “Unc” (Jefferson) who had a hilarious cut day going from out to making the roster in the few hours before the deadline. Special Teams (2): Cameron Dicker, Josh Harris The Chargers released punter JK Scott and for five minutes there was a massive moment of rejoice within fan base. However, that was short-lived until NFL insiders began reporting that the intent of the Chargers was to bring him back, similarly to when they started the 2025 season with only two specialist before signing a long snapper. I don’t see what the teams sees anymore with Scott. He’s wildly inconsistent and those inconsistencies tend to show their head in some of the worst moments possible. It’s HARD to shank a punt 20 yards when trying your best. It’s also hard to follow that with a 33-yard punt in the same game. That’s horrendous for a high school or college punter, nonetheless a professional who has been in the league for almost a decade. The Chargers need to find competition now, not after the season.

title: Sean McVay sits starters, Rams win preseason
summary: Sean McVay isn’t the first head coach to sit every starter and important reserve during the preseason, but the L.A. Rams may have perfected the practice. While every key player sat during the preseason, as has been the case since McVay’s second year on the job in 2018, the Rams were still praised for the […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 27: Ty Simpson #15 of the Los Angeles Rams looks on during the first half of a preseason game against the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium on August 27, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images) | Getty Images Sean McVay isn’t the first head coach to sit every starter and important reserve during the preseason, but the L.A. Rams may have perfected the practice. While every key player sat during the preseason, as has been the case since McVay’s second year on the job in 2018, the Rams were still praised for the performances of their two quarterbacks and added Aaron Donald . The Rams have even so far avoided suspension news for Puka Nacua and A.J. Jackson . They’re not out of the woods, but Nacua did return to practice on Sunday after missing a couple of weeks from a joint practice injury against the Cowboys. Although McVay sat over 40 players during the preseason because they were destined to make the final roster, rookie Ty Simpson was praised by the media for his efficient stat line and a high-level touchdown throw in the preseason finale. Compare that to Fernando Mendoza, the Raiders first overall pick who in all likelihood would have been named the Las Vegas starter if he had produced as well as Simpson . TRENDING: Ty Simpson’s BEST PASSES from his first preseason in the NFL. 47/60 (78%), 382 passing yards, 3 TD’s, 0 INT’s, 19 FD’s, 109.9 passer rating 😳🎯 pic.twitter.com/lcUZveANt9 — Rookie Watch (@RookieWatxh) August 28, 2026 It doesn’t matter if one quarterback has a better preseason than another quarterback. It just does not matter . But don’t tell that to Klint Kubiak and Mendoza. They would love to trade Mendoza’s first three games for Simpson’s right now. With a supporting cast that featured almost no players who made the final roster , save for C.J. Daniels, Max Klare, and a couple backup offensive linemen, plus not always having his plays called by McVay, Simpson avoided the rookie yips and the cries of “bust!” that typically come with first appearances. Of course, the Rams didn’t lose in the preseason either (also doesn’t matter) and didn’t turn it over or get sacked. The L.A. Rams succeeded in the preseason, avoided major injuries, got to see their first-round pick have a good first month of game action, kept Matthew Stafford upright, and are even happy with Stetson Bennett. On top of everything else, a future Hall of Famer was willing to reset his eligibility for the Hall of Fame by coming out of retirement. Zachary Pereles of CBS Sports cites the Rams as the biggest winners of the preseason : What more is there to say? After the Rams added one of the best defensive players of all time ( Myles Garrett ) and two cornerbacks ( Trent McDuffie , Jaylen Watson ) to address their biggest need, Aaron Donald officially un-retired on a one-year deal. Donald is now 35, but if he is even 70% of his peak self, he’s still a star. Los Angeles can work him in slowly if they need to. A pass rush with Garrett, Donald, Kobie Turner , Byron Young , Braden Fiske and others is nightmare fuel for opponents. Furthermore, unlike last year, Matthew Stafford has seemingly no back concerns entering the year. And if he should miss time, both Ty Simpson and Stetson Bennett flashed in preseason action. The Rams are even heavier favorites to win the Super Bowl after the preseason than they were before training camp, and they were already heavy favorites . Now comes the proof. "If this team is healthy,… I think it's gonna be hard to keep them within single digits." @danorlovsky7 says a healthy Rams team will reach the Super Bowl 👀 pic.twitter.com/KlMpDoNvRw — First Take (@FirstTake) August 31, 2026 The Rams still start the season with a series of difficult tests, including traveling across the world to face the 49ers, coming home to face the Giants (a slight reprieve), then going on the road in back-to-back weeks to face the Broncos and Eagles, prior to returning to SoFi Stadium to host the Buffalo Bills. Under most circumstances, any team would love to be 3-2 after that. Can the Rams accept less than 5-0? Sure. 3-2 actually would be good. The Rams have often started worse than that. But with as strong as their offseason has been, there’s no telling how good their actual season could be.

Though not a concern , for now, fans and the team would likely like to see Garrett back at practice sooner than later. Another major piece of news to come out on Sunday is that Aaron Donld is officially back with the Rams . This isn’t just Rams’ news; this is news that impacts the entire NFL. Now, will Donald be as effective as he once was? Do teams have a plan to use against the Rams that they aren’t ready for? Will the Rams be as good on the field as they look on paper? All fair questions. As it stands, the Rams look like one of the best teams in the NFL without playing a single game. We will see how they look on their opening day against the San Francisco 49ers. Puka Nacua returns to Rams practice, Myles Garrett still out (ramswire) “Nacua has been dealing with a psoas injury. After avoiding being placed on the NFL commissioner’s exempt list before the NFL’s roster cut-down deadline, he appears to be on pace to feature in the team’s season opener against the 49ers in Australia. The Rams were never overly concerned about Nacua’s injury but now that he’s returned to practice, he’s certainly on track to play in Week 1.“ Sources: Aaron Donald unretires, reaches $20M deal with Rams (espn) “Donald, who retired in March 2024 after 10 NFL seasons, is a three-time Defensive Player of the Year, an eight-time first-team All-Pro, a 10-time Pro Bowl selection and the 2014 Defensive Rookie of the Year. But the Rams’ trade for Myles Garrett in June spurred conversation about the possibility of Donald’s return for the chance to play with the reigning Defensive Player of the Year. Since the Rams’ June 1 trade for Garrett, Donald has been putting himself through a “very strict, regimented process that was similar to what he did when he played” to see whether he could return, head coach Sean McVay said.“ Rams Troll Heat Over LeBron James YouTube Video Post After Aaron Donald Signs New Contract (bleacherreport) “The Los Angeles Rams had a hilarious callback on social media after signing Aaron Donald on Sunday. The Rams referenced the Miami Heat’s accidental YouTube livestream link teasing LeBron James’ signing.“ All-time great Aaron Donald comes out of retirement to rejoin stacked LA Rams (theguardian.com) “During a 10-season career with the Rams, who drafted him with the 13th overall pick in 2014, Donald was a three-time defensive player of the year and an eight-time first team All-Pro. He won a Super Bowl with the Rams at the end of the 2021 season before announcing his retirement in March 2024 at the age of 32. The 35-year-old returns to a stacked Rams roster who were already betting favorites to win the Super Bowl this season. The team includes reigning MVP Matthew Stafford at quarterback and the reigning defensive player of the year, Myles Garrett, who Los Angeles acquired in a trade with the Cleveland Browns in June .“ Rams final moves ahead of 2026 53-man roster deadline include trade, three on IR, waived 28 players, five terminated vested veterans, one waived/injured (therams.com) “WOODLAND HILLS, Calif. – The Rams made multiple roster moves ahead of the 3 p.m. deadline on Sunday before ending with their initial 53-man roster for the 2026 season. Los Angeles made one trade by sending tight end Mark Redman to Green Bay in exchange for a 2028 seventh-round pick. The Rams also placed quarterback Matthew Caldwell and offensive linemen Keagen Trost and Justin Dedich on Injured Reserve. The final round of cuts included: 28 players waived, five terminated vested veterans and one waived/injured.“ Tutu Atwell is wearing his 3rd different jersey number with the Rams (ramswire) “Upon arriving in Los Angeles, Atwell learned that his old jersey number, 5, was taken by Kamren Kinchens. The number he wore before that, 15, has also been taken by Ty Simpson. So Atwell had to pivot. At practice, Atwell was spotted wearing his third different jersey number as a Ram, switching to No. 8. Obviously, No. 8 was last worn by Jared Verse, who was traded to the Browns this offseason for Myles Garrett.“ Rams news: Watch Aaron Donald move incredibly at practice (sports.yahoo) “There could not be a better outlook for the Los Angeles Rams than watching Aaron Donald back in action with full force. The star defensive tackle has been showing an impressive level of activity during team practice sessions after making the roster cut once the team finalized its 53-man roster. In a recent video shared by ESPN’s NFL reporter Lindsey Thiry, Donald could be seen performing bag drills and agility work on the field for the first time in years. The outlook is what the Rams fans were hoping for.“ Aaron Donald’s New LA Rams Jersey Just Dropped Online (si.com) “Luckily for fans, Nike and Fanatics wasted no time in turning around one of the new Rams’ jerseys for Donald. Online shoppers can buy the Aaron Donald Los Angeles Rams Nike Game Jersey (Royal) for $149.99 in adult sizes at Fanatics and select retailers.“ Aaron Donald reveals wife’s advice that helped him make decision to come out of retirement and re-join Rams (foxnews.com) “”I think my wife played a huge part of me making this decision period because if the wife wasn’t happy, it wasn’t going to get done. I got to make sure that the household was good, the kids were okay with it all,” he said. “Then having the hard conversations, figuring things out, what I wanted to do. If I was to do it, how would we do it? “My wife was on board. She said, ‘If you want to do this, (I’m) with (you) 100%,’ and there were days when I was like, ‘I don’t know.’ She talked to me enough to be like, ‘You want to do this. Don’t make no decisions faster than what you need to make a decision. Take your time.’ She played a huge part of me figuring this out because it really wasn’t an easy decision. It took a lot of hard work, a lot of long conversations with a lot of different people, but I felt good enough to make the decision to come back and do this.” 2026 NFL roster cuts tracker: All the moves made by all 32 teams on cutdown day (cbssports) “For the first time in 22 years, the NFL decided to hold final cuts on a Sunday, and things definitely got kind of crazy with nearly 1,200 players being released over the weekend. During the preseason, teams are allowed to carry 90 players on their roster, but that number had to be cut to just 53 by the cut deadline at 6 p.m. ET Sunday, which means a total of 1,184 players were released, including Titans QB Will Levis . Now that we have cuts out of the way, each team will still have plenty of opportunities to re-shape their roster, and the first big chance will come this week with the waiver wire . After getting cut, any player with less than four years of NFL experience will hit the waiver wire, where they can be claimed by another team. The waiver order is the same as the 2026 NFL Draft order, so the Raiders will have first dibs on claiming any player who goes on waivers. The deadline for claims is Monday at 1 p.m. ET. After that deadline, teams will be notified by the NFL whether their claim went through (if two teams claim the same player, the player will go to the team with higher priority in the waiver order). Any player with more than four years of experience will officially become a free agent after getting cut, so they won’t hit the waiver wire, and they’ll be eligible to sign with any team as soon as Monday, so we could see a rash of signings starting this week.“ Comment of the Day: “I hope AD can be 75…

title: 6 things we learned from the Rams’ 53-man roster
summary: The preseason is over. The Los Angeles Rams just finalized their initial 53-man roster. The regular season is right around the corner. But before we turn our attention to Week 1 against the San Francisco 49ers in Melbourne, Australia, let’s first take a deep dive into the newly minted roster and see what we can […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 27: Matthew Stafford #9 of the Los Angeles Rams laughs with Ty Simpson #15 and Stetson Bennett IV #13 on the sidelines during a preseason game between the Los Angeles Rams and the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium on August 27, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images The preseason is over. The Los Angeles Rams just finalized their initial 53-man roster . The regular season is right around the corner. But before we turn our attention to Week 1 against the San Francisco 49ers in Melbourne, Australia, let’s first take a deep dive into the newly minted roster and see what we can glean. These are six things the Rams and the NFL just told us: 1 – Aaron Donald is BACK It’s officially official . One of the greatest defenders in the history of professional football is giving it one more run in hopes of adding another ring to his collection. Donald will join Myles Garrett on the defensive line. Whether Donald can return to form is an open question. There is plenty of time to assess his capabilities as the season goes on. It’s at least nice to have closure and know that the Rams are taking advantage of every opportunity to bring another championship to Los Angeles. 2 – Rams won their recent trade with Dolphins? LA recently traded 2025 fourth-round running back Jarquez Hunter to the Miami Dolphins in exchange for receiver Tutu Atwell in a one-to-one player swap. Atwell has made the initial 53-man roster. Hunter was waived by Miami . Atwell needs to have a bigger impact on the team than he did in 2025 in order to truly call the Rams winners in this exchange. Still, at least he’s still around. Hunter is looking for new work. 3 – Two OL head to injured reserve Justin Dedich—who sat out the start of camp due to a July hand injury—was placed on injured reserve along with rookie Keagen Trost. This transaction does not rule them out for the entirety of the year. Both players will miss at least four games to start the season and then can be re-activated to join the team. Replacing Dedich and Trost are Dylan McMahon and Bill Murray. Murray was a preseason standout that made the most of ample playing time to make an impression on the coaching staff. 4 – A mysterious new NFL trend Much was made of LA’s deliberation between who to keep on the roster at quarterback behind Matthew Stafford. The Rams opted to keep Stetson Bennett, and Ty Simpson was never in danger of being released. Still, there are tradeoffs when it comes to rostering three QBs. But at least the Rams are in the position where things were so uncertain that they had to keep four signal callers. The Eagles, Falcons, Steelers, and Vikings all fell into this bucket. It’s the latest head scratching trend in terms of roster building. If you need four QB’s, you probably don’t have the right players. It’s a quantity over quality approach. 5 – Rookie report LA cut rookie seventh-rounder Tim Keenan, who likely was the direct loser of Donald re-joining the team. All other 2026 draft selections made the cut, other than Trost who is on injured reserve. Wesley Bailey also joined the fold as an undrafted free agent. This was foreshadowed by the fact he played on two snaps against the Los Angeles Chargers’ starters in the preseason before getting pulled. Nick Andersen also was pulled early but was excluded from the initial 53. He’s a favorite to return on the practice squad unless he draws attention from other teams. 6 – The biggest surprise The talk surrounding the Rams all offseason has centered around the idea they are doubling down on heavier personnel sets and therefore needed to roster five tight ends, including second-round rookie Max Klare. The next logical dot to connect is the idea that LA maybe needed less receivers; however, they kept seven at this position. Puka Nacua’s standing with the NFL is still an open matter , and perhaps the team is bracing for a potential suspension. Nacua did not start the year on the commissioner’s exempt list, as others with open matters did around the league.

Jordan’s simple two-word statement—”I’m back.”—sent shockwaves throughout the sports world and immediately transformed championship expectations. Now, Aaron Donald is creating […]

Garrabrant/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images “I’m Back.” Aaron Donald paid tribute to Michael Jordan announcing his return 🔥 (📸 @RamsNFL ) pic.twitter.com/nbJprGHLpo — Yahoo Sports (@YahooSports) August 30, 2026 Some sports moments transcend a single franchise. They become defining moments for an entire generation of fans. Michael Jordan returning to the Chicago Bulls after his first retirement remains one of those moments. Jordan’s simple two-word statement—”I’m back.”—sent shockwaves throughout the sports world and immediately transformed championship expectations. Now, Aaron Donald is creating his own version of that moment with the NFL and Los Angeles Rams. Aaron Donald’s decision to unretire today and return to the Los Angeles Rams carries the same type of significance. I hope in all of this, Aaron Donald finally understands that he is Michael Jordan in the eyes of Rams fans. Nothing in this franchises history would be more invigorating than seeing him back on the field. https://t.co/LmFhzBEqZM — Rams Bros. (@RamsBrothers) June 3, 2026 Aaron Donald is officially adding his name to one of the rarest lists in sports: legendary athletes who walked away from competition, only to eventually return. The Los Angeles Rams announced that the three-time Defensive Player of the Year is coming out of retirement to play during the 2026 season, more than two years after initially stepping away from the NFL. Donald now joins a select group of iconic athletes who have reversed course on retirement, including Michael Jordan, who famously returned to the NBA with the Chicago Bulls in 1995, and Serena Williams, who returned to professional tennis competition in 2026 after nearly three years away. While every comeback story is unique, Donald’s return is particularly fascinating given his dominance before retirement. Now, at 35 years old, he will attempt to prove he still has plenty left in the tank.
