title: Aaron Donald’s return is the worst news for this rookie
summary: Aaron Donald is officially returning to the Los Angeles Rams. Assuming he’s on the field for the season opener against the San Francisco 49ers, that is extremely bad news for a certain rookie. 2026 fourth-rounder Carver Willis just seized the starting job for the 49ers. His first game will be against one of the greatest […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - NOVEMBER 15: Former Pittsburgh Panthers player Aaron Donald points to where his jersey is hung during his jersey retirement ceremony at halftime of the game between the Pittsburgh Panthers and the Notre Dame Fighting Irish at Acrisure Stadium on November 15, 2025 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Justin Berl/Getty Images) | Getty Images Aaron Donald is officially returning to the Los Angeles Rams . Assuming he’s on the field for the season opener against the San Francisco 49ers, that is extremely bad news for a certain rookie. 2026 fourth-rounder Carver Willis just seized the starting job for the 49ers. His first game will be against one of the greatest defenders in the history of the NFL. Donald may not be 100% the same player after sitting out for two years. It may take him a few weeks in order to knock off the rust. But the superstar pass rusher must be licking his chops to face off against Willis. The rookie played 100 snaps for San Francisco in the preseason and allowed seven total pressures, according to Pro Football Focus (PFF). Willis finished with pass and run blocking grades of 50.9 and 53.7, respectively. Of the 109 rookie offensive linemen to participate in the preseason, Willis ranked safely towards the bottom at 82nd. Only three rookies allowed more pressures in the exhibition game: Alan Herron (Saints; allowed nine against the Rams and Wesley Bailey alone), Ethan Onianwa (Falcons), and Enrique Cruz (49ers). Cruz was drafted by San Francisco one round after Willis. Onianwa was a seventh rounder. Herron went undrafted. That’s not great company to be in. Whether Donald will play against the 49ers Week 1 in Melbourne remains to be seen, as the team has not yet confirmed. We also don’t know if Donald will pick up where he left off. But a favorable matchup against a rookie offensive lineman who proves porous in three exhibition games seems to suggest Donald can announce his return in a more impactful way—by again wrecking offensive game plans.

title: Aaron Donald announces return to Rams for 2026
summary: Aaron Donald is coming out of retirement and returning to the Los Angeles Rams, according to Adam Schefter. The three-time NFL Defensive Player of the Year and eight-time All-Pro is ending his retirement two years after his last game to rejoin the Rams for the 2026 season, giving Los Angeles one of the greatest defensive […]
full_text: Aaron Donald is coming out of retirement and returning to the Los Angeles Rams, according to Adam Schefter. The three-time NFL Defensive Player of the Year and eight-time All-Pro is ending his retirement two years after his last game to rejoin the Rams for the 2026 season, giving Los Angeles one of the greatest defensive players in NFL history as it pursues another Super Bowl. This news is just WOW. 🚨 🚨 🚨 He’s back: Rams star Aaron Donald is coming out of retirement and returning to the Rams on a one-year, $20M deal that with incentives could be worth up to $30M, per @rapsheet and me. After two seasons away, Donald now will join forces with Myles Garrett, giving the… pic.twitter.com/LO2SoKHFwG — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) August 30, 2026 After over a month of speculation since the Rams traded for edge rusher Myles Garrett , Donald has made his commitment official. In a highly-anticipated development, Donald has elected to come out of retirement and rejoin the Rams, giving Los Angeles one of the most intimidating defensive fronts the NFL has seen in recent memory. The future Hall of Famer stepped away from football following the 2023 season, ending a remarkable 10-year career that included three Defensive Player of the Year awards, eight First-Team All-Pro selections, and a Super Bowl championship. Now, he is back. For a Rams organization already viewed as a legitimate contender, Donald’s return instantly changes the outlook of the entire league. What was already one of the NFL’s most talented defensive units now has a chance to become a historically dominant unit. Few players have ever meant more to a franchise than Donald has to the Rams. Selected 13th overall in the 2014 NFL Draft, Donald quickly established himself as one of the greatest defensive players in NFL history. During his first decade in the league, he accumulated 111 career sacks, 543 tackles, 176 tackles for loss, and 24 forced fumbles despite playing defensive tackle, one of the most physically demanding positions in football. His retirement created a massive void in the Rams’ defense, both from a production standpoint and a leadership perspective. While younger players such as Jared Verse (now traded), Braden Fiske, Kobie Turner, and Byron Young helped soften the blow, replacing Donald was never truly possible. The most intriguing aspect of Donald’s return is what it means for the Rams’ defensive line. 🔥 @AaronDonald97 is completely dialed in (Via IG/210ths) pic.twitter.com/n1cAnogdpF — FOX Sports: NFL (@NFLonFOX) August 10, 2026 With Myles Garrett already in the fold, opposing offenses would be forced to account for arguably the two most disruptive defensive players of their generation. Garrett’s elite edge-rushing ability combined with Donald’s interior dominance would create impossible matchup decisions for offensive coordinators. Double-team Donald and Garrett gets one-on-one opportunities. Focus protection toward Garrett and Donald attacks the middle of the pocket. Either choice is a losing proposition.
author: Steven Ridings

(Photo by Ric Tapia/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NFL will not place anymore players on the commissioner’s exempt list on Sunday, after news broke that running back Josh Jacobs would be ruled ineligible to play indefinitely. However, that does not mean that L.A. Rams players Puka Nacua and Alaric Jackson are safe from suspension, as Adam Schefter reported on Sunday that both are still “under league’s review” for the time being. Losing either player would be a huge blow to L.A.‘s chances of beating the 49ers, or anyone else, but it does not sound like the Rams will know their fate for sure prior to final cuts.

title: Rams trade tight end to Packers before roster cut deadline
summary: The Los Angeles Rams have made a trade and cleared space in their logjam at tight end. As first reported by Jordan Schultz on Twitter, the Rams are sending Mark Redman to the Green Bay Packers, with the report coming just three and a half hours before cuts will be finalized. The return to Los […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 27: Junior Colson #25 of the Los Angeles Chargers tackles Mark Redman #83 of the Los Angeles Rams on a short pass play during the first half of a preseason game at SoFi Stadium on August 27, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams have made a trade and cleared space in their logjam at tight end. As first reported by Jordan Schultz on Twitter, the Rams are sending Mark Redman to the Green Bay Packers, with the report coming just three and a half hours before cuts will be finalized. Sources: The #Rams are trading TE Mark Redman to the #Packers . Former Louisville star was an undrafted free agent in 2025 who spent last year on LA’s practice squad. pic.twitter.com/4Ko6SIGHhQ — Jordan Schultz (@Schultz_Report) August 30, 2026 The return to Los Angeles hasn’t been confirmed as of press time. Redman signed a two-year futures deal with the Rams this past offseason, valued at just under $2 million. He was a limited contributor a pass catcher for Los Angeles in its three preseason games, hauling in just three balls for 16 yards. Of course, catching passes is the secondary role for Redman, whose true value comes as a blocking, “Y” tight end. That type of player is valued across the NFL these days and is one the Rams certainly can make use of, but he lost out on the numbers game here. In the end, this is a fringe roster trade that makes sense for both sides. The Rams have one fewer roster decision they need to think over at an already jammed position, and the Packers add the kind of tight end they’ve fruitlessly been searching for throughout the offseason. The Rams still have a number of decisions to make at tight end before rosters are finalized Sunday afternoon, chief among them being how many players to keep at the position overall. Mark Redman had a great camp for the #Rams . Unfortunately, there was no room so the Rams are trading him for something instead of losing him for nothing. He was not clearing waivers. https://t.co/a4hheKnzxW — JAKE OLIVER ELLENBOGEN (@JKBOGEN) August 30, 2026 Once that roster math is figured out, the pieces will fall into place. Colby Parkinson is a shoo-in to stay , as are recent draft picks Max Klare and Terrance Ferguson. Tyler Higbee is also probably in a good space to stay on the 53-man roster to start 2026, so there’s limited room for anyone else to squeeze in. With just a few hours left until the initial roster is set, it shouldn’t surprise anyone that Les Snead has been busy tweaking this roster right down to the wire.

title: Rams practice squad tracker
summary: The Los Angeles Rams are entering the final stage of their preseason roster construction, but getting to the initial 53-man roster will only be part of the process. Once the Rams make their final cuts Sunday, attention will quickly shift toward building the practice squad and then beginning their quest for a World Championship as […]
full_text: WOODLAND HILLS, CALIFORNIA - JUNE 01: Larrell Murchison #52 of the Los Angeles Rams rushes the edge during an OTA offseason workout at Rams Village at Warner Center on June 1, 2026 in Woodland Hills, California. (Photo by Ric Tapia/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams are entering the final stage of their preseason roster construction, but getting to the initial 53-man roster will only be part of the process. Once the Rams make their final cuts Sunday, attention will quickly shift toward building the practice squad and then beginning their quest for a World Championship as the current favorites (+550) according to FanDuel. NFL teams must reduce their active rosters to 53 players by 6 p.m. ET on Sunday, August 30. That deadline will create a large pool of players who are released, and the Rams will have an opportunity to bring some of those players back into the organization as practice squad members. The Rams can carry 16 players on their practice squad during the 2026 season. There is also an exception that allows a team to carry a 17th player if that player qualifies through the NFL’s International Player Pathway Program. That means there could be several familiar faces from training camp who ultimately return to the Rams after initially being released. However, the team cannot simply immediately re-sign every player it cuts. Players who are subject to waivers must first pass through the league’s waiver process before they can return to the practice squad. #Rams waiving Larrell Murchison, per a league source. Will be practice squad once he clears — Aaron Wilson (@AaronWilson_NFL) August 30, 2026 For the Rams, the key window begins after Sunday’s 6 p.m. ET deadline. Waiver claims from the final roster reduction are due Monday, August 31, at 1 p.m. ET , with teams then able to assemble their practice squads after the waiver results are processed. That makes the next 24 hours particularly important for general manager Les Snead and head coach Sean McVay. Some players who narrowly miss the 53-man roster could become practice squad priorities, while others could attract interest from teams around the league. The Rams’ practice squad tracker will remain intentionally blank for now. As players clear waivers and the team begins announcing signings, those additions can be added to the list. [No players signed to Practice Squad] For now, the important numbers are 53 players on the active roster, 16 practice squad spots, and potentially 17 with a qualifying International Player Pathway player. The regular season roster is almost finalized, but the Rams’ roster-building work is far from finished.

title: Raiders News: Keyron Crawford will officially miss rookie season
summary: The NFL’s cutdown day has come and gone, meaning the Las Vegas Raiders have their initial 53-man roster set. One player who isn’t on it is rookie third-round pick Keyron Crawford. Crawford was placed on injured reserve after suffering an ankle injury in the Raiders’ final preseason game against the San Francisco 49ers this past […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - AUGUST 27: Keyron Crawford #42 of the Las Vegas Raiders is driven off of the field on a cart after he was hurt on a play against the San Francisco 49ers in the third quarter of their preseason game at Allegiant Stadium on August 27, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. The 49ers defeated the Raiders 18-12. (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NFL’s cutdown day has come and gone, meaning the Las Vegas Raiders have their initial 53-man roster set. One player who isn’t on it is rookie third-round pick Keyron Crawford. Crawford was placed on injured reserve after suffering an ankle injury in the Raiders’ final preseason game against the San Francisco 49ers this past Thursday night. The defensive end had to be carted off the field, and while the full extent of his injury is still unknown, the fact that Las Vegas didn’t use one of its two return designations on the Auburn product means it’s significant. The Raiders did designate tight end Carter Runyon to return from IR after Runyon missed the majority of training camp with an undisclosed injury. Crawford likely wasn’t going to get much playing time behind Maxx Crosby, Kwity Paye and Malcolm Koonce in year one, anyway. Of course, practice reps are valuable for a young player’s development down the line, but the rookie being out will have a minimal impact on this year’s defense. Meanwhile, Crawford’s injury likely was the final boost Patrick Johnson needed to make the team. The 28-year-old was arguably the Silver and Black’s best top performer during the preseason, collecting 11 tackles, two sacks and four TFLs over the three games. Baring another move/waiver wire pickup on Monday, the Silver and Black will roll into the 2026 season with Crosby, Paye, Koonce and Crawford at edge defender. In Other Raiders’ Links: Cut tracker: A recap of all the cuts the Raiders made on Sunday. Jordan Meredith traded: “According to NFL Media, the Raiders have traded backup center/guard Jordan Meredith to the New York Jets,” S&BP’s Bill Williamson wrote. “The Raiders are sending a 2029 seventh-round pick to New York with Meredith for a 2027 sixth-round pick.” Laki Tasi waived by Titans: The former fan favorite and IPP/rugby player didn’t make Tennessee’s 53-man roster on cutdown day, via WSMV 4 . title: Las Vegas Raiders Cut Day: 4 Biggest Surprises
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders made it through cut day with an initial 53-man roster that makes sense. Nearly, 1200 men are losing out on either achieving their dream or proving to themselves that they can still hack it in this league. Once again, the Raiders made quality personnel moves and limited the head-scratcher to just […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - AUGUST 13: Cian Slone #48 of the Las Vegas Raiders sacks Kedon Slovis #12 of the Arizona Cardinals in the fourth quarter of the preseason game at Allegiant Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Ian Maule/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders made it through cut day with an initial 53-man roster that makes sense. Nearly, 1200 men are losing out on either achieving their dream or proving to themselves that they can still hack it in this league. Once again, the Raiders made quality personnel moves and limited the head-scratcher to just a depth chart casualty. RAIDERS ROSTER MOVES: – The Las Vegas Raiders have made the following transactions: #RaiderNation | @Raiders pic.twitter.com/vhd0FP2A2y — Raiders PR (@RAIDERS_PR) August 30, 2026 The headscratcher Cian Slone being cut was probably the most questionable move of cut day. Slone has been phenomenal in every opportunity he has been given. As a playmaker, a pass rusher, a stunter, a tackler and a hustler. Nearly everyone who had eyes expected his play to be enough for him to force his way onto a team in need of pass-rushing playmakers. Surprise cut #1….. bookmark this for when they’re struggling to find pass rushers outside of Crosby. I bet they are praying he clears waivers and can come back to the practice squad. https://t.co/DQSZlEpuUG — Phil Robinson III (@PhilRobinsonIII) August 30, 2026 A move that became even more eyebrow-raising when it was later revealed that Slone was cut despite third-round draft pick Keyron Crawford going on the season-ending Injured Reserve list. However, Slone is going to the waiver wire due to his lack of four years’ tenure. The waiver wire order mirrors the draft order, so the Raiders are more likely than not to put him on the practice squad. Why? Because they are only keeping four edges on the roster. John Spytek is a cold piece Spytek has been a busy man this offseason, laying the foundation for future successes. What he isn’t getting enough attention or credit for is the tenacity he has shown in finding ways to secure value out of cutting bait. Spytek has found teams to trade for players the entire world knows he was getting rid of. Trading Jordan Meredith, last season’s starting center and career backup guard, plus a 2029 seventh-round pick, for a 2027 sixth-round pick was a genius way to avoid outright cutting him. Meredith has struggled mightily at center, so much so that he was moved back to guard for the last preseason game and then moved on from. Corrected terms: It's a 2027 6th for a 2029 7th with Meredith going to the #Jets . https://t.co/0JzAU2bY4K — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) August 30, 2026 Spytek’s process may be a bit too methodical for many impatient fans in Raider Nation, but he’s doing it the right way, cutting bait, making trades and adding talent where needed. Meanwhile, he has opted to draft premium skill positions rather than overpay in free agency, thereby allowing the coaching staff to keep most of his draft picks. Crawford done for the year Keyron Crawford was the last Raider draft pick before the remaining prominent wide receivers were selected. Hindsight is always 20/20, but Jakobi Lane, Ted Hurst and Malachi Fields have all been lights out through training camp. Crawford getting injured in a preseason game and missing his rookie season is something no one wanted to see. His not being designated for return is a horrible outcome, especially for a player who was blessed with extremely raw talent. His all-gas-and-no-brakes style displayed encouraging potential, but in order to learn how to hone it and use it without waste requires him to be on the field. Is Atonio Mafi keeping a roster spot warm Atonio Mafi hasn’t pass protected well at all this preseason. In fact, one could say he’s been a major contributing factor to the pass rush pressures that Fernando Mendoza faced on the second team. Nonetheless, he is still here because something about his run blocking overrules the fact that he is feeding sacks and pressures to defensive linemen. Mafi is still practice squad eligible, so him making the 53-man roster implies that he is there for some purpose. Be it as depth or the first option to cut and send to the practice squad should Spytek and head coach Klint Kubiak feel the need to add a player.

title: Raiders initial 53-man roster notes
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders have set their initial 53-man roster. Here are some thoughts on the moves. It was no surprise the Raiders kept third-string quarterback Aidan O’Connell behind Kirk Cousins and Fernando Mendoza. Coach Klint Kubiak said it was a real possibility. The only question was if the Raiders would trade O’Connell. Now, it […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - FEBRUARY 24: General manager John Spytek of the Las Vegas Raiders speaks to the media during the 2026 NFL Scouting Combine at Lucas Oil Stadium on February 24, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders have set their initial 53-man roster. Here are some thoughts on the moves . It was no surprise the Raiders kept third-string quarterback Aidan O’Connell behind Kirk Cousins and Fernando Mendoza. Coach Klint Kubiak said it was a real possibility. The only question was if the Raiders would trade O’Connell. Now, it will be interesting to see if, as expected, Cousins starts Week 1, whether Mendoza or O’Connell will be the second-string quarterback in the regular season. Third-round pick, defensive end Keyron Crawford (ankle) was placed on the injured reserve and will miss the season. That hurts. Patrick Johnson will play a key backup role. Tight end Carter Runyon (undisclosed) is starting the season on the injured reserve. He must, miss, at least, four games. Receiver Dont’e Thornton, who hasn’t practiced in more than three weeks for an undisclosed reason, is on the roster. As expected, starting running back Ashton Jeanty wasn’t placed on the injured reserve, so the team expects him to be back by Week 4 at the latest. He injured his ankle a week ago. The Raiders cut veteran running back Dare Ogunbowale. I could see Las Vegas trying to the position in the coming days, perhaps looking for a veteran to complement a young tailback group with just three tailbacks on the roster. Defensive tackle Foley Fatukasi, a late signing, made the team after flashing in the run game. It will be interesting to see if undrafted rookie pass-rusher Cian Slone gets claimed. He had a terrific preseason. If he isn’t claimed, the Raiders will likely try to add him to the practice squad Monday. Something to remember about waiver clams Monday. Usually, about 30 players are claimed day after cut-down. That's not a lot. A player like Slone could be claimed, but you remember there are a ton of players available with an average of about 1 player being claimed per team. — Bill Williamson (@BWilliamsonNFL) August 30, 2026 Miami cut quarterback Cam Miller. Perhaps John Spytek, who drafted Miller in the sixth round last season, will try to sign him to the practice squad. He spent most of last season there before the Dolphins signed him to the 53-man roster late in the year. Seventh-round pick, Brandon Cleveland, was the only of the Raiders’ 10 draft picks to be waived.

Matsuzawa, dubbed “The Tokyo Toe,” was a dud, especially in preseason games. He never really pushed the veteran Gay. It was an easy, obvious decision. Is Gay safe? For now, but for many NFL placekickers, job security is a week-to-week audition and that may be the case for Gay. He played for two teams last season and has been just a so-so kicker in recent years. However, Gay,32, did have success under Raiders special teams coach Joe Decamillis earlier this decade with the Rams. So, there is belief in Gay. Still, if he struggles, the Raiders could look elsewhere. What’s next for Matsuzawa? The Raiders could put him on the practice squad to develop him. It has already been discussed, so that route wouldn’t be a surprise. The former Hawaii star has talent, but he’s raw and he needs to be developed. It may be worth the Raiders’ time to keep him in the program even if he’s a couple of years away from being NFL ready.

title: Miami Dolphins have NFL’s youngest roster heading into 2026 season
summary: The Miami Dolphins have concluded their preseason slate and have trimmed the roster down to 53 men after a flurry of cuts on Saturday and Sunday. As the dust settled, one thing became clear — the organization and new general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan have embraced a youth movement regarding the 2026 version of the Dolphins. […]
full_text: LANDOVER, MD - AUGUST 14: Miami Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis (2) hands the ball to running back De'Von Achane (28) during the Miami Dolphins preseason game versus the Washington Commanders at Northwest Stadium on August 14, 2026, in Landover, MD. (Photo by Lee Coleman/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Miami Dolphins have concluded their preseason slate and have trimmed the roster down to 53 men after a flurry of cuts on Saturday and Sunday. As the dust settled, one thing became clear — the organization and new general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan have embraced a youth movement regarding the 2026 version of the Dolphins. The numbers prove it. In a social media post sent out on Monday morning, Joe Schad of the Palm Beach Post compiled a list of the youngest teams in the National Football League — and the Miami Dolphins easily boast the youngest roster in the entire league, with an average age of 25.3 years. The Dolphins have – and it's not even close – the youngest roster in the NFL Patience required Average age of 53-man roster Dolphins 25.3 Browns 25.9 Chiefs 26.1 Patriots 26.2 Lions 26.2 Packers 26.3 Titans 26.3 Jaguars 26.3 — Joe Schad (@schadjoe) August 31, 2026 The Dolphins beat out the Cleveland Browns as the youngest team in the league — with an average age that is 0.6 years younger than the AFC South squad. The Kansas City Chiefs come in third — 0.8 years older than Miami’s average player. Conversely, the Pittsburgh Steelers and Atlanta Falcons have the oldest rosters in the league — with each having an average age of 27.4 years. Quarterback Aaron Rodgers is obviously dragging that number up for Pittsburgh, but that means the age of an average Steelers or Falcons player in 2026 is a whopping 3.1 years older than the average Dolphins player. Oldest 53-man rosters in the NFL Steelers 27.4 Falcons 27.4 Rams 27.3 Broncos 27.2 Commanders 27.2 49ers 27.2 — Joe Schad (@schadjoe) August 31, 2026 So, what does that mean for Miami in 2026? It means that if the squad hopes to compete against a difficult schedule of talented teams, they’ll need to lean on their youth and athleticism, while being coached to their fullest potential by a new coaching staff led by head coach Jeff Hafley. It could be a rocky road ahead for the Dolphins this season, but watching a young team come into their own as the year unfolds should be a rewarding experience — even if that doesn’t translate to a lot of wins in the process.

title: Miami Dolphins practice squad 2026: Tracking the rumors, reports, and signings
summary: The Miami Dolphins are in the midst of their roster cuts, dropping to the league’s 53-man regular-season limit. They have already started making moves and have until 6 p.m. Eastern on Sunday to finish trimming the roster. After that, the fun begins. After the league processes all the waiver claims from Sunday’s roster cuts, Miami […]
full_text: LANDOVER, MD - AUGUST 14: Miami Dolphins helmet resting on the sidelines prior to the Miami Dolphins preseason game versus the Washington Commanders at Northwest Stadium on August 14, 2026, in Landover, MD. (Photo by Lee Coleman/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Miami Dolphins are in the midst of their roster cuts, dropping to the league’s 53-man regular-season limit. They have already started making moves and have until 6 p.m. Eastern on Sunday to finish trimming the roster. After that, the fun begins. After the league processes all the waiver claims from Sunday’s roster cuts, Miami can sign players to the practice squad on Monday. This group is mostly younger players who need more development time, with a few veterans who could quickly find themselves on the field on game day. We will keep you updated on all the rumors, reports, signings, and changes as the practice squad fills up. Keep in mind that reports can be made, and then a player can land with another team when a better offer comes in. Nothing is official unless the Dolphins have announced the signing. Typically, the first players signed are those the team just cut, but there will also be moves to bring in free-agent veterans or players from other teams. The Dolphins have a young roster this season, and they hope development during one tough season will improve the team’s consistency and future winning. Miami remains the AFC team with the longest odds to make the playoffs, according to FanDuel Sportsbook , which has them listed at +1500 to make a postseason appearance this year. The practice squad, and the players who can develop there, might be critical to the franchise’s future. We also have all the rules for the practice squad so you can make sure to keep up with everything. When can players be signed? Teams can begin signing players to their practice squad at 1 p.m. Eastern on Monday. Before then, the league will complete the claims process for any players who were subject to waivers rather than receiving an outright release. Players with less than four accrued seasons in the NFL must go through the waivers process. To accrue a season of service time in the NFL, a player must be on a roster (to include injured reserve time) for more than six games in a season. Players on the practice squad are not receiving that service time (and that is why you will see players who are listed as in their first year, but not a rookie, on team rosters). Players with more than four accrued seasons are released by their former team and do not have to go through the waivers process. They are immediately considered free agents and can sign with another team – either their 53-man roster or onto the practice squad. How many players can be on the practice squad? Teams are limited to 16 players on the practice squad – with a 17th allocation authorized for a developmental player in the league’s International Player Pathway program. The Dolphins’ rookie tight end Seydou Traore, drafted in the fifth round, is eligible for the roster exemption as an IPP member if Miami waives him and then signs him back to the practice squad. Who is eligible for the practice squad? The 16 standard allocations for the practice squad have some limits on who can be signed to those positions. Ten of the slots are restricted to players with less than two accrued seasons in the NFL. The other six positions are not limited and can be used to sign veteran players who have been in the league for more than two seasons. What is the practice squad salary? For 2026, players two or fewer accrued seasons will earn $13,750 per week on the practice squad. Veteran players with more than two accrued seasons will earn at least $18,350 per week, with salaries negotiable up to$22,850 per week. Practice squad salaries do count against a team’s salary cap. What is “poaching”? A practice squad player is free to sign with another team as long as they are signing to the 53-man roster. Colloquially termed “poaching,” the player joins the new team, with a requirement that the player be on the 53-man roster for at least three weeks. A team can release them early, but they still must pay them for the three weeks of work. To limit a team from signing a player off the practice squad of their next opponent, potentially gaining game plan information, there are restrictions for those signings. A team may not sign a practice squad player from an upcoming opponent within six days of the scheduled game. That restriction is extended to 10 days if the team is on its bye week. What are elevations and how is that different than a promotion? Players on a practice squad may be promoted to their team’s active roster at any time. This is a standard transaction: signing a player like a free agent, with a corresponding roster move to free up a slot on the 53-man roster. Teams can also elevate a player to the active roster, which is different from a promotion. Up to three times per season, a practice squad player may be designated as available for a game without being added to the 53-man roster. They are elevated for game day but then revert to the practice squad after the game. This gives teams some flexibility and depth options, especially if a player on the 53-man roster is injured and cannot play but is not hurt enough to warrant placing them on injured reserve. Teams are allowed two elevations per game, giving them a potential pool of 55 players each week to construct their game-day roster. Teams are only authorized to have 48 players active for the game. Dolphins Practice Squad Rumors / Reports 8/30, 6:19 p.m.: Now that the roster cut deadline is passed, the rumors and reports of practice squad players will start. Throughout the day, when the Dolphins would release players, the post from a reported might include something about Miami hoping to re-sign the player to the practice squad. We are catching up with those now. Remember, nothing is official until the Dolphins announce a signing, and nothing can happen until 1 p.m. Eastern tomorrow, once the waiver wire process has been completed. Rodney McGraw, defensive end – He and his agents “hope” he lands back with the Dolphins practice squad. ( via Barry Jackson ) Jai’Onte’ McMillan, cornerback – The Dolphins claimed McMillan off waivers from the Colts last week and are “considering” him for a practice squad spot. ( via Barry Jackson ) Mark Gronowski, quarterback – The Dolphins waived Gronowski earlier in the preseason, then brought him back when Quinn Ewers was injured. Now they have waived him again, but they would like to bring him back if he clears waivers. ( via Mike Garafolo ) Practice Squad Roster None

title: Dolphins trade for quarterback Kyle McCord
summary: The Miami Dolphins traded away quarterback Quinn Ewers on Saturday, sending him to the Jacksonville Jaguars. On Sunday, they released quarterback Mark Gronowski and Cam Miller, leaving just starter Malik Willis on the roster. While the primary focus for the day is on dropping the roster from the preseason 90-man list to the regular-season 53-player […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - AUGUST 28: Kyle McCord #18 of the Green Bay Packers celebrates during the fourth quarter of a preseason game against the Arizona Cardinals at Lambeau Field on August 28, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Geoff Stellfox/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins traded away quarterback Quinn Ewers on Saturday, sending him to the Jacksonville Jaguars. On Sunday, they released quarterback Mark Gronowski and Cam Miller, leaving just starter Malik Willis on the roster. While the primary focus for the day is on dropping the roster from the preseason 90-man list to the regular-season 53-player size, with a deadline of 6 p.m. Eastern to meet the new standard, the Dolphins were clearly in need of adding a backup quarterback to the roster. They turned to a familiar place to add that quarterback. According to ESPN’s Adam Schefter , the Dolphins have agreed to a trade with the Green Bay Packers to acquire Kyle McCord. Willis was with the Packers last year, as were head coach Jeff Hafley and general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan. The ties between the two teams continue to grow with the addition of McCord. A 2025 sixth-round pick out of Syracuse, McCord spent his rookie season on the Philadelphia Eagles’ practice squad. He signed a reserve/futures contract with the Packers after the 2025 season ended, working with the team through the offseason workouts, training camp, and the 2026 preseason before now joining the Dolphins. McCord spent his first three years of college football at Ohio State before transferring for his final season at Syracuse. He was a two-year starter in college and finished his collegiate career with 8,555 passing yards, 61 touchdowns, and 20 interceptions on a 66.2 percent completion rate. His 4,779 passing yards at Syracuse led the NCAA in 2024. He threw for 446 yards and four touchdowns in the Packers preseason this year. Ahead of the 2025 NFL Draft, NFL.com’s Lance Zierlein compared McCord to Mitchell Trubisky and projected him as a third- to fourth-round pick. He wrote of McCord: Pocket passer with good size who played in a high-volume, pro-passing scheme that should give him a head start as a pro. McCord was too inconsistent at Ohio State, relative to the talent around him, but he proved to be confident and productive last season at Syracuse without that same level of supporting talent. His fundamentals are usually solid and he plays with adequate poise in the face of pressure. He has enough arm to make window throws and push the ball around the field. McCord seeks to attack coverages vertically instead of operating as a “Checkdown Charlie.” While he can hit chunk throws, his decision-making and ball placement aren’t always good fits for his gunslinger mentality. His mobility inside and outside the pocket is average. McCord has good size, adequate talent and commendable resilience. He could find a home as a backup quarterback with modest upside. Miami sent a 2028 sixth-round pick to the Packers in exchange for McCord. The Dolphins received a 2028 sixth-round pick from the Jaguars in the Ewers trade, but it was not immediately indicated if they sent that pick or their own sixth-round selection to the Packers.

title: Vikings Keep Four QBs: 53-Man Roster Breakdown & Preseason Recap
summary: Vikings 53-Man Roster Breakdown: Four QBs, Rookies Rising, and a Preseason to Forget — The Minnesota Vikings finalized their 53-man roster after a dismal preseason featuring just one offensive touchdown, and the biggest headline is keeping four quarterbacks — Kyler Murray, Carson Wentz, J.J. McCarthy, and Max Brosmer — on the active roster. Darren Campbell […]
full_text: EAGAN, MINNESOTA - JUNE 10: Kyler Murray #1 of the Minnesota Vikings participates in a drill during minicamp at Twin Cities Orthopedics Performance Center on June 10, 2026 in Eagan, Minnesota. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) | Getty Images Vikings 53-Man Roster Breakdown: Four QBs, Rookies Rising, and a Preseason to Forget — The Minnesota Vikings finalized their 53-man roster after a dismal preseason featuring just one offensive touchdown, and the biggest headline is keeping four quarterbacks — Kyler Murray, Carson Wentz, J.J. McCarthy, and Max Brosmer — on the active roster. Darren Campbell and Dave Stefano broke it all down on the latest episode of Two Old Bloggers, a Vikings 1st & SKOL production, covering roster surprises, quarterback controversy, defensive line questions, and a trip down franchise history lane. The Friday night 34-6 loss to Denver was, as Darren put it, “another very miserable viewing experience for Vikings fans.” With McCarthy sitting out due to a sore ankle, the quarterback depth chart remains unsettled. “This was his one last chance before the season started to give me some confidence in him as the backup quarterback, and he did not do that because he did not play,” Darren said. Yet he supports keeping McCarthy: “I want J.J. McCarthy to stay on this team right now… at times, he showed ability to move the team and have the offense hopping.” Dave agreed, noting all four QBs “all have injury histories,” which justified the unusual four-quarterback approach. Key Points from the Episode: Four QBs kept: Murray, Wentz, McCarthy, and Brosmer all made the 53 — a rarity in the NFL. Darren called it “a surprising roster decision,” noting Brosmer’s spot could’ve gone to a special teams contributor. Punter change: Johnny Hekker was released in favor of rookie Brett Thorson. “It’s not a case where Hekker clearly outplayed him,” Darren noted, citing Thorson’s bigger leg and lower cost. Jacob Thomas steals the show: The undrafted safety from James Madison was the surprise of camp. “Brian Flores was giving him flowers in press conferences,” Dave said. Darren added Thomas was “telling other players, veteran players like Jay Ward, where to be on the field” — remarkable for a UDFA. Defensive line goes young: With Jonathan Allen and Javon Hargrave gone, Levi Drake Rodriguez and Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins step into starting roles backed by rookies Caleb Banks and Domonique Orange. “The bar that those two departed guys set isn’t that high,” Darren offered as a silver lining. Running game revamp: New OL coach Keith Carter and run game coordinator Frank Smith bring a physical philosophy. Darren remains cautious: “We’ve heard this before… and the results always seem to be the same.” Rivalries uniform revealed: The Vikings unveiled new alternate jerseys for the December 20 Lions game. Darren admitted “jersey fatigue” but liked the Nordic rune designs. Pro Bowl abolished: The NFL scrapped the Pro Bowl game entirely. “Just have a legit decision on who the best players are and announce them,” Darren said. Franchise firsts: Chuck Foreman was the first 1,000-yard rusher (1975), Warren Moon the first 4,000-yard passer (1994), and John Gilliam the first 1,000-yard receiver (1972) — all explored in a fun history segment. Listen: Or on your favorite podcast aggregator. Watch: The 2026 season kicks off in two weeks against the Packers, and questions abound. Can Kyler Murray master KOC’s offense? Will the youthful defensive line hold up? Is Jacob Thomas the real deal? For the full breakdown — including roster bubble analysis, injury updates, and a deep dive into Vikings franchise history — tune in to Two Old Bloggers with Darren and Dave, a Minnesota Vikings podcast on the Bleav Network. Like, subscribe, and SKOL. Fan With Us! We have your Minnesota Vikings talk amongst the Two Old Bloggers , Darren @KickassblogVike and Dave @Luft_Krigare . Join the conversation! Fan with us at Vikings 1st & SKOL @Vikings1stSKOL and the at the @BleavNetwork . Open Question for Readers: What’s your biggest concern heading into Week 1 — the quarterback situation, the defensive line, or the running game? Drop your thoughts below and join the conversation.

title: Notes on Vikings Cutdown Day
summary: The Minnesota Vikings have cut their roster from 90 to 53 players per league requirements as they prepare for the start of the regular season. There will likely be more moves in the coming days as they navigate waivers and potential trade and free agent options. Here are some notes on who they cut and […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - AUGUST 22: Johnny Hekker #5 of the Minnesota Vikings stands on the sidelines during an NFL preseason football game against the Baltimore Ravens at U.S. Bank Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Kara Durrette/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings have cut their roster from 90 to 53 players per league requirements as they prepare for the start of the regular season. There will likely be more moves in the coming days as they navigate waivers and potential trade and free agent options. Here are some notes on who they cut and who they kept. Quarterback (4) Kyler Murray Carson Wentz J.J. McCarthy Max Brosmer Cuts: None Notes: It’s highly unlikely the Vikings will keep four quarterbacks on the roster. This is a temporary move as the Vikings figure out the best move/deal for McCarthy and Brosmer. I would not be surprised if both are not on the roster before the start of the season if not in the next few days. I’m guessing the market for McCarthy is less than robust and they may also be working on trade deal(s) for another quarterback(s). A trade for Anthony Richardson would not be terribly surprising, but the Vikings could have their eyes on another quarterback as well. I don’t think there is much of a trade market for McCarthy right now. Will Levis, who has more experience and better stats than McCarthy, was waived today. And the fact that McCarthy did not perform well in preseason and managed another minor injury that kept him out of the final preseason game doesn’t help his market value at all. Still, there may be some teams that were hoping the Vikings would simply waive McCarthy, but that has not been the case so far. Jim Harbaugh and the Chargers may have some interest in McCarthy, as they have just Trey Lance behind Justin Herbert on their initial 53-man roster. Obviously there is the Michigan connection with Harbaugh, but McCarthy also has some exposure to Mike McDaniel’s scheme via Frank Smith this offseason. Running Back / Fullback (4) Aaron Jones Jordan Mason Demond Claiborne Max Bredeson (FB) Cuts: Zavier Scott Jermar Jefferson Notes: Claiborne did not have an outstanding training camp or preseason, but he did show flashes of his upside as a quick and agile back capable of breaking explosive runs whenever he touches the ball. That upside is something Scott just doesn’t have, although Scott can do a lot of things reasonably well. Claiborne did show he could pass protect reasonably well- and actually graded better than Scott in that regard in preseason according to PFF. Tight End (4) T.J. Hockenson Josh Oliver Gavin Bartholomew Ben Yurosek Cuts: Marshall Lang Bryson Nesbit (waived/injured) Matt Lauter Notes: The Vikings put off a decision for the last tight end spot for now, but I wouldn’t be surprised if they cut Yurosek (or possibly Bartholomew) once they add to the offensive line group. Wide Receiver (6) Justin Jefferson Jordan Addison Jauan Jennings Tai Felton Myles Price Dillon Bell Suspended: Jeshaun Jones Cuts: Dontae Fleming (waived/injured) Trayvon Rudolph Marcus Sanders Jr. Michael Briscoe Terrill Sanders Notes: This position group was set early on, with Tai Felton and Myles Price showing improvement and the top three being roster locks. However, the Vikings opted to go with six wide receivers for now, with Dillon Bell making the roster as a result. Bell makes sense as a backup body type to Jauan Jennings, and the Vikings may have a fair number of packages with Jennings as a blocker, so if he went down they’ll need someone to replace that role. Bell has the body type to do that, if not Jennings’ skillset at the moment. Jones was suspended for performance-enhancing drug use, and I expect he’ll be released at the end of that suspension barring injury. Offensive Line (8) Christian Darrisaw Donovan Jackson Blake Brandel Will Fries Brian O’Neill Ryan Van Demark Joe Huber Caleb Tiernan IR (designated to return): Michael Jurgens Traded: Walter Rouse + 2027 7th round draft pick to Patriots for a 2027 6th round draft pick. Cuts: Delby Lemiuex Tristain Leigh Henry Byrd Joshua Gray Tomas Rimac Vershon Lee Gavin Gerhardt Notes: The Vikings will add one or two more to their offensive line roster in time. Michael Jurgens when he returns from IR, but possibly another free agent or waived player as well. I’m surprised the Vikings didn’t keep Rouse, but I suppose with a sixth-round pick they got enough to go get another offensive lineman next year if need be (Rouse was a sixth-round pick in 2024 with two years left on his contract). Byrd and Lee were somewhat disappointing in preseason, while Gerhardt never really had a chance to make the roster. I could see Rimac being kept on the practice squad as a more raw player with athletic upside, but otherwise I’d rather see the Vikings bring in some new depth players. Defensive Interior Line (6) Jalen Redmond Levi Drake Rodriquez Tyrion Ingram Dawkins Caleb Banks Domonique Orange Elijah Williams Cuts: Isaiahh Loudermilk Jahvaree Ritzie Smith Vilbert Jonathan Harris Notes: The only open spot in this group if they were keeping six was the last spot. Elijah Williams led the field from beginning to end, so no real surprises with this group. Loudermilk and Vilbert are vets the Vikings acquired to provide a baseline floor for the group, but Williams was able to exceed what they had to offer. Ritzie is a raw player with athletic upside that could come back on the practice squad. Edge Rusher (4) Andrew Van Ginkel Dallas Turner Bo Richter Chaz Chambliss IR (season ending): Tyler Batty Cuts: Cam’Ron Stewart Kenny Dyson Jr. Notes: I thought Richter, Chambliss and Batty were fighting for the last two spots on the depth chart here, but didn’t realize Batty was lost for the season, which made the decision of which two to keep much easier. Not sure what happened to Batty as I didn’t see his injury being reported. Update: Batty tore his ACL and sadly will miss the entire season. Inside Linebacker (4) Blake Cashman Eric Wilson Jake Golday Ivan Pace Jr. Cuts: Josh Ross Jacob Roberts (waived/injured) Bangally Kamara Notes: I thought Roberts, who graded very well in preseason, had a good chance to make the roster as a decent linebacker and core special teamer, but that was not to be. He was injured in the last preseason game and not sure how severe it was. Some potential to come back on practice squad. But Roberts was likely competing against a couple others across position groups on defense for one of the last roster spots. I suspect Zemaiah Vaughn beat out the others for that spot. Cornerback (5) Byron Murphy Jr. Isaiah Rodgers James Pierre Charles Demmings Zemaiah Vaughn Cuts: Dwight McGlothern Tre Hawkins Jared Washington Marcus Allen (waived/injured) Da’Veawn Armstead Notes: With the Vikings keeping just four cornerbacks on the roster and the first three roster locks, it was a tough group to break into. Charles Demmings outperformed the others from the get-go, seizing the last spot early on. Zemaiah Vaughn managed to make the roster initially as well- he seemed close to making the roster last year. The Vikings opting for five cornerbacks this year initially helped secure his spot for now. Safety (5) Josh Metellus Theo Jackson Jay Ward Jacob Thomas Jakobe Thomas Cuts: Tavierre Thomas Kahlef Hailassie Notes: Tavierre Thomas being cut was a bit of a surprise as the Vikings just gave him a two-year extension with nearly $2 million guaranteed. He was likely a casualty of Jacob Thomas’ rise, who was also good on special teams. Special Teams Coordinator Matt Daniels talked about Tavierre Thomas being one of the leaders on special teams this year. But I guess not. Specialists (3) Will Reichard (K) Andrew DePaola (LS) Brett Thorson (P/H) Cut: Johnny Hekker (P/H) Notes: The Vikings went with All-Pros at kicker and long-snapper but opted for the rookie Thorson over the aging former All-Pro Hekker. Thorson and Hekker basically played to a tie in the punting and holding…

title: Minnesota Vikings Practice Squad Tracker and Practice Squad Rules
summary: While we’re still awaiting the results of the final cuts for the Minnesota Vikings, we’re going to go over the rules governing the practice squads for the upcoming season. Once the final cuts are completed, this post will also serve as our practice squad tracker, so we’ll be updating this post with any news of […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NC - SEPTEMBER 25: Marcus Sherels #35 of the Minnesota Vikings returns a punt for a touchdown against the Carolina Panthers during the game at Bank of America Stadium on September 25, 2016 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by Grant Halverson/Getty Images) | Getty Images While we’re still awaiting the results of the final cuts for the Minnesota Vikings, we’re going to go over the rules governing the practice squads for the upcoming season. Once the final cuts are completed, this post will also serve as our practice squad tracker, so we’ll be updating this post with any news of signings to the practice squad for the purple as well. As we went over in the previous post about the roster cutdown rules, teams need to have their rosters trimmed to 53 players by 5:00 PM Central Time on Sunday, 30 August, which is today. After that, teams are allowed to claim any players who are subject to waivers. Those waiver claims will be processed by the league at 11:00 AM Central Time on Monday, 31 August. Once those claims are processed, any players who were not claimed on waivers are eligible to be signed by any team to their practice squad. An NFL practice squad will normally consist of sixteen players. The one exception to this is if a team brings on a player who is participating in the league’s International Player Pathway Program (IPPP), such as punter Brett Thorson, who has spent this offseason with the Vikings. If Thorson does not make the 53-man roster and clears waivers, the Vikings (or any other team) could bring him onto the practice squad as a 17th member with an exemption. Should that IPPP member get elevated to the main roster, he does not carry that exemption with him. He’s a regular member of the 53-man roster like anyone else. UPDATE : As you’ve seen by now if you’re following with our roster cut tracker (and you should be), Thorson made the 53-man roster for the Vikings. But the Vikings could sign a different IPPP participant to a 17th practice squad spot if they so chose. As far as the other sixteen players are concerned, at least ten of the sixteen spots must be occupied by players who have two or fewer accrued seasons of NFL experience. (An accrued season is one where a player spent at least six games in a full-pay status.) Any player can occupy any of the other six spots on a team’s practice squad, regardless of their experience level. During the regular season, a player can be “elevated” from the practice squad to the main roster up to three times. If the team wishes to bring a player up from the practice squad for a fourth time, they need to sign them to the active roster. During the postseason, player elevations are unlimited. In addition, if a team wants to sign a player from another team’s practice squad, it has to sign that player to its active roster. They can’t simply sign a player from one team’s practice squad to their practice squad. The signing team also has to keep that player on their active roster for a minimum of three weeks. A player also cannot sign with a team that is scheduled to play their current team in the upcoming week, unless they do so at least six days before the game (or ten days if the acquiring team is on a bye week). Those should be all of the rules that we need to be aware of when it comes to the practice squad. Again, once the final cuts are made, we’ll be using this post to track practice squad signings on Monday, so we’ll move it up to the top of the page so people can find it more easily. After all, if the Vikings are going to help people cash on a bet of +140 to win ten games or more (thank you, FanDuel Sportsbook ), some of the guys that end up on that practice squad are likely going to play a role at some point this season.

title: NFL roster cuts 2026: 6 waiver wire targets that would make sense for the Patriots
summary: The roster movement continues across the NFL on Monday after teams trimmed their rosters down to 53 players on Sunday. With hundreds of transactions across the league, a significant portion of them — those with fewer than four accrued seasons in the league — were placed on the waiver wire: where teams have until 1 […]
full_text: Aug 27, 2026; Orchard Park, New York, USA; Buffalo Bills defensive back Kani Walker (41) tackles Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver Brandon Smith (87) during the second quarter at New Highmark Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark Konezny-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The roster movement continues across the NFL on Monday after teams trimmed their rosters down to 53 players on Sunday. With hundreds of transactions across the league, a significant portion of them — those with fewer than four accrued seasons in the league — were placed on the waiver wire: where teams have until 1 p.m. ET on Monday to put in claims in order to add them to their 53-man rosters. The New England Patriots, who have the 31st spot in the waiver claim priority, have a full 53-man roster as of now. However, that roster will continue to be fluid over the upcoming days as they continue to search for depth upgrades. With that being said, let’s take a look at 6 potential targets that would make sense. WR/KR Charlie Jones The Patriots are set at wide receiver, but the team failed to find a kick returner this offseason. They rotated through several options in the preseason but did not have a return of at least 30 yards. Jones, meanwhile, has been a dynamic returner for the Bengals over the past three years, including a pair of kick return touchdowns. Is that enough to justify rostering seven wide receivers, or will the Patriots look to Kyle Williams to potentially fill the role? CB Kani Walker Six cornerbacks were kept on the 53-man roster, with Charles Woods and rookies Karon Prunty and Channing Canada making the team. But the group’s play was inconsistent throughout the summer, perhaps leading the Patriots to look for depth elsewhere. In the AFC East, Bills cornerback Kani Walker was a bit of a surprise cut after a strong preseason and brings good size (6’2) to the boundary. Edge Adisa Isaac New England’s pass-rush group remains the weakest on the roster, as the Patriots kept just Gabe Jacas and Quintayvious Hutchins to back up Dre’Mont Jones and Elijah Ponder. Adding pass-rush help should be on the to-do list, and Isaac is expected to draw interest around the league. The 2024 third-round pick has dealt with injuries to begin his career but showed his potential with a strong preseason. Edge Sam Williams Elsewhere along the edge, the 27-year-old Williams has recorded 9.5 sacks across three seasons as a rotational pass rusher for the Cowboys. Williams missed all of 2024 with a torn ACL and was suspended for three games for violating the league’s personal conduct policy. His physical, violent skill set should be appealing to New England, but he needs to improve his discipline. DL Joshua Weru and Uar Bernard The Patriots got a first-hand look at the Eagles’ roster this summer during a pair of joint practices and one preseason game. While Weru and Bernard are both project players as they are new to the game of football, the International Player Pathway Program players have intriguing skill sets and flashed at times this preseason. That included Weru recording a sack in the preseason game against New England, while Bernard is a freakish athlete along the interior of the defensive line.

title: NFL waiver wire, explained for Patriots fans: Rules, claim order, more
summary: After a preseason showdown against the Cleveland Browns, the New England Patriots will begin cutting down their 90-man roster. The team needs to make 37 moves ahead of the NFL’s deadline on Sunday, Aug. 30, at 6 p.m. ET. A majority of those personnel changes will come through the most straightforward roster reduction method: cutting […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 9: A detailed view of an official Wilson NFL football on the grass field during an NFL football game between the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and the New England Patriots at Raymond James Stadium on November 9, 2025 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images After a preseason showdown against the Cleveland Browns, the New England Patriots will begin cutting down their 90-man roster. The team needs to make 37 moves ahead of the NFL’s deadline on Sunday, Aug. 30, at 6 p.m. ET. A majority of those personnel changes will come through the most straightforward roster reduction method: cutting players. However, not all 37 transactions will be the same. The NFL has separate protocols for so-called vested veterans and players with less league experience. Veterans immediately enter the open market as free agents after being released, while the latter must pass through the waiver wire, where they can be claimed by another franchise or enter free agency if unclaimed. What exactly does all of this mean for a Patriots team with the sixth-best Super Bowl odds in the league, per FanDuel Sportsbook ? Let’s break it down. What is the NFL waiver wire? Franchises will make their final preparations before the season, with substantial changes being made to league rosters. Players will either be waived or released, but not all will instantly become free agents and be free to sign with any team. When a player is “waived,” they are subject to the waiver wire, where any team can claim them and assume their current contract. Currently, the waiver wire order is dependent on the NFL Draft order from this past April, but without any trades. Teams file waiver claims at the same time. That being said, only the team with the highest claim in the order will successfully pick up the player and their current contract. Which NFL players are subject to go on waivers and not be released? A player’s time in the NFL determines whether they enter the waiver wire or become a free agent. Players with at least four years of accrued NFL service time are released. If a player is released, their contract has ended, and they are eligible to sign with any team. However, if a player has less than four years of service time, they are waived and subject to waiver wire claims. Any player who is not claimed after being waived is eligible to sign wherever they’d like, including their former team’s practice squad. The group of players being waived primarily consists of those who are not currently eligible for unrestricted free agency status entering the season. They would instead be either an exclusive rights free agent (less than three years of service) or a restricted free agent (three years of service). Which Patriots cuts are subject to waivers? In total, 40 of the Patriots’ depth players (not including starters and primary backups, or “roster locks”) will first have to pass through the waiver wire, where they might get claimed by any NFL team, before entering the open market. QB Mehren Morton RB Lan Larison RB Jam Miller WR Cameron Dorner WR Kyle Dixon WR Nick DeGennaro WR Tejhaun Palmer TE Tanner Arkin TE Jack Westover TE C.J. Dippre OT Dametrious Crownover OT Lorenz Metz OL Jacob Rizy OL Joseph Michalski OL Darrian Dalcourt OL Jack Conley OL Mehki Butler OL JonDarius Morgan DT Eric Gregory DT Isaiah Iton DT Jeremiah Pharms Jr. DT Casey Rogers DT Leonard Taylor III ED Bradyn Swinson ED Xavier Holmes ED Quintayvious Hutchins ED Amari Gainer LB Khalil Jacobs LB Namdi Obiazor LB Riley Wilson CB Karon Prunty CB Charles Woods CB Kobee Minor CB Channing Canada CB Marcellas Dial Jr. CB Brandon Crossley S Dell Pettus S John Saunders Jr. S Eric Butler S Peter Manuma Which Patriots cuts are not subject to waivers? Seven of New England’s depth players are vested veterans. If released, they would become free agents as soon as the respective moves were made official, meaning that they would all be free to sign with any team of their choosing. RB JaMycal Hasty RB Hassan Haskins OT James Hudson III OL Greg Van Roten LB Chad Muma LB K.J. Britt CB Kindle Vildor What is the NFL waiver order right now? The NFL waiver order during the preseason and the first three weeks of the regular season mirrors the 2026 NFL Draft order. Once we get through four games, it resets to the current NFL standings. So, the Las Vegas Raiders have the first crack at every player on waivers. Las Vegas Raiders New York Jets Arizona Cardinals Tennessee Titans New York Giants Cleveland Browns Washington Commanders New Orleans Saints Kansas City Chiefs Cincinnati Bengals Miami Dolphins Dallas Cowboys Atlanta Falcons Baltimore Ravens Tampa Bay Buccaneers Indianapolis Colts Detroit Lions Minnesota Vikings Carolina Panthers Green Bay Packers Pittsburgh Steelers Los Angeles Chargers Philadelphia Eagles Jacksonville jaguars Chicago Bears Buffalo Bills Houston Texans San Francisco 49ers Los Angeles Rams Denver Broncos New England Patriots Seattle Seahawks How does the NFL waiver system work? Let’s assume the 31st-ranked Patriots and 32nd-ranked Seahawks are the two teams to place a claim for a player. He will end up in New England due to the organization’s superior ranking. The team with the lowest bid will always end up with the player. Teams can add as many players through waivers as they want, but they might have to make corresponding roster moves to fit them on their 53-man team and/or under the salary cap. Have the Patriots made any moves yet? In order to stay on top of every transaction involving the Patriots’ roster cutdowns on Sunday, ahead of the waiver claim deadline on Monday, make sure to regularly visit our Patriots roster cut tracker .

title: NFL practice squad, explained for Patriots fans
summary: The New England Patriots have finalized their initial 53-man roster, but that was only the first step in building the team for the upcoming 2026 season. Another big part of this process will kick off on Monday, when teams can start forming their 16-player practice squads. All of the players released over the last few […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - AUGUST 19: A member of the New England Patriots carries a helmet during a joint practice with the Philadelphia Eagles at Gillette Stadium on August 19, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Billie Weiss/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New England Patriots have finalized their initial 53-man roster , but that was only the first step in building the team for the upcoming 2026 season. Another big part of this process will kick off on Monday, when teams can start forming their 16-player practice squads. All of the players released over the last few days by both the Patriots and the league’s other 31 clubs are potential candidates to get added to that group. It would therefore not be a surprise if New England’s practice squad eventually consists primarily of familiar names, who spent some if not all of training camp with the organization. What exactly does all of that mean, though? And what is a practice squad to begin with? Glad you asked. What is the practice squad? Prior to the 2020 season, teams were able to keep 10 players on their practice squad. While they could not play in any games unless promoted to the 53-man team, the practice squad did still serve a purpose: is was essentially a second roster to develop younger guys and give teams more personnel to help prepare for upcoming opponents. The NFL-NFLPA Collective Bargaining Agreement signed into effect in 2020, however, introduced some changes. Practice squad limits initially increased to 12, before the league’s Covid-19 protocols added four more spots. Those protocols are a thing of the past, but the new practice squad size remains in place. As a result, teams are allowed to carry up to 16 players on top of the 53 already on the active roster. Who is eligible to join the practice squad? Despite the 16-player limit, there are some rules in place that govern who exactly can be added to a practice squad. Article 33, Section 4 of the CBA explains who is eligible to join the practice squad, with some modifications made in 2022: Section 4. Eligibility: Beginning in the 2022 League Year, the Practice Squad shall consist of the following players: (i) players who do not have an Accrued Season of NFL experience; (ii) free agent players who were on the Active List for fewer than nine regular season games during their only Accrued Season(s); (iii) a maximum of ten free agent players per Club who have earned no more than two Accrued Seasons, with such players having no limitation as to the number of games on the game day Active List in either of those seasons; and (iv) a maximum of six free agent players per Club with no limitations as to their number of earned Accrued Seasons; provided, however, that the combined total number of players in categories (iii) and (iv) above may not exceed ten. What does all of that mean? Let’s start with the basics: accrued seasons. Per the CBA, a player gets awarded an accrued season for each one during which “he was on, or should have been on, full pay status for a total of six or more regular season games.” This does include games spent on a team’s 53-man roster or its injured reserve and PUP lists but neither covers the non-football injury list (NFI) nor the practice squad itself. With that as the basis, the current practice squad rules can be broken down as follows: Players with unlimited number of accrued seasons: max. 6* Players with two or fewer accrued seasons: max. 10* Players with no accrued seasons/Players who were active less than 9 games in their only accrued season: max. 16 *the combination of those two categories may not exceed 10 players How much does a practice squad player get paid? The previous CBA, which was ratified in 2011, did not specify how much practice squad players would get paid; it only stated a minimum weekly salary. The most recent labor deal signed in 2020, meanwhile, has a more structured approach to practice squad pay. With the exception of the Group IV players and their two-plus accrued seasons, every player who is on the squad (groups I-III) will earn $13,7500 per week this year, which would amount to a total of $247,5000 over the course of the entire regular season. Players in Group IV, meanwhile, can get a bit more than that: they will earn up between $18,350 and $22,850 weekly. Practice squad salaries are paid on a bye week as well. They count against a team’s salary cap. Can a player be signed off a practice squad? The NFL allows practice squad players to be signed by other teams, but there are some rules governing the process: Players cannot be signed directly from one practice squad to another. They either have to be released first and become free agents, or get signed directly to an active 53-man roster. Practice squad players are not allowed to sign with upcoming opponents, unless done so a minimum of six days before the two teams’ game (or 10 if the team is on a bye). If a practice squad player is signed by another team, he receives a guaranteed three-week salary and will count against the 53-man roster for at least three weeks — even if released before those three weeks are over. What if a team promotes its own practice squad player? In the past, a practice squad player was ineligible to appear in a game unless signed to the active roster first. The 2020 CBA, however, introduced some changes. The standard rules still remained place. Practice squad members can be promoted by replacing other players on the 53-man squad; they can only return after being cut (and potentially going through waivers); they must be paid a weekly salary based on their NFL minimum for at least three weeks. The most recent bargaining agreement added another stipulation, though. Teams are allowed to elevate players from their practice squad to the game day roster without having to cut a member of the 53-man team. Accordingly, clubs can increase from the standard 53 to 55 players while game day active squads expand from a previous 46 to 47 players (or 48 if a team carries eight offensive linemen). Any practice squad player can be elevated and automatically reverts back to the developmental roster after a game. Teams can use this method of promotion on the same player no more than three times a year. If the Patriots, for example, want to have one of their practice squad players on their active game day roster for a fourth game, they will have to go the standard route of promotion, moving him to replace another player on the 53-man roster and, if necessary, exposing him to waivers if the plan is to revert him back to the practice squad. The emergency quarterback rule introduced in 2023, meanwhile, does not apply to players who were standard-elevated from the practice squad. The NFL tried to change this last offseason, but the players association vetoed the modification. How about international players? For a third year in a row, NFL’s International Player Pathway Program is relevant for the Patriots. Offensive tackle Lorenz Metz, after all, spent the entire spring and summer on their active roster as a roster-exempt 91st player. Metz was waived on Saturday , but he could return via the practice squad if making it through waivers unclaimed. They either could sign him as a “normal” practice squad player, which means he would be eligible for roster promotion or game day elevation, or use his IPPP status. In the latter case, he would be on the practice squad as an exempt 17th player who is allowed to practice but not play in any games while on IPPP status. The last two years, the Patriots opted to use International status on edge defender Jotham Russell and defensive tackle David Olajiga. Back in 2019, they opted to forgo it when signing fullback Jakob Johnson to their practice squad. Johnson later joined the 53-man roster and ended up playing in 38 games for the team between 2019 and 2021. When can teams start signing practice squad players? Every player who entered free agency and fits the eligibility criteria can sign with…

title: 8 winners and losers from Patriots roster cuts
summary: The New England Patriots were quite busy over the weekend, making 42 combined transactions to go from previously 91 to 53 players on their active roster. A majority of those moves were expected to happen, but the team of head coach Mike Vrabel nonetheless managed to pull off some minor surprises. With that in mind, […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - AUGUST 13: Channing Canada #29 of the New England Patriots completes a catch prior to an NFL preseason football game against the Indianapolis Colts at Gillette Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New England Patriots were quite busy over the weekend, making 42 combined transactions to go from previously 91 to 53 players on their active roster . A majority of those moves were expected to happen, but the team of head coach Mike Vrabel nonetheless managed to pull off some minor surprises. With that in mind, let’s take a look at the moves that can be qualified as surprises through the lens of our established winners and losers format. It would be easy to label the 53 men on the active roster as winners and the rest as losers, but every situation is different and the reality much more nuanced than simply asking who is in or out. Winners QB Behren Morton: With Drake Maye a franchise-caliber player and Tommy DeVito an able and experienced backup, the top of the Patriots’ quarterback depth chart was set in stone throughout the summer. The question was whether or not Morton had done enough to warrant being kept as one of the 53 players on the roster. Turns out he had. Despite some shortcomings elsewhere on the team, he made it through cutdown day as QB3 and the projected emergency option on game day. OT Dametrious Crownover: Shortly before the cutdown deadline at 6 p.m. ET on Sunday, the Patriots made a trade with the Vikings to bring in versatile offensive lineman Walter Rouse, a player capable of lining up at both tackle and guard. And yet, despite his presence, the team decided to keep four pure tackles on the initial 53. Three of those — Will Campbell, Morgan Moses, Caleb Lomu — were set in stone to begin with, but Crownover’s position seemed less secure with Rouse in the mix. However, he seemingly had nothing to worry about and done enough over the summer to secure a roster spot in lieu of nominal OT4 Marcus Bryant . ED Quintayvious Hutchins: The defensive edge had been in the spotlight going back to the offseason, and it remains a question at this point as well. Through the cutdown deadline, however, the Patriots opted to go with four players, Hutchins among them. His inclusion over fellow edges Bradyn Swinson and Jesse Luketa might have come surprisingly, but the seventh-round draft pick has developed nicely over the summer to make the pair expendable. LB Namdi Obiazor: Obiazor was only used occasionally with the first-team defense in training camp, but he quickly carved out a core role as a five-unit special teams presence. Ultimately, this played a key part in him making the 53-man team and the Patriots opening the year with five off-ball linebackers on the roster — perhaps a surprising number considering that the group as a whole had its ups and downs over the last few weeks. CB Channing Canada: Three undrafted rookie free agents made it onto New England’s initial 53-man team, the highest such number since 2017. Tight end Tanner Arkin and linebacker Khalil Jacobs had been in that conversation from early on in training camp, but Channing Canada might have come as a surprise. The youngster did have some positive moments, but on the whole appeared to be less actively involved with the top-level defense than other cornerbacks. His relative steadiness compared to some of his competition might have made the difference, though, as might have his ability to line up on special teams, most prominently as a gunner. The preseason injury group: The aforementioned Khalil Jacobs was one of multiple players heading into cutdown weekend facing injury questions. Not all of them were able to make it onto the 53-man team, but a handful of players were. Besides Jacobs, the Patriots have also kept interior offensive lineman Ben Brown and punter Bryce Baringer on their active roster to open the year — a positive development from a depth perspective. Losers DT Eric Gregory: Beyond the top trio of Milton Williams, Christian Barmore and Cory Durden, the Patriots’ interior defensive line was not settled coming out of preseason. This meant that a player like Gregory could have had a realistic shot at making it given that he had some solid moments in camp and at 319 pounds was the heaviest player out of the group, and thus possibly best-suited to fill the vacant nose tackle role. Alas, the team decided to go in a different direction and go with Joshua Farmer as the top backup run defender. CB Kindle Vildor: Signed as an unrestricted free agent in March, Vildor appeared to be in a competitive position to earn a role as a fourth or fifth cornerback since all the way back in the offseason. And while he did have a lull early in training camp, he seemingly was able to bounce back and put himself on the road to the roster by mid-August. However, he never fully grasped a spot and was eventually undone by a bad performance in the preseason finale — so much so that the team opted to carry rookies Karon Prunty and Channing Canada on the 53-man roster over him.
