title: What their final wave of roster cuts means for the Patriots
summary: The New England Patriots came out of Thursday’s preseason finale a total of 38 players over the NFL’s 53-man roster limit. In order to get the team below that number, head coach Mike Vrabel and company needed to make several moves. And make moves they did. For a full rundown of the transactions this weekend, […]
full_text: Aug 13, 2026; Foxborough, Massachusetts, USA; New England Patriots cornerback Kindle Vildor (28) looks on before a game against the Indianapolis Colts at Gillette Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Eric Canha-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The New England Patriots came out of Thursday’s preseason finale a total of 38 players over the NFL’s 53-man roster limit. In order to get the team below that number, head coach Mike Vrabel and company needed to make several moves. And make moves they did. For a full rundown of the transactions this weekend, please head over to our Patriots roster cuts tracker . We already discussed what Saturday’s moves meant for the team , now it’s time to find out more about Sunday’s. Rookie class largely intact The Patriots selected nine players in this year’s NFL Draft, but only three of them came in what is traditionally considered the “safe zone” for rookies to make the team: the first four rounds. Those three — OT Caleb Lomu, ED Gabe Jacas, TE Eli Raridon — all unsurprisingly are part of the initial 53-man roster. The other six did not uniformly make the cut, but a vast majority of them did. The only player to get cut was seventh-round running back Jam Miller, who was let go with an injury designation and therefore remains a candidate to return should he clear waivers. The rest all made the 53, as did undrafted free agents Tanner Arkin, Khalil Jacobs and Channing Canada. For comparison, two of 11 draft picks — Day 3 selections Bradyn Swinson and Kobee Minor — failed to make it onto the initial 53-man roster last year. Momentum not maintained The old saying about the NFL season being a marathon and not a spring is also true for training camp. Just because you look good early doesn’t mean you will remain on an upwards trajectory toward earning a spot on the 53-man roster. Just ask the likes of Bradyn Swinson, Chad Muma, Kindle Vildor and Mike Brown. All four looked to be on their way to earning spots on the roster at various points early in training camp. For one reason or another, however, they now find themselves on the outside looking in — be it because they never emerged past reserve status (Swinson), struggled in preseason (Muma), were inconsistent throughout the summer (Vildor), or never made the expected push (Brown). Leadership void Even though they will remain around the team, two of the Patriots’ captains from a year ago will not be on the active roster to start the season. Outside linebacker Harold Landry will open the year on the physically unable to perform list, with special teams safety Brenden Schooler on the non-football injury/illness list. Both were sent to their respective lists to open training camp, and remain there for at least the first four weeks of the regular season as well. This means that the Patriots will not only miss their contributions on the field, but also off it. Who will replace that part of their presence will be seen, but there are several candidates — from Milton Williams to Kevin Byard or Craig Woodson. “You can’t replace an All-Pro type of guy, so it’s always a loss from that leadership on the field,” Patriots special teams coordinator Jeremy Springer said about Schooler last week. “But he’s always around, he’s around helping us out, and when we get him back, we get him back. But until then, as long as he continues to progress and help our young guys out, that’s what I’m looking for.” Return candidates emerge Including Harold Landry, Brenden Schooler and backup offensive tackle Marcus Bryant — he will start the year on injured reserve with a return designation — the Patriots did move on from 21 players on Sunday. Of those, a large portion can be expected back via the practice squad. The prime candidates include running back Lan Larison, linebacker Chad Muma, safety John Saunders Jr. and punter Matt Haack. All of them were let go on Sunday, with the first three all having to pass through the waiver wire before possibly being retained. Chances are most if not all of them will end up in a position where they could re-sign with New England if they so choose. All eyes on waivers Of the 37 players cut by the Patriots on Saturday and Sunday, all but six — RB Hassan Haskins, RB JaMycal Hasty, OL James Hudson III, ED Jesse Luketa, CB Kindle Vildor, P Matt Haack — are subject to waivers. This means that other teams can bring them aboard via the waiver claim process; they can put in claims in the draft order in hopes of adding as much talent as they please (i.e. as many players as they can fit onto their 53-man roster). As noted above, however, a majority of the players waived by New England will end up passing through the wire without receiving any interest. Salary cap impact The Patriots’ business over the last two days also impacted their salary cap. According to cap expert Miguel Benzan, the team lost a total of $7.395 million through Sunday’s moves alone. New England probably is not overly worried about that number, though. The team still has $24.2 million in cap space at the moment while accounting for 62 contracts: the 53 on the active roster (despite the Top 51 rule officially still being in place until next week) as well as the salaries of seven players on injured reserve, and the aforementioned Harold Landry and Brenden Schooler on the PUP and NFI lists, respectively.

title: Patriots make final 11 moves down to initial 53-man roster
summary: Eleven moves remained in Foxborough. They arrived as the 2026 NFL roster deadline passed Sunday at 6 p.m. ET. The New England Patriots descended down to an initial 53-man roster by waiving running back Lan Larison, wide receiver Tejhaun Palmer, offensive tackle Jack Conley, defensive tackles Isaiah Iton and Casey Rogers, cornerback Kobee Minor and […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - AUGUST 22: Kindle Vildor #28 of the New England Patriots celebrates during an NFL preseason football game against the Philadelphia Eagles at Gillette Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Eleven moves remained in Foxborough. They arrived as the 2026 NFL roster deadline passed Sunday at 6 p.m. ET. The New England Patriots descended down to an initial 53-man roster by waiving running back Lan Larison, wide receiver Tejhaun Palmer, offensive tackle Jack Conley, defensive tackles Isaiah Iton and Casey Rogers, cornerback Kobee Minor and safety John Saunders Jr. The club also released vested veterans in cornerback Kindle Vildor, safety Mike Brown and punter Matt Haack, while outside linebacker Harold Landry III will officially begin the regular season on the physically unable to perform list. Now announced , those marked the last transactions left from a long weekend. Larison, 24, joined the Patriots as part of the organization’s 2025 undrafted class. The 5-foot-11, 209-pound running back out of UC Davis redshirted his rookie year on injured reserve after sustaining a foot injury last August. He went on log 39 rushing yards, 79 receiving yards, 78 kickoff return yards during his sophomore preseason while scoring one touchdown. Palmer, 26, was claimed off waivers during the first week of August. The 6-foot-2, 210-pound wide receiver entered the NFL in the sixth round of the 2024 draft at No. 191 overall after stops at Snow College and UAB. He spent the majority of his initial two regular seasons on the Arizona Cardinals’ practice squad and made his official debut as a member of the 53-man roster last January. Conley, 25, returned to New England in late August after originally entering the league as a rookie free agent out of Boston College in 2025. The 6-foot-7, 325-pounder offensive lineman had two brief stints on the Patriots’ practice squad last campaign. He went on to tour the practice squads of the Detroit Lions and Cleveland Browns. Iton, 24, re-signed with the Patriots heading into training camp in July after spending last year on injured reserve and not being tendered as an exclusive rights free agent in March. The 6-foot-2, 277-pound defensive lineman via Northern Colorado, Hutchinson Community College, Ole Miss and Rutgers had signed following a rookie minicamp tryout in 2025. He entered the league as an undrafted rookie in 2024. Rogers, 27, landed in Foxborough a week into training camp. The 6-foot-4, 294-pound defensive tackle originally entered the NFL as a rookie free agent out of Oregon in 2024. He started his career with the New York Giants, for whom he appeared in three games over two separate stints, and has also spent time with the Buffalo Bills and UFL’s DC Defenders. Minor, 24, became “Mr. Irrelevant” in the seventh round of the 2025 NFL draft at No. 257 overall. The cornerback by way of Texas Tech, Indiana and Memphis went on to appear in four games during his rookie regular season, posting one tackle across 39 snaps on defense and 21 snaps on special teams. Beginning as a member of the practice squad, he served as a three-time standard elevation on the way to taking a 53-man roster spot in January. Saunders, 24, found a series of interceptions in training camp for New England and added another in the preseason. The 6-foot-2, 211-pound safety had been added to the active roster off the practice squad of the Miami Dolphins last fall. He later agreed to remain in the fold as a member of the practice squad after clearing waivers and re-upped on a futures contract. The former Miami RedHawks and Ole Miss safety went undrafted in 2025. Vildor, 29, recorded one interception in preseason action for New England after agreeing to terms in March. The 5-foot-11, 189-pound cornerback entered the NFL with the Chicago Bears in the fifth round of the 2020 draft at No. 163 overall. Amid a series of stops, including last year with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, he has totaled 140 tackles, one sack, one forced fumble and two interceptions while appearing in 80 games and starting 27. Brown, 27, signed as an unrestricted free agent in March. The 6-foot-1, 218-pound safety originally entered the NFL as an undrafted free agent with the Minnesota Vikings out of Miami (Ohio) in 2022 and spent three years with the Tennessee Titans after stints on practice squads. He has played in 38 games, stating five, on the way to totaling 60 tackles and two passes defensed. Haack, 32, agreed to terms with New England leading up to the preseason finale and proceeded to average 46.5 yards per punt with a trio of inside-the-20 efforts and a long of 63. It marked the 10th different NFL stop for Haack, a 2017 undrafted free agent out of Arizona State. The 6-foot, 205-pound left-footed veteran began training camp with the Washington Commanders. Through 110 career games, he has averaged 45 yards per punt and 39.9 net yards per punt. Landry, 30, will now miss at least four games to begin the regular season. The 2025 Patriots captain opened training camp on physically unable to perform and had yet to resume practicing. Prior to arriving in Foxborough, the Boston College product accrued seven campaigns with the Tennessee Titans and earned one Pro Bowl nod. Taken in the second round of the 2018 draft at No. 41 overall, the 6-foot-2, 252-pound outside linebacker has tallied 446 tackles, 59 sacks, two interceptions, one safety, four forced fumbles and two recoveries. Head coach Mike Vrabel’s locker room reduced from 91 to 73 players on the eve of the league’s cutdown deadline. Reports continued to roll in from morning to evening on Sunday. That window saw running back Jam Miller , tight end Jack Westover , offensive linemen Joe Michalski and James Hudson III , defensive tackles Eric Gregory and Jeremiah Pharms Jr. , outside linebacker Bradyn Swinson , inside linebacker Chad Muma all let go from the active fold. Along the way came news that swing tackle Marcus Bryant and special teams captain Brenden Schooler would begin the regular season on injured reserve and the non-football injury list , respectively. And in the final hour, so did a trade with the Minnesota Vikings for lineman Walter Rouse. More movement lies ahead with waiver claims and the formation of practice squads around the NFL set for Monday.

summary: The New Orleans Saints ended the 2026 preseason on a high note, defeating the Dallas Cowboys 27-24 on Friday. This week’s breakout player had an eye-opening performance, though it ultimately wasn’t enough to save him from the chopping block: WR Ronnie Bell. Bell was released by the Saints on Saturday as the team begins trimming its […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CA - AUGUST 22: Ronnie Bell #11 of the New Orleans Saints warms up prior to an NFL preseason game between the New Orleans Saints and the Los Angeles Rams on August 22, 2026, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Greg Fiore/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The New Orleans Saints ended the 2026 preseason on a high note, defeating the Dallas Cowboys 27-24 on Friday. This week’s breakout player had an eye-opening performance, though it ultimately wasn’t enough to save him from the chopping block: WR Ronnie Bell . Bell was released by the Saints on Saturday as the team begins trimming its roster down to 53 players. While that news is undoubtedly disappointing for the former seventh-round pick, his performance in the victory over the Dallas Cowboys was still worth highlighting and could ultimately earn him a spot on the practice squad. Bell finished the game with six receptions on seven targets for 65 yards, including a long of 23 yards. More importantly, he consistently moved the chains, recording four first-down conversions while also recording a contested catch. The 26-year-old posted a team-high 91.7 overall grade from Pro Football Focus, along with a 91.4 receiving grade. That makes his release a little more notable. Bell was competing for a roster spot in a crowded Saints receiver room, and while his performance against Dallas gave him a strong finish to the preseason, the Saints ultimately went in another direction. Still, Bell put some quality film on tape. Cuts like this don’t necessarily mean a player’s chances with the team are over, but the timing is certainly unfortunate. Now, he’ll have to wait for the next opportunity to prove it again.

full_text: ARLINGTON, TEXAS - AUGUST 28: Spencer Rattler #2 of the New Orleans Saints runs with the ball toward the endzone during the second quarter of the 2026 NFL preseason game against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on August 28, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Sam Hodde/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New Orleans Saints were looking to bounce back after being shut out by the Los Angeles Rams when they faced the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on Friday night. Here’s a recap of all the action from the black and gold’s final preseason game. First Quarter Spencer Rattler started at quarterback for New Orleans and converted each of his first two passes for 15 yards as the Saints quickly entered Dallas territory on the opening drive. But the visitors were soon held to a field goal attempt, which Daniel Carlson converted from 38 yards. With Joe Milton starting at quarterback, the Cowboys quickly had a field goal of their own. Brandon Aubrey converted from 49 yards to level the game at 3-3. Rattler returned and continued to complete passes on the ensuing drive, though the bulk of the work was done on the ground through Audric Estime and Kendre Miller. But it was rookie receiver Barion Brown who ran in for a 7-yard score to cap off a 10-play, 71-yard touchdown drive for the Saints, restoring their advantage at 10-3. Milton and the Cowboys offense found themselves instantly in a third-and-long as they returned to the field. But the quarterback was able to extend the drive with a 27-yard pass to Camden Brown. Second Quarter Dallas was soon in another third-and-long situation, but this time had to settle for a field goal. Aubrey converted from 51 yards. Rattler found Estime for 13 yards as the Saints’ ensuing possession began positively. However, the black and gold were eventually forced to punt. The Cowboys offense responded with another decent possession. The highlight of the drive was Milton’s connection with Marquez Valdes-Scantling for 22 yards. But a 57-yard field goal attempt from Aubrey went wide right, and the score remained 10-6. Despite being sacked on the opening play of the next drive, Rattler and the Saints offense came back with a touchdown. A 4th-down run from CJ Donaldson preceded a 33-yard dash by Estime to set up 1st-and-goal, and it was Rattler himself who ran it in from 8 yards for the score. Milton converted all three of his passes on the next drive as Dallas looked for a quick response, but a holding penalty limited Dallas’ momentum. Aubrey was good from 58 yards this time. Third Quarter Sam Howell entered at quarterback for the hosts, and they went three-and-out to begin the half. Meanwhile, Zach Wilson entered for the Saints and completed his first pass to Ronnie Bell for 23 yards. The Saints’ running backs continued to move the ball effectively, and a 13-yard connection from Wilson to Donaldson set up an 11-yard touchdown run from Zamir White to put the black and gold up 24-9. The teams proceeded to exchange punts. As Dallas’ offense returned to the field, Howell found Jordan Hudson for 52 yards on the opening play of the drive. Fourth Quarter Howell then found Hudson again for a 26-yard touchdown pass, with the extra point pulling the Cowboys within one score of their visitors. The Saints then went three-and-out before Dallas came back with a 12-play, 67-yard touchdown drive highlighted by a 21-yard grab in the end zone by Mitch Van Vooren for the score. A successful two-point conversion attempt levelled the game at 24-24. With 6 minutes to play, Wilson and the Saints offense grabbed their opportunity to restore the lead. Wilson was 4/4 for 38 yards on what turned out to be the game-winning drive, and Carlson nailed his 53-yard field goal attempt after the two-minute warning. Trailing 27-24, Howell threw four straight incompletions as the Cowboys turned it over on downs. Wilson knelt out the clock to secure the win for the black and gold, their first of the preseason. Next up is the regular season, with a visit to Detroit on September 13th kicking things off for New Orleans.
author: Sam Mackenzie

title: 5 biggest surprises from the NY Giants’ final cuts
summary: The New York Giants have finally trimmed their 91-man roster down to their initial 53-man roster. Final cuts are a brutal day in the NFL when hundreds of men are looking for new jobs, or seeing their NFL dreams come to an end. It’s also a day that always comes with surprises, both in players […]
full_text: New York Giants center Bryan Hudson | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The New York Giants have finally trimmed their 91-man roster down to their initial 53-man roster. Final cuts are a brutal day in the NFL when hundreds of men are looking for new jobs, or seeing their NFL dreams come to an end. It’s also a day that always comes with surprises, both in players who are cut, and those who aren’t. Much of the Giants’ cuts went as expected and there weren’t any moves that had us exclaiming “what!?” However there were still plenty of surprises to be found, particularly in how multiple moves were done in conjunction with each other. So let’s take a look at some of the biggest surprises as the Giants carved out their initial 53-man roster. Bryan Hudson makes the 53 We got the sense late in camp and the preseason that Lucas Patrick’s job as the backup center could be in danger. After all, he missed a pretty significant amount of time with an “old knee” and 25-year-old Bryan Hudson even got second team work when Patrick returned to the practice field. That sense faded when he came on the field with the second team against the Jets, suggesting that he was firmly entrenched as John Michael Schmitz’s backup. But perhaps we should have listened to our gut here, because Patrick was one of the first really eyebrow raising cuts the Giants made and it seems as though Hudson won the battle in the end. The flip side of this is the former UDFA who started the summer running with the third team and clawed his way up the depth chart to be a primary depth piece. That he was able to unseat a veteran free agent addition and the Giants didn’t want to risk exposing him to the waiver wire is a surprise in and of itself as well. Of course, the Giants might not be done here and could be looking to both continue to upgrade their offensive line depth and perhaps find long-term competition for John Michael Schmitz. 5 wide receivers Reports seem to indicate that cutting Dalen Cambre is a move the Giants didn’t want to make. ambre had a good camp and preseason as both a receiver and special teams player, but he just couldn’t quite do enough to force the team’s hand. He’s a player they’ll likely love to sign to their practice squad as a developmental receiver — but he’ll have to survive the waiver wire first. That could be tough to do with the play he put on tape during the last two preseasons. Adam Schefter has already reported that Braxton Berrios will be part of a series of roster games. The Giants are planning on bringing the veteran receiver and special teams player back for Week 1 against the Dallas Cowboys. However, it’s still a bit eyebrow-raising to see both players get caught in final cutdowns, even if both might be back by the end of the week. Still, it’s a bit jarring to see just five wide receivers on an NFL roster. Releasing Berrios with the intention of bringing him back is a calculated risk, but it’s a risk nonetheless TE Thomas Fidone makes the 53 We need to qualify this one a bit: It isn’t a surprise that the Giants thought Fidone played well enough to make the 53-man roster. He performed well throughout camp and when he got on the field in the preseason. However, those looks all came late because Fidone was generally working with the third team. It was still enough to convince the Giants that he shouldn’t be exposed to the waiver wire. GM Joe Schoen has proven adept at reading the rest of the NFL, and it’s notable that 22 tight ends were drafted this year. That’s the most in nearly a quarter of a century (24 in 2002). Fidone has good play on tape, and he might well have been snapped up if he hit the waiver wire. Fidone might not be safe yet, and he could hit the waiver wire if the Giants make any claims. However, another team would have to waive or release of their players to claim him, so the odds of him making it through waivers might be better. No moves on the defensive front The Giants did trade for the ginormous (that’s the technical term) C.J. Okoye , but didn’t make any moves besides that. I mentioned to Ed when he was putting together his final roster projection that the only pure defensive tackles who should feel secure are D.J. Reader, Shelby Harris, Darius Alexander, and Bobby Jamison-Travis. I fully expected the Giants to bring in more help for their defensive interior. Okoye does qualify, but he also only just started playing the sport in 2023. At the same time, Ed was also unsure of going into the season with just three pure edge defenders. I do believe that the Giants could look at Arvell Reese (or Jack Kelly) as a “break glass” option on the edge, and there will certainly times when Reese walks up to the line of scrimmage to change looks and gap assignments. However, I also believe that Reese’s versatility will be too valuable to Dennard Wilson’s “Ravens Style” defense to be anything more than an emergency edge defender. I was expecting the Giants to try and find some way to get Trace Ford onto the roster, considering how active and disruptive he was in the preseason. Instead, he’s on the waiver wire and is one of the players I am most afraid will be claimed. Ford was highly active and made quite a few splash plays — and pass rusher is quickly becoming the second most valuable position on the field behind quarterback. The front was one area where I was expecting (at least) one more trade, though I wouldn’t be surprised if the Giants claim a defensive tackle. They’re fifth in priority on the waiver wire, and they’ll use that if they get the opportunity. Rookie specialists I can’t say that Ben Mann and Dominic Zvada making the team is a surprise. However, if you had told me 8 months ago that the Giants would be going into the season with two-thirds of their kicking battery being undrafted rookies, I would have said that something had gone very wrong. Instead, it seems as though something has gone very right — at least for now. While Zvada is a whip-thin 6-foot-3, 178 pounds, he has the kind of leg that the Giants largely lacked as Graham Gano declined. Zvada has been accurate, consistent, and has been drilling kicks with enough yardage to spare that he gives confidence that he can be a real weapon should an offensive series fizzle. By the same token, Mann has been crisp and reliable as a long snapper. There is very little margin for error in the operation at this level, and even slight miscues that we wouldn’t even notice on TV can spell doom for a field goal attempt. Yet Mann has been all but invisible on the field, and that’s the best compliment I can give him. Teams generally have little appetite for rookie specialists and almost always err on the side of experience. It says something that Zvada and Mann haven’t allowed any room for doubt to creep in.
author: Chris Pflum

title: NY Giants’ 53-man roster analysis: A player-by-player look at the initial 53
summary: The New York Giants have set their initial 53-man roster. The roster will likely change in the next 24 hours as waiver claims can be made until 1 p.m. ET on Monday. The Giants are No. 5 in the claiming order, so they should have an opportunity to add a player or two should they […]
full_text: The New York Giants have set their initial 53-man roster. The roster will likely change in the next 24 hours as waiver claims can be made until 1 p.m. ET on Monday. The Giants are No. 5 in the claiming order, so they should have an opportunity to add a player or two should they desire. When practice squads begin being assembled Monday afternoon, you can follow our practice squad tracker . A couple of quick thoughts: Good for Odell Beckham Jr. He earned his roster spot . Wide receiver Darius Slayton will make the initial roster after much speculation that he would not. Draft picks Jalin Hyatt, Darius Muasau, Evan Neal, and Eric Gray were among the players let go. Elijah Campbell made the roster as a special teamer. Dalen Cambre did not. Quarterback (2) Jaxson Dart — All the feel-good stories around the Giants with John Harbaugh now running the show won’t metter if Dart doesn’t take a big step forward in his second season. I think he will. Jameis Winston — The respect his teammates have for Winston was evidenced by the backup quarterback being named to the team’s Leadership Council. Winston is the type of veteran backup every team would like to have. One more thought Will Brandon Allen or Jake Haener stick on the practice squad as QB3, or will the Giants look elsewhere? Running back (4) Cam Skattebo — Skattebo has been running over and annoying teammates recently. They will be happy to see him run through somebody else. Najee Harris — When the Giants signed Harris after their first preseason game, Harbaugh said the veteran running back coming back from a torn Achilles tendon would be ready for Week 1. The 11 carries he got against the Jets would indicate that was on target. The 6-foot-1, 242-pound Harris is a physical back perfect for a Harbaugh team. Devin Singletary — During training camp, Harbaugh lauded Singletary’s consistency. Singletary isn’t speedy, but doing what you are supposed to do when you are supposed to do it is worth something. Tyrone Tracy — After a tumultuous summer, the third-year back is still on the roster. Fullback (1) Patrick Ricard — Yes, we get to see Skattebo and Harris run behind a 300-pound fullback. Tight end (4) Isaiah Likely — Likely emerged as a favorite target for Dart during the summer, especially in gotta have it situations. The Giants need Likely to be a major factor in their passing attack. Theo Johnson — The 2024 fourth-round pick is probably in the role that suits him best as a pass-catching No. 2 tight end. Chris Manhertz — The veteran blocking tight end is part of the team’s Leadership Council. His spot was never really in doubt. Thomas Fidone — Dan Duggan reported Fidone making the roster because “he’s the type of young player they definitely wanted to guard from hitting waivers.” I wasn’t certain the Giants would find room for the second-year player on the roster, but they have. At least for now. It didn’t hurt Fidone that Johnson has been dealing with a shoulder injury. Wide receiver (5) Malik Nabers — Nabers remains on track to play in the season-opener against the Dallas Cowboys. How close to his 2024 form will he look? Darnell Mooney — Maybe the Giants solicited offers for Mooney before the Calvin Austin injury. Maybe they did not. Either way, he is now on the roster and will be counted on to be a play-maker. Malachi Fields — The rookie third-round pick should have a big role as a receiver this season. Darius Slayton — After much speculation that Slayton would not make the team, he did. Slayton has been counted out before and produced good numbers for the Giants. Can he do it again? Odell Beckham Jr. — Cout me as a person who thought the Giants should have steered clear of giving Beckham a chance to make a comeback. Beckham, though, seems different than he was as a young player a decade ago. He earned his spot on the roster by getting on the practice field every day, and showing that he could both get open and still catch the football. Three more thoughts I had a feeling I would be wrong about Cambre making the roster. I do wonder if he gets picked up by someone. The Giants are playing roster gymnastics with Braxton Berrios. A vested veteran not subject to waivers, Adam Schefter is reporting that he should be back with the Giants before Week 1 . Pretty weird to see only five wide receivers on the initial roster, although Berrios is likely coming back. Offensive line (9) Andrew Thomas — When he is healthy, Thomas is one of the best left tackles in the NFL. He has had a healthy spring and summer, and has been able to practice every day. That bodes well for his 2026 season. Jon Runyan Jr. — In the spring, there was conjecture that Runyan could face a challenge for his starting left guard job. That never materialized. Runyan isn’t the mauling guard Harbaugh might prefer, but he is an adequate NFL starter. John Michael Schmitz — This is a big year for Schmitz. He is an adequate NFL starting center. In the final year of his rookie contract, can he show the Giants he is worth a second contract? Francis Mauigoa — The No. 10 overall pick was excellent during preseason. NY Giants 1st Round Rookie, Francis Mauigoa, had an incredible preseason. As of last night, he had the highest impact play rate percentile of any RG this preseason. Also nice to Deonte Banks making waves at the outside CB position. pic.twitter.com/D41RPUVQG6 — Matt Stopsky (@MStopsky) August 29, 2026 Can he carry that kind of play through the regular season? Jermaine Eluemunor — A rock-solid pass protector, can the veteran right tackle be a more consistent run blocker in 2026? Harbaugh will demand it. Marcus Mbow — I have long thought Mbow would be the swing tackle. I do wonder, though, if Mbow would get the nod over J.C. Davis at left tackle if something happened to Thomas. J.C. Davis — Until a couple of weeks ago, I didn’t believe the rookie sixth-round pick was making the roster. Now, keeping him on the roster was the only choice. Bryan Hudson — A practice squad member last season, Hudson got the nod over Lucas Patrick as the backup center. Aaron Stinnie — The veteran guard doesn’t get muh attention. He remains, though, a plug-and-play veteran who can step in if there is an emergency. Defensive line (6) D.J. Reader — In his 11th season, the 32-year-old is being counted on to anchor the Giants’ run defense. The Giants need to hope Reader’s two seasons with the Detroit Lions weren’t signs of a decline. Shelby Harris — Entering his 12th season, the 35-year-old Harris has long been a durable, quality player. He has played more than 500 snaps in four of the past five seasons. Does he still have enough in the tank to be a primary player on the interior of the Giants’ defensive line? C.J. Okoye — The Giants knew they needed help on the defensive line, and they turned to a player Harbaugh and defensive line coach Dennis Johnson are familiar with to get it. Okoye is a monstrous 6-foot-6, 365-pound player who is still relatively new to the game and should have immense upside at 24 years of age. Chauncey Golston — The versatile Golston couldn’t find a steady role on the defense a year ago. This summer, he emerged as a base 3-4 defensive end. It is going to be interesting to see how much Golston plays, and how impactful he is. Darius Alexander — After a preseason where his run defense has been questioned, you have to wonder how High Alexander will be in the pecking order when it comes to playing time. Bobby Jamison-Travis — Like Fidone, the rookie sixth-round pick probably fits the category of a young player the Giants did not want to risk exposing to waivers. Off-ball linebacker (5) Arvell Reese — This young man, the No. 5 overall pick, is going to be a star if he remains healthy. Tremaine Edmunds — I wasn’t sure that the Giants did the right thing when they signed Edmunds to a three-year, $36 million contract ($23.7 million guaranteed) this offseason. After watching the Reese-Edmunds combination, I feel much better about it. Micah McFadden — Maybe…

title: Aaron Donald return: Week 2 just got scarier for the Giants
summary: Party like it’s 2014, because not only is wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr. back with the New York Giants, defensive tackle Aaron Donald is back with the Los Angeles Rams. In a move that we all suspected was coming, the all-time great defensive tackle announced that he is unretiring to play for the Rams in […]
full_text: Los Angeles Rams defensive tackle Aaron Donald | Getty Images Party like it’s 2014, because not only is wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr. back with the New York Giants, defensive tackle Aaron Donald is back with the Los Angeles Rams. In a move that we all suspected was coming, the all-time great defensive tackle announced that he is unretiring to play for the Rams in 2026. At the same time, about 85 offensive linemen all swore under their breath. The Giants won’t have to wait long to see him in action, as they see the Rams in Week 2. Yes, Donald is 35 years old and retired after the 2023 season. However, he was still one of the most fearsome defensive tackles in the NFL when he retired. As Mina Kimes pointed out , Donald still led all defensive tackles in pass rush win rate despite teams routinely double and triple-teaming him. We don’t know what Donald has left after two years away from football, though it’d be foolhardy to think he won’t still be (at least) be a dangerous rotational pass rusher. And that’s what really makes the move scary. The Rams’ defensive front was already loaded after their trade for reigning DPOY and single-season sack king Myles Garrett . Garrett and Donald will now join forces with defensive tackles Braden Fiske , Kobie Turner , and Poona Ford , as well as starting edge defender Byron Young . The biggest saving grace for the Giants in Week 2 will be that the Rams have to travel back to Los Angeles from their Week 1 game in Australia. No team has ever done that before, and we simply don’t know how it’ll impact their recovery and preparation. Beyond that, the Giants will have their work cut out for them when it comes to game planning on offense. They’ll likely need to get creative to get the ball out of quarterback Jaxson Dart ’s hand safely, as well as do what they can to help interior linemen Jon Runyan Jr. , John Michael Schmitz , and rookie Sisi Mauigoa . The offense will likely have to get some help from the Giants’ own defense to keep Rams’ quarterback Matthew Stafford from putting too much pressure on the Giants to keep up in a shootout. This was never going to be an easy game, and we might see some truly funny odds from Vegas on it.

title: Odell Beckham will make the NY Giants’ 53-man roster
summary: Odell Beckham Jr. will be part of the New York Giants’ 2026 roster. Jordan Schultz reported that Beckham has made the team. After Friday’s preseason game against the New York Jets, Giants head coach John Harbaugh had said Beckham “has done enough to make an NFL roster.” At the time, though, he did not commit […]
full_text: Odell Beckham after making a catch Friday against the Jets. | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Odell Beckham Jr. will be part of the New York Giants’ 2026 roster. Jordan Schultz reported that Beckham has made the team . After Friday’s preseason game against the New York Jets, Giants head coach John Harbaugh had said Beckham “has done enough to make an NFL roster.” At the time, though, he did not commit to Beckham making the Giants’ roster. Now, that appears to be a reality. The 13th overall pick by the Giants in the 2014 NFL Draft, Beckham starred for the Giants for five seasons before they traded him to the Cleveland Browns. Beckham had four 1,000-yard receiving seasons with New York, and his flamboyant personality and incredible ability made him a celebrity and international superstar. Since being traded by the Giants, Beckham has played for the Browns, Los Angeles Rams, Baltimore Ravens, and Miami Dolphins. Beckham’s last 1,000-yard receiving season came in 2019 with Cleveland. His last productive season as an NFL player was 23 with the Ravens, when he caught 35 passes for 565 yards. Beckham caught just nine passes in nine games for the Dolphins in 2024, and did not play in the NFL last season. For his career, Beckham has 575 receptions for 7,987 yards. His relationship with John Harbaugh, his coach with the Ravens in 2023, led to Beckham getting an opportunity at a comeback with the Giants. In three preseason games, Beckham caught seven passes for 76 yards, an average of 10.9 yards per catch. His longest catch was a 23-yarder in the preseason finale against the New York Jets. When the Giants signed Beckham in June, Harbaugh said that he has high expectations for Beckham. “You can’t be just okay. You’re Odell Beckham,” Harbaugh said. “You’ve got to come out here and you have to be performing at a high level in workout, you’ve got to be performing at a high level in practice. You got to be a guy capable that we can see would have a chance to make a difference in NFL games. You have to be that kind of player.” Apparently Harbaugh believes that Beckham can be a difference maker for the Giants.
author: Ed Valentine

title: Giants waive a former starting linebacker in Darius Muasau
summary: The New York Giants made the first move of their final cutdowns that could be viewed as a surprise. The team waived LB Darius Muasau on Sunday afternoon, ending the 2024 6th round pick’s time with the Giants’ active roster. At first blush, waiving an athletically limited sixth-round pick after a couple years isn’t a […]
full_text: ﻿Darius Muasau | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The New York Giants made the first move of their final cutdowns that could be viewed as a surprise. The team waived LB Darius Muasau on Sunday afternoon, ending the 2024 6th round pick’s time with the Giants’ active roster. At first blush, waiving an athletically limited sixth-round pick after a couple years isn’t a surprising move. However, it is notable thanks to how Muasau stepped in as a starter over the last two seasons. The former UCLA linebacker has played in 27 games for the Giants over the last two years, with 18 starts at linebacker. He was never a great linebacker for the Giants, but his football IQ and competitive toughness allowed him to outplay perceptions of him when he was on the field. Muasau played 1,231 snaps for the Giants over the last two years between defense and special teams, most of which came on defense. It’s a mark of just how much the Giants have improved their linebacking corps that there isn’t even room to keep Muasau as a special teams player, let alone defensive depth. His is a name we’ll be watching to see if he signs with the Giants’ practice squad or if he’s claimed by another team. Follow our tracker for all the moves.

title: Giants practice squad tracker 2026: Predictions, signings, analysis
summary: The New York Giants are in the process of making the big cutdown from 90 to their initial 53-man roster. Once that’s done, the next big order of business for the Giants is to assemble their practice squad for the start of the season. The Giants have until 1 p.m. ET on Monday, Aug. 31 […]
full_text: ﻿A New York Giants helmet | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The New York Giants are in the process of making the big cutdown from 90 to their initial 53-man roster. Once that’s done, the next big order of business for the Giants is to assemble their practice squad for the start of the season. The Giants have until 1 p.m. ET on Monday, Aug. 31 to claim players on the waiver wire. They can then begin signing players to their practice squad. Vested veterans (veterans with at least four accrued seasons) can be signed immediately after being released by their former team, while non-vested players must pass through waivers before being signed to the practice squad. The Giants can have up to six (6) veterans on their practice squad, and any practice squad player can be elevated to the active roster on game day three times in a season without having to be signed to the active roster or subject to the waiver wire. The Giants are still (as of this writing) 2.5-point underdogs week 1 against the Dallas Cowboys, per FanDuel . And while being able to elevate a player off the practice squad is unlikely to swing those odds, having emergency depth — or not having it — has played a role in the outcome of games for the Giants before. The NFL’s practice squads are typically 16 players, with a 17th spot set aside for players in the International Pathway Program. For the Giants, 6-foot-7, 318-pound offensive lineman Jarrod Gray seems to be the likely candidate for that spot. Gray is a former rugby star from Australia who spent the summer as the 91st player on the Giants’ roster as an International player. 2026 practice squad signings To come as players are signed

Arian Smith made the team after a terrible set of performances in the preseason, but with his 4th round […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PA - AUGUST 21: Geno Smith #7 of the New York Jets warms up before the game against the Pittsburgh Steelers at Acrisure Stadium on August 21, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images) | Getty Images Good morning Gang Green Nation! Yesterday all NFL teams were required to cut down their rosters to the final 53 by 6 pm EDT. The New York Jets made their cuts, and there were few surprises. Arian Smith made the team after a terrible set of performances in the preseason, but with his 4th round draft pick status from a year ago and an uninspiring set of options at wide receiver behind Smith, this was not completely unexpected. Braiden McGregor made the team and Nate Lynn did not, but with Lynn arriving here less than two weeks before cuts, he probably never had enough time to make his case. Lynn is probably headed for the practice squad and may earn a call up at some point. Today the Jets get a chance to add more talent at the back end of the roster through the waiver wire. Mandatory Credit: Barry Reeger-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Jets have selected the players for their initial roster in 2026 . The work is not finished, however. The team can now begin assembling its practice squad. NFL teams are allowed to assemble a 17 players practice squad. These players practice with the team and attend meetings through the week. Every week, two players can be activated from the practice squad to play in games. These players do not need to be added to the active roster the first three times they are activated for a game. The fourth time, however, the team must add them to the 53 man roster. Practice squad players are technically free agents and able to sign with the active roster of any team aside from upcoming opponents. Who is eligible for the practice squad? Teams can use up to 16 of their 17 slots on players with no NFL seasons or one season (with less than nine games played) if they so choose. For a fully stocked practice squad, the minimum number of players with this level of experience is 6. Teams are also allowed to choose up to 10 practice squad players with more experience. No more than six can have more than two years of experience in the NFL. Finally, one spot must go to an international player. We will keep track of the players the Jets sign to the practice squad below.

title: How does the waiver wire work after cutdown day for the Jets?
summary: Today is cutdown day in the NFL. Teams must have their rosters at 53 players by 6:00 pm Eastern Time. Over the next day or two, you will hear a lot about the waiver wire. You might be curious what that is. Inevitably, players who are released today will generate interest from other teams across […]
full_text: Jan 27, 2025; Florham Park, NJ, USA; New York Jets head coach Aaron Glenn looks on during an introductory press conference at Atlantic Health Jets Training Center. Mandatory Credit: John Jones-Imagn Images | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Con Today is cutdown day in the NFL. Teams must have their rosters at 53 players by 6:00 pm Eastern Time. Over the next day or two, you will hear a lot about the waiver wire. You might be curious what that is. Inevitably, players who are released today will generate interest from other teams across the league. There is a good chance 54th best player on the Seahawks (who will be cut) is better than the 53rd best player on the Jets (who initially will be on the roster). How can the Jets acquire players who other teams cut? It depends on how much NFL experience they have. Players with at least four years of NFL service time instantly become free agents. Their contract is terminated immediately, and they are free to sign a new deal with any team to be on the roster or the practice squad. For players with less than four years of experience, it is a tad more complicated. These guys are subjected to the waiver process. The other 31 teams will have an opportunity to claim that player if they want him. If they put in a claim, they will be awarded that player, and his current contract is absorbed by that team. If nobody claims a player, he is said to have “cleared waivers.” Only at this point does his contract terminate, and he becomes a free agent able to sign with any team’s roster or practice squad. Additionally players the Jets waive will need to clear waivers before they can be signed to the practice squad. What happens if more than one team claims a player? He goes to the team with the highest waiver priority. Until we get three weeks into the regular season, the priority is determined by where that team’s pick fell in the first round of the most recent NFL Draft. The Jets picked second overall in the spring so they have the second priority on the waiver wire. For all intents and purposes, that means the Jets will get any player they claim off waivers unless the Raiders also claim that player. Those of you who play fantasy football might be familiar with the waiver wire and how priority works. In many fantasy leagues, if you successfully claim a player you immediately move to the bottom of the priority list. That’s not how it works in the NFL. The Jets remain number two no matter how many players they claim. The waiver process is designed to help the weaker teams get stronger. The Jets currently have +25000 odds to win the Super Bowl according to our partner , FanDuel Sportsbook so the oddsmakers clearly believe they can use all the help they can get. The first batch of waiver claims will be announced tomorrow. If the Jets add any players from waivers, they will need to clear a spot on their roster.

At the same time, it’s very on brand for how weird this QB2 situation has been every step of the way. Guess the Eagles holding onto both Dalton and McKee with the hope that a team will trade for one in the coming days? If so, great. But you can’t expect the return will be much. And it could’ve been nice to just actually focus on preparing QB2 for the season instead of doing a competition where the players split the reps and seemingly did not benefit from that setup. SB Nation Launches App Home for Its 200 Fan Communities – Sportico SB Nation is launching an app to pull together content and chats from its network of close to 200 team- and league-focused sports communities. The launch comes as artificial intelligence impacts the amount of web search traffic media publishers receive and algorithmic, video-heavy social media feeds alter how fans connect with each other on game days. The app’s home page will feature a personalized list of posts from a user’s preferred sites, with another tab dedicated to game threads. “People are exhausted by the toxicity of the conversation on social, but they’re also exhausted by feeling like AI worms its way into these conversations,” SB Nation’s head of network John Ness said. “What we supply to folks is like, I feel like I’m talking to real fans who care about what I care about, and it feels like once again I’m having an authentic conversation about the team that spends so much time in my brain overall.” Ness added that users currently talk about being a member of one of the company’s communities, such as the Philadelphia Eagles’ Bleeding Green Nation, but—until now—there was no formal way to signal that support. An audience of readers who go directly to a site is increasingly valuable as certain media leaders talk about a future in which Google potentially sends them close to zero referral traffic if AI answers become more popular. [BLG Note: Hey, a BGN mention AND an NFC East Mixtape mention in this article! Go download the SB Nation app!] Eagles’ Week 1 opponent will be missing several important players; waived players who make sense – PhillyVoice QB Will Levis: Levis is 6’4, 229, he has a big arm, and he can run around a little bit. There’s talent there, and he was not exactly drafted into the best situation in Tennessee. On the downside, he has had some of the more ridiculous lowlights of the last decade. The Eagles already have had a weird, non-sensical offseason in their handling of the backup quarterbacks, and they still have to get rid of one of them. I’m certainly not suggesting they add one to the mess they have on their active roster. But if Levis clears waivers is he worth a spot on the practice squad, just to get a look? Sure, why not? Backup WBs have mostly been needed late in the season. You can’t count on that, but it is worth noting. I’ve talked about how Howie does a good job of building rosters with one eye on the present and one on the future. This roster feels more like it was built for the present. There are 5 rookies (Lemon, Stowers, Bell, Morris and Payton), but a couple of them could be playing this season. Keeping guys like Moore and Jones makes this feel more about today than tomorrow. Vandervelde and Havili made their way back to the practice squad and both wound up playing for the Eagles – 18 games for Vandervelde and 15 for Rolle. We’ll learn Monday whether Wisniewski, Bernard and James-Newby clear waivers and find their way back to the Eagles’ practice squad. Who made the cut? title: NFL waiver wire rules and the Eagles’ position in the claiming order
summary: The NFL roster deadline has come and past, and teams have their initial 53-man roster as of Sunday, August 30 at 6 pm ET. Now, teams get an opportunity to put a claim on any player subject to the waiver wire — and they have until Monday, August 31 at 1:00 pm ET to make […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - AUGUST 22: Willie Lampkin #61 of the Philadelphia Eagles warms up before the preseason game against the New England Patriots at Gillette Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Maddie Meyer/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NFL roster deadline has come and past, and teams have their initial 53-man roster as of Sunday, August 30 at 6 pm ET. Now, teams get an opportunity to put a claim on any player subject to the waiver wire — and they have until Monday, August 31 at 1:00 pm ET to make those decisions. Players claimed will head off to their new teams, and those that pass through unclaimed, will become unrestricted free agents. From there, teams will fill their 16-man practice squads and finalize things heading into Week 1 of the regular season. Not all players are subject to the waiver wire, however, vested veterans — players who have four years of accrued NFL service time — are outright released. Those players became free agents right away. Teams who are concerned about losing a young player on the waiver wire, might consider releasing a vested veteran on the bubble instead, whom they can bring back immediately on the practice squad, or to the active roster after moving someone else to the scout team. The Eagles currently sit at the No. 23 spot on the waiver wire, which mirrors the 2026 NFL Draft order. Last year, Howie Roseman claimed center Willie Lampkin, who was waived by the Los Angeles Rams. And Lampkin has been a training camp standout this summer. Here’s the full waiver wire order The NFL waiver order during the preseason and the first three weeks of the regular season reflects the 2026 NFL Draft order, and then after four games, the order resets to the current league standings. So, right now, the Raiders currently have first pick at every player on waivers. The wire order is also fixed, so the Raiders will get first rights to every single player available regardless of whether they pick one (or many). CB Jakorian Bennett TE Grant Calcaterra PRACTICE SQUAD The Eagles can start signing players to their 16-man practice squad starting on Monday afternoon. THOUGHTS The Eagles kept 27 players on offense and 23 on defense. Last year at this time, the Eagles initially kept 26 players on offense and 25 on defense. The Eagles keeping four quarterbacks feels very silly. At the same time, it’s very on brand for how weird this QB2 situation has been every step of the way. Guess the Eagles holding onto both Dalton and McKee with the hope that a team will trade for one in the coming days? If so, great. But you can’t expect the return will be much. And it could’ve been nice to just actually focus on preparing QB2 for the season instead of doing a competition where the players split the reps and seemingly did not benefit from that setup. Not to mention trying to get Cole Payton developmental snaps in the preseason, which they didn’t really do outside of the first preseason game. Howie Roseman typically has a pretty good sense of which players are going to get claimed or not; you have to give him the benefit of the doubt with these kind of decisions. But in the event that at least one of the interesting players the Eagles waived does get claimed while the Eagles opted to keep four quarterbacks … that’ll be annoying. We’ll see. Some were surprised to see Carson Steele didn’t make the team but he looked better in the preseason games than he did in practice all camp long. Decent chance he’s back on the practice squad. He might not be RB4, though, because Dameon Pierce would probably be ahead of him if he’s back as well. Hollywood Brown didn’t have a great camp but he did enough by the end to prevent the team from moving on. That and cutting him wasn’t ideal from a financial perspective. Elijah Moore earned his spot on the roster with a very productive training camp. Doesn’t hurt that Jalen Hurts seems to be comfortable targeting him. I wonder if his inclusion on the roster is at least partially connected to Makai Lemon potentially not being ready for a major role very early in the season. Eli Stowers’ hamstring injury apparently isn’t serious enough to warrant a stint on injured reserve/designated for return. But we’ll see if the Eagles still move him to IR in the coming days. Stowers could conceivably be a healthy scratch, at least early in the season, if he avoids IR. E.J. Jenkins making the roster is a slight surprise. Thought they would go with Cameron Latu since he’s been a special teams standout. But Jenkins can also help there and the team seems to like his blocking. Good for him. Of course, he could be in jeopardy if the Eagles are able to find tight end help via waivers or trade in the coming days. Markel Bell’s thumb/leg injuries could have saved Fred Johnson from being cut. Bell might be the top swing tackle action if/when he’s healthy. Or at least the top backup at one spot. Johnson is more experienced but Bell had the better summer. And the rookie obviously offers more upside as well. Micah Morris did enough to earn his roster spot. But he’ll likely be a healthy scratch all year if the Eagles avoid multiple interior offensive line injuries. Drew Kendall is probably the top backup at both guard spots and center. With the Eagles likely keeping eight offensive linemen active, it’s the starters … plus Kendall. That’s six. The remaining two will come from Fred Johnson, Bell, and Lampkin. Very good news: Jonathan Greenard is able to begin the season on the roster and not the reserve/PUP list. He is not automatically ineligible to play in the Eagles’ first four games. Will he play in Week 1? Recent indications suggest not. But even if he’s able to play in that Week 4 game (against the Los Angeles Rams, who just brought Aaron Donald back ) at the latest, that’s worth not putting him on PUP. Interested to see how the playing time at edge rusher works out. The Eagles are pretty deep there. Greenard is an established player, Hunt had an awesome summer, Smith shouldn’t be slept on, Epenesa looks more than capable of contributing, and Ebiketie has something to offer as well. Early in camp, it looked like Ty Robinson was in danger of not making the team. He really turned things around to justify his roster spot. I still doubt he’ll be ahead of Byron Young (unless his recent injury flares up again). Vic Fangio said that Robinson still must prove himself against starting level competition. You have to feel good about the Eagles’ linebacker starters and depth. Nice to be able to say that now after years of that being far from the case. The Eagles will probably add Chance Campbell and/or Deontae Lawson to the practice squad for even more depth at that spot. The Eagles’ starting cornerback trio is set. The backup situation is less clear. Kelee Ringo making the team isn’t a surprise in the sense that he can help on special teams, at the very least, and Fangio talked him up a bit recently. Is he the top backup option on the outside? Could be. But the Eagles also kept Jones, who was a vested veteran, and he could contend for that spot. Jones also has experience at nickel corner as well. McWilliams looked better in practices than in games this season. Based on merit, it’s surprising he made the team. He could be in danger if the Eagles want to open up a roster spot in the coming days. The Eagles are going a bit lighter at safety but keep in mind that DeJean will be playing safety in base defense packages. Still, Mukuba and Epps are the only two true full-time safeties on the roster. Carter II has been learning that position after previously playing nickel corner, where he could still provide depth. Carter II is also likely the extra defensive back in the Eagles’ dime packages. Kudos to Underwood for making the team as an undrafted rookie free agent. It won’t take long for him to be in jeopardy if bad snaps become an issue, though. Surprised the Eagles are keeping Bennett around. I mean, no great reason to not stash him away on injured reserve/designated for return. But it just didn’t seem like they were keen on him. But I guess they don’t feel great about their corner depth and figured they might as well…

Porter dealt with a back injury at the start of camp, but contract talks are a significant reason why he remained sidelined. He is now eligible to resume practicing with the team. If Porter Jr. remained on PUP, he would have missed the first four games of the season. Whether this means Porter will actually begin practicing while he seeks a long-term contract remains to be seen. The Steelers traded 2023 first-round pick Broderick Jones to the Dallas Cowboys this weekend, but locked up three other members of the class this offseason. Nick Herbig, Darnell Washington, and Keeanu Benton all signed lucrative deals, while Porter Jr. remains the last unsigned impactful player. As the best of the bunch, it’s surprising the Steelers didn’t prioritize Porter Jr. to start, but NFL Network insider Ian Rapoport expects Porter Jr. to be the highest-paid cornerback in the measure. Porter Jr. hasn’t spoken publicly since being placed on the PUP list, and Mike McCarthy said last week that talks are at an “impasse” between Porter Jr. and the Steelers. full_text: The Pittsburgh Steelers will be without one of their top defenders in the secondary to start the season. The Steelers have placed safety DeShon Elliott on IR. Elliott will now miss at least the first four games of the season. After suffering a significant leg injury in Week 8 against the Packers and missing the remainder of the 2025 season, Elliott fought his way back onto the field this training camp. He made his return to live action against the Jets on August 21, but did not play against the Bills on Thursday. Injuries limited Elliott to only five games last year, totaling 38 tackles, one sack, and one interception. Elliott signed a two-year extension in June of 2025 that keeps him under contract through 2027. The Steelers’ secondary is already thin and missing Elliott is a significant blow. Pittsburgh signed veteran Jaquan Brisker in the offseason and has occasionally deployed Jalen Ramsey at safety, needing to fill a gap left by Elliott. Seventh-round pick Robert Spears-Jennings also made the initial 53-man roster, and veteran Rayshawn Jenkins will also be expected to play a major role in Elliott’s absence. The Steelers list Ramsey as a nickel corner, but did play some safety in Mike Tomlin’s defense. The Atlanta Falcons visit Acrisure Stadium for the season opener two weeks from now on September 13. summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers have cut their roster down to 53 players, and their 2026 season will officially begin in two weeks when they host the Atlanta Falcons. full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - DECEMBER 21: The Pittsburgh Steelers logo is pictured on a helmet during the game against the Detroit Lions at Ford Field on December 21, 2025 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Nic Antaya/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers have cut their roster down to 53 players, and their 2026 season will officially begin in two weeks when they host the Atlanta Falcons. Pittsburgh is currently a three-point favorite, per FanDuel Sportsbook The roster moves aren’t done, though, as Pittsburgh will now build its practice squad. Practice squads have been expanded in recent years, and with roster elevation rules, the squads can play important roles in not just long-term development, but even game days. Follow along here at BTSC for all the latest on the Steelers’ 2026 practice squad. Steelers practice squad signings 2026 Practice squad basics NFL practice squads currently fit 16 players, with an additional 17th spot for International Pathway Program players. Outside linebacker Julius Welschof has filled this exemption in recent seasons for Pittsburgh. Only six players on the practice squad can have unlimited past NFL seasons. A maximum of 10 players with up to two accrued seasons are allowed. However, the number of players in those two categories cannot exceed 10 total players . All players with no accrued seasons, or fewer than nine regular-season games in one accrued season, are eligible. Accrued seasons are seasons (six-plus games) spent on a 53-man roster, the active-inactive list, or on injured reserve or reserve PUP. Teams can temporarily promote two practice squad players per week to the active roster. However, they can only do so up to three times per player before having to officially sign that player to the 53-man roster. Teams can “protect” four practice squad players each week from being poached (signed to another 53-man roster) by another team.

full_text: PITTSBURGH, PA - OCTOBER 09: Isaac Redman #33 of the Pittsburgh Steelers runs with the ball against the Tennessee Titans during the game on October 9, 2011 at Heinz Field in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Jared Wickerham/Getty Images) | Getty Images The votes are in. The numbers have been tallied. The BTSC readers have spoken. And the winner of the 2026 Isaac Redman Award is… Rookie defensive lineman Gabriel Rubio. Rubio held the lead throughout the entire process, and when the polls closed, he had secured 43% of the vote. Second place, rookie safety Robert Spears-Jennings, also made a strong push for the award with 28%. An award meant to celebrate players who emerged from the “furthest reaches of obscurity to reach general heightened fame and appeal” among Steeler fans during the preseason, it’s hard to argue that anyone fit the bill better than Rubio. Drafted in the sixth round, the big defensive tackle received hardly any draft buzz despite playing at Notre Dame, eliciting plenty of “Who?” reactions when his name was announced. However, during the preseason he quickly played his way from unknown status to becoming a 53-man roster favorite, showing great run-stuffing ability and even some power as a pass rusher. And as the cutdown deadline approaches and the Steelers have already cut Dean Lowry and Esezi Otomewo, Rubio’s roster odds are looking strong. The son of another former Pittsburgh draft pick in Angel Rubio, Gabriel has added another highlight to his family’s Steelers legacy.

full_text: PITTSBURGH, PA - DECEMBER 15: Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. (24) rallies the fans in the fourth quarter during the game between the Pittsburgh Steelers and the Miami Dolphins at Acrisure Stadium on December 15, 2025 in Pittsburgh, PA. (Photo by Shelley Lipton/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers have been more than willing to dish out money for new contracts this offseason. First, the team handed edge rusher Nick Herbig a four-year, $100 million contract. Not long after, the Steelers extended tight end Darnell Washington on a four-year $42 million deal. Most recently, the team gave defensive tackle Keeanu Benton a four-year $72 million contract. All of these players were a part of the 2023 draft class, but the biggest contract extension domino from the infamous 2023 class in cornerback Joey Porter Jr. has yet to fall. Appearing on SportsCenter, ESPN NFL insider Jeremy Fowler provided an update on the contract stalemate between the star corner and the Steelers. Fowler added that Porter Jr. may be upset that the franchise is prioritizing extensions with other players from his draft class. “This one is a classic stalemate. I’m told the player has not been happy with the way things have gone because they paid other players,” Fowler said. “They haven’t made him a formal offer to measure with his skillset. He feels like he’s been a really good corner for them, and it’s a situation where they want him to play out the contract essentially because they haven’t made him an offer.” Earlier in the week, Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy described the contract situation as an “impasse” between the player and organization. This latest update suggests that Porter Jr. has some hard feelings about the way the organization has treated him compared to others from his draft class. The more we learn about the situation, the more it becomes clear that there is still a lot to work through. Jeremy Fowler is as good as it gets when it comes to NFL insiders. This report on Joey Porter Jr. provides some new information. Like Peezy Jr not being happy that guys from his draft class have gotten paid this offseason. And not him. This doesn’t look good. pic.twitter.com/FqjBYqSl1m — Andrew Fillipponi (@ThePoniExpress) August 29, 2026 All reports continue to suggest that the Steelers haven’t made the star corner an initial offer. With the regular season just about two weeks away, something is going to give between the Steelers and Porter Jr. Whenever a deal is made, Porter Jr. is expected to become one of the highest-paid defensive backs in the league, making upwards of $30 million per season. title: Seahawks 2026 practice squad tracker
summary: The Seattle Seahawks took care first part of their roster-building process for the 2026 season. Seattle begins its Super Bowl repeat push on Sept. 9 against the New England Patriots, a familiar opponent after the Seahawks defeated New England to win Super Bowl 60. The defending champions are currently 3.5-point favorites over the Patriots at […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - AUGUST 23: Will Levis #8 of the Tennessee Titans is tackled by D'Anthony Bell #23 and Aaron Smith #42 of the Seattle Seahawks during the second half of Week 2 of the preseason game at Nissan Stadium on August 23, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Johnnie Izquierdo/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks took care first part of their roster-building process for the 2026 season. Seattle begins its Super Bowl repeat push on Sept. 9 against the New England Patriots, a familiar opponent after the Seahawks defeated New England to win Super Bowl 60 . The defending champions are currently 3.5-point favorites over the Patriots at FanDuel Sportsbook . After finishing the preseason, Seattle must reduce its roster to a maximum of 53 players by 3 p.m. PT on Sunday, August 30 . But the initial 53-man roster is only part of the process. Once the waiver wire process is completed, the Seahawks will begin assembling their practice squad, which can provide additional developmental players and emergency depth throughout the season. The claiming period for players placed on waivers during the final roster reduction expires at 10 a.m. PT on Monday, August 31 . After the league distributes the subsequent Personnel Notice confirming the results of the waiver process, teams can begin forming their practice squads. Seattle enters the waiver process with the 32nd and final priority , meaning all 31 other teams will have an opportunity to claim a player before the Seahawks. The waiver order is based on the 2025 regular-season standings through the first three weeks of the 2026 regular season, with Seattle at the bottom after winning the Super Bowl. That makes the Seahawks’ own collection of players particularly important. Several young players who don’t make the initial 53-man roster could potentially return to Seattle after clearing waivers, while veteran players who are not subject to waivers can immediately negotiate with teams or sign with a practice squad. We’ll track every Seahawks practice squad addition, as well as Seattle’s waiver claims, throughout the process. Practice squad formation rules Teams can begin forming their practice squads after the waiver period expires at 1 p.m. ET on Monday, August 31. The NFL will send a subsequent Personnel Notice confirming the results of the waiver process, and teams can begin signing practice squad players after receiving that notice. A player claimed off waivers cannot go directly to a practice squad. A successful waiver claim means that player goes onto the claiming team’s 53-man roster. The player must first clear waivers before becoming eligible to sign with a practice squad. A standard practice squad consists of 16 players. Teams can have a 17th player if that player qualifies for and is designated under the NFL’s International Player Pathway Program. It is worth mentioning that Seahawks have Federico Maranges, iOL that is part of this program. Players who are not subject to waivers can immediately sign with another team or join a practice squad. Players with four or more accrued seasons are unrestricted free agents when released and are not subject to waivers. Players with three or fewer accrued seasons are subject to the waiver process. As such, players like Eric Saubert and Noah Igbinoghene could be cut and brought back to the team later, just as the Seahawks have done in other years with other veterans. For purposes of an accrued season, a player generally needs to be on full pay status for at least six regular-season games. That includes time on a club’s active/inactive list or certain reserve lists like IR and PUP. Seahawks players claimed off waivers N/A This section will be updated if Seattle makes any waiver claims. Waived Seahawks players who can sign to the practice squad This section will be updated following the Seahawks’ final roster cuts and the completion of the waiver process. QB RB WR TE OL DL LB CB S Players listed here will only be eligible to return to Seattle’s practice squad after they clear waivers, assuming they meet the NFL’s practice squad eligibility requirements. Reported Seahawks practice squad signings No signings yet. This section will be updated as reports emerge and the Seahawks officially assemble their practice squad. Offense Quarterback Running back Wide receiver Tight end Offensive line Defense Defensive line Linebacker Cornerback Safety Special teams Kicker Punter Long snapper Seahawks’ initial practice squad Once Seattle begins making its additions, we’ll organize the initial practice squad by position here. Offense QB: RB: WR: TE: OL: Defense DL: LB: CB: S: Special teams K: P: LS: International Player The practice squad can change frequently throughout the season. Players can be signed, released or elevated to the active roster depending on injuries and roster needs, so the initial group assembled after roster cuts is unlikely to remain unchanged all year. The NFL’s standard elevation mechanism allows practice squad players to be moved to the active roster for a game and subsequently return to the practice squad without immediately being subjected to waivers, subject to the league’s elevation limits. For Seattle, the practice squad will therefore be an important part of maintaining depth behind the 53-man roster, particularly as the defending Super Bowl champions begin the 2026 regular season.

title: NFL Top 100 Players of 2026: Jaxon Smith-Njigba slots in at No. 5
summary: It’d be easy to argue the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks were disrespected on the NFL’s hottest offseason ranking, but their superstar wideout certainly wasn’t. Jaxon Smith-Njigba was ranked 5th on the NFL’s Top 100 Players of 2026 list, marking his first career appearance and the highest of any wide receiver this year. He […]
full_text: It’d be easy to argue the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks were disrespected on the NFL’s hottest offseason ranking, but their superstar wideout certainly wasn’t. Jaxon Smith-Njigba was ranked 5th on the NFL’s Top 100 Players of 2026 list, marking his first career appearance and the highest of any wide receiver this year. He also joined Russell Wilson (No. 2, 2020) Richard Sherman (No. 7, 2014) and Marshawn Lynch (No. 9, 2015) as the only Seahawks to ever be placed in the Top 10. No. 5 on the NFL Top 100 Players of 2026… @Seahawks WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba! @NFLFilms pic.twitter.com/cttIMrAnWn — NFL (@NFL) August 31, 2026 In regards to this season, linebacker LB Ernest Jones IV (No. 97) and quarterback Sam Darnold (No. 21) were previously the only two players from Seattle’s roster to be featured. The four players ranked above JSN (in a TBA order) are Bijan Robinson, Josh Allen, Matthew Stafford, and Myles Garrett. Although Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua (No. 7) was also included in the Top 10 when the list’s final players were released on August 21, there was little doubt Smith-Njigba would earn the edge on the ranking and be the top-ranked receiver on this list. Following an offseason where the Seahawks moved on from longtime receivers DK Metcalf and Tyler Lockett, Smith-Njigba was given the lead duties and took advantage of them, accumulating 119 receptions for a league-leading 1,793 receiving yards en route to winning the Offensive Player of the Year award . His historic season landed him a much deserved four-year, $168.6 million extension , making him the highest paid wide receiver in league history — and perhaps slightly less notably, earning himself a spot in the NFL Top 100. So, while several Seahawks such as defensive tackle Leonard Williams, cornerback Devon Witherspoon and safety Nick Emmanwori may have missed the cut and the respect they deserved, it’s good to know Smith-Njigba didn’t.
