full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - APRIL 24: A general view of the video board on stage with The Pick Is In with the Seattle Seahawks 18th pick during the first round of the 2025 NFL Draft on April 24, 2025 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks made one trade during roster cut-down day, giving up next year’s sixth-rounder to the Los Angeles Chargers for undrafted rookie corner Avery Smith. It’s another bit of roster churn in the secondary for the Super Bowl champions, who are probably not done tinkering at the cornerback position. If you want to stay up to date on Seattle’s 2027 NFL Draft capital, you’ve come to the right place! For a little switch-up, we’re separating the Seahawks’ current, untouched draft picks from the picks they’re slated to receive at some point next March. Seahawks current 2027 draft picks Round 1 Round 2 Round 3 Round 5 Round 7 They lost their 2027 fourth-rounder to the Cleveland Browns to get Beau Stephens , while their sixth-rounder belongs to the Chargers from that aforementioned Smith trade. Now here comes the fun part: the extra picks. Seahawks tentative additional 2027 draft picks Round 3 ( Nolan Teasley comp pick ) Round 4 ( Boye Mafe projected comp pick ) Round 5 ( Kenneth Walker projected comp pick ) Round 5 ( Riq Woolen projected comp pick ) Round 6 ( Coby Bryant projected comp pick ) Round 7 ( conditional pick from Michael Jerrell trade ) Yes, the Seahawks are still poised for 11 total draft picks, with a whopping five compensatory picks on the docket. The Coby Bryant comp pick has been downgraded to a projected sixth-rounder due to Bryant’s potentially season-ending knee injury , which will (obviously) impact his snap count and therefore the comp pick formula. Nolan Teasley going to the Minnesota Vikings to be their GM means that, as a minority candidate, the Seahawks will receive third-round comp picks in the 2027 and 2028 drafts. Lastly, we do not know the conditions of the seventh-rounder the Seahawks received from the Atlanta Falcons in the Michael Jerrell trade, but if it involved making the 2026 Falcons roster then he’s just done that . If for some reason they tied the conditional pick to snaps played even though he’s a career reserve, then maybe it gets dicier. Seattle gave up two picks this offseason/preseason and still has double-digit picks projected for next year. I think the Seahawks can live with only 11 instead of 12, even if the latter is more appropriate for the organization.

title: Seahawks Football 101: What are the different Kinds of safeties?
summary: Safety is a position of pride for the Seattle Seahawks. Some of the biggest contributors to the defense for the team throughout its history have played the position. Within that position, two main variants emerge and have very different roles. In this final installation of Football 101, we will be looking at those two variants […]
full_text: Safety is a position of pride for the Seattle Seahawks. Some of the biggest contributors to the defense for the team throughout its history have played the position. Within that position, two main variants emerge and have very different roles. In this final installation of Football 101, we will be looking at those two variants and explain their roles, while providing examples from the Seahawks history of players who have played those roles. Let’s do this! BAM BAM 💥 Happy birthday, @KamChancellor !! pic.twitter.com/SBDlbbn2d7 — NFL Legacy (@NFLLegacy) April 3, 2019 Free Safety: Earl Thomas III/Julian Love The free safety is an important position, being the “safety net” of the secondary. Their main job is to be the ballhawk, lining up anywhere between 10 to 15 yards back from the line of scrimmage to prevent big plays by the offense, whether it be a big pass, or if a running back is able to break past the front seven. Earl Thomas III and Julian Love are Seahawk examples of free safeties. NFL starts in 29 days. So we shoutout Earl Thomas. When Kam Chancellor tipped the pass to Gronk & BOOM ET comes in and knocks the wind out of Gronk Seahawks LOB was insanely tough. pic.twitter.com/ToKlN5ftBt — Sami ON Tap (@SamiOnTap) August 9, 2023 Strong Safety: Kenny Easley/Kam Chancellor Strong safeties are enforcers on the defense, assisting the linebackers in run support and covering tight ends and slot receivers. They handle more of the short-to-medium routes by receivers, and can also be used in blitz packages to be an extra pass rusher. Kenny Easley (famously nicknamed ‘The Enforcer’ during his decorated, Pro Football Hall of Fame playing career) and Kam Chancellor are the quintessential examples of strong safeties the Seahawks have had on the defense. Legend. Leader. Enforcer. Remembering Kenny Easley. pic.twitter.com/Dq90TblgUR — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) November 15, 2025 Big Nickel Safety: Nick Emmanwori/Jordan Babineaux As discussed in the cornerback 101 I previously wrote , Big Nickel’s are generally a bigger safety that come in to replace a slot corner or linebacker. They are there to assist in run defense, can be used in blitz packages, help cover tight ends, and provide scheme flexibility being able to drop back into coverage if needed. Nick Emmanwori and Jordan Babineaux are the main examples of Big Nickel’s for the Seahawks. They are very flexible, being able to line up in outside linebacker, the slot, or in deeper coverage as needed for the scheme. Jordan Babineaux aka "Big Play Babs" always made big time plays for the Seahawks in the playoffs. One of my favorite Seahawks of the early 2000s. pic.twitter.com/TqsJRKfjSi — Seattle ON Tap (@SeattleONTap) January 5, 2024 Safety is a key position. It ensures plays do not get out of hand and can set the tone for the game. Legends like Chancellor, Thomas, and Easley were the definition of tone setters, while current examples like Love, Okada, Emmanwori and Clark hope to live up to the legacy. Who is on your Mt Rushmore of Seahawk safeties? Discuss in the comments, and Go Hawks! Julian Love said GIVE ME THAT Super Bowl LX on NBC Stream on @NFLPlus + Peacock pic.twitter.com/GxxhuXSzPi — NFL (@NFL) February 9, 2026

title: 5 takeaways from the Seahawks’ initial 53-man roster
summary: The Seattle Seahawks have made their roster cuts to get from 91 players to 53. They’ll keep working on their “70-man roster” by forming their practice squad on Monday, then tinker with the roster some more before Week 1 of the regular season kicks off against the New England Patriots. Best story: Montorie Foster Jr […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MO - AUGUST 28: Montorie Foster Jr #87 of the Seattle Seahawks runs after a catch in the second quarter of an NFL preseason game between the Seattle Seahawks and Kansas City Chiefs on Aug 28, 2026 at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City, MO. (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks have made their roster cuts to get from 91 players to 53 . They’ll keep working on their “70-man roster” by forming their practice squad on Monday, then tinker with the roster some more before Week 1 of the regular season kicks off against the New England Patriots. Best story: Montorie Foster Jr makes the team Perhaps there’s a reason why “Hard Knocks” sought to spotlight Foster from the second episode onward. Foster had an impressive training camp, a somewhat up-and-down preseason but with a few splash plays on offense and some down-and-dirty work on special teams, and he’s been rewarded with a spot on the 53. Not bad for someone who just got his real estate license and spent time as a substitute teacher in Ohio. For now, Foster is Seattle’s fifth wide receiver, and while he may not have the blocking chops of Jake Bobo, he can replace his special teams value and maybe provide a little bit more of a route tree in his limited snaps on offense. Foster is one of those players you root for to succeed, and it helps when his parents have both been a wonderful follow. Their son is now more than just a Seahawks training camp body. Seahawks keep their young offensive linemen With the caveat that Mason Richman’s ACL tear probably shuffled the numbers a tad, Seattle opted to keep both Bryce Cabeldue and Christian Haynes as backup guards. Haynes looked to be in jeopardy of leaving the Seahawks when Beau Stephens was drafted, but instead he enters 2026 off the best camp and preseason of his career. Cabeldue assumed a few snaps at center, just as he (and Haynes) did last year. What Seattle lacks in tackle depth it makes up for in guard depth. Cabeldue was a tackle in college, so he could go out there if needed. Don’t always fall for the “final preseason game” hype We’re firmly entrenched in an era where the final roster cuts are all done in one shot instead of the gradual 90-80-75-53 processes of yesteryear. Starters rarely played in preseason finales over a decade ago and they scarcely get a series today. That means we get a whole lot of dudes who won’t be on the 53-man roster playing out the string in the last preseason game. If you liked the performances of Jared Ivey, Jalen Gaines, Aidan Hubbard, and Andre Fuller against the Kansas City Chiefs, that’s cool. Preseason games are only one marker of many that determine a player’s fate on the team, and only three of the 23 Seahawks defensive players who played more than one series survived roster cuts. I’m not sure Patrick O’Connell would’ve played on Friday night if he didn’t already sit out the Tennessee Titans game the week prior. If there are preseason names who’ve caught your eye by what they did with extended snaps in the last exhibition, you’re essentially watching practice squad football. Seattle’s offense had a few more who made the roster from this game, but when Emmanuel Henderson has a strong showing and is second in wide receiver snaps played (30) when he had 19 total over the previous two games (and ONE in the first half), you have to take the hint. The Seahawks secondary depth remains far from settled We know that Josh Jobe, Devon Witherspoon, Ty Okada, and Julian Love are the starting secondary players for Seattle. Nehemiah Pritchett might be the Day 1 CB3/nickel corner. Nick Emmanwori will obviously factor in whenever he’s ready to play, and he’s damn near closer to a linebacker in disguise than a traditional safety. Every other spot is up for grabs. Trevon Diggs will start on the practice squad in all likelihood , possibly the same for Noah Igbinoghene (although that’s TBD), and they traded for rookie corner Avery Smith . The Julian Neal injury has obviously cost him some valuable practice and game reps time, so he’s essentially behind the curve in year one. At the safety position, by waiving A.J. Finley and Maxen Hook, as well as cutting D’Anthony Bell and Rodney Thomas II, the Seahawks have three safeties (Okada, Love, and Emmanwori) on the roster. That ain’t gonna hold up over the course of the season. There will be more moves made here, but the Bud Clark injury definitely changed the picture here. Bell and Thomas seem like safe bets for the practice squad and some elevations, but over the course of the season they probably need an extra safety at some point. This is currently a 4-player Seahawks 2026 draft class (and that’s fine) None of Emmanuel Henderson Jr, Deven Eastern, Michael Dansby, or Andre Fuller made the initial 53. I would expect at least a couple of those players to make the practice squad, but this is also not a surprise. This was considered a weak draft class across the league, so this year’s seventh-rounders were like UDFAs for stronger classes. At the moment, the rookies on the active roster are Jadarian Price, Julian Neal, and Beau Stephens. Bud Clark is on IR, so he’ll be seen again in 2027. Neal has missed a lot of time due to a quad injury, so it’s basically on Price’s shoulders to provide some rookie contributions this year. Seattle also had none of its own UDFA rookies make the roster, which is similarly unsurprising, but Foster may as well be a UDFA rookie given he was injured last season. Add in Avery Smith and I guess there’s your other UDFA rookie. What’s your biggest takeaway from the Seahawks’ initial roster? Tell us in the comments! Or tell us in The Feed ! Take your pick! summary: The Seattle Seahawks opted to keep just the three running backs during their cut down to their initial 53-man roster on Sunday. Jadarian Price, George Holani, and Emanuel Wilson will be the trio for the early portion of the season, all while Zach Charbonnet recovers from his ACL surgery. As expected, the Seahawks kept Charbonnet […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - JANUARY 3: Zach Charbonnet #26 of the Seattle Seahawks carries the ball during the first quarter of an NFL football game against the San Francisco 49ers at Levi's Stadium on January 03, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks opted to keep just the three running backs during their cut down to their initial 53-man roster on Sunday . Jadarian Price, George Holani, and Emanuel Wilson will be the trio for the early portion of the season, all while Zach Charbonnet recovers from his ACL surgery . As expected, the Seahawks kept Charbonnet on the physically unable to perform (PUP) list to start the regular season. He will have to miss a minimum of four games before he’s eligible to return, so the earliest he could make his debut is Week 5 versus the San Francisco 49ers. It’s worth noting, however, that Week 5 and 6 is a Sunday-Thursday short week, so if they want to be safe then his debut could be Week 7 against the Kansas City Chiefs. One thing to note regarding Charbonnet’s PUP status is an NFL rule change enacted this season. Charbonnet, whose offseason recovery has seemingly gone smoothly, can have his 21-day practice window activated after the second regular season game is completed . Previously, a practice window couldn’t be opened until after the four games were up, so if Charbonnet could be ready to return to practice as early as Week 3. There’s no rush to have Charbonnet available for that 49ers game, but it’d be a full circle moment if his first game back is against the same opponent he scored the only touchdown against in the de facto NFC West title showdown , as well as the same foe in which his season cruelly ended.

title: Which 49ers player landing on the IR would be the worst-case scenario?
summary: The San Francisco 49ers’ 53-man roster is finalized — until they make another five or so moves today. With the team parting ways with long-snapper Jon Weeks and punter Corliss Waitman temporarily, there are a couple of roster spots that are up for grabs. Unfortunately, the 49ers have several options on the roster to place […]
full_text: The San Francisco 49ers’ 53-man roster is finalized — until they make another five or so moves today. With the team parting ways with long-snapper Jon Weeks and punter Corliss Waitman temporarily, there are a couple of roster spots that are up for grabs. Unfortunately, the 49ers have several options on the roster to place on the Injured Reserve. We don’t know how severe some of these injuries are. What we do know is that you can designate up to eight players to return in the regular season — two of those were used on Christian Kirk and Austen Pleasants. Let’s take the linebackers, for example. Luke Gifford and Nick Martin are both dealing with hamstring injuries. Martin’s happened in the second preseason game, while Gifford sustained his injury early on in training camp. Keeping seven linebackers makes it feel like at least one of these players is destined to land on the IR. In the secondary, the 49ers have a pair of players who were in line to start nursing hamstring injuries. Renardo Green’s injury happened in the second preseason game, while Malik Mustapha has been out since the end of July . The team has been mum on both injuries. The lack of depth paired with the importance of both positions in Raheem Morris’s defense makes for a scary proposition if either were to miss time. The unknown for seemingly every injury leads to speculation. Kyle Shanahan said Vederian Lowe was an IR candidate along with Kirk. Lowe has missed a month with a high-ankle sprain. If he goes on the IR, that would mean rookie Enrqiue Cruz is the swing tackle, unless the team would shuffle the deck enough where the rookie wouldn’t see the field. Lowe isn’t the only player dealing with an ankle injury. Rookie Romello Height has had two ankle injuries in the past month. Height could return to practice on Monday. But he didn’t play in the preseason finale, making you wonder if it’s an injury that’ll linger into the regular season. There are six IR candidates, and we left out a couple. Rookie Ephesians Prysock (shoulder) and Nate Hobbs (groin) could easily be on the list. Which 49ers player landing on the IR would be the worst-case scenario? My answer: The obvious answer is Renardo Green. He’s the closest “matchup cornerback” the team has. Height would be a big blow to the 49ers’ pass-rushing depth. The options at edge are thin as it is, and that’s under the assumption that Nick Bosa will be ready to roll for Week 1 — which is a dangerous game to play, knowing it’s unlikely he plays 80% of the snaps. But I’ll go with Malik Mustapha. You have Ji’Ayir Brown, Marques Sigle, and that’s the depth chart. The only defensive snaps Siran Neal played in the preseason were at cornerback. I’m sure Upton Stout could play safety in a pinch, but that would mean you move Deommodore Lenoir inside and Jack Jones has to play on the outside — moves most fans would probably root for. The point is the depth at the position is shaky. You’re one injury away from needing to uproot everything. Mustapha could stabilize that if he’s healthy. While Mustapha isn’t a lock to start, he has the best sample size as a pro (he was quite good as a rookie) and has the highest ceiling of the three safeties. In my mind, Mustapha is one of the wild cards on the 49ers’ defense this season and a player who could really help unlock the ceiling of this defense. Not having him early in the season would be detrimental to the defense. Who is your answer? Scroll down and let us know in the comments.
author: Kyle Posey

title: 49ers ‘final’ 53-man roster: The roster gymnastics are underway
summary: Finally, the San Francisco 49ers’ 53-man roster is here. Quarterbacks (3): Brock Purdy, Mac Jones, Kurtis Rourke The only question here was what the team would do with Rourke. full_text: Finally, the San Francisco 49ers’ 53-man roster is here. Quarterbacks (3): Brock Purdy, Mac Jones, Kurtis Rourke The only question here was what the team would do with Rourke. Would he be stashed on the Injured Reserve, or make the roster? That question was answered. Rourke was healthy enough to make the roster. Running backs(4): Christian McCaffrey, Kaelon Black, Jordan James, Kyle Juszczyk With Isaac Guerendo landing on the PUP and the top three backs returning to practice, there were no real surprises as to who made the roster. It’s worth noting that the 49ers had Jordan James covering punts and kicks in the preseason finale. Perhaps that was to see how he fared and whether he could handle the role. Kaelon Black did not play special teams, which is a sign he’s the RB2, if there was ever any doubt. Wide receivers (6): Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel, De’Zhaun Stribling, Jacob Cowing, Demarcus Robinson, Jordan Watkins Cowing secured a job with an 83-yard punt return in Week 2 of the preseason. The next question was whether Jordan Watkins would stay and whether Christian Kirk would become an IR stash. The 49ers kept Watkins and Cowing. I wonder if Watkins will cover kicks or be the kickoff returner. That’s a role where Deebo excels. Tight ends(4): George Kittle, Luke Farrell, Jake Tonges, Brayden Willis Good ‘ol Mike Florio woke up on Sunday morning trying to agitate the masses, only for Adam Schefter to shoot it down and say Kittle is still in line to play in Week 1. Kittle returning is massive for the 49ers. Everybody knows what he means to the offense. Willis making the roster in Week 1 feels like a hedge in the event Kittle isn’t ready. Offensive line (9): Trent Williams, Carver Willis, Jake Brendel, Dominick Puni, Colton McKivitz, Jarrett Patterson, Vederian Lowe, Enrique Cruz Jr., Connor Colby The Patterson trade is being chalked up as a depth signing, but he has more experience than Carver Willis and has spent multiple seasons playing in the Niners’ scheme under Bobby Slowik. I wonder if the team will give Patterson a look as a starter if they feel like Willis isn’t ready. Even if he is, Patterson is an option down the line. The other question was what the 49ers would do with Connor Colby and Enrique Cruz. Vederian Lowe’s health could’ve potentially sealed Cruz’s fate, while the same is true for Brett Toth and Colby. Toth will begin the season on the IR . Defensive line (9): Nick Bosa, Osa Odighizuwa, Alfred Collins, Sam Okuayinonu, Romello Height, Gracen Halton, CJ West, Keion White, James Thompson Jr. The first two names on this list are going to do a lot of the heavy lifting this season for the 49ers. This team may go as those two do. The rest of the group is largely young and inexperienced. We’ll quickly find out who can and cannot play, and how much seasoning they need before they’re ready. Get well soon, Mykel. Good for Thompson Jr., by the way. He had the fifth-highest win percentage in the preseason among all defensive tackles in true pass sets at 30 percent. Thompson Jr. made the most of his opportunity. He is a mountain of a man who should contribute as a role player as he learns under Kris Kocurek. The defensive tackle rotation figures to be fluid for a while. We’ll see if the team re-signs Ogbo Okonkwo if they feel they cannot add another body at the position after waivers settle. Linebackers (7): Fred Warner, Dre Greenlaw, Jaden Dugger, Luke Gifford, Tatum Bethune, Garret Wallow, Nick Martin Nick Martin and Luke Gifford were the question marks at this spot. Both are battling injuries. We haven’t seen Gifford since the first week of August, while Martin’s injury happened late in the second preseason game. The question was whether the team would place both Martin and Gifford on IR and use their roster spots for another linebacker. The 49ers kept both on the roster — for now. Don’t be surprised if they land on the IR at some point this week. Bethune feels like a core special-teamer. Kyle Shanahan raved about him last year when Bethune was in for Fred Warner. He’s a great run defender. Cornerbacks (7): Renardo Green, Deommodore Lenoir, Upton Stout, Jack Jones, Ephesians Prysock, Nate Hobbs, Siran Neal What you see is what you get with the 49ers cornerbacks. This group was relatively set in stone, barring a Jakob Robinson or Siran Neal making it. Neal means too much to the special teams. However, Nate Hobbs making the roster means the Niners weren’t willing to give up on him, despite missing all of training camp and the preseason. I wouldn’t be shocked to see Hobbs and Prysock placed on the IR this week. Safety(3): Ji’Ayir Brown, Marques Sigle, Malik Mustapha Copy and paste from above, but there weren’t any options outside of Ashtyn Davis, who will live on special teams. However, he was released. When will we see Malik? The safety competition never materialized after Mustapha missed most of the month. He wasn’t a lock to start, for what it’s worth. Mustapha was in the rotation. Specials(1): Eddy Pineiro If they perform as they did in the preseason, the 49ers’ combination of punter and kicker has a chance to be the best it’s been under this regime. The 49ers waived punter Corliss Waitman and long snapper Jon Weeks. They’ve done this move before. It’s another way to ensure players they don’t want to risk losing on the waiver wire stay on the roster. We can expect both players to re-sign and be on the team by Monday. Neither player is subject to waivers. There are a handful of IR candidates the 49ers can use to make room for Waitman and Weeks.

full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - DECEMBER 1: Isaac Guerendo #31 of the San Francisco 49ers scores a touchdown during the second half of an NFL football game against the Buffalo Bills at Highmark Stadium on December 1, 2024 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers placed running back Isaac Guerendo on the reserve/PUP. He will miss the first four games of the season. Guerendo missed all of training camp after suffering a pec injury back in late May . He was an obvious PUP candidate. Guerendo wasn’t going to impact the team in the first month of the season. Placing him on the PUP lets Guerendo return whenever without using one of the Injured Reserve spots. You get to stash him on the PUP. This may have been a different conversation if Christian McCaffrey, Kaelon Black, or Jordan James hadn’t returned from their August injuries. But that is not the case, and the 49ers do the prudent thing here in what figures to be a couple of days full of roster gymnastics. Mykel Williams is another PUP candidate. With the new rule, Guerendo or Williams could have his 21-day practice window opened after Week 2. The team officially placed Williams on the PUP. As for the Injured Reserve, the 49ers could place Kurtis Rourke, Brett Toth, Luke Gifford, Ephesians Prysock, and Nick Martin all on the list. You can effectively keep all of those players without having to “waste” a roster spot. Then you can designate two players to return, likely Christian Kirk and Vederian Lowe. Decisions, decisions.

full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - JANUARY 18: Christian Kirk #13 of the Houston Texans warms up prior to an NFL divisional playoff football game against the New England Patriots at Gillette Stadium on January 18, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan hinted at wide receiver Christian Kirk beginning the season on the Injured Reserve with a designation for return. He said the same about Vederian Lowe. According to Matt Maiocco, that’s true for Kirk, but not the case for Lowe. Instead, Austen Pleasants gets that designation. Pleasants is currently dealing with a knee injury. His ability to play tackle and guard may have made him more valuable to the 49ers with the current state of their offensive line. It also might speak to how serious Lowe’s injury was. Lowe suffered a high-ankle sprain at the end of July. I wonder if he had a setback, or if the injury was bad enough that the team didn’t think he’d be an option to return early in the season. It doesn’t have to be an either/or. It could mean Lowe is close enough to returning that he doesn’t need a designation and can return to practice this week. We shall see. As for Kirk, it’s no surprise that the team will be patient with him. It’s one of the benefits of the Injured Reserve. He has experience in ways that Jacob Cowing and Jordan Watkins do not in the NFL as receivers. Plus, Kirk has production. He will add an element to the passing game the Niners have been missing once he returns. We’ll see how both of these moves impact the 49ers once they release their 53-man roster. Brett Toth and Nick Zakelj were the other two players placed on the Injured Reserve List.

title: 49ers Practice Squad Tracker: KhaDarel Hodge was released
summary: The San Francisco 49ers are starting to make some moves, trimming the 90-man roster to 53. Those that don’t make the 53 have a chance of being placed on the practice squad. The practice squad is important: players on it can travel with the team and do much of the work that any other active […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - FEBRUARY 07: (L-R) General manager John Lynch and head coach Kyle Shanahan speak during San Francisco 49ers practice ahead of Super Bowl LVIII at Fertitta Football Complex on February 07, 2024 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Chris Unger/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers are starting to make some moves, trimming the 90-man roster to 53. Those that don’t make the 53 have a chance of being placed on the practice squad. The practice squad is important: players on it can travel with the team and do much of the work that any other active player does. They just don’t suit up on game day. That means they can help the 49ers prepare for their Week 1 matchup against the Los Angeles Rams. The 49ers sit as 3.5-point underdogs over at FanDuel Sportsbook . The game is in Melbourne, Australia, with the Rams as the designated home team. Without the Rams’ field to help (which usually gets invaded by 49ers fans), the playing field is severely leveled. An NFL practice squad consists of 17 players. One of which is part of the NFL International Pathway Program, six can be veterans with no cap on experience, and the final 10 must be rookies or second-year players. As of this writing, the full 17 spots are available, so the 49ers have lots of flexibility. Of that practice squad, the 49ers get to designate four protected players, which means they can’t be placed on another team’s active roster (basically to stop poaching). Two players can be promoted to the active roster for one week and return to the squad. If they play an additional consecutive week, then the 49ers have to offer the player a one-year deal. In other words, the 49ers want both young talent they can develop over the season and players who can be absolute backups when injuries occur. Some of these players will be protected and won’t even sniff the field for a year while they develop. Others are chances the 49ers take to hold onto unless they sign to another team’s active roster. Isaac Alarcon will be the International Player Pathway exemption following his release, per Matt Maiocco. That allows the 49ers to have 17 on their practice squad. Maiocco also hinted that running back Khalil Herbert, wide receiver KhaDarel Hodge, and edge rusher Ogbo Okoronkwo would be on the plane for Australia on Wednesday. Whether those are “handshake deals” after being released, or they make the initial 53-man roster remains to be seen. We’ll update this thread in the meantime with any rumors or reports of who the 49ers plan to use to fill out the 17 spots on the squad. Kyle’s update, 9:42 a.m. PT: The Ravens released Adisa Isaac, a former third-round pick from the 2024 NFL Draft. The #Ravens are expected to release OLB Adisa Isaac. A former third-round pick who has been hampered by injuries, Isaac is expected to draw interest from teams looking for a young pass rusher. — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) August 30, 2026 Isaac has a long list of injuries in his short career. He only played four games as a rookie due to a hamstring injury that lingered into the season after sustaining it during training camp. Last August, Isaac dislocated his elbow in the preseason. That elbow injury cost Isaac his 2025 season after he underwent surgery in November. Isaac entered the NFL as a raw, toolsy pass rusher. He has elite traits. While he’s only listed at around 247 pounds, Isaac had a broad jump in the 83rd percentile, while his height, arm length, 40, and vertical jump were all in the 60th percentile. The 49ers could buy low on a player like Isaac and hopefully develop him into a role player. Isaac can also contribute on special teams. He’d be a better fit in Raheem Morris’s scheme, as Isaac could play from a two-point stance. The cupboard is bare at the position after Nick Bosa, Mykel Williams, Sam O, and Romello Height. You’re unlikely to have Williams healthy to begin the season. Isaac gives you a power rusher who can drop in coverage with traits to build on. Why not roll the dice on a former third-rounder to see if he can give you more than what Ogbo Okoronkwo can? title: 49ers trade for offensive line depth after releasing Rob Jones
summary: The San Francisco 49ers released Rob Jones, who may not have been healthy enough to practice this upcoming week. We’ll see if Jones re-signs with the team or lands on the practice squad. full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - AUGUST 09: Jarrett Patterson #54 of the Houston Texans looks on prior to the NFL Preseason 2025 game between Houston Texans and Minnesota Vikings at U.S. Bank Stadium on August 09, 2025 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers released Rob Jones , who may not have been healthy enough to practice this upcoming week. We’ll see if Jones re-signs with the team or lands on the practice squad. They may have believed Jones was expendable, which is why the 49ers traded for former Texans guard Jarrett Patterson. The 49ers gave up a 7th-round pick in the 2027 NFL Draft for Patterson. Patterson was drafted by former 49ers offensive coordinator Bobby Slowik back in 2023. As a rookie, Patterson started the first eight games of the season at center. Patterson suffered a fractured fibula in his right leg in Week 8, which cost him the rest of his rookie year in 2023. In 2024, Patterson played 537 snaps at center for Houston. He essentially started every game from Week 10 on that year. During the 2025 regular season, Patterson played 267 snaps at left guard and 67 at center. Last preseason, he was exclusively a center. Patterson spent time playing left and right guard this past preseason for the Texans. According to Sports Info Solutions, Patterson had an above-average blown block rate of 1.5% in 2024. He was close to perfect in pass protection, with only two blown blocks on 341 attempts. Most of his struggles came in the running game. That blown block rate jumped to 3.3%. League average is around 2.7%. Patterson is on a one-year deal in 2026. His guaranteed salary is $1,145 million. The Texans will pay Patterson’s $442,000 signing bonus, so the 49ers are on the hook for Patterson’s cap hit of $1.395 million for 2026. ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler said the Niners were looking to add interior depth. Patterson is that signing. Being able to play left guard in a pinch gives the Niners much-needed versatility. We’ll see if Patterson’s addition spells the end for Drake Nugent, Connor Colby, or both in about an hour and a half. Patterson played most of the preseason finale for the Texans, which is usually a sign that he would’ve been waived.

title: Brandon Aiyuk remains on reserve/left squad list; 49ers don’t have to release him
summary: The San Francisco 49ers are trimming things down to their 53-man roster, and many of you might be looking for the obvious name: Brandon Aiyuk. Well, the thing is, Aiyuk hasn’t shown up to the 49ers’ facility yet and remains on the reserve/left squad list. He is still contractually bound to the 49ers, but he […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 06: Brandon Aiyuk #11 of the San Francisco 49ers warms up prior to a game against the Arizona Cardinals at Levi's Stadium on October 06, 2024 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers are trimming things down to their 53-man roster, and many of you might be looking for the obvious name: Brandon Aiyuk. Well, the thing is, Aiyuk hasn’t shown up to the 49ers’ facility yet and remains on the reserve/left squad list. He is still contractually bound to the 49ers, but he will not count against the 53-man roster. That means the 49ers do not need to take any action on Aiyuk at all. They can trim their roster down to 53 players + Aiyuk. In other words, as long as Aiyuk doesn’t report, the 49ers don’t have to make a move with him. Taking what might have been an August or September release and stretching it indefinitely. It’s been documented that Aiyuk needs to report to the 49ers facility to get this designation removed; however, he’s repeatedly said he’s not “doing any kind of business” with the team, despite everyone telling him the opposite is necessary. While there might not be room for Aiyuk on the 2026 49ers roster, he’s been vocal about wanting to go to Washington. Well, until he got into it with Washington quarterback Jayden Daniels over Instagram. Aiyuk’s latest contributions to 49ers news were his response last week to 49ers owner Jed York’s arrest. In it he mocked York for “getting arrested before him [Aiyuk].” As long as Aiyuk doesn’t report to the 49ers and remains on the reserve/left squad list, the 49ers do not have to remove him to make room for the 53-man roster. He can go to social media all he wants, but that is what would be needed if he wanted to end his relationship with the organization. All of a sudden, the tag of “soon-to-be-former” wide receiver will be “soon-to-be-former-at-some-point” when describing Aiyuk.

title: George Kittle has not had a setback, will practice this week
summary: A throwaway comment from Kyle Shanahan had raised suspicion George Kittle has suffered a setback in his recovery from a torn Achilles. But that is clearly not the case, with a report on Sunday indicating the 49ers’ star tight end is still in with a shot of playing in San Francisco’s season opener against the […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CA - AUGUST 13: George Kittle #85 of the San Francisco 49ers walks on the field before a preseason NFL game against the Tennessee Titans on August 13, 2026 at Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara, CA. (Photo by Matthew Huang/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images A throwaway comment from Kyle Shanahan had raised suspicion George Kittle has suffered a setback in his recovery from a torn Achilles. But that is clearly not the case, with a report on Sunday indicating the 49ers’ star tight end is still in with a shot of playing in San Francisco’s season opener against the Los Angeles Rams in Melbourne. ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported on Sunday that Kittle is set to return to practice this coming week. Schefter added that Kittle has not had any setbacks and still has “a legitimate chance” of playing Week 1. Schefter’s report comes after Shanahan raised eyebrows with his remarks on Kittle following the 49ers’ win over the Las Vegas Raiders in their preseason finale. On injuries impacting the team for Week 1, Shanahan said: “Those are things that we got to evaluate sooner than later. There’s just guys that are going to be close, guys like Mykel Williams, guys like George Kittle who are taking a step back. I want to see how Nick Bosa does in these practices. They’re guys who are healthy and doing good, but are they ready to get back and play right away? That’s why we have these mandatory three days off right now. When we get back, we have those two and a half days before we get on the plane, in those two and a half days we’ll see our practice schedule, we’ll at least get two big ones in maybe a possible third. I’m really curious to how it goes those three days before we go down there.” It may have just been a clumsy choice of words from Shanahan, but Kittle’s return to practice is no guarantee of him featuring in Week 1. It would not be advisable for Kittle to rush his return, particularly for a game that involves traveling on a 15-hour flight. The smart play would likely be to bring Kittle along slowly and have him make his season debut in Week 2 against the Miami Dolphins. But if there is a chance Kittle can play against a division rival, he will likely to push to make sure he does. The 49ers have difficult decisions to make in terms of their roster cuts, but their most important choice ahead of Week 1 will be to decide whether to protect one of their most important offensive players from himself.

NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported Sunday that Tampa Bay is moving forward with Daniels as its primary backup, capping an impressive rise for the former Kansas quarterback. Daniels entered training camp competing simply to earn a roster spot, but his play throughout August pushed him past veteran Jake Browning, who the Buccaneers are releasing. Daniels finished the preseason completing 27 of 44 passes for 239 yards, one touchdown and no interceptions. He also added 37 rushing yards and a touchdown on the ground. The rookie helped spark comeback wins over the Jets and Chiefs before struggling, along with the rest of Tampa Bay’s offense, in Friday’s 19-0 preseason-finale loss to Jacksonville. At Kansas, Daniels appeared in 49 games across six seasons and completed 734 of 1,193 passes for 9,282 yards, 67 touchdowns and 31 interceptions. He also rushed for 1,445 yards and 23 touchdowns. Daniels finished his Jayhawks career second in program history in passing yards and passing touchdowns while becoming one of only two Kansas players to surpass 10,000 yards of total offense.

Among the bigger surprises, veteran guard Cordell Volson and wide receiver Bryce Oliver got cut. Transactions will be processed on Monday at 12 noon ET. We’ve identified three Titans players at risk of immediately losing their roster spot. Austin Deculus, OT Titans fans were disappointed to see Austin Deculus make the initial roster. The veteran swing tackle was absolutely dreadful throughout training camp and the preseason. Despite playing against backups, Deculus allowed three sacks and was terrible in pass protection. Imagine if he had to play against regular-season starters. The Titans desperately need to find an upgrade via the waiver wire process. Former Titan Oli Udoh and Tank Lichtenhan qualify as potential options. Garrett Dellinger, IOL Analyzing the entire 53-man roster, Garrett Dellinger is arguably the biggest surprise inclusion. He garnered little-to-no fan hype during training camp and the preseason. The Titans even kept him over Volson, who plays the same guard position and had guaranteed money on his contract. It’s a heartwarming story for Dellinger, but the Titans could be considering him a placeholder for an upcoming waiver claim at cornerback. Do they need him, Jackson Slater, and Pat Coogan? Probably not. Jerrick Reed II, S Jerrick Reed II was among the slightly surprising defensive backs. He made the roster over guys like Keydrain Calligan, Mario Goodrich III, and Bishop Fitzgerald. Kendell Brooks was waived-injured, and could have taken this roster spot if he was healthy. Reed is an experienced special teams player, and he’s currently the fourth safety. We might be wrong by including him on this list. Perhaps Mike Borgonzi will identify a safety upgrade via waivers.

title: Players the Washington Commanders could pursue after the roster deadline
summary: The preseason schedule is complete, and NFL teams trimmed their rosters to 53 players on Sunday afternoon. Both rookies and veterans alike were released, with different rules applying for each. Players with fewer than four accrued seasons must pass through the waiver wire to become unrestricted free agents. An accrued season is defined as six […]
full_text: The preseason schedule is complete, and NFL teams trimmed their rosters to 53 players on Sunday afternoon. Both rookies and veterans alike were released, with different rules applying for each. Players with fewer than four accrued seasons must pass through the waiver wire to become unrestricted free agents. An accrued season is defined as six or more games on either a team’s roster, injured reserve, or physically unable to perform list. Players that have four or more accrued seasons are immediately free agents and don’t have to go through waivers. Commanders GM Adam Peters continues to build the talent of the roster in his third year at the helm, but some positions are still deficient as quarterback Jayden Daniels enters a critical third season. The following is a list of players that Peters could consider following the cutdown deadline. Some are subject to waivers. Keep in mind that relatively few players are claimed during this period, and last year Washington submitted no claims . This year may be different, as the team finds themselves with obvious needs, especially along the offensive line. The Commanders hold the seventh spot on the waiver order by virtue of last season’s 5-12 finish, so they should have an opportunity to add some talent if they see the right fit. Any player claimed on waivers needs to go directly on the 53-man roster. Center We start with the most obvious area of need. Nick Allegretti has missed the majority of training camp and preseason. Julian Good-Jones looked the part of a perennial practice-squad player and was cut after taking first-team reps through out camp. Sixth-round rookie Matt Gulbin made the final 53-man roster but appeared to need more development. A center is currently the most pressing issue for the team, but Washington did not acquire an additional one before the roster-cuts deadline. Fans have been waiting for this list for a couple of weeks now, but it was projected to be much longer just a mere 24 hours ago. Lucas Patrick (Free Agent) A 33-year-old NFL veteran, Lucas Patrick was originally an undrafted free agent signed by the Green Bay Packers. After spending a few years with the team, he continued his career with several different teams, including the Chicago Bears (2022-2023), New Orleans Saints (2024), and Cincinnati Bengals (2025). Lucas Patrick versus Philadelphia pic.twitter.com/FLGRHcCpl6 — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) August 9, 2025 Patrick has started 28 games at center, 19 games at left guard, and 18 games at right guard in his career, with over 1,000 snaps played at all three spots while being credited with allowing just eight total sacks on 2,607 pass block snaps across his nine NFL seasons, according to Pro Football Focus. Lucas reportedly had a good training camp with no sacks or pressures in 28 pass-blocking snaps this season but found himself caught in the numbers game after the Giants traded for Joshua Ezeudu. Injuries are a concern, but if they are looking for an immediate, experienced, and reliable backup over Matt Gulbin, the Commanders should consider signing him. Nick Dawkins (Waivers) With limited veteran experience available, the Commanders may choose to look for a newer, high-upside addition. An undrafted free agent acquisition of the Baltimore Ravens, Dawkins originally came out of Penn State and has already caught the eye of Hogs Haven writer MattInBrisVegas. He included the Penn State graduate in his pre-draft center roundup , citing Dawkins’ plus athleticism and blocking metrics. In 2025, he split rushing between gap and zone concepts. According to Williams, he thrives on inside zone runs, where he generates movement, with length and mobility to reach, seal, and climb effectively to the second level. The blocking performance metrics show him to be significantly above average in both phases. His Pressure Rate in pass protection ranked 7 th among consensus-ranked centers and was at the 87 th percentile among FBS centers. His Run Blocking Grade ranked 10 th out of 22 consensus ranked centers and was at the 78 th percentile in the FBS. Nick Dawkins is a OC prospect in the 2026 draft class. He scored a 9.77 RAS out of a possible 10.00. This ranked 18 out of 735 OC from 1987 to 2026. https://t.co/PMTG2dWzg7 pic.twitter.com/sd3VTCAUbD — RAS.football (@MathBomb) April 12, 2026 Dawkins received plenty of run in the preseason behind Ethan Pocic, as Danny Pinter went out early with a knee injury and last year’s backup Corey Bullock missed time during the preseason. Nick’s draft profile indicates he is a high IQ player that GM Adam Peters and head coach Dan Quinn seem to look for in a player. Functional strength and experience are needed, but the upside is there. Penn State's OL imposed their will on Oregon's DL. Checkout Nick Dawkins blocking 2 guys at one time ⬇️ pic.twitter.com/ph3uvyMwC4 — LandonTengwall (@LandonTengwall) December 9, 2024 Guard Sam Cosmi has the starting right guard position locked down, but Chris Paul won the left guard spot by default after Brandon Coleman took over left tackle for Laremy Tunsil. He has reportedly struggled in camp this season, but the team has yet to field a legitimate contender for the starting role. At a minimum the team needs to upgrade the depth at the position. The team kept undrafted guard Tanoa Togiai, but will most certainly look for an upgrade. Evan Neal (Free Agent) Peters may need to get creative and try to convert a tackle to acquire a starting-level talent. Originally drafted as tackle prospect, the Giants switched No. 7 overall selection Evan Neal to guard during the 2025 season, but the project never got off the ground due to setbacks from an offseason ankle surgery. New Giants head coach John Harbaugh saw something in Neal and offered him a one-year contract to stay with the team in 2026, and while he has reportedly shown some progress this offseason, Neal was cut by the Giants on Sunday. Fans may be skeptical of his potential, but a film review of his play at guard by SB Nation’s Big Blue View is encouraging. Guard seems to agree with Neal when it comes to pass protection. His feet are much more controlled, which translates to improved hand usage. Neal tended to let his hands drift high and wide as he used them for balance while mirroring speed at tackle. He’s able to keep his punch loaded without as much ground to cover, which allows him to fire his punch into defenders’ chest plates and win inside leverage……Neal’s power and play strength leap off the screen in both run blocking and pass protection. His height demands that he plays with good hip and pad level, but he’s the type of blocker who can take a defender out of the play once he latches on. It is not all positive, as his height works against him when trying to create leverage, he tends to lunge at times, and his overall game is inconsistent. Still, for a player available in late August, Neal represents potential the Washington Commanders do not currently have at the position. The team had some success reclaiming Ereck Flowers in 2019; perhaps Evan Neal could be the next Giants tackle to succeed for them at the guard position. Pin-pull Evan Neal to the play side to lead. Skip, square to target, and hit to the inside of No. 41 behind the blocks of J.C. Davis and Thomas Fidone II. pic.twitter.com/vxtFtjbfeK — Nick Falato (@nickfalato) August 29, 2026 Elijah Klein (Waivers) A sixth-round selection of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in 2024, Elijah Klein is profiled with NFL length and power but average athleticism. He offers the desired versatility with 55 collegiate starts, including right guard, tackle, and guard/center flexibility. . @UTEPFB @ElijahKlein79 has game experience; versatility; length; good raw strength; and he enjoys hitting people. And Tuff. Who doesnt love Elijah Klein??? Look forward to watching him at the next level. #nfldraft #BaldysBreakdowns pic.twitter.com/SLElGxkTCm — Brian Baldinger (@BaldyNFL) April 16, 2024 While the Elijah’s athleticism may be…

title: Commanders designate Trey Amos, Jeremy McNichols to return off injured reserve
summary: On Sunday, the Washington Commanders placed cornerback Trey Amos and running back Jeremy McNichols on injured reserve with a designation to return as part of the team’s initial 53-man roster cut.   Also, defensive lineman Deatrich Wise Jr. was placed on the physically unable to perform list. He hasn’t practiced at all in camp while […]
full_text: On Sunday, the Washington Commanders placed cornerback Trey Amos and running back Jeremy McNichols on injured reserve with a designation to return as part of the team’s initial 53-man roster cut. Also, defensive lineman Deatrich Wise Jr. was placed on the physically unable to perform list. He hasn’t practiced at all in camp while recovering from a torn quadriceps during the 2025 campaign. All three of those guys must miss at least the first four weeks/games. NFL teams are allowed to designate two players to return off IR that don’t count as part of the 53-man roster right at roster cuts. Amos missed the entire offseason program recovering from a fractured fibula that ended his 2025 season. He dealt with soft-tissue soreness early in training camp, before he was finally cleared to return in mid-August. Amos suffered an ankle sprain in his second practice back and hasn’t returned since. Starting the season on IR will allow him to rehab at a proper pace without taking up a roster spot while doing so. It’s a setback for the Commanders defense, considering he was expected to be their No. 1 cornerback. They’ll make do with a combination of Amik Robertson, Mike Sainristil and Rasul Douglas, among others. McNichols suffered a significant quadriceps injury early in camp and hasn’t been back since. He’s a versatile veteran who’s a solid third-down back and quality pass protector, which is why they wanted him in Washington. Each team can designate a maximum of eight players to return off injured reserve, though the rest of them must be on the initial 53-man roster or sign with Washington after it’s formed. With uncertainty about whether left tackle Laremy Tunsil (torn triceps) and defensive lineman Johnny Newton (torn pec) can return this season, those guys remain on the active roster for a short while. They’ll be moved to IR soon, without the formal designation to return. If it’s determined later — both guys had surgery in recent weeks — that they can’t return, the Commanders won’t have to burn a return designation. Tunsil got hurt during a one-on-one rep with edge rusher Odafe Oweh on Aug. 8. It didn’t look bad at first, but the severity of the injury came to light later that day. He has since had surgery and is on the path to recovery. That sent the Commanders offensive line into a spiral, with Brandon Coleman moving to left tackle after previously battling Chris Paul to be the starting left guard. The front hasn’t been the same since. Tunsil will only be of use if they Commanders can be competitive without him and position themselves for a playoff berth. Newton suffered a torn pectoral muscle during the preseason game against the Miami Dolphins and had surgery on Aug. 19 .
author: Scott Bair

title: Analyzing Washington Commanders 53-man roster position by position
summary: The initial Commanders 53-man roster has been set. Washington had to make a series of cuts before Sunday’s 6 p.m. ET deadline to do so, and formally announced those transactions shortly after. The word “initial” in that first sentence is key, considering there are obvious gaps to fill and adjustments to be made before facing […]
full_text: The initial Commanders 53-man roster has been set. Washington had to make a series of cuts before Sunday’s 6 p.m. ET deadline to do so, and formally announced those transactions shortly after. The word “initial” in that first sentence is key, considering there are obvious gaps to fill and adjustments to be made before facing off against the Philadelphia Eagles on Sept. 13. This remaining group battled through a training camp and preseason designed to heighten competition throughout the roster. The Commanders went through some trials over the last six-ish weeks, with injuries impacting most every position group listed below. Losing elite left tackle Laremy Tunsil was a major blow that set the offensive line off its axis. Going through most of this summer’s work without center Nick Allegretti (calf) exposed flaws in offensive line depth, at that position and guard. Trey Amos is dealing with ankle issues and was placed on injured reserve with a designation to return. So was running back Jeremy McNichols (quad). In addition, the three best members of the defensive front – Odafe Oweh, K’Lavon Chaisson and Daron Payne – have been out the past few weeks. Expect general manager Adam Peters to keep an eye on the waiver wire and make some pickups as we move forward. While we know moves are coming, let’s break down this 53-man roster as currently constructed by position group, with an eye on what comes next: QUARTERBACKS (3) Jayden Daniels Marcus Mariota Athan Kaliakmanis Analysis: The Commanders stick with three quarterbacks, a smart move for right now considering Marcus Mariota’s recovering from a right MCL sprain. The Commanders obviously hope Jayden Daniels takes every snap representing the quarterbacks. Kaliakmanis showed well in the preseason, and has the developmental QB spot previously held by Sam Hartman. RUNNING BACKS (3) Bill Croskey-Merritt Rachaad White Kaytron Allen Note: Jeremy McNichols was placed on injured reserve with a designation to return Analysis: The Commanders have just three running backs on the roster right now, but that figures to change in the coming days. Going with three runners seems like a razor-thin margin. Bill Croskey-Merritt and Rachaad White will take most of the carries, with Allen in reserve. RECEIVERS (7) Terry McLaurin Stefon Diggs Antonio Williams Luke McCaffrey Jaylin Lane Treylon Burks Dyami Brown Analysis: Keeping seven receivers should be considered unorthodox, but Jaylin Lane and Luke McCaffrey are the primary returners and essential components of the kick/punt coverage teams. Will Washington hang on to seven receivers all season? That seems doubtful. The Commanders clearly weren’t ready to give up on McCaffrey, a dynamic playmaker who had an up-and-down camp. Overall, this group is super deep and clearly fortified by the Stefon Diggs signing. Antonio Williams looks like the real deal and should see significant playing time right away. TIGHT ENDS (4) John Bates Chig Okonkwo Ben Sinnott Colson Yankoff Analysis: The Commanders need four tight ends considering how many multiple-TE sets they’ll run. This was always the intended quartet, with a versatile group that can block and be impactful in the passing game. Colson Yankoff earned his spot with a strong camp and former second-rounder Ben Sinnott has potential to be weapon in Washington’s new scheme. OFFENSIVE LINE (10) Brandon Coleman Chris Paul Nick Allegretti Sam Cosmi Josh Conerly Jr. D.J. Humphries Andrew Wylie Matt Gulbin Laremy Tunsil Tanoa Togiai Analysis: There’s just no way this collection will be what Washington brings to the regular-season opener. They need another center, possibly an interior lineman to round out the group. Expect Washington to be active on the waiver wire come Monday. Undrafted guard Tanoa Togiai was a surprise inclusion, but the Utah product is a people mover and will be a top reserve at the guard spot. Or he might be a short-term player on the active roster, moved in favor of a more experienced guard or center acquired via waivers or free agency. Laremy Tunsil is on the active roster but will surely be placed on injured reserve tomorrow. This move allows the Commanders to save one of eight designations to return should it be determined down the line that he’s done for the year. DEFENSIVE LINE (6) Daron Payne Charles Omenihu Tim Settle Javon Kinlaw Johnny Newton Ricky Barber Analysis: Seeing Shy Tuttle cut was a bit of a surprise, but ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports that Washington expects to bring him back before Week 1. That means there’s a handshake deal to get him back on the roster – he’s a veteran and therefore not subject to waivers – that will help the Commanders sneak another player onto the roster. Newton will move to IR tomorrow, with Tuttle likely returning. As with the Tunsil scenario, this allows Washington to preserve a designation to return should Newton not be able to come back. Ricky Barber earned his place in this group with a strong preseason. He should be helpful on the back end of the rotation. EDGE RUSHERS (4) Odafe Oweh K’Lavon Chaisson Joshua Josephs Javontae Jean-Baptiste NOTE: Dorance Armstrong was placed on the reserve/suspended list. Analysis: Expect Odafe Oweh and K’Lavon Chaisson to play a ton on rushing and passing downs. Joshua Josephs looks pretty good for a rookie Day 3 pick. Javontae Jean-Baptiste had a strong preseason as well. And don’t forget that Dorance Armstrong will be a heavy part of the mix once he returns from a one-game suspension for violating the NFL’s personal conduct policy. INSIDE LINEBACKERS (5) Sonny Styles Frankie Luvu Leo Chenal Jordan Magee Kain Medrano Analysis: While Kain Medrano didn’t finish strong — his preseason finale was not the best — the athletic linebacker will be a core piece of Washington’s special teams and fits the profile of athletic linebackers. Jordan Magee should be the primary backup, with Sonny Styles, Frankie Luvu and Leo Chenal playing a ton. CORNERBACKS (3) Mike Sainristil Amik Robertson Rasul Douglas NOTE: Trey Amos was placed on injured reserve with a designation to return. Analysis: Let’s just be frank. There is no way in holy heck that the Commanders go into Week 1 with just three cornerbacks, even with a versatile group of safeties who can play in the slot and a number of three-safety looks in store this season. You’d think that Fabian Moreau will be back soon . Either him or Antonio Hamilton Sr. Also, this Trey Amos situation is concerning. He has practiced just twice since fracturing his fibula last season, and has now been placed on IR. Washington fortified the position group with savvy veteran Rasul Douglas. It’ll be interesting to see who plays in the slot, whether it’s Mike Sainristil or Amik Robertson or a safety. Coordinator Daronte Jone has options. SAFETIES (5) Quan Martin Nick Cross Jeremy Reaves Tyler Owens Percy Butler Analysis: The Will Harris cut settled the safety group into this fashion. Nick Cross is a true three-down player, and while Jeremy Reaves has generally been a first-teamer, don’t count Quan Martin out after a strong preseason. Tyler Owens’ excellent work this summer may have earned him a defensive role. He’s a thumper, man, a tone setter who could play well in the slot. Martin can play inside as well. SPECIALISTS (3) Drew Stevens Tress Way Tyler Ott Analysis: Drew Stevens being named the kicker over Jake Moody took the intrigue out of this segment of the roster. Tress Way’s as good as punters get and Tyler Ott’s a cagey vet.

title: Commanders News: Has Adam Peters given Dan Quinn a winning roster?
summary: The Daily Slop – 30 August 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links Articles The Athletic (paywall) […]
full_text: The Daily Slop – 30 August 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links Articles The Athletic (paywall) Commanders’ shaky preseason requires immediate fortification before the regular season The Commanders sat 41 players before a 41-3 loss to the Ravens, capping an ugly end to training camp which started with Baltimore’s first-team defense dominating Washington’s available starters for most of last Wednesday’s joint practice. The Ravens’ third- and fourth-teamers then smacked Washington’s around at M&T Bank Stadium for four quarters. Dan Quinn had clarified going into the week that Wednesday would be the last bit of preseason business for not just Jayden Daniels, but almost everyone on the two-deep chart. Almost no one Friday made a case for making the team that hadn’t already done so, leaving Quinn miffed. The Commanders’ OTAs and (most of) training camp point to a team that should be more competitive than last season’s 5-12 version — though a brutal schedule the first eight weeks may render that preparation moot. They point to an offense that first-year offensive coordinator David Blough spun up that could put points on the board behind a more balanced attack around Daniels. Though the long-term triceps injury to star tackle Laremy Tunsil has shaken the offensive line’s depth and potential. Still, amid the finite disappointment of this last week, alongside a mistake-filled outing in Detroit a week ago, there’s hope for a turnaround once the games start to count. The staff, including new defensive coordinator Daronte Jones, threw a lot at this group. They absorbed much of it, but there is much to clean up. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE The Ringer NFC East Preview: Is This the Cowboys’ Year? What’s at Stake for the Commanders I’m not saying for sure that Dan Quinn is on tilt about saving his job. But if he were on tilt about saving his job, this is what that would look like: Fire both coordinators. Hire two new coordinators who have no experience doing the job. And implement spelling bees and friendship quizzes to improve team morale. Quinn seems like a nice enough guy. And I think he can be (and has been) a good coach in the right situation. But we all know the score here. If the Commanders underperform like they did last season, Quinn will be gone, and they will try to find a young, offensive-minded head coach who can maximize Jayden Daniels’s talents. How I See It If you squint, you can see some upside for this team. But there are a lot of ifs. And the Commanders are facing the NFL’s ninth-hardest schedule . The truth is that there are as many unknowns here as there are for any team in the NFL. If some bounces go the Commanders’ way, they could be a little sleepery and compete for a playoff spot. But I think that the most likely scenario is a season stuck in mediocrity. Projected record: 8-9 To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Sports Illustrated Washington owns the No. 7 waiver priority as it works toward its initial 53-man roster The Washington Commanders officially have until 6 p.m. Sunday to cut their roster from 91 down to 53 players , a process they started Saturday night . One thing to keep in mind: no matter who is on the original list, it can and likely will change frequently before the team kicks off the season in Week 1 against the Philadelphia Eagles. Currently, Washington owns the No. 7 position in the waiver order, meaning Commanders GM Adam Peters has the priority to claim players before 25 other teams get a chance. Through the third regular-season game, the waiver wire order will reflect the 2026 NFL Draft order. The six teams that can claim players before Washington are the Las Vegas Raiders, New York Jets, Arizona Cardinals, Tennessee Titans, New York Giants, and the Cleveland Browns. For a Washington claim to succeed, none of the six teams ahead of them can put in a claim for that same player. The waiver order gives the Commanders’ front office leverage over the teams at the bottom of the stack as Washington continues working to improve the bottom of its roster. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Riggo’s Rag Commanders must resist glaring waiver-wire trap from Dan Quinn’s past According to reports, the New York Jets have waived defensive lineman Mazi Smith following a brief yet underwhelming stint with the AFC East club. He was part of the trade package that sent Quinnen Williams to the Dallas Cowboys, but he didn’t do enough to make any sort of impact. Commanders should not entertain Mazi Smith waiver claims after Jets exit Of course, Quinn was the defensive coordinator in Dallas when Smith was selected No. 26 overall in the 2023 NFL Draft. His lack of consistency and effort led to his failings, and the Cowboys were only too willing to give him away in their quest to acquire a legitimate difference-maker in Williams. Quinn is extremely loyal to his players, old and new. The Commanders also have some depth concerns in the defensive trenches after losing 2024 second-round pick Johnny Newton to a torn pectoral muscle . However, they should not remotely consider Smith as a viable option. The Michigan product just doesn’t look interested in playing football most of the time. Quinn gave him countless chances as a rookie in Dallas, but he almost always fluffed his lines. Things didn’t get much better once the coach departed, and the Jets were signing guys off the street rather than giving him game time over the second half of 2025. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE NFC East links Bleeding Green Nation Eagles part ways with former Commanders DB TARIQ CASTRO-FIELDS TCF was having a decent summer before suffering a heel injury that landed him on injured reserve on August 21. Now he’s leaving Philly after reaching an injury settlement with the team. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Eagles waive OL Myles Hinton The Philadelphia Eagles waived 2025 sixth-round pick Myles Hinton on Saturday, according to a report from NFL insider Adam Schefter . Hinton’s departure doesn’t come as a surprise ; he really struggled this summer. The Eagles originally experimented with moving the 24-year-old to guard earlier this offseason before putting him back at offensive tackle, where he didn’t play well. Perhaps the Eagles will bring Hinton back on the practice squad if he clears waivers but I tend to think he might look for a fresh start. It’s worth noting that Jeff Stoutland, who left the Eagles earlier this year, seemed to be a big fan of Hinton when he was drafted. Hinton is the third member of the Eagles’ 2025 NFL Draft class to be dismissed by the team. They previously cut Kyle McCord and Antwaun Powell-Ryland Jr. (who made some plays against the Birds for the Cincinnati Bengals on Friday night) last year. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Blogging the Boys Here is what the Cowboys are getting in Broderick Jones Jones was the fourth offensive lineman selected in the 2023 draft because of his great athleticism. He showed impressive speed for a guy his size. He possessed agility and power from heavy hands and a strong grip. He didn’t allow a single sack in 2022, and he helped the Georgia Bulldogs win back-to-back National Championships. The sky was the limit for this athletically gifted lineman. Unfortunately, his NFL adventure has not been so pleasant. The Steelers moved him to right tackle midway through his rookie season, where he did okay in run support, but struggled mightily in pass protection. It was a mixed bag, but there was definitely something to work with. Things went south during his second year. Right tackle wasn’t his thing. He wasn’t technically sound, and speed rushers abused him regularly. He gave up 11 sacks and frequently committed penalties. Last season, he moved back to his…
